questions.questionStem: The reasoning above conforms most closely to which one of the following principles?

answerChoices.A: Political freedom is a virtue that a community can attain through an external force.
answerChoices.B: Self-determination is not the first political virtue that the members of a community achieve in their struggle to become free.
answerChoices.C: A community cannot remain free without first having developed certain political virtues.
answerChoices.D: Political self-determination is required if a community is to remain truly free.
answerChoices.E: Real freedom should not be imposed on a community by external forces.

questions.stimulus: Some residents of Midville claim that Midville is generally more expensive to live in than nearby towns are, but these people are mistaken. They focus on Midville’s relatively high tax rate while ignoring the services paid for by their taxes. Only Midville provides residents with trash removal, rent- and mortgage-assistance programs, and reasonably priced public transportation. In nearby towns individuals pay for their own trash removal, and housing and transportation costs are high in comparison to Midville.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is the main point of the argument?

answerChoices.A: Midville is generally no more expensive to live in than nearby towns are.
answerChoices.B: Some of the residents of Midville consider their taxes to be too high.
answerChoices.C: Services funded by a municipality are generally less expensive than those services would be if privately funded.
answerChoices.D: Some residents of Midville are unaware of many of the services that Midville provides.
answerChoices.E: Most of the residents of Midville make use of all of the services the town provides.

questions.stimulus: A student has taken twelve courses and received a B in a majority of them. The student is now taking another course and will probably, given her record, receive a B in it.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, strengthens the argument except:

answerChoices.A: The student previously studied alone but is receiving help from several outstanding students during the present course.
answerChoices.B: The twelve courses together covered a broad range of subject matter.
answerChoices.C: The student previously studied in the library and continues to do so.
answerChoices.D: The student received a B in all but one of the twelve courses.
answerChoices.E: The current course is a continuation of one of the twelve courses in which the student received a B.

questions.stimulus: If the government increases its funding for civilian scientific research, private patrons and industries will believe that such research has become primarily the government’s responsibility. When they believe that research is no longer primarily their responsibility, private patrons and industries will decrease their contributions toward research. Therefore, in order to keep from depressing the overall level of funding for civilian scientific research, the government should not increase its own funding.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument relies?

answerChoices.A: Governments should bear the majority of the financial burden of funding for civilian scientific research.
answerChoices.B: Any increase in government funding would displace more private funding for civilian scientific research than it would provide.
answerChoices.C: Private donations toward research are no longer welcomed by researchers whose work receives government funding.
answerChoices.D: Civilian scientific research cannot be conducted efficiently with more than one source of funding.
answerChoices.E: Funding for civilian scientific research is currently at the highest possible level.

questions.stimulus: For any given ticket in a 1000-ticket lottery, it is reasonable to believe that that ticket will lose. Hence, it is reasonable to believe that no ticket will win.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following exhibits flawed reasoning most similar to the flawed reasoning in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: It is reasonable to believe for any randomly drawn playing card that it will not be an ace, so it is reasonable to believe that an ace will never be drawn.
answerChoices.B: When the chances of a certain horse winning the race are 999 out of 1000, it is reasonable to believe that that horse will win. So it is reasonable to believe that no one other than that horse can win.
answerChoices.C: It is unreasonable to believe that 1000 consecutive coin flips will turn up heads, so it is reasonable to believe that this never happens.
answerChoices.D: It is reasonable to believe that if the most recent flip of a given coin was tails, the next flip will be heads. So if a coin has turned up tails the last 1000 times it was flipped, it is reasonable to believe that it will turn up heads the next time it is flipped.
answerChoices.E: For any given group of five-year-old children, the average height is one meter, so it is reasonable to believe that if Pat is five years old, she is exactly one meter tall.

questions.stimulus: Dental researcher: Filling a cavity in a tooth is not a harmless procedure: it inevitably damages some of the healthy parts of the tooth. Cavities are harmful only if the decay reaches the nerves inside the tooth, and many cavities, if left untreated, never progress to that point. Therefore, dentists should not fill a cavity unless the nerves inside the tooth are in imminent danger from that cavity.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most strongly supports the researcher’s reasoning?

answerChoices.A: Dentists should perform any procedure that is likely to be beneficial in the long term, but only if the procedure does not cause immediate damage.
answerChoices.B: Dentists should help their patients to prevent cavities rather than waiting until cavities are present to begin treatment.
answerChoices.C: A condition that is only potentially harmful should not be treated using a method that is definitely harmful.
answerChoices.D: A condition that is typically progressive should not be treated using methods that provide only temporary relief.
answerChoices.E: A condition that is potentially harmful should not be left untreated unless it can be kept under constant surveillance.

questions.stimulus: The number of codfish in the North Atlantic has declined substantially as the population of harp seals has increased from two million to more than three million. Some blame the seal for the shrinking cod population, but cod plays a negligible role in the seal’s diet. It is therefore unlikely that the increase in the seal population has contributed significantly to the decline in the cod population.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: People who fish for cod commercially are inconvenienced by the presence of large numbers of seals near traditional fishing grounds.
answerChoices.B: Water pollution poses a more serious threat to cod than to the harp seal.
answerChoices.C: The harp seal thrives in water that is too cold to support a dense population of cod.
answerChoices.D: Cod feed almost exclusively on capelin, a fish that is a staple of the harp seal’s diet.
answerChoices.E: The cod population in the North Atlantic began to decline before the harp-seal population began to increase.

questions.stimulus:
Hospital auditor: The Rodriguez family stipulated that the funds they donated to the neurological clinic all be used to minimize patients’ suffering. The clinic administration is clearly violating those terms, since it has allocated nearly one fifth of those funds for research into new diagnostic technologies, instead of letting that money flow directly to its patients.

Clinic administrator: But the successful development of new technologies will allow early diagnosis of many neurological disorders. In most cases, patients who are treated in the early stages of neurological disorders suffer far less than do patients who are not treated until their neurological disorders reach advanced stages.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is the main point at issue between the hospital auditor and the clinic administrator?

answerChoices.A: Whether early treatment of many neurological disorders lessens the suffering associated with those disorders rather than completely eliminating such suffering
answerChoices.B: Whether the patients being treated at the neurological clinic are currently receiving adequate treatment for the neurological disorders from which they suffer
answerChoices.C: Whether the Rodríguez family clearly stipulated that the funds they donated to the neurological clinic be used to minimize patients’ suffering
answerChoices.D: Whether the neurological clinic is adhering strictly to the conditions the Rodríguez family placed on the allocation of the funds they donated to the clinic
answerChoices.E: Whether the Rodríguez family anticipated that some of the funds they donated to the neurological clinic would be used to pay for research into new diagnostic technologies

questions.stimulus:
Hospital auditor: The Rodriguez family stipulated that the funds they donated to the neurological clinic all be used to minimize patients’ suffering. The clinic administration is clearly violating those terms, since it has allocated nearly one fifth of those funds for research into new diagnostic technologies, instead of letting that money flow directly to its patients.

Clinic administrator: But the successful development of new technologies will allow early diagnosis of many neurological disorders. In most cases, patients who are treated in the early stages of neurological disorders suffer far less than do patients who are not treated until their neurological disorders reach advanced stages.
questions.questionStem: The clinic administrator responds to the hospital auditor by doing which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Demonstrating that the hospital auditor’s conclusion, though broadly correct, stands in need of a minor qualification
answerChoices.B: Showing that the hospital auditor’s argument fails to separate what is the case from what ought to be the case
answerChoices.C: Reminding the hospital auditor that, in the case at issue, being told what to do is tantamount to being told how to do it
answerChoices.D: Arguing that, in assessing the severity of a violation, the reasoning motivating the violation needs to be considered
answerChoices.E: Reinterpreting a key phrase in the hospital auditor’s argument so as to undermine an assumption underlying that argument

questions.stimulus: Generally speaking, if the same crop is sown in a field for several successive years, growth in the later years is poorer than growth in the earlier years, since nitrogen in the soil becomes depleted. Even though alfalfa is a nitrogen-fixing plant and thus increases the amount of nitrogen in the soil, surprisingly, it too, if planted in the same field year after year, grows less well in the later years than it does in the earlier years.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the similarity described above between alfalfa and non-nitrogen-fixing plants?

answerChoices.A: Some kinds of plants grow more rapidly and are more productive when they are grown among other kinds of plants rather than being grown only among plants of their own kind.
answerChoices.B: Alfalfa increases the amount of nitrogen in the soil by taking nitrogen from the air and releasing it in a form that is usable by most kinds of plants.
answerChoices.C: Certain types of plants, including alfalfa, produce substances that accumulate in the soil and that are toxic to the plants that produce those substances.
answerChoices.D: Alfalfa increases nitrogen in the soil in which it grows only if a certain type of soil bacteria is present in the soil.
answerChoices.E: Alfalfa is very sensitive to juglone, a compound that is exuded from the leaves of black walnut trees.

questions.stimulus: Political commentators see recent policies of the government toward Country X as appeasement, pure and simple. This view is fundamentally mistaken, for polls show that most people disagree with the political commentators’ assessment of government policies toward Country X.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is questionable because

answerChoices.A: the term “policies” is used ambiguously in the argument
answerChoices.B: the political commentators discussed in the passage are not identified
answerChoices.C: a claim is inferred to be false merely because a majority of people believe it to be false
answerChoices.D: the claim that the political commentators are mistaken is both a premise and a conclusion in the argument
answerChoices.E: it is assumed that what is true of persons individually is true of a country as a whole

questions.stimulus: It is a principle of economics that a nation can experience economic growth only when consumer confidence is balanced with a small amount of consumer skepticism.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an application of the economic principle above?

answerChoices.A: Any nation in which consumer confidence is balanced with a small amount of consumer skepticism will experience economic growth.
answerChoices.B: Any nation in which the prevailing attitude of consumers is not skepticism will experience economic growth.
answerChoices.C: Any nation in which the prevailing attitude of consumers is either exclusively confidence or exclusively skepticism will experience economic growth.
answerChoices.D: Any nation in which the prevailing attitude of consumers is exclusively confidence will not experience economic growth.
answerChoices.E: Any nation in which consumer skepticism is balanced with a small amount of consumer confidence will experience economic growth.

questions.stimulus: Sharks have a higher ratio of cartilage mass to body mass than any other organism. They also have a greater resistance to cancer than any other organism. Shark cartilage contains a substance that inhibits tumor growth by stopping the development of a new blood network. In the past 20 years, none of the responses among terminal cancer patients to various therapeutic measures has been more positive than the response among those who consumed shark cartilage.
questions.questionStem: If the claims made above are true, then each of the following could be true except:

answerChoices.A: No organism resists cancer better than sharks do, but some resist cancer as well as sharks.
answerChoices.B: The organism most susceptible to cancer has a higher percentage of cartilage than some organisms that are less susceptible to cancer.
answerChoices.C: The substance in shark cartilage that inhibits tumor growth is found in most organisms.
answerChoices.D: In the past 20 years many terminal cancer patients have improved dramatically following many sorts of therapy.
answerChoices.E: Some organisms have immune systems more efficient than a shark’s immune system.

questions.stimulus:
The following passage is used for Section 1, questions 12 through 13.
People who say that Dooney County is flat are clearly wrong. On flat land, soil erosion by water is not a problem. Consequently, farmers whose land is flat do not build terraces to prevent erosion. Yet I hear that the farms in Dooney County are dotted with terraces.
questions.questionStem: The author’s conclusion in the passage depends on the assumption that

answerChoices.A: the only cause of soil erosion is water
answerChoices.B: there are terraces on farmland in Dooney County which were built to prevent soil erosion
answerChoices.C: terraces of the kind found on farmland in Dooney County have been shown to prevent soil erosion
answerChoices.D: on flat land there is no soil erosion
answerChoices.E: the only terraces in Dooney County are on farmland

questions.stimulus:
The following passage is used for Section 1, questions 12 through 13.
People who say that Dooney County is flat are clearly wrong. On flat land, soil erosion by water is not a problem. Consequently, farmers whose land is flat do not build terraces to prevent erosion. Yet I hear that the farms in Dooney County are dotted with terraces.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the passage is most similar to that in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: If we paint the room white, it will get smudged, and we will have to paint it again soon. Therefore, we should paint it dark blue.
answerChoices.B: People with children need more space than those without children. Yet people with no children can usually afford bigger houses.
answerChoices.C: People who get a lot of exercise have no trouble falling asleep; hence, people who get a lot of exercise do not use medication to help them fall asleep. Jack is taking many kinds of medication, so he must not be getting a lot of exercise.
answerChoices.D: If I go grocery shopping when I am hungry, I buy snack foods and cannot resist eating them. Therefore, I cannot lose weight.
answerChoices.E: People who have many friends tend to go out often, so they need cars. Therefore, if Joe wants to have many friends, he must buy a car.

questions.stimulus: The axis of Earth’s daily rotation is tilted with respect to the plane of its orbit at an angle of roughly 23 degrees. That angle can be kept fairly stable only by the gravitational influence of Earth’s large, nearby Moon. Without such a stable and moderate axis tilt, a planet’s climate is too extreme and unstable to support life. Mars, for example, has only very small moons, tilts at wildly fluctuating angles, and cannot support life.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true on the basis of them?

answerChoices.A: If Mars had a sufficiently large nearby moon, Mars would be able to support life.
answerChoices.B: If Earth’s Moon were to leave Earth’s orbit, Earth’s climate would be unable to support life.
answerChoices.C: Any planet with a stable, moderate axis tilt can support life.
answerChoices.D: Gravitational influences other than moons have little or no effect on the magnitude of the tilt angle of either Earth’s or Mars’s axis.
answerChoices.E: No planet that has more than one moon can support life.

questions.stimulus: The town of Springhill frequently must declare a water emergency, making it temporarily unlawful to use water for such nonessential purposes as car washing. These emergencies could be avoided if Springhill would introduce permanent economic incentives for water conservation. Actually, Springhill discourages conservation because each household pays a modest monthly flat fee for any amount of water below a certain usage threshold, and a substantial per-liter rate only after the threshold is reached.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: The Springhill authorities do a poor job of enforcing its water emergency laws and many people break the laws without incurring a penalty.
answerChoices.B: The town council of Springhill recently refused to raise the threshold.
answerChoices.C: The threshold is kept at a high enough level to exceed the water requirements of most households in Springhill.
answerChoices.D: The threshold is not as high in Springhill as it is in neighboring towns.
answerChoices.E: The threshold remains at the predetermined level specified by law until a change is approved by the Springhill town council.

questions.stimulus: Poppy petals function to attract pollinating insects. The pollination of a poppy flower triggers the release into that flower of a substance that causes its petals to wilt within one or two days. If the flower is not pollinated, the substance will not be released and the petals will remain fresh for a week or longer, as long as the plant can nourish them. Cutting an unpollinated poppy flower from the plant triggers the release into the flower of the same substance whose release is triggered by pollination.
questions.questionStem: The statements above, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Pollinating insects are not attracted to wilted poppy flowers.
answerChoices.B: Even if cut poppies are given all necessary nutrients, their petals will tend to wilt within a few days.
answerChoices.C: Flowers of all plants release the substance that causes wilting when they are cut, although the amount released may vary.
answerChoices.D: The pollen on pollinated poppy flowers prevents their petals from absorbing the nutrients carried to them by their stems.
answerChoices.E: Poppy plants are unable to draw nutrients from soil or water after the substance that causes wilting has been released.

questions.stimulus:
When a community opens a large shopping mall, it often expects a boost to the local economy, and in fact a large amount of economic activity goes on in these malls. Yet the increase in the local economy is typically much smaller than the total amount of economic activity that
goes on in the mall.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the discrepancy described above?

answerChoices.A: When large shopping malls are new they attract a lot of shoppers but once the novelty has worn off they usually attract fewer shoppers than does the traditional downtown shopping district.
answerChoices.B: Most of the money spent in a large shopping mall is spent by tourists who are drawn specifically by the mall and who would not have visited the community had that mall not been built.
answerChoices.C: Most of the jobs created by large shopping malls are filled by people who recently moved to the community and who would not have moved had there been no job offer in the community.
answerChoices.D: Most of the money spent in a large shopping mall is money that would have been spent elsewhere in the same community had that mall not been built.
answerChoices.E: Most of the jobs created by the construction of a large shopping mall are temporary, and most of the permanent jobs created are low paying.

questions.stimulus: Essayist: The way science is conducted and regulated can be changed. But we need to determine whether the changes are warranted, taking into account their price. The use of animals in research could end immediately, but only at the cost of abandoning many kinds of research and making others very expensive. The use of recombinant DNA could be drastically curtailed. Many other restrictions could be imposed, complete with a system of fraud police. But such massive interventions would be costly and would change the character of science.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the essayist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: We should not make changes that will alter the character of science.
answerChoices.B: If we regulate science more closely, we will change the character of science.
answerChoices.C: The regulation of science and the conducting of science can be changed.
answerChoices.D: The imposition of restrictions on the conduct of science would be very costly.
answerChoices.E: We need to be aware of the impact of change in science before changes are made.

questions.stimulus: The postmodern view involves the rejection of modern assumptions about order and the universality of truth. The grand theories of the modern era are now seen as limited by the social and historical contexts in which they were elaborated. Also, the belief in order has given way to a belief in the importance of irregularity and chaos. It follows that we inhabit a world full of irregular events, and in which there are no universal truths.
questions.questionStem: The argument’s reasoning is questionable because the argument

answerChoices.A: infers that something is the case because it is believed to be the case
answerChoices.B: uses the term “universal” ambiguously
answerChoices.C: relies on the use of emotional terms to bolster its conclusion
answerChoices.D: uses the term “order” ambiguously
answerChoices.E: fails to cite examples of modern theories that purport to embody universal truths

questions.stimulus: If the economy is weak, then prices remain constant although unemployment rises. But unemployment rises only if investment decreases. Fortunately, investment is not decreasing.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, then which one of the following must be false?

answerChoices.A: Either the economy is weak or investment is decreasing.
answerChoices.B: If unemployment rises, then prices remain constant.
answerChoices.C: The economy is weak only if investment decreases.
answerChoices.D: Either the economy is weak or prices are remaining constant.
answerChoices.E: Either unemployment is rising or the economy is not weak.

questions.stimulus: Psychologist: Some astrologers claim that our horoscopes completely determine our personalities, but this claim is false. I concede that identical twins— who are, of course, born at practically the same time—often do have similar personalities. However, birth records were examined to find two individuals who were born 40 years ago on the same day and at exactly the same time—one in a hospital in Toronto and one in a hospital in New York. Personality tests revealed that the personalities of these two individuals are in fact different.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the psychologist’s argument depends?

answerChoices.A: Astrologers have not subjected their claims to rigorous experimentation.
answerChoices.B: The personality differences between the two individuals cannot be explained by the cultural differences between Toronto and New York.
answerChoices.C: The geographical difference between Toronto and New York did not result in the two individuals having different horoscopes.
answerChoices.D: Complete birth records for the past 40 years were kept at both hospitals.
answerChoices.E: Identical twins have identical genetic structures and usually have similar home environments.

questions.stimulus: Under the influence of today’s computer-oriented culture, publishing for children has taken on a flashy new look that emphasizes illustrations and graphic design; the resulting lack of substance leads to books that are shortlived items covering mainly trendy subjects. The changes also include more humorous content, simplification of difficult material, and a narrower focus on specific topics.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: The inclusion of humorous material and a narrower focus detract from the substance of a children’s book.
answerChoices.B: The substance of a children’s book is important to its longevity.
answerChoices.C: Children of the computer generation cannot concentrate on long, unbroken sections of prose.
answerChoices.D: Children judge books primarily on the basis of graphic design.
answerChoices.E: The lack of substance of a children’s book is unlikely to be important to its popularity.

questions.stimulus: Further evidence of a connection between brain physiology and psychological states has recently been uncovered in the form of a correlation between electroencephalograph patterns and characteristic moods. A study showed that participants who suffered from clinical depression exhibited less left frontal lobe activity than right, while, conversely, characteristically goodnatured participants exhibited greater left lobe activity. Thus one’s general disposition is a result of the activity of one’s frontal lobe.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, weakens the argument except:

answerChoices.A: Many drugs prescribed to combat clinical depression act by causing increased left lobe activity.
answerChoices.B: Excessive sleep, a typical consequence of clinical depression, is known to suppress left lobe activity.
answerChoices.C: Frontal lobe activity is not subject to variation the way general disposition is.
answerChoices.D: Earlier studies indicated that frontal lobe activity and emotive states are both caused by activity in the brain’s limbic system.
answerChoices.E: Social interaction of the kind not engaged in by most clinically depressed people is known to stimulate left lobe activity.

questions.stimulus: We ought to pay attention only to the intrinsic properties of a work of art. Its other, extrinsic properties are irrelevant to our aesthetic interactions with it. For example, when we look at a painting we should consider only what is directly presented in our experience of it. What is really aesthetically relevant, therefore, is not what a painting symbolizes, but what it directly presents to experience.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is added to the premises?

answerChoices.A: What an artwork symbolizes involves only extrinsic properties of that work.
answerChoices.B: There are certain properties of our experiences of artworks that can be distinguished as symbolic properties.
answerChoices.C: Only an artwork’s intrinsic properties are relevant to our aesthetic interactions with it.
answerChoices.D: It is possible in theory for an artwork to symbolize nothing.
answerChoices.E: An intrinsic property of an artwork is one that relates the work to itself.

questions.stimulus:
McKinley: A double-blind study, in which neither the patient nor the primary researcher knows whether the patient is being given the drug being tested or a placebo, is the most effective procedure for testing the efficacy of a drug. But we will not be able to perform such a study on this new drug, since the drug will have various effects on the patients’ bodies, which will make us aware of whether the patients are getting the drug or a placebo. Engle: You cannot draw that conclusion at this point, for
you are assuming you know what the outcome of the study will be.
questions.questionStem: Engle’s statement indicates that he is most likely interpreting McKinley’s remarks to be

answerChoices.A: presuming that a double-blind study is the only effective way to test new drugs
answerChoices.B: denying that the drug will be effective
answerChoices.C: presuming that the placebo will produce no effects whatever on the patients’ bodies
answerChoices.D: referring to the drug’s therapeutic effects rather than to any known side effects
answerChoices.E: based on a confusion about when a drug is efficacious

questions.stimulus: Modern navigation systems, which are found in most of today’s commercial aircraft, are made with low-power circuitry, which is more susceptible to interference than the vacuum-tube circuitry found in older planes. During landing, navigation systems receive radio signals from the airport to guide the plane to the runway. Recently, one plane with low-power circuitry veered off course during landing, its dials dimming, when a passenger turned on a laptop computer. Clearly, modern aircraft navigation systems are being put at risk by the electronic devices that passengers carry on board, such as cassette players and laptop computers.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, least strengthens the argument above?

answerChoices.A: After the laptop computer was turned off, the plane regained course and its navigation instruments and dials returned to normal.
answerChoices.B: When in use all electronic devices emit electromagnetic radiation, which is known to interfere with circuitry.
answerChoices.C: No problems with navigational equipment or instrument dials have been reported on flights with no passenger-owned electronic devices on board.
answerChoices.D: Significant electromagnetic radiation from portable electronic devices can travel up to eight meters, and some passenger seats on modern aircraft are located within four meters of the navigation systems.
answerChoices.E: Planes were first equipped with low-power circuitry at about the same time portable electronic devices became popular.

questions.stimulus: Critic: People today place an especially high value on respect for others; yet, in their comedy acts, many of today’s most popular comedians display blatant disrespect for others. But when people fail to live up to the very ideals they hold in highest esteem, exaggeration of such failings often forms the basis of successful comedy. Thus the current popularity of comedians who display disrespect in their acts is hardly surprising.
questions.questionStem: The critic’s argument depends on which one of the following assumptions?

answerChoices.A: People who enjoy comedians who display disrespect in their acts do not place a high value on respect for others.
answerChoices.B: Only comedians who display blatant disrespect in their acts are currently successful.
answerChoices.C: Many people disapprove of the portrayal of blatant disrespect for others in comedy acts.
answerChoices.D: People who value an ideal especially highly do not always succeed in living up to this ideal.
answerChoices.E: People today fail to live up to their own ideals more frequently than was the case in the past.

questions.stimulus: The law firm of Sutherlin, Pérez, and Associates is one of the most successful law firms whose primary specialization is in criminal defense cases. In fact, the firm has a better than 90 percent acquittal rate in such cases. Dalton is an attorney whose primary specialization is in divorce cases, so Dalton certainly cannot be a member of Sutherlin, Pérez, and Associates.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: offers in support of its conclusion pieces of evidence that are mutually contradictory
answerChoices.B: overlooks the possibility that a person can practice law without being a member of a law firm
answerChoices.C: concludes that someone is not a member of a group on the grounds that that person does not have a characteristic that the group as a whole has
answerChoices.D: takes a high rate of success among the members of a group to indicate that the successes are evenly spread among the members
answerChoices.E: states a generalization based on a selection that is not representative of the group about which the generalization is supposed to hold true

questions.stimulus: Opponents of allowing triple-trailer trucks to use the national highway system are wrong in claiming that these trucks are more dangerous than other commercial vehicles. In the western part of the country, in areas where triple-trailers are now permitted on some highways, for these vehicles the rate of road accident fatalities per mile of travel is lower than the national rate for other types of commercial vehicles. Clearly, triple-trailers are safer than other commercial vehicles.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most substantially weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: It takes two smaller semitrailers to haul as much weight as a single triple-trailer can.
answerChoices.B: Highways in the sparsely populated West are much less heavily traveled and consequently are far safer than highways in the national system as a whole.
answerChoices.C: Opponents of the triple-trailers also once opposed the shorter twin-trailers, which are now common on the nation’s highways.
answerChoices.D: In areas where the triple-trailers are permitted, drivers need a special license to operate them.
answerChoices.E: For triple-trailers the rate of road accident fatalities per mile of travel was higher last year than in the two previous years.

questions.stimulus: Whittaker: There can be no such thing as the number of medical school students who drop out before their second year, because if they drop out, they never have a second year. Hudson: By your reasoning I cannot help but become rich, because there is similarly no such thing as my dying before my first million dollars is in the bank.
questions.questionStem: Hudson responds to Whittaker by

answerChoices.A: showing that a relevantly analogous argument leads to an untenable conclusion
answerChoices.B: citing a specific example to counter Whittaker’s general claim
answerChoices.C: pointing out that Whittaker mistakes a necessary situation for a possible situation
answerChoices.D: claiming that what Whittaker says cannot be true because Whittaker acts as if it were false
answerChoices.E: showing that Whittaker’s argument relies on analyzing an extreme and unrepresentative case

questions.stimulus: A newly developed light bulb is much more cost-effective than conventional light bulbs: it costs only about 3 times what a conventional light bulb costs but it lasts up to 10 times as long as a conventional light bulb. Despite the manufacturer’s intense efforts to publicize the advantages of the new bulb, one analyst predicts that these new bulbs will prove to sell very poorly.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, provides support for the analyst’s prediction EXCEPT:

answerChoices.A: The light generated by the new bulb is in the yellow range of the spectrum, a type of artificial light most people find unappealing.
answerChoices.B: Most people who purchase light bulbs prefer to buy inexpensive light bulbs rather than more durable but expensive light bulbs.
answerChoices.C: A manufacturer of one brand of conventional light bulb has advertised claims that the new light bulb uses more electricity than do conventional light bulbs.
answerChoices.D: The new bulb is to be marketed in several different quantities, ranging from packages containing one bulb to packages containing four bulbs.
answerChoices.E: A competing manufacturer is about to introduce a light bulb that lasts 10 times as long as a conventional bulb but costs less than a conventional bulb.

questions.stimulus: The Rienzi, a passenger ship, sank as a result of a hole in its hull, possibly caused by sabotage. Normally, when a holed ship sinks as rapidly as the Rienzi did, water does not enter the ship quickly enough for the ship to be fully flooded when it reaches the ocean floor. Full flooding can be achieved, however, by sabotage. Any ship that sinks deep into the ocean when not fully flooded will implode. Deep-sea photographs, taken of the sunken Rienzi where it rests on the ocean floor, reveal that the Rienzi did not implode.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the information above?

answerChoices.A: The Rienzi was so constructed as to reduce the risk of sinking by impact.
answerChoices.B: If the Rienzi became fully flooded, it did so only after it reached the ocean floor.
answerChoices.C: If the Rienzi was not sunk by sabotage, water flooded into it unusually fast.
answerChoices.D: If the Rienzi had sunk more slowly, it would have imploded.
answerChoices.E: The Rienzi was so strongly constructed as to resist imploding under deep-sea pressure.

questions.stimulus: For every 50 dogs that contract a certain disease, one will die from it. A vaccine exists that is virtually 100 percent effective in preventing this disease. Since the risk of death from complications of vaccination is one death per 5,000 vaccinations, it is therefore safer for a dog to receive the vaccine than not to receive it.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following would it be most helpful to know in order to evaluate the argument?

answerChoices.A: the total number of dogs that die each year from all causes taken together
answerChoices.B: whether the vaccine is effective against the disease in household pets other than dogs
answerChoices.C: the number of dogs that die each year from diseases other than the disease in question
answerChoices.D: the likelihood that a dog will contract another disease such as rabies
answerChoices.E: the likelihood that an unvaccinated dog will contract the disease in question

questions.stimulus: The symptoms of mental disorders are behavioral, cognitive, or emotional problems. Some patients with mental disorders can be effectively treated with psychotherapy. But it is now known that in some patients mental disorders result from chemical imbalances affecting the brain. Thus these patients can be effectively treated only with medication that will reduce or correct the imbalance.
questions.questionStem: The argument depends on assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Treatment by psychotherapy can produce no effective reduction in or correction of chemical imbalances that cause mental disorders.
answerChoices.B: Treatment with medication always shows faster results for patients with mental disorders than does treatment with psychotherapy.
answerChoices.C: Most mental disorders are not the result of chemical imbalances affecting the brain.
answerChoices.D: Medication is always more effective in treating patients with mental disorders than is psychotherapy.
answerChoices.E: Treatment with psychotherapy has no effect on mental disorders other than a reduction of the symptoms.

questions.stimulus:
Curator: The decision to restore the cloak of the central figure in Veronese’s painting from its present red to the green found underneath is fully justified. Reliable x-ray and chemical tests show that the red pigment was applied after the painting had been completed, and that the red paint was not mixed in Veronese’s workshop. Hence it appears likely that an artist other than Veronese tampered with Veronese’s painting after its completion.

Art critic: But in a copy of Veronese’s painting made shortly after Veronese died, the cloak is red. It is highly unlikely that a copyist would have made so major a change so soon after Veronese’s death.
questions.questionStem: The assertion that a later artist tampered with Veronese’s painting serves which one of the following functions in the curator’s argument?

answerChoices.A: It is the main point toward which the argument as a whole is directed.
answerChoices.B: It is a subsidiary conclusion that supports the argument’s main conclusion.
answerChoices.C: It is a clarification of a key term of the argument.
answerChoices.D: It is a particular instance of the general position to be defended.
answerChoices.E: It is a reiteration of the main point that is made for the sake of emphasis.

questions.stimulus:
Curator: The decision to restore the cloak of the central figure in Veronese’s painting from its present red to the green found underneath is fully justified. Reliable x-ray and chemical tests show that the red pigment was applied after the painting had been completed, and that the red paint was not mixed in Veronese’s workshop. Hence it appears likely that an artist other than Veronese tampered with Veronese’s painting after its completion.

Art critic: But in a copy of Veronese’s painting made shortly after Veronese died, the cloak is red. It is highly unlikely that a copyist would have made so major a change so soon after Veronese’s death.
questions.questionStem: The art critic’s response to the curator would provide the strongest support for which one of the following conclusions?

answerChoices.A: The copy of Veronese’s painting that was made soon after the painter’s death is indistinguishable from the original.
answerChoices.B: No painting should be restored before the painting is tested with technologically sophisticated equipment.
answerChoices.C: The proposed restoration will fail to restore Veronese’s painting to the appearance it had at the end of the artist’s lifetime.
answerChoices.D: The value of an artist’s work is not necessarily compromised when that work is tampered with by later artists.
answerChoices.E: Veronese did not originally intend the central figure’s cloak to be green.

questions.stimulus: John works five days each week except when on vacation or during weeks in which national holidays occur. Four days a week he works in an insurance company; on Fridays he works as a blacksmith. Last week there were no holidays, and John was not on vacation. Therefore, he must have worked in the insurance company on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday last week.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: John never takes a vacation of more than one week in length.
answerChoices.B: Every day last week that John worked, he worked for an entire workday.
answerChoices.C: John does not take vacations in weeks in which national holidays occur.
answerChoices.D: Last week John worked neither on Saturday nor on Sunday.
answerChoices.E: There were no days last week on which John both worked in the insurance company and also worked as a blacksmith.

questions.stimulus: After several attempts to distract his young parrot from chewing on furniture, George reluctantly took an expert’s advice and gently hit the parrot’s beak whenever the bird started to chew furniture. The bird stopped chewing furniture, but it is now afraid of hands and will sometimes bite. Since chewing on the furniture would not have hurt the bird, George should not have hit it. When Carla’s puppy escaped from her yard, it bounded into a busy street. Although Carla does not generally approve of physical discipline, she hit the puppy sharply with her hand. Now the puppy enters the street only when accompanied by Carla, so Carla was justified in disciplining the puppy.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if established, would justify the judgments about George’s and Carla’s actions?

answerChoices.A: When disciplining an animal physically, a trainer should use an object such as a rolled up newspaper to avoid making the animal frightened of hands.
answerChoices.B: When training an animal, physical discipline should be used only when such discipline is necessary to correct behavior that could result in serious harm to the animal.
answerChoices.C: Using physical discipline to train an animal is justified only when all alternative strategies for correcting undesirable behavior have failed.
answerChoices.D: Physical discipline should not be used on immature animals.
answerChoices.E: Physical discipline should not be used by an animal trainer except to correct persistent behavior problems.

questions.stimulus: Mature white pines intercept almost all the sunlight that shines on them. They leave a deep litter that dries readily, and they grow to prodigious height so that, even when there are large gaps in a stand of such trees, little light reaches the forest floor. For this reason white pines cannot regenerate in their own shade. Thus, when in a dense forest a stand of trees consists of nothing but mature white pines, it is a fair bet that _______.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most logically concludes the argument?

answerChoices.A: the ages of the trees in the stand do not differ from each other by much more than the length of time it takes a white pine to grow to maturity
answerChoices.B: the land on which the stand is now growing had been cleared of all trees at the time when the first of the white pines started growing
answerChoices.C: competition among the trees in the stand for sunlight will soon result in some trees’ dying and the stand thus becoming thinner
answerChoices.D: other species of trees will soon begin to colonize the stand, eventually replacing all of the white pines
answerChoices.E: any differences in the heights of the trees in the stand are attributable solely to differences in the ages of the trees

questions.stimulus: Advertisement: A leading economist has determined that among people who used computers at their place of employment last year, those who also owned portable (“laptop”) computers earned 25 percent more on average than those who did not. It is obvious from this that owning a laptop computer led to a higher-paying job.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following identifies a reasoning error in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It attempts to support a sweeping generalization on the basis of information about only a small number of individuals.
answerChoices.B: Its conclusion merely restates a claim made earlier in the argument.
answerChoices.C: It concludes that one thing was caused by another although the evidence given is consistent with the first thing’s having caused the second.
answerChoices.D: It offers information as support for a conclusion when that information actually shows that the conclusion is false.
answerChoices.E: It uncritically projects currently existing trends indefinitely into the future.

questions.stimulus: Rhonda will see the movie tomorrow afternoon only if Paul goes to the concert in the afternoon. Paul will not go to the concert unless Ted agrees to go to the concert. However, Ted refuses to go to the concert. So Rhonda will not see the movie tomorrow afternoon.
questions.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning displayed above is most closely paralleled in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: If Janice comes to visit, Mary will not pay the bills tomorrow. Janice will not come to visit unless she locates a babysitter. However, Janice has located a babysitter, so she will visit Mary.
answerChoices.B: Gary will do his laundry tomorrow only if Peter has to go to work. Unless Cathy is ill, Peter will not have to go to work. Since Cathy is not ill, Gary will not do his laundry tomorrow.
answerChoices.C: Kelly will barbecue fish tonight if it does not rain and the market has fresh trout. Although the forecast does not call for rain, the market does not have fresh trout. So Kelly will not barbecue fish tonight.
answerChoices.D: Lisa will attend the family reunion next week only if one of her brothers, Jared or Karl, also attends. Karl will not attend the reunion, but Jared will. So Lisa will attend the reunion.
answerChoices.E: George will not go to the museum tomorrow unless Mark agrees to go. Mark will go to the museum only if he can postpone most of his appointments. Mark has postponed some of his appointments, so he will go to the museum.

questions.stimulus: Private industry is trying to attract skilled research scientists by offering them high salaries. As a result, most research scientists employed in private industry now earn 50 percent more than do comparably skilled research scientists employed by the government. So, unless government-employed research scientists are motivated more by a sense of public duty than by their own interests, the government is likely to lose its most skilled research scientists to private industry, since none of these scientists would have problems finding private-sector jobs.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: Government research scientists are less likely to receive acknowledgment for their research contributions than are research scientists in the private sector.
answerChoices.B: None of the research scientists currently employed by the government earns more than the highest-paid researchers employed in the private sector.
answerChoices.C: The government does not employ as many research scientists who are highly skilled as does any large company in the private sector which employs research scientists.
answerChoices.D: The government does not provide its research scientists with unusually good working conditions or fringe benefits that more than compensate for the lower salaries they receive.
answerChoices.E: Research scientists employed in the private sector generally work longer hours than do researchers employed by the government.

questions.stimulus: Using fossil energy more efficiently is in the interest of the nation and the global environment, but major improvements are unlikely unless proposed government standards are implemented to eliminate products or practices that are among the least efficient in their class. Objection: Decisions on energy use are best left to the operation of the market.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most directly undermines the objection above?

answerChoices.A: It would be unrealistic to expect society to make the changes necessary to achieve maximum energy efficiency all at once.
answerChoices.B: There are products, such as automobiles, that consume energy at a sufficient rate that persons who purchase and use them will become conscious of any unusual energy inefficiency in comparison with other products in the same class.
answerChoices.C: Whenever a new mode of generating energy, such as a new fuel, is introduced, a number of support systems, such as a fuel-distribution system, must be created or adapted.
answerChoices.D: When energy prices rise, consumers of energy tend to look for new ways to increase energy efficiency, such as by adding insulation to their houses.
answerChoices.E: Often the purchaser of a product, such as a landlord buying an appliance, chooses on the basis of purchase price because the purchaser is not the person who will pay for energy used by the product.

questions.stimulus: Dobson: Some historians claim that the people who built a ring of stones thousands of years ago in Britain were knowledgeable about celestial events. The ground for this claim is that two of the stones determine a line pointing directly to the position of the sun at sunrise at the spring equinox. There are many stones in the ring, however, so the chance that one pair will point in a celestially significant direction is large. Therefore, the people who built the ring were not knowledgeable about celestial events.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an error of reasoning in Dobson’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The failure of cited evidence to establish a statement is taken as evidence that that statement is false.
answerChoices.B: Dobson’s conclusion logically contradicts some of the evidence presented in support of it.
answerChoices.C: Statements that absolutely establish Dobson’s conclusion are treated as if they merely give some support to that conclusion.
answerChoices.D: Something that is merely a matter of opinion is treated as if it were subject to verification as a matter of fact.
answerChoices.E: Dobson’s drawing the conclusion relies on interpreting a key term in two different ways.

questions.stimulus: Nearly all mail that is correctly addressed arrives at its destination within two business days of being sent. In fact, correctly addressed mail takes longer than this only when it is damaged in transit. Overall, however, most mail arrives three business days or more after being sent.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must be true?

answerChoices.A: A large proportion of the mail that is correctly addressed is damaged in transit.
answerChoices.B: No incorrectly addressed mail arrives within two business days of being sent.
answerChoices.C: Most mail that arrives within two business days of being sent is correctly addressed.
answerChoices.D: A large proportion of mail is incorrectly addressed.
answerChoices.E: More mail arrives within two business days of being sent than arrives between two and three business days after being sent.

questions.stimulus: The report released by the interior ministry states that within the past 5 years the national land-reclamation program has resulted in a 19 percent increase in the amount of arable land within the country. If these figures are accurate, the program has been a resounding success. Senator Armand, a distinguished mathematician and a woman of indisputable brilliance, maintains, however, that the reclamation program could not possibly have been successful. Clearly, therefore, the figures cited in the report cannot be accurate.
questions.questionStem: The argument above exhibits an erroneous pattern of reasoning most similar to that exhibited by which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Albert’s father claims that Albert does not know where the spare car keys are hidden. Yesterday, however, Albert reported that he had discovered the spare car keys in the garage toolbox, so his father’s claim cannot be true.
answerChoices.B: Gloria’s drama teacher claims that her policy is to give each student the opportunity to act in at least one play during the year but, since Gloria, who attended every class, reports that she was not given such an opportunity, the teacher’s claim cannot be true.
answerChoices.C: Amos claims that he can hold his breath under water for a full hour. Dr. Treviso, a cardiopulmonary specialist, has stated that humans are physiologically incapable of holding their breath for even half that long; so Amos’ claim cannot be true.
answerChoices.D: Evelyn reports that she got home before midnight. Robert, who always knows the time, insists that she did not. If Robert is right, Evelyn could not possibly have listened to the late news; since she admits not having listened to the late news, her report cannot be true.
answerChoices.E: Moira, after observing the finish of the 60-kilometer bicycle race, reports that Lee won with Adams a distant third. Lomas, a bicycle engineering expert, insists, however, that Lee could not have won a race in which Adams competed; so Moira’s report cannot be true.

questions.stimulus:
Wirth: All efforts to identify a gene responsible for predisposing people to manic-depression have failed. In fact, nearly all researchers now agree that there is no “manic-depression gene.” Therefore, if these researchers are right, any claim that some people are genetically predisposed to manic-depression is simply false.

Chang: I do not dispute your evidence, but I take issue with your conclusion. Many of the researchers you refer to have found evidence that a set of several genes is involved and that complex interactions among these genes produce a predisposition to manic-depression.
questions.questionStem: The point at issue between Wirth and Chang is whether

answerChoices.A: efforts to identify a gene or set of several genes responsible for predisposing people to manic-depression have all failed
answerChoices.B: it is likely that researchers will ever be able to find a single gene that predisposes people to manic-depression
answerChoices.C: nearly all researchers now agree that there is no manic-depression gene
answerChoices.D: current research supports the claim that no one is genetically predisposed to manic-depression
answerChoices.E: the efforts made to find a gene that can produce a predisposition to manic-depression were thorough

questions.stimulus:
Wirth: All efforts to identify a gene responsible for predisposing people to manic-depression have failed. In fact, nearly all researchers now agree that there is no “manic-depression gene.” Therefore, if these researchers are right, any claim that some people are genetically predisposed to manic-depression is simply false.

Chang: I do not dispute your evidence, but I take issue with your conclusion. Many of the researchers you refer to have found evidence that a set of several genes is involved and that complex interactions among these genes produce a predisposition to manic-depression.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses Chang’s criticism of Wirth’s argument?

answerChoices.A: It presupposes only one possibility where more than one exists.
answerChoices.B: It depends on separate pieces of evidence that contradict each other.
answerChoices.C: It relies on the opinion of experts in an area outside the experts’ field of expertise.
answerChoices.D: It disallows in principle any evidence that would disconfirm its conclusion.
answerChoices.E: It treats something that is merely unlikely as though it were impossible.

questions.stimulus: Garbage dumps do not harm wildlife. Evidence is furnished by the Masai-Mara reserve in Kenya, where baboons that use the garbage dumps on the reserve as a food source mature faster and have more offspring than do baboons on the reserve that do not scavenge on garbage.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following statements, if true, casts doubt on the argument EXCEPT:

answerChoices.A: The baboons that feed on the garbage dump are of a different species from those that do not.
answerChoices.B: The life expectancy of baboons that eat garbage is significantly lower than that of baboons that do not eat garbage.
answerChoices.C: The cholesterol level of garbage-eating baboons is dangerously higher than that of baboons that do not eat garbage.
answerChoices.D: The population of hyenas that live near unregulated garbage landfills north of the reserve has doubled in the last two years.
answerChoices.E: The rate of birth defects for the baboon population on the reserve has doubled since the first landfills were opened.

questions.stimulus: Marianne is a professional chess player who hums audibly while playing her matches, thereby distracting her opponents. When ordered by chess officials to cease humming or else be disqualified from professional chess, Marianne protested the order. She argued that since she was unaware of her humming, her humming was involuntary and that therefore she should not be held responsible for it.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to support Marianne’s argument against the order?

answerChoices.A: Chess players who hum audibly while playing their matches should not protest if their opponents also hum.
answerChoices.B: Of a player’s actions, only those that are voluntary should be used as justification for disqualifying that player from professional chess.
answerChoices.C: A person should be held responsible for those involuntary actions that serve that person’s interests.
answerChoices.D: Types of behavior that are not considered voluntary in everyday circumstances should be considered voluntary if they occur in the context of a professional chess match.
answerChoices.E: Chess players should be disqualified from professional chess matches if they regularly attempt to distract their opponents.

questions.stimulus: Marianne is a professional chess player who hums audibly while playing her matches, thereby distracting her opponents. When ordered by chess officials to cease humming or else be disqualified from professional chess, Marianne protested the order. She argued that since she was unaware of her humming, her humming was involuntary and that therefore she should not be held responsible for it.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most undermines Marianne’s argument against the order?

answerChoices.A: The officials of chess have little or no authority to control the behavior of its professional players outside of matches.
answerChoices.B: Many of the customs of amateur chess matches are not observed by professional chess players.

questions.stimulus: Smoking in bed has long been the main cause of home fires. Despite a significant decline in cigarette smoking in the last two decades, however, there has been no comparable decline in the number of people killed in home fires.
questions.questionStem: Each one of the following statements, if true over the last two decades, helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy above EXCEPT:

answerChoices.A: Compared to other types of home fires, home fires caused by smoking in bed usually cause relatively little damage before they are extinguished.
answerChoices.B: Home fires caused by smoking in bed often break out after the home’s occupants have fallen asleep.
answerChoices.C: Smokers who smoke in bed tend to be heavy smokers who are less likely to quit smoking than are smokers who do not smoke in bed.
answerChoices.D: An increasing number of people have been killed in home fires that started in the kitchen.
answerChoices.E: Population densities have increased, with the result that one home fire can cause more deaths than in previous decades.

questions.stimulus: Flavonoids are a common component of almost all plants, but a specific variety of flavonoid in apples has been found to be an antioxidant. Antioxidants are known to be a factor in the prevention of heart disease.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

answerChoices.A: A diet composed largely of fruits and vegetables will help to prevent heart disease.
answerChoices.B: Flavonoids are essential to preventing heart disease.
answerChoices.C: Eating at least one apple each day will prevent heart disease.
answerChoices.D: At least one type of flavonoid helps to prevent heart disease.
answerChoices.E: A diet deficient in antioxidants is a common cause of heart disease.

questions.stimulus: A number of Grandville’s wealthiest citizens have been criminals. So, since it is of utmost importance that the Grandville Planning Committee be composed solely of individuals whose personal standards of ethics are beyond reproach, no wealthy person should be appointed to that committee.
questions.questionStem: The argument is most vulnerable to the criticism that it

answerChoices.A: confuses a result with something that is sufficient for bringing about that result
answerChoices.B: mistakes a temporal relationship for a causal relationship
answerChoices.C: assumes that because a certain action has a certain result the person taking that action intended that result
answerChoices.D: judges only by subjective standards something that can be readily evaluated according to objective standards
answerChoices.E: generalizes on the basis of what could be exceptional cases

questions.stimulus: Birds startled by potential predators generally try to take cover in nearby vegetation. Yet many birds that feed at bird feeders placed in suburban gardens are killed when, thus startled, they fly away from the vegetation in the gardens and into the windowpanes of nearby houses.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the anomalous behavior of the birds that fly into windowpanes?

answerChoices.A: Predator attacks are as likely to occur at bird feeders surrounded by dense vegetation as they are at feeders surrounded by little or no vegetation.
answerChoices.B: The bird feeders in some suburban gardens are placed at a considerable distance from the houses.
answerChoices.C: Large birds are as likely as small birds to fly into windowpanes.
answerChoices.D: Most of the birds startled while feeding at bird feeders placed in suburban gardens are startled by loud noises rather than by predators.
answerChoices.E: The windowpanes of many houses clearly reflect surrounding vegetation.

questions.stimulus: Raising the humidity of a room protects furniture, draperies, and computers from damage caused by excessively dry air. Further, it can make people feel warmer, helps the body’s defenses against viruses, and alleviates some skin rashes.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following is supported by the information above except:

answerChoices.A: Humidity can be bad for computers.
answerChoices.B: A room can be too dry for the optimal maintenance of its furnishings.
answerChoices.C: Dry air can feel cooler than humid air of the same temperature.
answerChoices.D: Increased humidity can be beneficial to the skin.
answerChoices.E: The human immune system can benefit from humidity.

questions.stimulus:
The following passage is used for Section 3, questions 5 through 6.
Jane: Television programs and movies that depict violence among teenagers are extremely popular. Given how influential these media are, we have good reason to believe that these depictions cause young people to engage in violent behavior. Hence, depictions of violence among teenagers should be prohibited from movies and television programs, if only in those programs and movies promoted to young audiences.
Maurice: But you are recommending nothing short of
censorship! Besides which, your claim that television and movie depictions of violence cause violence is mistaken: violence among young people predates movies and television by centuries.
questions.questionStem: Maurice’s attempted refutation of Jane’s argument is vulnerable to criticism on which one of the following grounds?

answerChoices.A: It presupposes that an unpopular policy cannot possibly achieve its intended purpose.
answerChoices.B: It confuses a subjective judgment of private moral permissibility with an objective description of social fact.
answerChoices.C: It rules out something as a cause of a current phenomenon solely on the ground that the phenomenon used to occur without that thing.
answerChoices.D: It cites purported historical facts that cannot possibly be verified.
answerChoices.E: It relies on an ambiguity in the term “violence” to justify a claim.

questions.stimulus:
The following passage is used for Section 3, questions 5 through 6.
Jane: Television programs and movies that depict violence among teenagers are extremely popular. Given how influential these media are, we have good reason to believe that these depictions cause young people to engage in violent behavior. Hence, depictions of violence among teenagers should be prohibited from movies and television programs, if only in those programs and movies promoted to young audiences.
Maurice: But you are recommending nothing short of censorship! Besides which, your claim that television and movie depictions of violence cause violence is mistaken: violence among young people predates movies and television by centuries.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens Jane’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The most violent characters depicted in movies and on television programs are adult characters who are portrayed by adult actors.

questions.stimulus:
Sam: In a recent survey, over 95 percent of people who purchased a Starlight automobile last year said they were highly satisfied with their purchase. Since people who have purchased a new car in the last year are not highly satisfied if that car has a manufacturing defect, Starlight automobiles are remarkably free from such defects.
Tiya: But some manufacturing defects in automobiles
become apparent only after several years of use.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes how Tiya’s response is related to Sam’s argument?

answerChoices.A: It argues that Sam’s conclusion is correct, though not for the reasons Sam gives.
answerChoices.B: It provides evidence indicating that the survey results Sam relies on in his argument do not accurately characterize the attitudes of those surveyed.

questions.stimulus: Some environmentalists question the prudence of exploiting features of the environment, arguing that there are no economic benefits to be gained from forests, mountains, or wetlands that no longer exist. Many environmentalists claim that because nature has intrinsic value it would be wrong to destroy such features of the environment, even if the economic costs of doing so were outweighed by the economic costs of not doing so.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following can be logically inferred from the passage?

answerChoices.A: It is economically imprudent to exploit features of the environment.
answerChoices.B: Some environmentalists appeal to a noneconomic justification in questioning the defensibility of exploiting features of the environment.
answerChoices.C: Most environmentalists appeal to economic reasons in questioning the defensibility of exploiting features of the environment.
answerChoices.D: Many environmentalists provide only a noneconomic justification in questioning the defensibility of exploiting features of the environment.
answerChoices.E: Even if there is no economic reason for protecting the environment, there is a sound noneconomic justification for doing so.

questions.stimulus: Market research traditionally entails surveying consumers about why they buy and use particular products and brands. Observational research—actually watching consumers shopping and interacting with products— is now increasingly used by market researchers to supplement surveys. Market researchers claim that observational research yields information about consumer behavior that surveys alone cannot provide.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, provides the strongest support for the market researchers’ claim?

answerChoices.A: Even consumers who are unable to explain their preference for or rejection of particular brands reveal which brands they are considering by picking up and putting down products while they are shopping.
answerChoices.B: Market researchers find that consumers are almost always willing to participate in observational research for which the consumer is paid by the hour.
answerChoices.C: Consumers are becoming increasingly selfconscious about their buying habits, and some consumers have stopped buying some items that they normally used to buy.
answerChoices.D: Market researchers say they find data collection more enjoyable in observational research than in survey research, because observational research requires more creative judgment on their part.
answerChoices.E: Consumers are more likely to respond to oral surveys than they are to respond to written questionnaires.

questions.stimulus:
Laura: Harold is obviously lonely. He should sell his cabin in the woods and move into town. In town he will be near other people all the time, so he will not be lonely any more.
Ralph: Many very lonely people live in towns. What is needed to avoid loneliness is not only the proximity of other people but also genuine interaction with them.
questions.questionStem: Ralph responds to Laura by pointing out that

answerChoices.A: something needed for a certain result does not necessarily guarantee that result
answerChoices.B: what is appropriate in one case is not necessarily appropriate in all cases
answerChoices.C: what is logically certain is not always intuitively obvious
answerChoices.D: various alternative solutions are possible for a single problem
answerChoices.E: a proposed solution for a problem could actually worsen that problem

questions.stimulus:

answerChoices.A: A larger number of 18-year-old high school graduates were recruited for the republic’s armed services in 1986 than in 1980.
answerChoices.B: Many of the high-technology systems used by the republic’s armed services can be operated only by individuals who have completed a high school education.

answerChoices.E: The proportion of recruits who had completed at least two years of college education was greater in 1986 than in 1980.

questions.stimulus:
Letter to the Editor: Your article on effective cockroach control states that vexone is effective against only one of the more than 4,000 cockroach species that infest North America: the German cockroach. In actuality, vexone has been utilized effectively for almost a decade against all of the species that infest North America. In testing our product, Roach Ender, which contains vexone, we have conducted many well-documented studies that
prove this fact.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following statements conflicts with the letter writer’s view except:

answerChoices.A: Vexone is effective against only two species of cockroach that infest North America.
answerChoices.B: Not all of the major species of cockroach that infest North America can be controlled by Roach Ender.
