answerChoices.D: attempting to prove a claim on the basis of evidence that a number of people hold that claim to be true
answerChoices.E: treating one of several plausible explanations of a phenomenon as the only possible explanation

questions.stimulus: For newborns of age four to six weeks whose mothers have been the primary caregivers, the following is true: When the newborns are crying due to hunger or other similar discomfort, merely hearing the mother’s voice will lead to a temporary halt in crying, while the voices of others do not have this effect.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most reasonably supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Babies more easily learn to recognize the voices of their mothers than the voices of other people.
answerChoices.B: A mother’s voice is the first thing a baby learns to recognize.
answerChoices.C: Babies associate the voice of the primary caregiver with release from discomfort.
answerChoices.D: Often only a primary caregiver can provide comfort to a newborn.
answerChoices.E: Discomfort in newborns is best relieved by hearing the mother’s voice.

questions.stimulus: Many elementary schools have recently offered computer-assisted educational programs. Students’ reactions after several years have been decidedly mixed. Whereas students have found computers very useful in studying arithmetic, they have found them of little help in studying science, and of no help at all with their reading and writing skills.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the students’ mixed reactions?

answerChoices.A: Students in these schools began reading and doing arithmetic before learning to use computers.
answerChoices.B: Of the disciplines and skills mentioned, the exactness of arithmetic makes it most suitable to computer-assisted education.
answerChoices.C: Many elementary school teachers are reluctant to use computer technology in their classrooms.
answerChoices.D: Young students are more likely to maintain interest in training programs that use the newest computers and video graphics than in those that do not.
answerChoices.E: The elementary schools have offered more computer-assisted programs in reading and writing than in arithmetic and science.

questions.stimulus: The notion that one might be justified in behaving irrationally in the service of a sufficiently worthy end is incoherent. For if such an action is justified, then one would be behaving rationally, not irrationally.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

answerChoices.A: A representative of the law, such as a judge or a police officer, ought not to commit crimes. For if representatives of the law commit crimes, they will be ineffective in preventing crime.
answerChoices.B: One cannot intend to spill a glass of water accidentally. Spilling it accidentally means that the act will not have been done intentionally.
answerChoices.C: One cannot live the good life and be unhappy. If one’s own neighbors see that one is unhappy, then they will see that one is not living the good life.
answerChoices.D: Doctors cannot perform self-diagnosis, for they cannot objectively evaluate their own symptoms, and thus will be practicing poor medicine.
answerChoices.E: One ought not to have both a cat and a goldfish. The goldfish is the natural prey of the cat, so it is unethical to place it at the cat’s disposal.

questions.stimulus: A certain moral system holds that performing good actions is praiseworthy only when one overcomes a powerful temptation in order to perform them. Yet this same moral system also holds that performing good actions out of habit is sometimes praiseworthy.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, does the most to reconcile the apparent conflict in the moral system described above?

answerChoices.A: People who perform good actions out of habit have often acquired this habit after years of having resisted temptation.
answerChoices.B: Most people face strong moral temptation from time to time but few people have to endure it regularly.
answerChoices.C: People virtually always perform actions they think are good, regardless of what other people may think.
answerChoices.D: Since it is difficult to tell what is going on in another person’s mind, it is often hard to know exactly how strongly a person is tempted.
answerChoices.E: It is far more common for people to perform good actions out of habit than for them to do so against strong temptation.

questions.stimulus:
Conservationist: The risk to airplane passengers from collisions between airplanes using the airport and birds from the wildlife refuge is negligible. In the 10 years since the refuge was established,
only 20 planes have been damaged in collisions with birds, and no passenger has been injured as a result of such a collision. The wildlife refuge therefore poses no safety risk.
Pilot: You neglect to mention that 17 of those 20 collisions occurred within the past 2 years, and that the number of birds in the refuge is rapidly increasing. As the number of collisions between birds and airplanes increases, so does the likelihood that at least one such collision will result in passenger injuries.
questions.questionStem: The pilot counters the conservationist by

answerChoices.A: attempting to show that the conservationist’s description of the facts is misleading
answerChoices.B: questioning the conservationist’s motives for reaching a certain conclusion
answerChoices.C: asserting that dangerous situations inevitably become more dangerous with the passage of time
answerChoices.D: discrediting the moral principle on which the conservationist’s argument is based
answerChoices.E: disputing the accuracy of the figures cited by the conservationist

questions.stimulus: A university study reported that between 1975 and 1983 the length of the average workweek in a certain country increased significantly. A governmental study, on the other hand, shows a significant decline in the length of the average workweek for the same period. Examination of the studies shows, however, that they used different methods of investigation; thus there is no need to look further for an explanation of the difference in the studies’ results.
questions.questionStem: The argument’s reasoning is flawed because the argument fails to

answerChoices.A: distinguish between a study produced for the purposes of the operation of government and a study produced as part of university research
answerChoices.B: distinguish between a method of investigation and the purpose of an investigation
answerChoices.C: recognize that only one of the studies has been properly conducted
answerChoices.D: recognize that two different methods of investigation can yield identical results
answerChoices.E: recognize that varying economic conditions result in the average workweek changing in length

questions.stimulus: Although the charter of Westside School states that the student body must include some students with special educational needs, no students with learning disabilities have yet enrolled in the school. Therefore, the school is currently in violation of its charter.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion of the argument follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: All students with learning disabilities have special educational needs.
answerChoices.B: The school currently has no students with learning disabilities.
answerChoices.C: The school should enroll students with special educational needs.
answerChoices.D: The only students with special educational needs are students with learning disabilities.
answerChoices.E: The school’s charter cannot be modified in order to avoid its being violated.

questions.stimulus:
Some psychologists claim that, in theory, the best way
to understand another person would be through deep empathy, whereby one would gain a direct and complete grasp of that person’s motivations. But suppose they are right; then there would be no way at all to achieve understanding, since it is psychologically impossible to gain a direct and complete grasp of another person’s motivations. But obviously one can understand other people; thus these psychologists are wrong.
questions.questionStem: The argument is most vulnerable to the criticism that it

answerChoices.A: fails to adequately define the key phrase “deep empathy”
answerChoices.B: assumes something that it later denies, resulting in a contradiction
answerChoices.C: confuses a theoretically best way of accomplishing something with the only way of accomplishing it
answerChoices.D: accepts a claim on mere authority, without requiring sufficient justification
answerChoices.E: fails to consider that other psychologists may disagree with the psychologists cited

questions.stimulus: The five senses have traditionally been viewed as distinct yet complementary. Each sense is thought to have its own range of stimuli that are incapable of stimulating the other senses. However, recent research has discovered that some people taste a banana and claim that they are tasting blue, or see a color and say that it has a specific smell. This shows that such people, called synesthesiacs, have senses that do not respect the usual boundaries between the five recognized senses.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Synesthesiacs demonstrate a general, systematic impairment in their ability to use and understand words.
answerChoices.B: Recent evidence strongly suggests that there are other senses besides sight, touch, smell, hearing, and taste.
answerChoices.C: The particular ways in which sensory experiences overlap in synesthesiacs follow a definite pattern.
answerChoices.D: The synesthetic phenomenon has been described in the legends of various cultures.
answerChoices.E: Synesthesiacs can be temporarily rid of their synesthetic experiences by the use of drugs.

questions.stimulus: Essayist: One of the claims of laissez-faire economics is that increasing the minimum wage reduces the total number of minimum-wage jobs available. In a recent study, however, it was found that after an increase in the minimum wage, fast-food restaurants kept on roughly the same number of minimum-wage employees as before the increase. Therefore, laissez-faire economics is not entirely accurate.
questions.questionStem: The essayist’s argument depends on assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: If laissez-faire economics makes an incorrect prediction about the minimum wage, then all the doctrines of laissez-faire economics are inaccurate.
answerChoices.B: Minimum-wage job availability at fastfood restaurants included in the study was representative of minimum-wage job availability in general.
answerChoices.C: No study has ever found that a business has decreased the number of its minimum-wage employees after an increase in the minimum wage.
answerChoices.D: The fast-food restaurants included in the study did not increase the average wage paid to employees.
answerChoices.E: The national unemployment rate did not increase following the increase in the minimum wage.

questions.stimulus: Some people claim that every human discovery or invention is an instance of self-expression. But what they seem to ignore is that, trivially, anything we do is selfexpressive. So, until they can give us a more interesting interpretation of their claim, we are not obliged to take their claim seriously.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, provides the most support for the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: All claims that are trivial are uninteresting.
answerChoices.B: Most people do not take trivial claims seriously.
answerChoices.C: No claims that are trivial are worthy of serious consideration.
answerChoices.D: Every claim is open to both interesting and uninteresting interpretations.
answerChoices.E: Every interpretation is either trivial or uninteresting.

questions.stimulus:
The following passage is used for Section 2, questions 15 through 16.
Camera manufacturers typically advertise their products by citing the resolution of their cameras’ lenses, the resolution of a lens being the degree of detail the lens is capable of reproducing in the image it projects onto the film. Differences between cameras in this respect are irrelevant for practical photography, however, since all modern lenses are so excellent that they project far more detail onto the film than any photographic film is capable of reproducing in a developed image.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately states the main point of the argument?

answerChoices.A: Camera manufacturers ought to concentrate on building other desirable qualities into their cameras’ lenses, rather than concentrating only on the lenses’ resolution.
answerChoices.B: Apart from differences in resolution, there is no practical difference among modern cameras in the quality of the images that they produce.
answerChoices.C: Advertised differences among cameras in the resolution of their lenses have no practical bearing on the cameras’ relative quality as photographic tools.
answerChoices.D: In concentrating their advertising on the issue of image quality, manufacturers are making a mistake about the interests of potential purchasers of cameras.
answerChoices.E: Differences among photographic films in the amount of detail they reproduce have a more significant effect on the quality of the developed image than do differences in the resolution of camera lenses.

questions.stimulus:
The following passage is used for Section 2, questions 15 through 16.
Camera manufacturers typically advertise their products by citing the resolution of their cameras’ lenses, the resolution of a lens being the degree of detail the lens is capable of reproducing in the image it projects onto the film. Differences between cameras in this respect are irrelevant for practical photography, however, since all modern lenses are so excellent that they project far more detail onto the film than any photographic film is capable of reproducing in a developed image.
questions.questionStem: The argument depends on assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: The definition of the term “resolution” does not capture an important determinant of the quality of photographic instruments and materials.
answerChoices.B: In determining the amount of detail reproduced in the developed photographic image, differences in the resolutions of available lenses do not compound the deficiencies of available film.
answerChoices.C: Variations in the method used to process the film do not have any significant effect on the film’s resolution.
answerChoices.D: Flawless photographic technique is needed to achieve the maximum image resolution possible with the materials and equipment being used.
answerChoices.E: The only factors important in determining the degree of detail reproduced in the final photographic print are the resolution of the camera’s lens and the resolution of the film.

questions.stimulus: Dietary researcher: A recent study reports that laboratory animals that were fed reduced-calorie diets lived longer than laboratory animals whose caloric intake was not reduced. In response, some doctors are advocating reduced-calorie diets, in the belief that North Americans’ life spans can thereby be extended. However, this conclusion is not supported. Laboratory animals tend to eat much more than animals in their natural habitats, which leads to their having a shorter life expectancy. Restricting their diets merely brings their caloric intake back to natural, optimal levels and reinstates their normal life spans.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most weaken the dietary researcher’s argument?

answerChoices.A: North Americans, on average, consume a higher number of calories than the optimal number of calories for a human diet.
answerChoices.B: North Americans with high-fat, low-calorie diets generally have a shorter life expectancy than North Americans with low-fat, low-calorie diets.
answerChoices.C: Not all scientific results that have important implications for human health are based on studies of laboratory animals.
answerChoices.D: Some North Americans who follow reducedcalorie diets are long-lived.
answerChoices.E: There is a strong correlation between diet and longevity in some species of animals.

questions.stimulus: Editorialist: The positions advanced by radical environmentalists often contain hypotheses that are false and proposals that are economically infeasible. But there is a positive role to be played even by these extremists, for the social and political inertia that attends environmental issues is so stubborn that even small areas of progress can be made only if the populace fears environmental disaster, however untenable the reasons for those fears may be.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the editorialist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The little progress that has been made in improving the environment is mainly due to the fear created by radical environmentalists.
answerChoices.B: Radical environmentalists, by promoting their views, stimulate progress on environmental issues.
answerChoices.C: Social and political inertia is most effectively overcome by an extremely fearful populace, regardless of whether its fears are well-founded.
answerChoices.D: Radical environmentalists often put forth untenable positions in order to produce the fear that is required to bring about moderate reforms.
answerChoices.E: Radical environmentalists advocate positions without regard for factual support or economic feasibility.

questions.stimulus: People should avoid taking the antacid calcium carbonate in doses larger than half a gram, for despite its capacity to neutralize stomach acids, calcium carbonate can increase the calcium level in the blood and thus impair kidney function. Moreover, just half a gram of it can stimulate the production of gastrin, a stomach hormone that triggers acid secretion.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Cessation of gastrin production is a more effective method of controlling excess stomach acid than is direct neutralization of stomach acid.
answerChoices.B: People who avoid taking more than half a gram of calcium carbonate are less likely than average to suffer from impaired kidney function.
answerChoices.C: Doses of calcium carbonate smaller than half a gram can reduce stomach acid more effectively than much larger doses do.
answerChoices.D: Half a gram of calcium carbonate can causally contribute to both the secretion and the neutralization of stomach acids.
answerChoices.E: Impaired kidney function may increase the level of calcium in the blood.

questions.stimulus:
The following passage is used for Section 2, questions 20 through 21.
Professor Chan: The literature department’s
undergraduate courses should cover only true literary works, and not such frivolous material as advertisements.
Professor Wigmore: Advertisements might or might not be true literary works but they do have a powerfully detrimental effect on society— largely because people cannot discern their real messages. The literature department’s courses give students the critical skills to analyze and understand texts. Therefore, it is the literature department’s responsibility to include the study of advertisements in its undergraduate courses.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles most strongly supports Professor Wigmore’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Advertisements ought to be framed in such a way that their real messages are immediately clear.
answerChoices.B: Any text that is subtly constructed and capable of affecting people’s thought and action ought to be considered a form of literature.
answerChoices.C: All undergraduate students ought to take at least one course that focuses on the development of critical skills.
answerChoices.D: The literature department’s courses ought to enable students to analyze and understand any text that could have a harmful effect on society.
answerChoices.E: Any professor teaching an undergraduate course in the literature department ought to be free to choose the material to be covered in that course.

questions.stimulus:
The following passage is used for Section 2, questions 20 through 21.
Professor Chan: The literature department’s undergraduate courses should cover only true literary works, and not such frivolous material as advertisements.
Professor Wigmore: Advertisements might or might not be true literary works but they do have a powerfully detrimental effect on society— largely because people cannot discern their real messages. The literature department’s courses give students the critical skills to analyze and understand texts. Therefore, it is the literature department’s responsibility to include the study of advertisements in its undergraduate courses.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which Professor Wigmore’s argument depends?

answerChoices.A: Texts that are true literary works never have a detrimental effect on society.
answerChoices.B: Courses offered by the literature department cannot include both true literary works and material such as advertisements.
answerChoices.C: Students who take courses in the literature department do not get from those courses other skills besides those needed to analyze and understand texts.
answerChoices.D: Forms of advertising that convey their message entirely through visual images do not have a detrimental effect on society.
answerChoices.E: The literature department’s responsibility is not limited to teaching students how to analyze true literary works.

questions.stimulus:
Sociologist: Some people argue that capital punishment for theft was an essential part of the labor discipline of British capitalism. Critics of such a view argue that more people were executed for theft in preindustrial England than were executed in England after industrialization. But such a criticism overlooks the fact that industrialization and capitalism are two very different social phenomena, and that the latter predated the
former by several centuries.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the role played in the passage by the point that capitalism and industrialization are distinct?

answerChoices.A: It is cited as some evidence against the claim that capital punishment for theft was an essential part of the labor discipline of British capitalism.
answerChoices.B: It is cited as a direct contradiction of the claim that capital punishment for theft was an essential part of the labor discipline of British capitalism.
answerChoices.C: It is an attempt to conclusively prove the claim that capital punishment for theft was an essential part of the labor discipline of British capitalism.
answerChoices.D: It is cited as a fact supporting the critics of the view that capital punishment for theft was an essential part of the labor discipline of British capitalism.
answerChoices.E: It is an attempt to undermine the criticism cited against the claim that capital punishment for theft was an essential part of the labor discipline of British capitalism.

questions.stimulus: To be horrific, a monster must be threatening. Whether or not it presents psychological, moral, or social dangers, or triggers enduring infantile fears, if a monster is physically dangerous then it is threatening. In fact, even a physically benign monster is horrific if it inspires revulsion.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following logically follows from the statements above?

answerChoices.A: Any horror-story monster that is threatening is also horrific.
answerChoices.B: A monster that is psychologically dangerous, but that does not inspire revulsion, is not horrific.
answerChoices.C: If a monster triggers infantile fears but is not physically dangerous, then it is not horrific.
answerChoices.D: If a monster is both horrific and psychologically threatening, then it does not inspire revulsion.
answerChoices.E: All monsters that are not physically dangerous, but that are psychologically dangerous and inspire revulsion, are threatening.

questions.stimulus: Lawyer: The defendant wanted to clear the snow off his car and in doing so knocked snow on the sidewalk. This same snow melted and refroze, forming ice on which the plaintiff fell, breaking her hip. We argue that the defendant maliciously harmed the plaintiff, because malice is intention to cause harm and the defendant intentionally removed the snow from his car and put it on the sidewalk, which, unbeknownst to the defendant at the time, would subsequently cause the injury suffered by the plaintiff.
questions.questionStem: The flawed reasoning in which one of the following is most similar to that in the lawyer’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Alice asked her sister to lie in court. Unbeknownst to Alice’s sister, lying in court is against the law. So what Alice asked her sister to do was illegal.
answerChoices.B: Bruce wanted to eat the mincemeat pie. Unbeknownst to Bruce, the mincemeat pie was poisonous. So Bruce wanted to eat poison.
answerChoices.C: Cheryl denigrated the wine. Cheryl’s sister had picked out the wine. So though she may not have realized it, Cheryl indirectly denigrated her sister.
answerChoices.D: Deon had lunch with Ms. Osgood. Unbeknownst to Deon, Ms. Osgood is generally thought to be an industrial spy. So Deon had lunch with an industrial spy.
answerChoices.E: Edwina bought a car from Mr. Yancy, then resold it. Unbeknownst to Edwina, Mr. Yancy had stolen the car. So Edwina sold a stolen car.

questions.stimulus: Although wood-burning stoves are more efficient than open fireplaces, they are also more dangerous. The smoke that wood-burning stoves release up the chimney is cooler than the smoke from an open flame. Thus it travels more slowly and deposits more creosote, a flammable substance that can clog a chimney—or worse, ignite inside it.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: The most efficient wood-burning stoves produce less creosote than do many open fireplaces.
answerChoices.B: The amount of creosote produced depends not only on the type of flame but on how often the stove or fireplace is used.
answerChoices.C: Open fireplaces pose more risk of severe accidents inside the home than do wood-burning stoves.
answerChoices.D: Open fireplaces also produce a large amount of creosote residue.
answerChoices.E: Homeowners in warm climates rarely use fireplaces or wood-burning stoves.

questions.stimulus: If a doctor gives a patient only a few options for lifestyle modification, the patient is more likely to adhere to the doctor’s advice than if the doctor gives the patient many options.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the principle illustrated above?

answerChoices.A: People are especially likely to ignore the advice they get from doctors if they are confused about that advice.
answerChoices.B: People dislike calculating the best of a variety of choices unless they can see a clear difference among the benefits that would result from each choice.
answerChoices.C: The tendency people have to alter their behavior varies inversely with the number of alternatives available to them for behavior modification.
answerChoices.D: Most people are unlikely to follow their doctor’s advice unless they can vividly imagine the consequences of not following the advice.
answerChoices.E: In getting good results, the clarity with which a doctor instructs a patient is of equal importance to the accuracy of the doctor’s diagnosis on which that instruction is based.

questions.stimulus: To acquire a better understanding of the structure and development of the human personality, some psychologists study the personalities of animals.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, contributes to an explanation of the practice mentioned above EXCEPT:

answerChoices.A: The actions of humans and animals are believed to be motivated by similar instincts, but these instincts are easier to discern in animals.
answerChoices.B: The law forbids certain experiments on humans but permits them on animals.
answerChoices.C: It is generally less expensive to perform experiments on animals than it is to perform them on humans.
answerChoices.D: Proper understanding of human personality is thought to provide a model for better understanding the personality of animals.
answerChoices.E: Field observations of the behavior of young animals often inspire insightful hypotheses about human personality development.

questions.stimulus: Sigatoka disease drastically reduces the yield of banana trees and is epidemic throughout the areas of the world where bananas are grown. The fungus that causes the disease can be controlled with fungicides, but the fungicides can pose a health hazard to people living nearby. The fungicides are thus unsuitable for small banana groves in populated areas. Fortunately, most large banana plantations are in locations so isolated that fungicides can be used safely there. Therefore, most of the world’s banana crop is not seriously threatened by Sigatoka disease.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: It will eventually be possible to breed strains of bananas that are resistant to Sigatoka disease.
answerChoices.B: Large plantations produce most or all of the world’s bananas.
answerChoices.C: Sigatoka disease spreads more slowly on large plantations than in small banana groves.
answerChoices.D: Sigatoka disease is the only disease that threatens bananas on a worldwide scale.
answerChoices.E: Most of the banana trees that have not been exposed to the Sigatoka fungus grow in small banana groves.

questions.stimulus: A group of 1,000 students was randomly selected from three high schools in a medium-sized city and asked the question, “Do you plan to finish your high school education?” More than 89 percent answered “Yes. ” This shows that the overwhelming majority of students want to finish high school, and that if the national dropout rate among high school students is high, it cannot be due to a lack of desire on the part of the students.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning of the argument above is questionable because the argument

answerChoices.A: fails to justify its presumption that 89 percent is an overwhelming majority
answerChoices.B: attempts to draw two conflicting conclusions from the results of one survey
answerChoices.C: overlooks the possibility that there may in fact not be a high dropout rate among high school students
answerChoices.D: contradicts itself by admitting that there may be a high dropout rate among students while claiming that most students want to finish high school
answerChoices.E: treats high school students from a particular medium-sized city as if they are representative of high school students nationwide

questions.stimulus: Columnist: A democratic society cannot exist unless its citizens have established strong bonds of mutual trust. Such bonds are formed and strengthened only by participation in civic organizations, political parties, and other groups outside the family. It is obvious then that widespread reliance on movies and electronic media for entertainment has an inherently corrosive effect on democracy.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the columnist’s argument depends?

answerChoices.A: Anyone who relies on movies and electronic media for entertainment is unable to form a strong bond of mutual trust with a citizen.
answerChoices.B: Civic organizations cannot usefully advance their goals by using electronic media.
answerChoices.C: Newspapers and other forms of print media strengthen, rather than weaken, democratic institutions.
answerChoices.D: Relying on movies and electronic media for entertainment generally makes people less likely to participate in groups outside their families.
answerChoices.E: People who rely on movies and electronic media for entertainment are generally closer to their families than are those who do not.

questions.stimulus: Standard archaeological techniques make it possible to determine the age of anything containing vegetable matter, but only if the object is free of minerals containing carbon. Prehistoric artists painted on limestone with pigments composed of vegetable matter, but it is impossible to collect samples of this prehistoric paint without removing limestone, a mineral containing carbon, with the paint. Therefore, it is not possible to determine the age of prehistoric paintings on limestone using standard archaeological techniques.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: There exist several different techniques for collecting samples of prehistoric pigments on limestone.
answerChoices.B: Laboratory procedures exist that can remove all the limestone from a sample of prehistoric paint on limestone.
answerChoices.C: The age of the limestone itself can be determined from samples that contain no vegetable-based paint.
answerChoices.D: Prehistoric artists did not use anything other than vegetable matter to make their paints.
answerChoices.E: The proportion of carbon to other elements in limestone is the same in all samples of limestone.

questions.stimulus: Dr. Jones: The new technology dubbed “telemedicine” will provide sustained improvement in at least rural patient care since it allows rural physicians to televise medical examinations to specialists who live at great distances—specialists who will thus be able to provide advice the rural patient would otherwise not receive. Dr. Carabella: Not so. Telemedicine might help rural patient care initially. However, small hospitals will soon realize that they can minimize expenses by replacing physicians with technicians who can use telemedicine to transmit examinations to large medical centers, resulting in fewer patients being able to receive traditional, direct medical examinations. Eventually, it will be the rare individual who ever gets truly personal attention. Hence, rural as well as urban patient care will suffer.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is a point at issue between Dr. Jones and Dr. Carabella?

answerChoices.A: whether medical specialists in general offer better advice than rural physicians
answerChoices.B: whether telemedicine technology will be installed only in rural hospitals and rural medical centers
answerChoices.C: whether telemedicine is likely to be widely adopted in rural areas in future years
answerChoices.D: whether the patients who most need the advice of medical specialists are likely to receive it through telemedicine
answerChoices.E: whether the technology of telemedicine will benefit rural patients in the long run

questions.stimulus:
Dr. Jones: The new technology dubbed “telemedicine” will provide sustained improvement in at least rural patient care since it allows rural physicians to televise medical examinations to specialists who live at great distances-specialists who will thus be able to provide advice the rural patient would otherwise not receive.

Dr. Carabella: Not so. Telemedicine might help rural patient care initially. However, small hospitals will soon realize that they can minimize expenses by replacing physicians with technicians who can use telemedicine to transmit examinations to large medical centers, resulting in fewer patients being able to receive traditional, direct medical examination. Eventually, it will be the rare individual who ever gets truly personal attention. Hence, rural as well as urban patient care will suffer.
questions.questionStem: Dr. Carabella uses which one of the following strategies in responding to Dr. Jones?

answerChoices.A: listing a set of considerations to show that a prescribed treatment that seems to be benefiting a patient in fact harms that patient
answerChoices.B: describing the application of the technology discussed by Dr. Jones as one step that initiates a process that leads to an undesirable end
answerChoices.C: citing evidence that Dr. Jones lacks the professional training to judge the case at issue
answerChoices.D: invoking medical statistics that cast doubt on the premises used in Dr. Jones’s argument
answerChoices.E: providing grounds for dismissing Dr. Jones’s interpretation of a key term in medical technology

questions.stimulus: Lines can be parallel in a Euclidean system of geometry. But the non-Euclidean system of geometry that has the most empirical verification is regarded by several prominent physicists as correctly describing the universe we inhabit. If these physicists are right, in our universe there are no parallel lines.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption that is required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: There are no parallel lines in the non-Euclidean system of geometry that has the most empirical verification.
answerChoices.B: Most physicists have not doubted the view that the universe is correctly described by the non-Euclidean system of geometry that has the most empirical verification.
answerChoices.C: There are no parallel lines in every non-Euclidean system of geometry that has any empirical verification.
answerChoices.D: The universe is correctly described by the non-Euclidean system of geometry that has the most empirical verification if prominent physicists maintain that it is.
answerChoices.E: Only physicists who are not prominent doubt the view that the universe is correctly described by the non-Euclidean system of geometry that has the most empirical verification.

questions.stimulus: Philosopher: People are not intellectually well suited to live in large bureaucratic societies. Therefore, people can find happiness, if at all, only in smaller political units such as villages.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the philosopher’s argument is flawed because the argument takes for granted that

answerChoices.A: no one can ever be happy living in a society in which she or he is not intellectually well suited to live
answerChoices.B: the primary purpose of small political units such as villages is to make people happy
answerChoices.C: all societies that are plagued by excessive bureaucracy are large
answerChoices.D: anyone who lives in a village or other small political unit that is not excessively bureaucratic can find happiness
answerChoices.E: everyone is willing to live in villages or other small political units

questions.stimulus: The present goal of the field of medicine seems to be to extend life indefinitely. Increasingly, the ability to transplant such organs as hearts, lungs, livers, and kidneys will allow us to live longer. But we can never achieve brain transplants. There are, for a start, ten million nerves running from the brain down the neck, not to mention the millions joining the brain to the sensing organs. Clearly, then, as the transplantation of organs allows more and more people to live longer, those with degenerative brain disorders will form an ever-increasing proportion of the population.
questions.questionStem: The argument above is based on which one of the following assumptions?

answerChoices.A: Degenerative brain disorders will increasingly strike younger and younger patients.
answerChoices.B: It is still quite rare for people to live long enough to need more than one transplant of any given organ.
answerChoices.C: There are degenerative brain disorders that will not be curable without brain transplants.
answerChoices.D: Degenerative brain disorders account for a very small proportion of deaths in the population at large.
answerChoices.E: More is being spent on research into degenerative brain disorders than on research into transplantation.

questions.stimulus: Politician: My opponents argue that the future of our city depends on compromise—that unless the city’s leaders put aside their differences and work together toward common goals, the city will suffer. However, the founders of this city based the city’s charter on definite principles, and anyone who compromises those principles betrays the city founders’ goals. What my opponents are advocating, therefore, is nothing less than betraying the goals of the city’s founders. Critic: I’m afraid your argument is flawed. Unless you’re assuming that the differences among the city’s leaders are differences of principle, your argument depends on a misleading use of the term _______.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following provides the most logical completion of the critic’s statement?

answerChoices.A: betray
answerChoices.B: common
answerChoices.C: compromise
answerChoices.D: principles
answerChoices.E: opponents

questions.stimulus: Though many insects die soon after reproducing for the first time, some may live for years after the survival of the next generation has been secured. Among the latter are some insects that work for the benefit of the ecosystem—for example, bees.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the information above?

answerChoices.A: Survival of the species, rather than of the individual, is the goal of most insect populations.
answerChoices.B: Insects that do not play a vital role in the ecosystem are more likely to die after reproducing for the first time.
answerChoices.C: Most bees live well beyond the onset of the generation that follows them.
answerChoices.D: Those bees that reproduce do not always die soon after reproducing for the first time.
answerChoices.E: Most insects are hatched self-sufficient and do not need to be cared for by adult insects.

questions.stimulus: People’s political behavior frequently does not match their rhetoric. Although many complain about government intervention in their lives, they tend not to reelect inactive politicians. But a politician’s activity consists largely in the passage of laws whose enforcement affects voters’ lives. Thus, voters often reelect politicians whose behavior they resent.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the role played in the argument by the claim that people tend not to reelect inactive politicians?

answerChoices.A: It describes a phenomenon for which the argument’s conclusion is offered as an explanation.
answerChoices.B: It is a premise offered in support of the conclusion that voters often reelect politicians whose behavior they resent.
answerChoices.C: It is offered as an example of how a politician’s activity consists largely in the passage of laws whose enforcement interferes with voters’ lives.
answerChoices.D: It is a generalization based on the claim that people complain about government intervention in their lives.
answerChoices.E: It is cited as evidence that people’s behavior never matches their political beliefs.

questions.stimulus:
Lea: Contemporary art has become big business. Nowadays art has less to do with self-expression than with making money. The work of contemporary artists is utterly bereft of spontaneity and creativity, as a visit to any art gallery demonstrates.

Susan: I disagree. One can still find spontaneous, innovative new artwork in most of the smaller, independent galleries.
questions.questionStem: Lea’s and Susan’s remarks provide the most support for holding that they disagree about whether

answerChoices.A: large galleries contain creative artwork
answerChoices.B: most galleries contain some artwork that lacks spontaneity and creativity
answerChoices.C: contemporary art has become big business
answerChoices.D: some smaller art galleries still exhibit creative new artwork
answerChoices.E: contemporary art, in general, is much less concerned with self-expression than older art is

questions.stimulus: Ethicist: In a recent judicial decision, a contractor was ordered to make restitution to a company because of a bungled construction job, even though the company had signed a written agreement prior to entering into the contract that the contractor would not be financially liable should the task not be adequately performed. Thus, it was morally wrong for the company to change its mind and seek restitution.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the ethicist’s reasoning?

answerChoices.A: It is morally wrong for one party not to abide by its part of an agreement only if the other party abides by its part of the agreement.
answerChoices.B: It is morally wrong to seek a penalty for an action for which the agent is unable to make restitution.
answerChoices.C: It is morally wrong for one person to seek to penalize another person for an action that the first person induced the other person to perform.
answerChoices.D: It is morally wrong to ignore the terms of an agreement that was freely undertaken only if there is clear evidence that the agreement was legally permissible.
answerChoices.E: It is morally wrong to seek compensation for an action performed in the context of a promise to forgo such compensation.

questions.stimulus: Zoologist: Animals can certainly signal each other with sounds and gestures. However, this does not confirm the thesis that animals possess language, for it does not prove that animals possess the ability to use sounds or gestures to refer to concrete objects or abstract ideas.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the zoologist’s argument depends?

answerChoices.A: Animals do not have the cognitive capabilities to entertain abstract ideas.
answerChoices.B: If an animal’s system of sounds or gestures is not a language, then that animal is unable to entertain abstract ideas.
answerChoices.C: When signaling each other with sounds or gestures, animals refer neither to concrete objects nor abstract ideas.
answerChoices.D: If a system of sounds or gestures contains no expressions referring to concrete objects or abstract ideas, then that system is not a language.
answerChoices.E: Some animals that possess a language can refer to both concrete objects and abstract ideas.

questions.stimulus: A person is more likely to become disabled as that person ages. Among adults in the country of East Wendell, however, the proportion receiving disability benefit payments shrinks from 4 percent among 55 to 64 year olds to 2 percent for those aged 65 to 74 and 1 percent for those aged 75 and older. The explanation of this discrepancy is that the proportion of jobs offering such a disability benefit has greatly increased in recent years.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true about East Wendell, shows that the explanation above is at best incomplete?

answerChoices.A: The treatment of newly incurred disabilities is more successful now than in the past in restoring partial function in the affected area within six months.
answerChoices.B: Some people receive disability benefit payments under employers’ insurance plans, and some receive them from the government.
answerChoices.C: Medical advances have prolonged the average lifespan beyond what it was 20 years ago.
answerChoices.D: For persons receiving disability benefit payments, those payments on average represent a smaller share of their predisability income now than was the case 20 years ago.
answerChoices.E: Under most employers’ plans, disability benefit payments stop when an employee with a disability reaches the usual retirement age of 65.

questions.stimulus: Light is registered in the retina when photons hit molecules of the pigment rhodopsin and change the molecules’ shape. Even when they have not been struck by photons of light, rhodopsin molecules sometimes change shape because of normal molecular motion, thereby introducing error into the visual system. The amount of this molecular motion is directly proportional to the temperature of the retina.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following conclusions is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: The temperature of an animal’s retina depends on the amount of light the retina is absorbing.
answerChoices.B: The visual systems of animals whose body temperature matches that of their surroundings are more error-prone in hot surroundings than in cold ones.
answerChoices.C: As the temperature of the retina rises, rhodopsin molecules react more slowly to being struck by photons.
answerChoices.D: Rhodopsin molecules are more sensitive to photons in animals whose retinas have large surface areas than in animals whose retinas have small surface areas.
answerChoices.E: Molecules of rhodopsin are the only pigment molecules that occur naturally in the retina.

questions.stimulus: Critic: Political utility determines the popularity of a metaphor. In authoritarian societies, the metaphor of society as a human body governed by a head is pervasive. Therefore, the society-as-body metaphor, with its connection between society’s proper functioning and governance by a head, promotes greater acceptance of authoritarian repression than do other metaphors, such as likening society to a family.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most weakens the critic’s argument?

answerChoices.A: In authoritarian societies, the metaphor of society as a family is just as pervasive as the society-as-body metaphor.
answerChoices.B: Every society tries to justify the legitimacy of its government through the use of metaphor.
answerChoices.C: The metaphor of society as a human body is sometimes used in nonauthoritarian societies.
answerChoices.D: Authoritarian leaders are always searching for new metaphors for society in their effort to maintain their power.
answerChoices.E: The metaphor of society as a human body governed by a head is rarely used in liberal democracies.

questions.stimulus: Thirty years ago, the percentage of their income that single persons spent on food was twice what it is today. Given that incomes have risen over the past thirty years, we can conclude that incomes have risen at a greater rate than the price of food in that period.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, helps most to justify the conclusion drawn above?

answerChoices.A: The amount of food eaten per capita today is identical to the amount of food eaten per capita thirty years ago.
answerChoices.B: In general, single persons today eat healthier foods and eat less than their counterparts of thirty years ago.
answerChoices.C: Single persons today, on average, purchase the same kinds of food items in the same quantities as they did thirty years ago.
answerChoices.D: The prices of nonfood items single persons purchase have risen faster than the price of food over the past thirty years.
answerChoices.E: Unlike single persons, families today spend about the same percentage of their income on food as they did thirty years ago.

questions.stimulus: Viruses can have beneficial effects. For example, some kill more-complex microorganisms, some of which are deadly to humans. But viruses have such simple structures that replacing just a few of a beneficial virus’s several million atoms can make it deadly to humans. Clearly, since alterations of greater complexity than this are commonly produced by random mutations, any virus could easily become dangerous to humans.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, then each of the following statements could also be true EXCEPT:

answerChoices.A: Random mutation makes some deadly viruses beneficial to humans.
answerChoices.B: Some organisms of greater complexity than viruses are no more likely than viruses to undergo significant alterations through random mutation.
answerChoices.C: Some microorganisms that are more complex than viruses are beneficial to humans.
answerChoices.D: Some viruses that fail to kill other viruses that are deadly to humans are nevertheless beneficial to humans.
answerChoices.E: No virus that is deadly to organisms of greater complexity than itself is beneficial to humans.

questions.stimulus: Societies in which value is measured primarily in financial terms invariably fragment into isolated social units. But since money is not the main measure of value in nonindustrial societies, they must tend in contrast to be socially unified.
questions.questionStem: The flawed reasoning in which one of the following is most similar to that in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Animals of different genera cannot interbreed. But that does not prove that jackals and wolves cannot interbreed, for they belong to the same genus.
answerChoices.B: Ecosystems close to the equator usually have more species than those closer to the poles. Thus, the Sahara Desert must contain more species than Siberia does, since the latter is farther from the equator.
answerChoices.C: Insects pass through several stages of maturation: egg, larva, pupa, and adult. Since insects are arthropods, all arthropods probably undergo similar maturation processes.
answerChoices.D: Poets frequently convey their thoughts via nonliteral uses of language such as metaphors and analogies. But journalists are not poets, so surely journalists always use language literally.
answerChoices.E: Technologically sophisticated machines often cause us more trouble than simpler devices serving the same function. Since computers are more technologically sophisticated than pencils, they must tend to be more troublesome.

questions.stimulus: Ringtail opossums are an Australian wildlife species that is potentially endangered. A number of ringtail opossums that had been orphaned and subsequently raised in captivity were monitored after being returned to the wild. Seventy-five percent of these opossums were killed by foxes, a species not native to Australia. Conservationists concluded that the native ringtail opossum population was endangered not by a scarcity of food, as had been previously thought, but by non-native predator species against which the opossum had not developed natural defenses.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strongly supports the conservationists’ argument?

answerChoices.A: There are fewer non-native predator species that prey on the ringtail opossum than there are native species that prey on the ringtail opossum.
answerChoices.B: Foxes, which were introduced into Australia over 200 years ago, adapted to the Australian climate less successfully than did some other foreign species.
answerChoices.C: The ringtail opossums that were raised in captivity were fed a diet similar to that which ringtail opossums typically eat in the wild.
answerChoices.D: Few of the species that compete with the ringtail opossum for food sources are native to Australia.
answerChoices.E: Ringtail opossums that grow to adulthood in the wild defend themselves against foxes no more successfully than do ringtail opossums raised in captivity.

questions.stimulus: Jordan: If a business invests the money necessary to implement ecologically sound practices, its market share will decrease. But if it doesn’t implement these practices, it pollutes the environment and wastes resources. Terry: But if consumers demand environmental responsibility of all businesses, no particular business will be especially hurt.
questions.questionStem: In which one of the following exchanges is the logical relationship between Jordan’s and Terry’s statements most similar to the logical relationship between their statements above?

answerChoices.A: Jordan: Either it will rain and our plans for a picnic will be thwarted or it won’t rain and the garden will go yet another day without much-needed watering. Terry: But if it doesn’t rain, we can buy a hose and water the garden with the hose.
answerChoices.B: Jordan: Each person can have either an enjoyable life or a long life, for one must eat vegetables and exercise continuously to stay healthy. Terry: That’s not true: there are many happy health-conscious people.
answerChoices.C: Jordan: If taxes are raised, many social problems could be solved, but if they’re lowered, the economy will grow again. So we can’t have both social reform and a growing economy. Terry: But if taxes remain at their current level, neither social problems nor the economy will get worse.
answerChoices.D: Jordan: If we remodel the kitchen, the house will be more valuable, but even if we do, there’s no guarantee that we’ll actually get more for the house when we sell it. Terry: But if we don’t remodel the kitchen, we might get even less for the house than we paid for it.
answerChoices.E: Jordan: If the dam’s spillway is opened, the river might flood the eastern part of town, but if the spillway is not opened, the dam might burst. Terry: There’s no real danger of the dam’s bursting, but if we get more heavy rain, opening the spillway is the most prudent policy.

questions.stimulus: The media now devote more coverage to crime than they did ten years ago. Yet this is not because the crime rate has increased, but rather because the public is now more interested in reading and hearing about crime. After all, a crucial factor in the media’s decisions about what issues to cover and to what extent to cover them is the interests of their audiences.
questions.questionStem: The proposition that the public is now more interested in reading and hearing about crime plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It supports the conclusion that the media now devote more coverage to crime than the crime rate alone justifies.
answerChoices.B: It is presented as evidence that the media decide what to cover and to what extent to cover it depending on the interests of the public.
answerChoices.C: It is a counterexample to the claim that the media devote more coverage to crime now than they did ten years ago.
answerChoices.D: It is a generalization based on the claim that the crime rate has increased over the past ten years.
answerChoices.E: It is offered as an alternative explanation of why the media devote more coverage to crime now than they did ten years ago.

questions.stimulus: Some critics argue that an opera’s stage directions are never reflected in its music. Many comic scenes in Mozart’s operas, however, open with violin phrases that sound like the squeaking of changing scenery. Clearly Mozart intended the music to echo the sounds occurring while stage directions are carried out. Hence, a change of scenery—the most basic and frequent stage direction— can be reflected in the music, which means that other operatic stage directions can be as well.
questions.questionStem: In the argument, the statement that many comic scenes in Mozart’s operas open with violin phrases that sound like the squeaking of changing scenery is offered in support of the claim that

answerChoices.A: a change of scenery is the stage direction most frequently reflected in an opera’s music
answerChoices.B: an opera’s stage directions are never reflected in its music
answerChoices.C: an opera’s music can have an effect on the opera’s stage directions
answerChoices.D: a variety of stage directions can be reflected in an opera’s music
answerChoices.E: the most frequent relation between an opera’s music and its stage directions is one of musical imitation of the sounds that occur when a direction is carried out

questions.stimulus:
Lecturer: Given our current state of knowledge and technology, we can say that the generalization that the entropy of a closed system cannot decrease for any spontaneous process has not been falsified by any of our tests of that generalization. So we conclude it to be true
universally. Yet, it must be admitted that this generalization has not been conclusively verified, in the sense that it has not been tested in every corner of the universe, under every feasible condition. Nevertheless, this generalization is correctly regarded as a scientific law; indeed, it is referred to as the Second Law of Thermodynamics.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most justifies the lecturer’s classification of the generalization described above?

answerChoices.A: Whatever is a scientific law has not been falsified.
answerChoices.B: If a generalization is confirmed only under a few circumstances, it should not be considered a scientific law.
answerChoices.C: Whatever is true universally will eventually be confirmed to the extent current science allows.
answerChoices.D: If a generalization is confirmed to the extent current science allows, then it is considered a scientific law.
answerChoices.E: Whatever is regarded as a scientific law will eventually be conclusively verified.

questions.stimulus: More women than men suffer from Alzheimer’s disease—a disease that is most commonly contracted by elderly persons. This discrepancy has often been attributed to women’s longer life span, but this theory may be wrong. A recent study has shown that prescribing estrogen to women after menopause, when estrogen production in the body decreases, may prevent them from developing the disease. Men’s supply of testosterone may help safeguard them against Alzheimer’s disease because much of it is converted by the body to estrogen, and testosterone levels stay relatively stable into old age.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

answerChoices.A: A decrease in estrogen, rather than longer life span, may explain the higher occurrence of Alzheimer’s disease in women relative to men.
answerChoices.B: As one gets older, one’s chances of developing Alzheimer’s disease increase.
answerChoices.C: Women who go through menopause earlier in life than do most other women have an increased risk of contracting Alzheimer’s disease.
answerChoices.D: The conversion of testosterone into estrogen may help safeguard men from Alzheimer’s disease.
answerChoices.E: Testosterone is necessary for preventing Alzheimer’s disease in older men.

questions.stimulus:
Parent P: Children will need computer skills to deal with tomorrow’s world. Computers should be introduced in kindergarten, and computer languages should be required in high school.
Parent Q: That would be pointless. Technology advances so rapidly that the computers used by today’s kindergartners and the computer languages taught in today’s high schools would become obsolete by the time these children are adults.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, is the strongest logical counter parent P can make to parent Q’s objection?

answerChoices.A: When technology is advancing rapidly, regular training is necessary to keep one’s skills at a level proficient enough to deal with the society in which one lives.
answerChoices.B: Throughout history people have adapted to change, and there is no reason to believe that today’s children are not equally capable of adapting to technology as it advances.
answerChoices.C: In the process of learning to work with any computer or computer language, children increase their ability to interact with computer technology.
answerChoices.D: Automotive technology is continually advancing too, but that does not result in one’s having to relearn to drive cars as the new advances are incorporated into new automobiles.
answerChoices.E: Once people have graduated from high school, they have less time to learn about computers and technology than they had during their schooling years.

questions.stimulus:
The following passage is used for Section 1, questions 5 through 6.
Proponent: Irradiation of food by gamma rays would keep it from spoiling before it reaches the consumer in food stores. The process leaves no radiation behind, and vitamin losses are comparable to those that occur in cooking, so there is no reason to reject irradiation on the grounds of nutrition or safety. Indeed, it kills harmful Salmonella bacteria, which in contaminated poultry have caused serious illness to consumers.
Opponent: The irradiation process has no effect on the bacteria that cause botulism, a very serious form of food poisoning, while those that cause bad odors that would warn consumers of botulism are killed. Moreover, Salmonella and the bacteria that cause botulism can easily be killed in poultry by using a safe chemical dip.
questions.questionStem: The opponent’s argument proceeds by

answerChoices.A: isolating an ambiguity in a crucial term in the proponent’s argument
answerChoices.B: showing that claims made in the proponent’s argument result in a self-contradiction
answerChoices.C: establishing that undesirable consequences result from the adoption of either one of two proposed remedies
answerChoices.D: shifting perspective from safety with respect to consumers to safety with respect to producers
answerChoices.E: pointing out an alternative way of obtaining an advantage claimed by the proponent without risking a particular disadvantage

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could the opponent properly cite as indicating a flaw in the proponent’s reasoning concerning vitamin losses?

questions.stimulus: Due to wider commercial availability of audio recordings of authors reading their own books, sales of printed books have dropped significantly.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following conforms most closely to the principle illustrated above?

answerChoices.A: Because of the rising cost of farm labor, farmers began to make more extensive use of machines.
answerChoices.B: Because of the wide variety of new computer games on the market, sales of high-quality computer video screens have improved.
answerChoices.C: Because a new brand of soft drink entered the market, consumers reduced their consumption of an established brand of soft drink.
answerChoices.D: Because a child was forbidden to play until homework was completed, that child did much less daydreaming and focused on homework.
answerChoices.E: Because neither of the two leading word processing programs has all of the features consumers want, neither has been able to dominate the market.

questions.stimulus:
Lobsters and other crustaceans eaten by humans are more
likely to contract gill diseases when sewage contaminates their water. Under a recent proposal, millions of gallons of local sewage each day would be rerouted many kilometers offshore. Although this would substantially reduce the amount of sewage in the harbor where lobsters are caught, the proposal is pointless, because hardly any lobsters live long enough to be harmed by those diseases.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Contaminants in the harbor other than sewage are equally harmful to lobsters.
answerChoices.B: Lobsters, like other crustaceans, live longer in the open ocean than in industrial harbors.
answerChoices.C: Lobsters breed as readily in sewage-contaminated water as in unpolluted water.
answerChoices.D: Gill diseases cannot be detected by examining the surface of the lobster.
answerChoices.E: Humans often become ill as a result of eating lobsters with gill diseases.

questions.stimulus: Researcher: The rate of psychological problems is higher among children of divorced parents than among other children. But it would be a mistake to conclude that these problems are caused by the difficulty the children have adjusting to divorce. It is just as reasonable to infer that certain behaviors that increase the likelihood of divorce—hostility, distrust, lack of empathy— are learned by children from their parents, and that it is these learned behaviors, rather than the difficulty of adjusting to divorce, that cause the children’s psychological problems.
questions.questionStem: The assertion that children of divorced parents have a higher rate of psychological problems than other children figures in the argument in which one of the following ways?

answerChoices.A: It is the conclusion of the argument.
answerChoices.B: It is the claim that the argument tries to refute.
answerChoices.C: It is offered as evidence for the claim that divorce is harmful to the children of the divorcing parents.
answerChoices.D: It is offered as evidence for the claim that certain behaviors are often responsible for divorce.
answerChoices.E: It is cited as an established finding for which the argument proposes an explanation.

questions.stimulus: Although marathons are 26.2 miles (42.2 kilometers) long and take even world-class marathoners over 2 hours to run, athletes who train by running 90 minutes a day fare better in marathons than do those who train by running 120 minutes or more a day.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, contributes to an explanation of the difference in marathon performances described above except:

answerChoices.A: The longer the period of time that one runs daily, the greater the chances of suffering adverse health effects due to air pollution.
answerChoices.B: The longer the period of time that one runs daily, the easier it is to adjust to different race lengths.
answerChoices.C: The longer the run, the more frequent is the occurrence of joint injuries that significantly interfere with overall training.
answerChoices.D: Runners who train over 90 minutes per day grow bored with running and become less motivated.
answerChoices.E: Runners who train over 90 minutes per day deplete certain biochemical energy reserves, leaving them less energy for marathons.

questions.stimulus: Linguist: Some people have understood certain studies as showing that bilingual children have a reduced “conceptual map” because bilingualism overstresses the child’s linguistic capacities. Vocabulary tests taken by bilingual children appear to show that these children tend to have a smaller vocabulary than do most children of the same age group. But these studies are deeply flawed, since the tests were given in only one language. Dual-language tests revealed that the children often expressed a given concept with a word from only one of their two languages.
questions.questionStem: The linguist’s argument proceeds by

answerChoices.A: offering evidence for the advantages of bilingualism over monolingualism
answerChoices.B: pointing out an inconsistency in the view that bilingualism overstresses a child’s linguistic capabilities
answerChoices.C: offering evidence that undermines the use of any vocabulary test to provide information about a child’s conceptual map
answerChoices.D: providing a different explanation for the apparent advantages of bilingualism from the explanation suggested by the results of certain studies
answerChoices.E: pointing out a methodological error in the technique used to obtain the purported evidence of a problem with bilingualism

questions.stimulus: Gene splicing can give rise to new varieties of farm animals that have only a partially understood genetic makeup. In addition to introducing the genes for whichever trait is desired, the technique can introduce genes governing the production of toxins or carcinogens, and these latter undesirable traits might not be easily discoverable.
questions.questionStem:
The statements above, if true, most strongly support
which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: All toxin production is genetically controlled.
answerChoices.B: Gene splicing to produce new varieties of farm animals should be used cautiously.
answerChoices.C: Gene splicing is not effective as a way of producing new varieties of farm animals.
answerChoices.D: Most new varieties of farm animals produced by gene splicing will develop cancer.
answerChoices.E: Gene splicing will advance to the point where unforeseen consequences are no longer a problem.

questions.stimulus: Journal: In several psychological studies, subjects were given statements to read that caused them to form new beliefs. Later, the subjects were told that the original statements were false. The studies report, however, that most subjects persevered in their newly acquired beliefs, even after being told that the original statements were false. This strongly suggests that humans continue to hold onto acquired beliefs even in the absence of any credible evidence to support them.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most undermines the journal’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Regardless of the truth of what the subjects were later told, the beliefs based on the original statements were, for the most part, correct.
answerChoices.B: It is unrealistic to expect people to keep track of the original basis of their beliefs, and to revise a belief when its original basis is undercut.
answerChoices.C: The statements originally given to the subjects would be highly misleading even if true.
answerChoices.D: Most of the subjects had acquired confirmation of their newly acquired beliefs by the time they were told that the original statements were false.
answerChoices.E: Most of the subjects were initially skeptical of the statements originally given to them.

questions.stimulus: Novelists cannot become great as long as they remain in academia. Powers of observation and analysis, which schools successfully hone, are useful to the novelist, but an intuitive grasp of the emotions of everyday life can be obtained only by the kind of immersion in everyday life that is precluded by being an academic.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: Novelists require some impartiality to get an intuitive grasp of the emotions of everyday life.
answerChoices.B: No great novelist lacks powers of observation and analysis.
answerChoices.C: Participation in life, interspersed with impartial observation of life, makes novelists great.
answerChoices.D: Novelists cannot be great without an intuitive grasp of the emotions of everyday life.
answerChoices.E: Knowledge of the emotions of everyday life cannot be acquired by merely observing and analyzing life.

questions.stimulus:
Statistician: A financial magazine claimed that its survey of its subscribers showed that North Americans are more concerned about their personal finances than about politics. One question was: “Which do you think about more: politics or the joy of earning money?” This question is clearly biased. Also, the readers of the magazine are a self-selecting sample. Thus, there is reason to be skeptical about the conclusion drawn in the
magazine’s survey.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, would strengthen the statistician’s argument except:

answerChoices.A: The credibility of the magazine has been called into question on a number of occasions.
answerChoices.B: The conclusions drawn in most magazine surveys have eventually been disproved.
answerChoices.C: Other surveys suggest that North Americans are just as concerned about politics as they are about finances.
answerChoices.D: There is reason to be skeptical about the results of surveys that are biased and unrepresentative.
answerChoices.E: Other surveys suggest that North Americans are concerned not only with politics and finances, but also with social issues.

questions.stimulus:
The following passage is used for Section 1, questions 16 through 17.
On the basis of the available evidence, Antarctica has generally been thought to have been covered by ice for at least the past 14 million years. Recently, however, three-million-year-old fossils of a kind previously found only in ocean-floor sediments were discovered under the ice sheet covering central Antarctica. About three million years ago, therefore, the Antarctic ice sheet must temporarily have melted. After all, either severe climatic warming or volcanic activity in Antarctica’s mountains could have melted the ice sheet, thus raising sea levels and submerging the continent.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is the main conclusion of the argument?

answerChoices.A: Antarctica is no longer generally thought to have been covered by ice for the past 14 million years.
answerChoices.B: It is not the case that ancient fossils of the kind recently found in Antarctica are found only in ocean-floor sediments.
answerChoices.C: The ice sheet covering Antarctica has not been continuously present throughout the past 14 million years.
answerChoices.D: What caused Antarctica to be submerged under the sea was the melting of the ice sheet that had previously covered the continent.
answerChoices.E: The ice sheet covering Antarctica was melted either as a result of volcanic activity in Antarctica’s mountains or as a result of severe climatic warming.

answerChoices.D: A claim that has a very general application is based entirely on evidence from a narrowly restricted range of cases.

questions.stimulus: The current pattern of human consumption of resources, in which we rely on nonrenewable resources, for example metal ore, must eventually change. Since there is only so much metal ore available, ultimately we must either do without or turn to renewable resources to take its place.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: There are renewable resource replacements for all of the nonrenewable resources currently being consumed.
answerChoices.B: We cannot indefinitely replace exhausted nonrenewable resources with other nonrenewable resources.
answerChoices.C: A renewable resource cannot be exhausted by human consumption.
answerChoices.D: Consumption of nonrenewable resources will not continue to increase in the near future.
answerChoices.E: Ultimately we cannot do without nonrenewable resources.

questions.stimulus:
Lathyrism, a debilitating neurological disorder caused by the consumption of the legume Lathyrus sativus,
is widespread among the domestic animals of some countries. Attempts to use rats to study lathyrism have generally failed. Rats that ingested Lathyrus sativus did not produce the symptoms associated with the disorder.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: The physiology of rats is radically different from that of domestic animals.
answerChoices.B: The rats did not consume as much Lathyrus sativus as did the domestic animals that contracted lathyrism.
answerChoices.C: Not all animal species are equally susceptible to lathyrism.
answerChoices.D: Most of the animals that can contract lathyrism are domestic.
