questions.stimulus: Columnist: Almost anyone can be an expert, for there are no official guidelines determining what an expert must know. Anybody who manages to convince some people of his or her qualifications in an area—whatever those may be—is an expert.
questions.questionStem: The columnist’s conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Almost anyone can convince some people of his or her qualifications in some area.
answerChoices.B: Some experts convince everyone of their qualifications in almost every area.
answerChoices.C: Convincing certain people that one is qualified in an area requires that one actually be qualified in that area.
answerChoices.D: Every expert has convinced some people of his or her qualifications in some area.
answerChoices.E: Some people manage to convince almost everyone of their qualifications in one or more areas.

questions.stimulus: A patient complained of feeling constantly fatigued. It was determined that the patient averaged only four to six hours of sleep per night, and this was determined to contribute to the patient’s condition. However, the patient was not advised to sleep more.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

answerChoices.A: The shorter one’s sleep time, the easier it is to awaken from sleeping.
answerChoices.B: The first two hours of sleep do the most to alleviate fatigue.
answerChoices.C: Some people require less sleep than the eight hours required by the average person.
answerChoices.D: Most people who suffer from nightmares experience them in the last hour of sleep before waking.
answerChoices.E: Worry about satisfying the need for sufficient sleep can make it more difficult to sleep.

questions.stimulus: No chordates are tracheophytes, and all members of Pteropsida are tracheophytes. So no members of Pteropsida belong to the family Hominidae.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: All members of the family Hominidae are tracheophytes.
answerChoices.B: All members of the family Hominidae are chordates.
answerChoices.C: All tracheophytes are members of Pteropsida.
answerChoices.D: No members of the family Hominidae are chordates.
answerChoices.E: No chordates are members of Pteropsida.

questions.stimulus: Some statisticians claim that the surest way to increase the overall correctness of the total set of one’s beliefs is: never change that set, except by rejecting a belief when given adequate evidence against it. However, if this were the only rule one followed, then whenever one were presented with any kind of evidence, one would have to either reject some of one’s beliefs or else leave one’s beliefs unchanged. But then, over time, one could only have fewer and fewer beliefs. Since we need many beliefs in order to survive, the statisticians’ claim must be mistaken.
questions.questionStem: The argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it

answerChoices.A: presumes, without providing any justification, that the surest way of increasing the overall correctness of the total set of one’s beliefs must not hinder one’s ability to survive
answerChoices.B: neglects the possibility that even while following the statisticians’ rule, one might also accept new beliefs when presented with some kinds of evidence
answerChoices.C: overlooks the possibility that some large sets of beliefs are more correct overall than are some small sets of beliefs
answerChoices.D: takes for granted that one should accept some beliefs related to survival even when given adequate evidence against them
answerChoices.E: takes for granted that the beliefs we need in order to have many beliefs must all be correct beliefs

questions.stimulus: In every case of political unrest in a certain country, the police have discovered that some unknown person or persons organized and fomented that unrest. Clearly, therefore, behind all the cases of political unrest in that country there has been a single mastermind who organized and fomented them all.
questions.questionStem: The flawed reasoning in the argument above most closely parallels that in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Every Chicago driver has a number on his or her license, so the number on some Chicago driver’s license is the exact average of the numbers on all Chicago drivers’ licenses.
answerChoices.B: Every telephone number in North America has an area code, so there must be at least as many area codes as telephone numbers in North America.
answerChoices.C: Every citizen of Edmonton has a social insurance number, so there must be one number that is the social insurance number for all citizens of Edmonton.
answerChoices.D: Every loss of a single hair is insignificant, so no one who has a full head of hair at twenty ever becomes bald.
answerChoices.E: Every moment in Vladimir’s life is followed by a later moment in Vladimir’s life, so Vladimir’s life will never end.

questions.stimulus: A company that produces men’s cologne had been advertising the product in general-circulation magazines for several years. Then one year the company decided to advertise its cologne exclusively in those sports magazines with a predominantly male readership. That year the company sold fewer bottles of cologne than it had in any of the three immediately preceding years.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, best helps to explain why the sale of the company’s cologne dropped that year?

answerChoices.A: Television advertising reaches more people than does magazine advertising, but the company never advertised its cologne on television because of the high cost.
answerChoices.B: The general-circulation magazines in which the company had placed its advertisements experienced a large rise in circulation recently.
answerChoices.C: Most men do not wear cologne on a regular basis.
answerChoices.D: Women often buy cologne as gifts for male friends or relatives.
answerChoices.E: Successful advertisements for men’s cologne often feature well-known athletes.

questions.stimulus:
Kim: The rapidly growing world population is increasing demands on food producers in ways that threaten our natural resources. With more land needed for both food production and urban areas, less land will be available for forests and wildlife habitats.
Hampton: You are overlooking the promise of technology. I am confident that improvements in agriculture will allow us to feed the world population of ten billion predicted for 2050 without significantly increasing the percentage of the world’s land now devoted to agriculture.
questions.questionStem: Kim’s and Hampton’s statements most strongly support the claim that both of them would agree with which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Efforts should be taken to slow the rate of human population growth and to increase the amount of land committed to agriculture.
answerChoices.B: Continued research into more-efficient agricultural practices and innovative biotechnology aimed at producing more food on less land would be beneficial.
answerChoices.C: Agricultural and wilderness areas need to be protected from urban encroachment by preparing urban areas for greater population density.
answerChoices.D: In the next half century, human population growth will continue to erode wildlife habitats and diminish forests.
answerChoices.E: The human diet needs to be modified in the next half century because of the depletion of our natural resources due to overpopulation.

questions.stimulus: More and more computer programs that provide solutions to mathematical problems in engineering are being produced, and it is thus increasingly unnecessary for practicing engineers to have a thorough understanding of fundamental mathematical principles. Consequently, in training engineers who will work in industry, less emphasis should be placed on mathematical principles, so that space in the engineering curriculum will be available for other important subjects.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument given for the recommendation above?

answerChoices.A: The effective use of computer programs that provide solutions to mathematical problems in engineering requires an understanding of mathematical principles.
answerChoices.B: Many of the computer programs that provide solutions to mathematical problems in engineering are already in routine use.
answerChoices.C: Development of composites and other such new materials has meant that the curriculum for engineers who will work in industry must allow time for teaching the properties of these materials.

questions.stimulus: Raymond Burr played the role of Perry Mason on television. Burr’s death in 1993 prompted a prominent lawyer to say, “Although not a lawyer, Mr. Burr strove for such authenticity that we feel as if we lost one of our own.” This comment from a prestigious attorney provides appalling evidence that, in the face of television, even some legal professionals are losing their ability to distinguish fiction from reality.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: takes the views of one lawyer to represent the views of all lawyers
answerChoices.B: criticizes the lawyer rather than the lawyer’s statement
answerChoices.C: presumes that the lawyer is qualified to evaluate the performance of an actor
answerChoices.D: focuses on a famous actor’s portrayal of a lawyer rather than on the usual way in which lawyers are portrayed on television

questions.stimulus: Opponents of peat harvesting in this country argue that it would alter the ecological balance of our peat-rich wetlands and that, as a direct consequence of this, much of the country’s water supply would be threatened with contamination. questions.stimulus: For the next year, the Chefs’ Union has requested a 10 percent salary increase for each of its members, whereas the Hotel Managers’ Union has requested only an 8 percent salary increase for each of its members. questions.stimulus: Parent: I had tried without success to get my young child to brush her teeth. I had hoped that she would imitate me, or that she would be persuaded by reason to brush her teeth. questions.stimulus: The student body at this university takes courses in a wide range of disciplines. Miriam is a student at this university, so she takes courses in a wide range of disciplines.

questions.stimulus: A running track with a hard surface makes for greater running speed than a soft one, at least under dry conditions, because even though step length is shorter on a hard surface, the time the runner’s foot remains in contact with the running surface is less with a hard surface.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, is evidence that the explanation given above is only a partial one?

answerChoices.A: Dry running conditions can be guaranteed for indoor track races only.
answerChoices.B: In general, taller runners have greater average step length than shorter runners do.
answerChoices.C: Hard tracks enhance a runner’s speed by making it easier for the runner to maintain a posture that minimizes wind resistance.
answerChoices.D: The tracks at which the world’s fastest running times have been recorded are located well above sea level, where the air is relatively thin.
answerChoices.E: To remain in top condition, a soft track surface requires different maintenance procedures than does a hard one.

questions.stimulus: Goswami: I support the striking workers at Ergon Foods. They are underpaid. The majority of them make less than $20,000 per year. Nordecki: If pay is the issue, I must disagree. The average annual salary of the striking workers at Ergon Foods is over $29,000.
questions.questionStem: Goswami and Nordecki disagree over the truth of which one of the following statements?

answerChoices.A: The average annual salary at Ergon Foods is over $29,000.
answerChoices.B: Pay is the primary issue over which the workers are striking at Ergon Foods.
answerChoices.C: It is reasonable to support striking workers who are underpaid.
answerChoices.D: The striking workers at Ergon Foods are underpaid.
answerChoices.E: It was unreasonable for the workers at Ergon Foods to go on strike.

questions.stimulus: Teacher to a student: You agree that it is bad to break promises. But when we speak to each other we all make an implicit promise to tell the truth, and lying is the breaking of that promise. So even if you promised Jeanne that you would tell me she is home sick, you should not tell me that, if you know that she is well.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the teacher’s argument depends?

answerChoices.A: Most people always tell the truth.
answerChoices.B: It is sometimes better to act in a friend’s best interests than to keep a promise to that friend.
answerChoices.C: Breaking a promise leads to worse consequences than does telling a lie.
answerChoices.D: Some implicit promises are worse to break than some explicit ones.
answerChoices.E: One should never break a promise.

questions.stimulus: Despite the fact that antilock brakes are designed to make driving safer, research suggests that people who drive cars equipped with antilock brakes have more accidents than those who drive cars not equipped with antilock brakes.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, would help resolve the apparent discrepancy described above except:

answerChoices.A: Most cars equipped with antilock brakes are, on average, driven more carelessly than cars not equipped with antilock brakes.
answerChoices.B: Antilock brakes malfunction more often than regular brakes.
answerChoices.C: Antilock brakes require expensive specialized maintenance to be even as effective as unmaintained regular brakes.
answerChoices.D: Most people who drive cars equipped with antilock brakes do not know how to use those brakes properly.
answerChoices.E: Antilock brakes were designed for safety in congested urban driving, but accidents of the most serious nature take place on highways.

questions.stimulus: President of the Regional Chamber of Commerce: We are all aware of the painful fact that almost no new businesses have moved into our region or started up here over the last ten years. But the Planning Board is obviously guilty of a gross exaggeration in its recent estimate that businesses are leaving the region at the rate of about four a week. After all, there were never more than about one thousand businesses in the region, so if they were really leaving at such a rate, they would all have been gone long ago.
questions.questionStem: The argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the ground that it

answerChoices.A: focuses on what is going out of a system while ignoring the issue of what is coming into the system
answerChoices.B: confuses a claim about a rate of change within a system with a claim about the absolute size of the system
answerChoices.C: argues against a position simply by showing that the position serves the interest of the Planning Board
answerChoices.D: treats a claim about what is currently the case as if it were a claim about what has been the case for an extended period
answerChoices.E: attacks what was offered as an estimate on the ground that it is not precise

questions.stimulus: It is inaccurate to say that a diet high in refined sugar cannot cause adult-onset diabetes, since a diet high in refined sugar can make a person overweight, and being overweight can predispose a person to adult-onset diabetes.
questions.questionStem: The argument is most parallel, in its logical structure, to which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: It is inaccurate to say that being in cold air can cause a person to catch a cold, since colds are caused by viruses, and viruses flourish in warm, crowded places.
answerChoices.B: It is accurate to say that no airline flies from Halifax to Washington. No airline offers a direct flight, although some airlines have flights from Halifax to Boston and others have flights from Boston to Washington.
answerChoices.C: It is correct to say that overfertilization is the primary cause of lawn disease, since fertilizer causes lawn grass to grow rapidly and rapidly growing grass has little resistance to disease.
answerChoices.D: It is incorrect to say that inferior motor oil cannot cause a car to get poorer gasoline mileage, since inferior motor oil can cause engine valve deterioration, and engine valve deterioration can lead to poorer gasoline mileage.
answerChoices.E: It is inaccurate to say that Alexander the Great was a student of Plato; Alexander was a student of Aristotle and Aristotle was a student of Plato.

questions.stimulus: During the recent economic downturn, banks contributed to the decline by loaning less money. Prior to the downturn, regulatory standards for loanmaking by banks were tightened. Clearly, therefore, banks will lend more money if those standards are relaxed.
questions.questionStem: The argument assumes that

answerChoices.A: the downturn did not cause a significant decrease in the total amount of money on deposit with banks which is the source of funds for banks to lend
answerChoices.B: the imposition of the tighter regulatory standards was not a cause of the economic downturn
answerChoices.C: the reason for tightening the regulatory standards was not arbitrary
answerChoices.D: no economic downturn is accompanied by a significant decrease in the amount of money loaned out by banks to individual borrowers and to businesses
answerChoices.E: no relaxation of standards for loanmaking by banks would compensate for the effects of the downturn

questions.stimulus: Zoos have served both as educational resources and as entertainment. Unfortunately, removing animals from their natural habitats to stock the earliest zoos reduced certain species’ populations, endangering their survival. Today most new zoo animals are obtained from captive breeding programs, and many zoos now maintain breeding stocks for continued propagation of various species. This makes possible efforts to reestablish endangered species in the wild.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Zoos have played an essential role in educating the public about endangered species.
answerChoices.B: Some specimens of endangered species are born and bred in zoos.
answerChoices.C: No zoos exploit wild animals or endanger the survival of species.
answerChoices.D: Nearly all of the animals in zoos today were born in captivity.
answerChoices.E: The main purpose of zoos has shifted from entertainment to education.

questions.stimulus: Only a very small percentage of people from the service professions ever become board members of the 600 largest North American corporations. This shows that people from the service professions are underrepresented in the most important corporate boardrooms in North America.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following points out a flaw committed in the argument?

answerChoices.A: Six hundred is too small a sample on which to base so sweeping a conclusion about the representation of people from the service professions.
answerChoices.B: The percentage of people from the service professions who serve on the boards of the 600 largest North American corporations reveals little about the percentage of the members of these boards who are from the service professions.
answerChoices.C: It is a mistake to take the 600 largest North American corporations to be typical of corporate boardrooms generally.
answerChoices.D: It is irrelevant to smaller corporations whether the largest corporations in North America would agree to have significant numbers of workers from the service professions on the boards of the largest corporations.
answerChoices.E: The presence of people from the service professions on a corporate board does not necessarily imply that that corporation will be more socially responsible than it has been in the past.

questions.stimulus: If there are any inspired performances in the concert, the audience will be treated to a good show. But there will not be a good show unless there are sophisticated listeners in the audience, and to be a sophisticated listener one must understand one’s musical roots.
questions.questionStem: If all of the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

answerChoices.A: If there are no sophisticated listeners in the audience, then there will be no inspired musical performances in the concert.
answerChoices.B: No people who understand their musical roots will be in the audience if the audience will not be treated to a good show.
answerChoices.C: If there will be people in the audience who understand their musical roots, then at least one musical performance in the concert will be inspired.
answerChoices.D: The audience will be treated to a good show unless there are people in the audience who do not understand their musical roots.
answerChoices.E: If there are sophisticated listeners in the audience, then there will be inspired musical performances in the concert.

questions.stimulus: Columnist: A recent study suggests that living with a parrot increases one’s risk of lung cancer. But no one thinks the government should impose financial impediments on the owning of parrots because of this apparent danger. So by the same token, the government should not levy analogous special taxes on hunting gear, snow skis, recreational parachutes, or motorcycles.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following principles is logically consistent with the columnist’s conclusion except:

answerChoices.A: The government should fund education by taxing nonessential sports equipment and recreational gear.
answerChoices.B: The government should not tax those who avoid dangerous activities and adopt healthy lifestyles.
answerChoices.C: The government should create financial disincentives to deter participation in activities it deems dangerous.
answerChoices.D: The government should not create financial disincentives for people to race cars or climb mountains, even though these are dangerous activities.
answerChoices.E: The government would be justified in levying taxes to provide food and shelter for those who cannot afford to pay for them.

questions.stimulus: Scientist: Some critics of public funding for this research project have maintained that only if it can be indicated how the public will benefit from the project is continued public funding for it justified. If the critics were right about this, then there would not be the tremendous public support for the project that even its critics acknowledge.
questions.questionStem: If the scientist’s claims are true, which one of the following must also be true?

answerChoices.A: The benefits derived from the research project are irrelevant to whether or not its funding is justified.
answerChoices.B: Continued public funding for the research project is justified.
answerChoices.C: Public support for the research project is the surest indication of whether or not it is justified.
answerChoices.D: There is tremendous public support for the research project because it can be indicated how the public will benefit from the project.
answerChoices.E: That a public benefit can be indicated is not a requirement for the justification of the research project’s continued public funding.

questions.stimulus: The new agriculture bill will almost surely fail to pass. The leaders of all major parties have stated that they oppose it.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, adds the most support for the prediction that the agriculture bill will fail to pass?

answerChoices.A: Most bills that have not been supported by even one leader of a major party have not been passed into law.
answerChoices.B: Most bills that have not been passed into law were not supported by even one member of a major party.
answerChoices.C: If the leaders of all major parties endorse the new agriculture bill, it will pass into law.
answerChoices.D: Most bills that have been passed into law were not unanimously supported by the leaders of all major parties.
answerChoices.E: Most bills that have been passed into law were supported by at least one leader of a major party.

questions.stimulus: The folktale that claims that a rattlesnake’s age can be determined from the number of sections in its rattle is false, but only because the rattles are brittle and sometimes partially or completely break off. So if they were not so brittle, one could reliably determine a rattlesnake’s age simply from the number of sections in its rattle, because one new section is formed each time a rattlesnake molts.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption the argument requires in order for its conclusion to be properly drawn?

answerChoices.A: Rattlesnakes molt exactly once a year.
answerChoices.B: The rattles of rattlesnakes of different species are identical in appearance.
answerChoices.C: Rattlesnakes molt more frequently when young than when old.
answerChoices.D: The brittleness of a rattlesnake’s rattle is not correlated with the length of the rattlesnake’s life.
answerChoices.E: Rattlesnakes molt as often when food is scarce as they do when food is plentiful.

questions.stimulus: The following passage is used for Section 3, questions 23 through 24. Tony: A new kind of videocassette has just been developed. It lasts for only half as many viewings as the old kind does but costs a third as much. Therefore, video rental stores would find it significantly more economical to purchase and stock movies recorded on the new kind of videocassette than on the old kind.Anna: But the videocassette itself only accounts for 5 percent of the price a video rental store pays to buy a copy of a movie on video; most of the price consists of royalties the store pays to the studio that produced the movie. So the price that video rental stores pay per copy would decrease by considerably less than 5 percent, and royalties would have to be paid on additional copies.
questions.questionStem: Anna’s reply is structured to lead to which one of the following conclusions?

answerChoices.A: The royalties paid to movie studios for movies sold on videotape are excessively large.
answerChoices.B: Video rental stores should always stock the highest-quality videocassettes available, because durability is more important than price.
answerChoices.C: The largest part of the fee a customer pays to rent a movie from a video rental store goes toward the royalties the store paid in purchasing that movie.
answerChoices.D: The cost savings to video rental stores that buy movies recorded on the cheaper videocassettes rather than movies recorded on the more durable ones will be small or nonexistent.
answerChoices.E: If the price a video rental store pays to buy a movie on videocassette does not decrease, the rental fee the store charges on the movie will not decrease.

questions.stimulus: The following passage is used for Section 3, questions 23 through 24. Tony: A new kind of videocassette has just been developed. It lasts for only half as many viewings as the old kind does but costs a third as much. Therefore, video rental stores would find it significantly more economical to purchase and stock movies recorded on the new kind of videocassette than on the old kind.Anna: But the videocassette itself only accounts for 5 percent of the price a video rental store pays to buy a copy of a movie on video; most of the price consists of royalties the store pays to the studio that produced the movie. So the price that video rental stores pay per copy would decrease by considerably less than 5 percent, and royalties would have to be paid on additional copies.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would contribute most to a defense of Tony’s position against Anna’s reply?

answerChoices.A: The price that video rental stores pay for movies recorded on videocassettes is considerably less than the retail price of those movies.
answerChoices.B: A significant proportion of the movies on videocassette purchased by video rental stores are bought as replacements for worn-out copies of movies the stores already have in stock.
answerChoices.C: The royalty fee included in the price that video rental stores pay for movies on the new kind of videocassette will be half that included in the price of movies on the old kind.
answerChoices.D: Given a choice, customers are more likely to buy a movie on videocassette than to rent it if the rental fee is more than half of the purchase price.
answerChoices.E: Many of the movies rented from video rental stores, particularly children’s movies, average several viewings per rental fee.

questions.stimulus: Physician: Heart disease generally affects men at an earlier age than it does women, who tend to experience heart disease after menopause. Both sexes have the hormones estrogen and testosterone, but when they are relatively young, men have ten times as much testosterone as women, and women abruptly lose estrogen after menopause. We can conclude, then, that testosterone tends to promote, and estrogen tends to inhibit, heart disease.
questions.questionStem: The physician’s argument is questionable because it presumes which one of the following without providing sufficient justification?

answerChoices.A: Hormones are the primary factors that account for the differences in age-related heart disease risks between women and men.
answerChoices.B: Estrogen and testosterone are the only hormones that promote or inhibit heart disease.
answerChoices.C: Men with high testosterone levels have a greater risk for heart disease than do postmenopausal women.
answerChoices.D: Because hormone levels are correlated with heart disease they influence heart disease.
answerChoices.E: Hormone levels do not vary from person to person, especially among those of the same age and gender.

questions.stimulus: People ought to take into account a discipline’s blemished origins when assessing the scientific value of that discipline. Take, for example, chemistry. It must be considered that many of its landmark results were obtained by alchemists—a group whose superstitions and appeals to magic dominated the early development of chemical theory.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning above is most susceptible to criticism because the author

answerChoices.A: fails to establish that disciplines with unblemished origins are scientifically valuable
answerChoices.B: fails to consider how chemistry’s current theories and practices differ from those of the alchemists mentioned
answerChoices.C: uses an example to contradict the principle under consideration
answerChoices.D: does not prove that most disciplines that are not scientifically valuable have origins that are in some way suspect
answerChoices.E: uses the word “discipline” in two different senses

questions.stimulus: The graphical illustrations mathematics teachers use enable students to learn geometry more easily by providing them with an intuitive understanding of geometric concepts, which makes it easier to acquire the ability to manipulate symbols for the purpose of calculation. Illustrating algebraic concepts graphically would be equally effective pedagogically, even though the deepest mathematical understanding is abstract, not imagistic.
questions.questionStem: The statements above provide some support for each of the following except:

answerChoices.A: Pictorial understanding is not the final stage of mathematical understanding.
answerChoices.B: People who are very good at manipulating symbols do not necessarily have any mathematical understanding.
answerChoices.C: Illustrating geometric concepts graphically is an effective teaching method.
answerChoices.D: Acquiring the ability to manipulate symbols is part of the process of learning geometry.
answerChoices.E: There are strategies that can be effectively employed in the teaching both of algebra and of geometry.

questions.stimulus: Bureaucratic mechanisms are engineered to resist change. Thus, despite growing dissatisfaction with complex bureaucratic systems, it is unlikely that bureaucracies will be simplified.
questions.questionStem: The claim that bureaucratic mechanisms are engineered to resist change plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It is a premise offered in support of the claim that it is unlikely that bureaucracies will be simplified.
answerChoices.B: It is a conclusion for which the only support offered is the claim that dissatisfaction with complex bureaucratic systems is growing.
answerChoices.C: It is cited as evidence that bureaucratic systems are becoming more and more complex.
answerChoices.D: It is used to weaken the claim that bureaucracies should be simplified.
answerChoices.E: It is a conclusion for which the claim that bureaucracies are unlikely to be simplified is offered as support.

questions.stimulus: In speech, when words or sentences are ambiguous, gesture and tone of voice are used to indicate the intended meaning. Writers, of course, cannot use gesture or tone of voice and must rely instead on style; the reader detects the writer’s intention from the arrangement of words and sentences.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: The primary function of style in writing is to augment the literal meanings of the words and sentences used.
answerChoices.B: The intended meaning of a piece of writing is indicated in part by the writer’s arrangement of words and sentences.
answerChoices.C: It is easier for a listener to detect the tone of a speaker than for a reader to detect the style of a writer.
answerChoices.D: A writer’s intention will always be interpreted differently by different readers.
answerChoices.E: The writer’s arrangement of words and sentences completely determines the aesthetic value of his or her writing.

questions.stimulus: Last year a large firm set a goal of decreasing its workforce by 25 percent. Three divisions, totaling 25 percent of its workforce at that time, were to be eliminated and no new people hired. These divisions have since been eliminated and no new people have joined the firm, but its workforce has decreased by only 15 percent.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, contributes most to an explanation of the difference in the planned versus the actual reduction in the workforce?

answerChoices.A: The three divisions that were eliminated were well run and had the potential to earn profits.
answerChoices.B: Normal attrition in the retained divisions continued to reduce staff because no new people were added to the firm.
answerChoices.C: Some of the employees in the eliminated divisions were eligible for early retirement and chose that option.
answerChoices.D: As the divisions were being eliminated some of their employees were assigned to other divisions.
answerChoices.E: Employees in the retained divisions were forced to work faster to offset the loss of the eliminated divisions.

questions.stimulus: One of the advantages of Bacillus thuringiensis (B.t.) toxins over chemical insecticides results from their specificity for pest insects. The toxins have no known detrimental effects on mammals or birds. In addition, the limited range of activity of the toxins toward insects means that often a particular toxin will kill pest species but not affect insects that prey upon the species. This advantage makes B.t. toxins preferable to chemical insecticides for use as components of insect pest management programs.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Chemical insecticides cause harm to a greater number of insect species than do B.t. toxins.
answerChoices.B: No particular B.t. toxin is effective against all insects.
answerChoices.C: B.t. toxins do not harm weeds that do damage to farm crops.
answerChoices.D: Insects build up resistance more readily to B.t. toxins than to chemical insecticides.
answerChoices.E: Birds and rodents often do greater damage to farm crops than do insects.

questions.stimulus: Many people are alarmed about the population explosion. They fail to appreciate that the present rise in population has in fact been followed by equally potent economic growth. Because of this connection between an increase in population and an increase in economic activity, population control measures should not be taken.
questions.questionStem: The questionable pattern of reasoning in the argument above is most similar to that in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Subscribers to newsmagazines are concerned that increased postage costs will be passed on to them in the form of higher subscription rates. But that is a price they have to pay for having the magazines delivered. No group of users of the postal system should be subsidized at the expense of others.
answerChoices.B: Most of the salespeople are concerned with complaints about the sales manager’s aggressive behavior. They need to consider that sales are currently increasing. Due to this success, no action should be taken to address the manager’s behavior.
answerChoices.C: Parents are concerned about their children spending too much time watching television. Those parents should consider television time as time they could spend with their children. Let the children watch television, but watch it with them.
answerChoices.D: Nutritionists warn people not to eat unhealthy foods. Those foods have been in people’s diets for years. Before cutting all those foods out of diets it would be wise to remember that people enjoy culinary variety.
answerChoices.E: Some consumers become concerned when the price of a product increases for several years in a row, thinking that the price will continue to increase. But these consumers are mistaken since a long-term trend of price increases indicates that the price will probably decline in the future.

questions.stimulus: Attorney: I ask you to find Mr. Smith guilty of assaulting Mr. Jackson. Regrettably, there were no eyewitnesses to the crime, but Mr. Smith has a violent character: Ms. Lopez testified earlier that Mr. Smith, shouting loudly, had threatened her. Smith never refuted this testimony.
questions.questionStem: The attorney’s argument is fallacious because it reasons that

answerChoices.A: aggressive behavior is not a sure indicator of a violent character
answerChoices.B: Smith’s testimony is unreliable since he is loud and aggressive
answerChoices.C: since Smith never disproved the claim that he threatened Lopez, he did in fact threaten her
answerChoices.D: Lopez’s testimony is reliable since she is neither loud nor aggressive
answerChoices.E: having a violent character is not necessarily associated with the commission of violent crimes

questions.stimulus: It is widely believed that by age 80, perception and memory are each significantly reduced from their functioning levels at age 30. However, a recent study showed no difference in the abilities of 80-year-olds and 30-year-olds to play a card game devised to test perception and memory. Therefore, the belief that perception and memory are significantly reduced by age 80 is false.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning above is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it fails to consider the possibility that

answerChoices.A: the study’s card game does not test cognitive abilities other than perception and memory
answerChoices.B: card games are among the most difficult cognitive tasks one can attempt to perform
answerChoices.C: perception and memory are interrelated in ways of which we are not currently aware
answerChoices.D: the belief that 80-year-olds’ perception and memory are reduced results from prejudice against senior citizens
answerChoices.E: playing the study’s card game perfectly requires fairly low levels of perception and memory

questions.stimulus: Moralist: Humans have a natural disposition to altruism—that is, to behavior that serves the needs of others regardless of one’s own needs— but that very disposition prevents some acts of altruism from counting as moral. Reason plays an essential role in any moral behavior. Only behavior that is intended to be in accordance with a formal set of rules, or moral code, can be considered moral behavior.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately states the main conclusion of the moralist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: All moral codes prohibit selfishness.
answerChoices.B: All moral behavior is motivated by altruism.
answerChoices.C: Behavior must serve the needs of others in order to be moral behavior.
answerChoices.D: Not all altruistic acts are moral behavior.
answerChoices.E: Altruism develops through the use of reason.

questions.stimulus: A recent study suggests that Alzheimer’s disease, which attacks the human brain, may be caused by a virus. In the study, blood from 11 volunteers, each of whom had the disease, was injected into rats. The rats eventually exhibited symptoms of another degenerative neurological disorder, Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, which is caused by a virus. This led the scientist who conducted the study to conclude that Alzheimer’s disease might be caused by a virus.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, would most strengthen the scientist’s hypothesis that Alzheimer’s disease is caused by a virus?

answerChoices.A: Alzheimer’s disease in rats is not caused by a virus.
answerChoices.B: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease affects only motor nerves in rats’ limbs, not their brains.
answerChoices.C: The virus that causes Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in rats has no effect on humans.
answerChoices.D: The symptoms known, respectively, as Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease and Alzheimer’s disease are different manifestations of the same disease.
answerChoices.E: Blood from rats with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease produced no symptoms of the disease when injected into other experimental rats.

questions.stimulus: One approach to the question of which objects discussed by a science are real is to designate as real all and only those entities posited by the most explanatorily powerful theory of the science. But since most scientific theories contain entities posited solely on theoretical grounds, this approach is flawed.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: Any object that is posited by a scientific theory and that enhances the explanatory power of that theory should be designated as real.
answerChoices.B: Objects posited for theoretical reasons only should never be designated as real.
answerChoices.C: A scientific theory should not posit any entity that does not enhance the explanatory power of the theory.
answerChoices.D: A scientific theory should sometimes posit entities on grounds other than theoretical ones.
answerChoices.E: Only objects posited by explanatorily powerful theories should be designated as real.

questions.stimulus: Most doctors recommend that pregnant women eat a nutritious diet to promote the health of their babies. However, most babies who are born to women who ate nutritious diets while pregnant still develop at least one medical problem in their first year.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, does most to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

answerChoices.A: Women who regularly eat a nutritious diet while pregnant tend to eat a nutritious diet while breast-feeding.
answerChoices.B: Most of the babies born to women who did not eat nutritious diets while pregnant develop no serious medical problems later in childhood.
answerChoices.C: Babies of women who did not eat nutritious diets while pregnant tend to have more medical problems in their first year than do other babies.
answerChoices.D: Medical problems that develop in the first year of life tend to be more serious than those that develop later in childhood.
answerChoices.E: Many of the physicians who initially recommended that pregnant women consume nutritious diets have only recently reaffirmed their recommendation.

questions.stimulus: Mayor: The law prohibiting pedestrians from crossing against red lights serves no useful purpose. After all, in order to serve a useful purpose, a law must deter the kind of behavior it prohibits. But pedestrians who invariably violate this law are clearly not dissuaded by it; and those who comply with the law do not need it, since they would never cross against red lights even if there were no law prohibiting pedestrians from crossing against red lights.
questions.questionStem: The mayor’s argument is flawed because it

answerChoices.A: takes for granted that most automobile drivers will obey the law that prohibits them from driving through red lights
answerChoices.B: uses the word “law” in one sense in the premises and in another sense in the conclusion
answerChoices.C: ignores the possibility that a law might not serve a useful purpose even if it does deter the kind of behavior it prohibits
answerChoices.D: fails to consider whether the law ever dissuades people who sometimes but not always cross against red lights
answerChoices.E: provides no evidence that crossing against red lights is more dangerous than crossing on green lights

questions.stimulus: Marian Anderson, the famous contralto, did not take success for granted. We know this because Anderson had to struggle early in life, and anyone who has to struggle early in life is able to keep a good perspective on the world.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion of the argument follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Anyone who succeeds takes success for granted.
answerChoices.B: Anyone who is able to keep a good perspective on the world does not take success for granted.
answerChoices.C: Anyone who is able to keep a good perspective on the world has to struggle early in life.
answerChoices.D: Anyone who does not take success for granted has to struggle early in life.
answerChoices.E: Anyone who does not take success for granted is able to keep a good perspective on the world.

questions.stimulus: Geneticist: Ethicists have fears, many of them reasonable, about the prospect of cloning human beings, that is, producing exact genetic duplicates. But the horror-movie image of a wealthy person creating an army of exact duplicates is completely unrealistic. Clones must be raised and educated, a long-term process that could never produce adults identical to the original in terms of outlook, personality, or goals. More realistic is the possibility that wealthy individuals might use clones as living “organ banks.”
questions.questionStem: The claim that cloning will not produce adults with identical personalities plays which one of the following roles in the geneticist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: It is a reason for dismissing the various fears raised by ethicists regarding the cloning of human beings.
answerChoices.B: It is evidence that genetic clones will never be produced successfully.
answerChoices.C: It illustrates the claim that only wealthy people would be able to have genetic duplicates made of themselves.
answerChoices.D: It is evidence for the claim that wealthy people might use genetic duplicates of themselves as sources of compatible organs for transplantation.
answerChoices.E: It is a reason for discounting one possible fear concerning the cloning of human beings.

questions.stimulus: Publicity campaigns for endangered species are unlikely to have much impact on the most important environmental problems, for while the ease of attributing feelings to large mammals facilitates evoking sympathy for them, it is more difficult to elicit sympathy for other kinds of organisms, such as the soil microorganisms on which large ecosystems and agriculture depend.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: The most important environmental problems involve endangered species other than large mammals.
answerChoices.B: Microorganisms cannot experience pain or have other feelings.
answerChoices.C: Publicity campaigns for the environment are the most effective when they elicit sympathy for some organism.
answerChoices.D: People ignore environmental problems unless they believe the problems will affect creatures with which they sympathize.
answerChoices.E: An organism can be environmentally significant only if it affects large ecosystems or agriculture.

questions.stimulus: Politician: All nations that place a high tax on income produce thereby a negative incentive for technological innovation, and all nations in which technological innovation is hampered inevitably fall behind in the international arms race. Those nations that, through historical accident or the foolishness of their political leadership, wind up in a strategically disadvantageous position are destined to lose their voice in world affairs. So if a nation wants to maintain its value system and way of life, it must not allow its highest tax bracket to exceed 30 percent of income.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, weakens the politician’s argument except:

answerChoices.A: The top level of taxation must reach 45 percent before taxation begins to deter inventors and industrialists from introducing new technologies and industries.
answerChoices.B: Making a great deal of money is an insignificant factor in driving technological innovation.
answerChoices.C: Falling behind in the international arms race does not necessarily lead to a strategically less advantageous position.
answerChoices.D: Those nations that lose influence in the world community do not necessarily suffer from a threat to their value system or way of life.
answerChoices.E: Allowing one’s country to lose its technological edge, especially as concerns weaponry, would be foolish rather than merely a historical accident.

questions.stimulus: Philosopher: Scientists talk about the pursuit of truth, but, like most people, they are self-interested. Accordingly, the professional activities of most scientists are directed toward personal career enhancement, and only incidentally toward the pursuit of truth. Hence, the activities of the scientific community are largely directed toward enhancing the status of that community as a whole, and only incidentally toward the pursuit of truth.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the philosopher’s argument is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: improperly infers that each and every scientist has a certain characteristic from the premise that most scientists have that characteristic
answerChoices.B: improperly draws an inference about the scientific community as a whole from a premise about individual scientists
answerChoices.C: presumes, without giving justification, that the aim of personal career enhancement never advances the pursuit of truth
answerChoices.D: illicitly takes advantage of an ambiguity in the meaning of “self-interested”
answerChoices.E: improperly draws an inference about a cause from premises about its effects

questions.stimulus: Several critics have claimed that any contemporary poet who writes formal poetry—poetry that is rhymed and metered—is performing a politically conservative act. This is plainly false. Consider Molly Peacock and Marilyn Hacker, two contemporary poets whose poetry is almost exclusively formal and yet who are themselves politically progressive feminists.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion drawn above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: No one who is a feminist is also politically conservative.
answerChoices.B: No poet who writes unrhymed or unmetered poetry is politically conservative.
answerChoices.C: No one who is politically progressive is capable of performing a politically conservative act.
answerChoices.D: Anyone who sometimes writes poetry that is not politically conservative never writes poetry that is politically conservative.
answerChoices.E: The content of a poet’s work, not the work’s form, is the most decisive factor in determining what political consequences, if any, the work will have.

questions.stimulus: Archaeologist: A skeleton of a North American mastodon that became extinct at the peak of the Ice Age was recently discovered. It contains a human-made projectile dissimilar to any found in that part of Eurasia closest to North America. Thus, since Eurasians did not settle in North America until shortly before the peak of the Ice Age, the first Eurasian settlers in North America probably came from a more distant part of Eurasia.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the archaeologist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The projectile found in the mastodon does not resemble any that were used in Eurasia before or during the Ice Age.
answerChoices.B: The people who occupied the Eurasian area closest to North America remained nomadic throughout the Ice Age.
answerChoices.C: The skeleton of a bear from the same place and time as the mastodon skeleton contains a similar projectile.
answerChoices.D: Other North American artifacts from the peak of the Ice Age are similar to ones from the same time found in more distant parts of Eurasia.
answerChoices.E: Climatic conditions in North America just before the Ice Age were more conducive to human habitation than were those in the part of Eurasia closest to North America at that time.

questions.stimulus: All social systems are based upon a division of economic roles. The values of a social system are embodied in the prestige accorded persons who fill various economic roles. It is therefore unsurprising that, for any social system, the introduction of labor-saving technology that makes certain economic roles obsolete will tend to undermine the values in that social system.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following can most reasonably be concluded on the basis of the information above?

answerChoices.A: Social systems will have unchanging values if they are shielded from technological advancement.
answerChoices.B: No type of technology will fail to undermine the values in a social system.
answerChoices.C: A social system whose values are not susceptible to change would not be one in which technology can eliminate economic roles.
answerChoices.D: A technologically advanced society will place little value on the prestige associated with an economic role.
answerChoices.E: A technological innovation that is implemented in a social system foreign to the one in which it was developed will tend to undermine the foreign social system.

questions.stimulus: Multiple sclerosis is an autoimmune disease: white blood cells attack the myelin sheath that protects nerve fibers in the spinal cord and brain. Medical science now has a drug that can be used to successfully treat multiple sclerosis, but the path that led medical researchers to this drug was hardly straightforward. Initially, some scientists believed attacks characteristic of multiple sclerosis might be triggered by chronic viral infections. So in 1984 they began testing gamma interferon, one of the body’s own antiviral weapons. To their horror, all the multiple sclerosis patients tested became dramatically worse. The false step proved to be instructive however.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is least compatible with the results of the gamma interferon experiment?

answerChoices.A: Gamma interferon stops white blood cells from producing myelin-destroying compounds.
answerChoices.B: Administering gamma interferon to those without multiple sclerosis causes an increase in the number of white blood cells.
answerChoices.C: Medical researchers have discovered that the gamma interferon level in the cerebrospinal fluid skyrockets just before and during multiple sclerosis attacks.
answerChoices.D: It has now been established that most multiple sclerosis sufferers do not have chronic viral infections.
answerChoices.E: The drug now used to treat multiple sclerosis is known to inhibit the activity of gamma interferon.

questions.stimulus: The higher the altitude, the thinner the air. Since Mexico City’s altitude is higher than that of Panama City, the air must be thinner in Mexico City than in Panama City.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

answerChoices.A: As one gets older one gets wiser. Since Henrietta is older than her daughter, Henrietta must be wiser than her daughter.
answerChoices.B: The more egg whites used and the longer they are beaten, the fluffier the meringue. Since Lydia used more egg whites in her meringue than Joseph used in his, Lydia’s meringue must be fluffier than Joseph’s.
answerChoices.C: The people who run the fastest marathons these days are faster than the people who ran the fastest marathons ten years ago. Charles is a marathon runner. So Charles must run faster marathons these days than he did ten years ago.
answerChoices.D: The older a tree, the more rings it has. The tree in Lou’s yard is older than the tree in Theresa’s yard. Therefore, the tree in Lou’s yard must have more rings than does the tree in Theresa’s yard.
answerChoices.E: The bigger the vocabulary a language has, the harder it is to learn. English is harder to learn than Italian. Therefore, English must have a bigger vocabulary than Italian.

questions.stimulus: A recent study of 6,403 people showed that those treated with the drug pravastatin, one of the effects of which is to reduce cholesterol, had about one-third fewer nonfatal heart attacks and one-third fewer deaths from coronary disease than did those not taking the drug. This result is consistent with other studies, which show that those who have heart disease often have higher than average cholesterol levels. This shows that lowering cholesterol levels reduces the risk of heart disease.
questions.questionStem: The argument’s reasoning is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: neglects the possibility that pravastatin may have severe side effects
answerChoices.B: fails to consider that pravastatin may reduce the risk of heart disease but not as a consequence of its lowering cholesterol levels
answerChoices.C: relies on past findings, rather than drawing its principal conclusion from the data found in the specific study cited
answerChoices.D: draws a conclusion regarding the effects of lowering cholesterol levels on heart disease, when in fact the conclusion should focus on the relation between pravastatin and cholesterol levels
answerChoices.E: fails to consider what percentage of the general population might be taking pravastatin

questions.stimulus: Zachary: The term “fresco” refers to paint that has been applied to wet plaster. Once dried, a fresco indelibly preserves the paint that a painter has applied in this way. Unfortunately, additions known to have been made by later painters have obscured the original fresco work done by Michelangelo in the Sistine Chapel. Therefore, in order to restore Michelangelo’s Sistine Chapel paintings to the appearance that Michelangelo intended them to have, everything except the original fresco work must be stripped away. Stephen: But it was extremely common for painters of Michelangelo’s era to add painted details to their own fresco work after the frescos had dried.
questions.questionStem: Stephen’s response to Zachary proceeds by

answerChoices.A: calling into question an assumption on which Zachary’s conclusion depends
answerChoices.B: challenging the definition of a key term in Zachary’s argument
answerChoices.C: drawing a conclusion other than the one that Zachary reaches
answerChoices.D: denying the truth of one of the stated premises of Zachary’s argument
answerChoices.E: demonstrating that Zachary’s conclusion is not consistent with the premises he uses to support it

questions.stimulus: Zachary: The term “fresco” refers to paint that has been applied to wet plaster. Once dried, a fresco indelibly preserves the paint that a painter has applied in this way. Unfortunately, additions known to have been made by later painters have obscured the original fresco work done by Michelangelo in the Sistine Chapel. Therefore, in order to restore Michaelangelo’s Sistine Chapel paintings to the appearance that Michelangelo intended them to have, everything except the original fresco work must be stripped away.Stephen: But it was extremely common for painters of Michelangelo’s era to add painted details to their own fresco work after the frescos had dried.
questions.questionStem: Stephen’s response to Zachary, if true, most strongly supports which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: It is impossible to distinguish the later painted additions made to Michelangelo’s Sistine Chapel paintings from the original fresco work.
answerChoices.B: Stripping away everything except Michelangelo’s original fresco work from the Sistine Chapel paintings would be unlikely to restore them to the appearance Michelangelo intended them to have.
answerChoices.C: The painted details that painters of Michelangelo’s era added to their own fresco work were not an integral part of the completed paintings’ overall design.
answerChoices.D: None of the painters of Michelangelo’s era who made additions to the Sistine Chapel paintings was an important artist in his or her own right.
answerChoices.E: Michelangelo was rarely satisfied with the appearance of his finished works.

questions.stimulus:
Joanna: The only way for a company to be successful, after emerging from bankruptcy, is to produce the same goods or services that it did before going bankrupt. It is futile for such a company to try to learn a whole new business.
Ruth: Wrong. The Kelton Company was a major mining operation that went into bankruptcy. On emerging from bankruptcy, Kelton turned its mines into landfills and is presently a highly successful waste-management concern.
questions.questionStem: Ruth uses which one of the following argumentative techniques in countering Joanna's argument?

answerChoices.A: She presents a counterexample to a claim.
answerChoices.B: She offers an alternative explanation for a phenomenon.
answerChoices.C: She supports a claim by offering a developed and relevant analogy.
answerChoices.D: She undermines a claim by showing that it rests on an ambiguity.
answerChoices.E: She establishes a conclusion by excluding the only plausible alternative to that conclusion.

questions.stimulus: Nutritionist: Recently a craze has developed for home juicers, $300 machines that separate the pulp of fruits and vegetables from the juice they contain. Outrageous claims are being made about the benefits of these devices: drinking the juice they produce is said to help one lose weight or acquire a clear complexion, to aid digestion, and even to prevent cancer. But there is no indication that juice separated from the pulp of the fruit or vegetable has any properties that it does not have when unseparated. Save your money. If you want carrot juice, eat a carrot.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most calls into question the nutritionist's argument?

answerChoices.A: Most people find it much easier to consume a given quantity of nutrients in liquid form than to eat solid foods containing the same quantity of the same nutrients.
answerChoices.B: Drinking juice from home juicers is less healthy than is eating fruits and vegetables because such juice does not contain the fiber that is eaten if one consumes the entire fruit or vegetable.
answerChoices.C: To most people who would be tempted to buy a home juicer, $300 would not be a major expense.
answerChoices.D: The nutritionist was a member of a panel that extensively evaluated early prototypes of home juicers.
answerChoices.E: Vitamin pills that supposedly contain nutrients available elsewhere only in fruits and vegetables often contain a form of those compounds that cannot be as easily metabolized as the varieties found in fruits and vegetables.

questions.stimulus: Finnish author Jaakko Mikkeli was accused by Norwegian author Kirsten Halden of plagiarizing a book that she had written and that had been published 20 years before Mikkeli's. The two books, although set in different periods and regions, contain enough plot similarities to make coincidental resemblance unlikely. Mikkeli's defense rests on his argument that plagiarism was impossible in this case because Halden's book has been published only in Norwegian, a language Mikkeli does not understand, and because no reviews of Halden's book have ever been published.
questions.questionStem: The argument in Mikkeli's defense depends on the assumption that

answerChoices.A: Mikkeli has never met Halden
answerChoices.B: Halden's book did not become popular in Norway
answerChoices.C: nobody related the plot of Halden's book in detail to Mikkeli before Mikkeli wrote his book
answerChoices.D: there is a common European myth to which both authors referred subconsciously in the books in question
answerChoices.E: Mikkeli is not familiar with Old Icelandic, an extinct language related to an earlier form of Norwegian

questions.stimulus: Most antidepressant drugs cause weight gain. While dieting can help reduce the amount of weight gained while taking such antidepressants, some weight gain is unlikely to be preventable.
questions.questionStem: The information above most strongly supports which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: A physician should not prescribe any antidepressant drug for a patient if that patient is overweight.
answerChoices.B: People who are trying to lose weight should not ask their doctors for an antidepressant drug.
answerChoices.C: At least some patients taking antidepressant drugs gain weight as a result of taking them.
answerChoices.D: The weight gain experienced by patients taking antidepressant drugs should be attributed to lack of dieting.
answerChoices.E: All patients taking antidepressant drugs should diet to maintain their weight.

questions.stimulus: Company policy: An employee of our company must be impartial, particularly when dealing with family members. This obligation extends to all aspects of the job, including hiring and firing practices and the quality of service the employee provides customers.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following employee behaviors most clearly violates the company policy cited above?

answerChoices.A: refusing to hire any of one's five siblings, even though they are each more qualified than any other applicant
answerChoices.B: receiving over a hundred complaints about the service one's office provides and sending a complimentary product to all those who complain, including one's mother
answerChoices.C: never firing a family member, even though three of one's siblings work under one's supervision and authority
answerChoices.D: repeatedly refusing to advance an employee, claiming that he has sometimes skipped work and that his work has been sloppy, even though no such instances have occurred for over two years
answerChoices.E: promoting a family member over another employee in the company

questions.stimulus: It is widely believed that eating chocolate can cause acne. Indeed, many people who are susceptible to acne report that, in their own experience, eating large amounts of chocolate is invariably followed by an outbreak of that skin condition. However, it is likely that common wisdom has mistaken an effect for a cause. Several recent scientific studies indicate that hormonal changes associated with stress can cause acne and there is good evidence that people who are fond of chocolate tend to eat more chocolate when they are under stress.
questions.questionStem: Of the following, which one most accurately expresses the main point of the argument?

answerChoices.A: People are mistaken who insist that whenever they eat large amounts of chocolate they invariably suffer from an outbreak of acne.
answerChoices.B: The more chocolate a person eats, the more likely that person is to experience the hormonal changes associated with stress.
answerChoices.C: Eating large amounts of chocolate is more likely to cause stress than it is to cause outbreaks of acne.
answerChoices.D: It is less likely that eating large amounts of chocolate causes acne than that both the chocolate eating and the acne are caused by stress.
answerChoices.E: The more stress a person experiences, the more likely that person is to crave chocolate.

questions.stimulus: It is widely believed that eating chocolate can cause acne. Indeed, many people who are susceptible to acne report that, in their own experience, eating large amounts of chocolate is invariably followed by an outbreak of that skin condition. However, it is likely that common wisdom has mistaken an effect for a cause. Several recent scientific studies indicate that hormonal changes associated with stress can cause acne and there is good evidence that people who are fond of chocolate tend to eat more chocolate when they are under stress.
questions.questionStem: The argument employs which one of the following argumentative strategies?

answerChoices.A: It cites counterevidence that calls into question the accuracy of the evidence advanced in support of the position being challenged.
answerChoices.B: It provides additional evidence that points to an alternative interpretation of the evidence offered in support of the position being challenged.
answerChoices.C: It invokes the superior authority of science over common opinion in order to dismiss out of hand the relevance of evidence based on everyday experience.
answerChoices.D: It demonstrates that the position being challenged is inconsistent with certain well-established facts.
answerChoices.E: It provides counterexamples to show that, contrary to the assumption on which the commonly held position rests, causes do not always precede their effects.

questions.stimulus: It has been claimed that television networks should provide equal time for the presentation of opposing views whenever a television program concerns scientific issues—such as those raised by the claims of environmentalists about which people disagree. However, although an obligation to provide equal time does arise in the case of any program concerning social issues, it does so because social issues almost always have important political implications and seldom can definitely be settled on the basis of available evidence. If a program concerns scientific issues, that program gives rise to no such equal time obligation.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: No scientific issues raised by the claims of environmentalists have important political implications.
answerChoices.B: There are often more than two opposing views on an issue that cannot be definitely settled on the basis of available evidence.
answerChoices.C: Some social issues could be definitely settled on the basis of evidence if the opposing sides would give all the available evidence a fair hearing.
answerChoices.D: Many scientific issues have important political implications and cannot be definitely settled on the basis of the available evidence.
answerChoices.E: Some television networks refuse to broadcast programs on issues that have important political implications and that cannot be definitely settled by the available evidence.

questions.stimulus: Raisins are made by drying grapes in the sun. Although some of the sugar in the grapes is caramelized in the process, nothing is added. Moreover, the only thing removed from the grapes is the water that evaporates during the drying, and water contains no calories or nutrients. The fact that raisins contain more iron per calorie than grapes do is thus puzzling.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain why raisins contain more iron per calorie than do grapes?

answerChoices.A: Since grapes are bigger than raisins, it takes several bunches of grapes to provide the same amount of iron as a handful of raisins does.
answerChoices.B: Caramelized sugar cannot be digested, so its calories do not count toward the calorie content of raisins.
answerChoices.C: The body can absorb iron and other nutrients more quickly from grapes than from raisins because of the relatively high water content of grapes.
answerChoices.D: Raisins, but not grapes, are available year-round, so many people get a greater share of their yearly iron intake from raisins than from grapes.
answerChoices.E: Raisins are often eaten in combination with other iron-containing foods, while grapes are usually eaten by themselves.

questions.stimulus: Cotrell is, at best, able to write magazine articles of average quality. The most compelling pieces of evidence for this are those few of the numerous articles submitted by Cotrell that are superior, since Cotrell, who is incapable of writing an article that is better than average, must obviously have plagiarized superior ones.
questions.questionStem: The argument is most vulnerable to criticism on which one of the following grounds?

answerChoices.A: It simply ignores the existence of potential counterevidence.
answerChoices.B: It generalizes from atypical occurrences.
answerChoices.C: It presupposes what it seeks to establish.
answerChoices.D: It relies on the judgment of experts in a matter to which their expertise is irrelevant.
answerChoices.E: It infers limits on ability from a few isolated lapses in performance.

questions.stimulus: Any sale item that is purchased can be returned for store credit but not for a refund of the purchase price. Every home appliance and every piece of gardening equipment is on sale along with selected construction tools.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

answerChoices.A: Any item that is not a home appliance or a piece of gardening equipment is returnable for a refund.
answerChoices.B: Any item that is not on sale cannot be returned for store credit.
answerChoices.C: Some construction tools are not returnable for store credit.
answerChoices.D: No piece of gardening equipment is returnable for a refund.
answerChoices.E: None of the things that are returnable for a refund are construction tools.

questions.stimulus: The consumer price index is a measure that detects monthly changes in the retail prices of goods and services. The payment of some government retirement benefits is based on the consumer price index so that those benefits reflect the change in the cost of living as the index changes. However, the consumer price index does not consider technological innovations that may drastically reduce the cost of producing some goods. Therefore, the value of government benefits is sometimes greater than is warranted by the true change in costs.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is most vulnerable to the criticism that the argument

answerChoices.A: fails to consider the possibility that there are years in which there is no change in the consumer price index
answerChoices.B: fails to make explicit which goods and services are included in the consumer price index
answerChoices.C: presumes, without providing warrant, that retirement benefits are not generally used to purchase unusual goods
answerChoices.D: uncritically draws an inference from what has been true in the past to what will be true in the future
answerChoices.E: makes an irrelevant shift from discussing retail prices to discussing production costs

questions.stimulus: When astronomers observed the comet Schwassman-Wachmann 3 becoming 1,000 times brighter in September 1995, they correctly hypothesized that its increased brightness was a result of the comet's breaking up—when comets break up, they emit large amounts of gas and dust, becoming visibly brighter as a result. However, their observations did not reveal comet Schwassman-Wachmann 3 actually breaking into pieces until November 1995, even though telescopes were trained on it throughout the entire period.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent conflict in the statements above?

answerChoices.A: Comets often do not emit gas and dust until several weeks after they have begun to break up.
answerChoices.B: The reason comets become brighter when they break up is that the gas and dust that they emit refract light.
answerChoices.C: Gas and dust can be released by cracks in a comet even if the comet is not broken all the way through.
answerChoices.D: The amount of gas and dust emitted steadily increased during the period from September through November.
answerChoices.E: The comet passed close to the sun during this period and the gravitational strain caused it to break up.

questions.stimulus: If Slater wins the election, McGuinness will be appointed head of the planning commission. But Yerxes is more qualified to head it since she is an architect who has been on the planning commission for fifteen years. Unless the polls are grossly inaccurate, Slater will win.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the information above?

answerChoices.A: If the polls are grossly inaccurate, someone more qualified than McGuinness will be appointed head of the planning commission.
answerChoices.B: McGuinness will be appointed head of the planning commission only if the polls are a good indication of how the election will turn out.
answerChoices.C: Either Slater will win the election or Yerxes will be appointed head of the planning commission.
answerChoices.D: McGuinness is not an architect and has not been on the planning commission for fifteen years or more.
answerChoices.E: If the polls are a good indication of how the election will turn out, someone less qualified than Yerxes will be appointed head of the planning commission.

questions.stimulus: In one study, engineering students who prepared for an exam by using toothpicks and string did no worse than similar students who prepared by using an expensive computer with sophisticated graphics. In another study, military personnel who trained on a costly high-tech simulator performed no better on a practical exam than did similar personnel who trained using an inexpensive cardboard model. So one should not always purchase technologically advanced educational tools.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: One should use different educational tools to teach engineering to civilians than are used to train military personnel.
answerChoices.B: High-tech solutions to modern problems are ineffective unless implemented by knowledgeable personnel.
answerChoices.C: Spending large sums of money on educational tools is at least as justified for nonmilitary training as it is for military training.
answerChoices.D: One should not invest in expensive teaching aids unless there are no other tools that are less expensive and at least as effective.
answerChoices.E: One should always provide students with a variety of educational materials so that each student can find the materials that best suit that student's learning style.
