questions.stimulus: A number of measures indicate the viability of a nation's economy. The level and rate of growth of aggregate output are the most significant indicators, but unemployment and inflation rates are also important. Further, Switzerland, Austria, Israel, Ireland, Denmark, and Finland all have viable economies, but none has a very large population. Switzerland and Austria each have populations of about seven million; the other populations are at least one-fourth smaller.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: A nation's economic viability is independent of the size of its population.
answerChoices.B: Having a population larger than seven million ensures that a nation will be economically viable.
answerChoices.C: Economic viability does not require a population of at least seven million.
answerChoices.D: A nation's population is the most significant contributor to the level and rate of growth of aggregate output.
answerChoices.E: A nation's population affects the level and rate of growth of aggregate output more than it affects unemployment and inflation rates.

questions.stimulus: The best way to write a good detective story is to work backward from the crime. The writer should first decide what the crime is and who the perpetrator is, and then come up with the circumstances and clues based on those decisions.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following illustrates a principle most similar to that illustrated by the passage?

answerChoices.A: When planning a trip, some people first decide where they want to go and then plan accordingly, but, for most of us, much financial planning must be done before we can choose where we are going.
answerChoices.B: In planting a vegetable garden, you should prepare the soil first, and then decide what kinds of vegetables to plant.
answerChoices.C: Good architects do not extemporaneously construct their plans in the course of an afternoon; an architectural design cannot be divorced from the method of constructing the building.
answerChoices.D: In solving mathematical problems, the best method is to try out as many strategies as possible in the time allotted. This is particularly effective if the number of possible strategies is fairly small.
answerChoices.E: To make a great tennis shot, you should visualize where you want the shot to go. Then you can determine the position you need to be in to execute the shot properly.

questions.stimulus: Moderate exercise lowers the risk of blockage of the arteries due to blood clots, since anything that lowers blood cholesterol levels also lowers the risk of hardening of the arteries, which in turn lowers the risk of arterial blockage due to blood clots; and, if the data reported in a recent study are correct, moderate exercise lowers blood cholesterol levels.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion drawn above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: The recent study investigated the relationship between exercise and blood cholesterol levels.
answerChoices.B: Blockage of the arteries due to blood clots can be prevented.
answerChoices.C: Lowering blood cholesterol levels lowers the risk of blockage of the arteries.
answerChoices.D: The data reported in the recent study are correct.
answerChoices.E: Hardening of the arteries increases the risk of blockage of the arteries due to blood clots.

questions.stimulus: Although it has been suggested that Arton's plays have a strong patriotic flavor, we must recall that, at the time of their composition, her country was in anything but a patriotic mood. Unemployment was high, food was costly, and crime rates were soaring. As a result, the general morale of her nation was at an especially low point. Realizing this, we see clearly that any apparent patriotism in Arton's work must have been intended ironically.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning above is questionable because it

answerChoices.A: posits an unstated relationship between unemployment and crime
answerChoices.B: takes for granted that straightforward patriotism is not possible for a serious writer
answerChoices.C: takes for granted that Arton was attuned to the predominant national attitude of her time
answerChoices.D: overlooks the fact that some citizens prosper in times of high unemployment
answerChoices.E: confuses irony with a general decline in public morale

questions.stimulus: Editorialist: To ensure justice in the legal system, citizens must be capable of criticizing anyone involved in determining the punishment of criminals. But when the legal system's purpose is seen as deterrence, the system falls into the hands of experts whose specialty is to assess how potential lawbreakers are affected by the system's punishments. Because most citizens lack knowledge about such matters, justice is not then ensured in the legal system.
questions.questionStem: The editorialist's argument requires assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Most citizens view justice as primarily concerned with the assignment of punishment to those who deserve it.
answerChoices.B: In order to be just, a legal system must consider the effect that punishment will have on individual criminals.
answerChoices.C: The primary concern in a legal system is to administer punishments that are just.
answerChoices.D: In a legal system, a concern for punishment is incompatible with an emphasis on deterrence.
answerChoices.E: Citizens without knowledge about how the legal system's punishments affect potential lawbreakers are incapable of criticizing experts in that area.

questions.stimulus: Kostman's original painting of Rosati was not a very accurate portrait. Therefore, your reproduction of Kostman's painting of Rosati will not be a very accurate reproduction of the painting.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most similar in its flawed reasoning to the flawed reasoning in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: George's speech was filled with half-truths and misquotes. So the tape recording made of it cannot be of good sound quality.
answerChoices.B: An artist who paints a picture of an ugly scene must necessarily paint an ugly picture, unless the picture is a distorted representation of the scene.
answerChoices.C: If a child's eyes resemble her mother's, then if the mother's eyes are brown the child's eyes also must be brown.
answerChoices.D: Jo imitated Layne. But Jo is different from Layne, so Jo could not have imitated Layne very well.
answerChoices.E: Harold's second novel is similar to his first. Therefore, his second novel must be enthralling, because his first novel won a prestigious literary prize.

questions.stimulus: Any writer whose purpose is personal expression sometimes uses words ambiguously. Every poet's purpose is personal expression. Thus no poetry reader's enjoyment depends on attaining a precise understanding of what the poet means.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion can be properly inferred if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Writers who sometimes use words ambiguously have no readers who try to attain a precise understanding of what the writer means.
answerChoices.B: Writers whose purpose is personal expression are unconcerned with whether anyone enjoys reading their works.
answerChoices.C: No writer who ever uses words ambiguously has any reader whose enjoyment depends on attaining a precise understanding of what the writer means.
answerChoices.D: Most writers whose readers' enjoyment does not depend on attaining a precise understanding of the writers' words are poets.
answerChoices.E: Readers who have a precise understanding of what a writer has written derive their enjoyment from that understanding.

questions.stimulus: It is clear that humans during the Upper Paleolithic period used lamps for light in caves. Though lamps can be dated to the entire Upper Paleolithic, the distribution of known lamps from the period is skewed, with the greatest number being associated with the late Upper Paleolithic period, when the Magdalenian culture was dominant.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, contributes to an explanation of the skewed distribution of lamps except:

answerChoices.A: Artifacts from early in the Upper Paleolithic period are harder to identify than those that originated later in the period.
answerChoices.B: More archaeological sites have been discovered from the Magdalenian culture than from earlier cultures.
answerChoices.C: More efficient lamp-making techniques were developed by the Magdalenian culture than by earlier cultures.
answerChoices.D: Fire pits were much more common in caves early in the Upper Paleolithic period than they were later in that period.
answerChoices.E: More kinds of lamps were produced by the Magdalenian culture than by earlier cultures.

questions.stimulus: Columnist: George Orwell's book 1984 has exercised much influence on a great number of this newspaper's readers. One thousand readers were surveyed and asked to name the one book that had the most influence on their lives. The book chosen most often was the Bible; 1984 was second.
questions.questionStem: The answer to which one of the following questions would most help in evaluating the columnist's argument?

answerChoices.A: How many books had each person surveyed read?
answerChoices.B: How many people chose books other than 1984?
answerChoices.C: How many people read the columnist's newspaper?
answerChoices.D: How many books by George Orwell other than 1984 were chosen?
answerChoices.E: How many of those surveyed had actually read the books they chose?

questions.stimulus: A 1991 calculation was made to determine what, if any, additional health-care costs beyond the ordinary are borne by society at large for people who live a sedentary life. The figure reached was a lifetime average of $1,650. Thus people's voluntary choice not to exercise places a significant burden on society.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true and not taken into account by the calculation, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Many people whose employment requires physical exertion do not choose to engage in regular physical exercise when they are not at work.
answerChoices.B: Exercise is a topic that is often omitted from discussion between doctor and patient during a patient's visit.
answerChoices.C: Physical conditions that eventually require medical or nursing-home care often first predispose a person to adopt a sedentary life-style.
answerChoices.D: Individuals vary widely in the amount and kind of exercise they choose, when they do exercise regularly.
answerChoices.E: A regular program of moderate exercise tends to increase circulation, induce a feeling of well-being and energy, and decrease excess weight.

questions.stimulus: In the paintings by seventeenth-century Dutch artist Vermeer, we find several recurrent items: a satin jacket, a certain Turkish carpet, and wooden chairs with lion's-head finials. These reappearing objects might seem to evince a dearth of props. Yet we know that many of the props Vermeer used were expensive. Thus, while we might speculate about exactly why Vermeer worked with a small number of familiar objects, it was clearly not for lack of props that the recurrent items were used.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Vermeer often borrowed the expensive props he represented in his paintings.
answerChoices.B: The props that recur in Vermeer's paintings were always available to him.
answerChoices.C: The satin jacket and wooden chairs that recur in the paintings were owned by Vermeer's sister.
answerChoices.D: The several recurrent items that appeared in Vermeer's paintings had special sentimental importance for him.
answerChoices.E: If a dearth of props accounted for the recurrent objects in Vermeer's paintings, we would not see expensive props in any of them.

questions.stimulus: Scientists agree that ingesting lead harms young children. More lead paint remains in older apartment buildings than newer ones because the use of lead paint was common until only two decades ago. Yet these same scientists also agree that laws requiring the removal of lead paint from older apartment buildings will actually increase the amount of lead that children living in older apartment buildings ingest.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the scientists' beliefs?

answerChoices.A: Lead-free paints contain substances that make them as harmful to children as lead paint is.
answerChoices.B: The money required to finance the removal of lead paint from apartment walls could be spent in ways more likely to improve the health of children.
answerChoices.C: Other sources of lead in older apartment buildings are responsible for most of the lead that children living in these buildings ingest.
answerChoices.D: Removing lead paint from walls disperses a great deal of lead dust, which is more easily ingested by children than is paint on walls.
answerChoices.E: Many other environmental hazards pose greater threats to the health of children than does lead paint.

questions.stimulus: Several companies will soon offer personalized electronic news services, delivered via cable or telephone lines and displayed on a television. People using these services can view continually updated stories on those topics for which they subscribe. Since these services will provide people with the information they are looking for more quickly and efficiently than printed newspapers can, newspaper sales will decline drastically if these services become widely available.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: In reading newspapers, most people not only look for stories on specific topics but also like to idly browse through headlines or pictures for amusing stories on unfamiliar or unusual topics.
answerChoices.B: Companies offering personalized electronic news services will differ greatly in what they charge for access to their services, depending on how wide a range of topics they cover.
answerChoices.C: Approximately 30 percent of people have never relied on newspapers for information but instead have always relied on news programs broadcast on television and radio.
answerChoices.D: The average monthly cost of subscribing to several channels on a personalized electronic news service will approximately equal the cost of a month's subscription to a newspaper.
answerChoices.E: Most people who subscribe to personalized electronic news services will not have to pay extra costs for installation since the services will use connections installed by cable and telephone companies.

questions.stimulus: Muscular strength is a limited resource, and athletic techniques help to use this resource efficiently. Since top athletes do not differ greatly from each other in muscular strength, it follows that a requirement for an athlete to become a champion is a superior mastery of athletic techniques.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the conclusion of the argument?

answerChoices.A: Only champion athletes have a superior mastery of athletic techniques.
answerChoices.B: Superior muscular strength is a requirement for an athlete to become a champion.
answerChoices.C: No athlete can become a champion without a superior mastery of athletic techniques.
answerChoices.D: The differences in muscular strength between top athletes are not great.
answerChoices.E: Athletic techniques help athletes use limited resources efficiently.

questions.stimulus:
Mary: Computers will make more information available to ordinary people than was ever available before, thus making it easier for them to acquire knowledge without consulting experts.
Joyce: As more knowledge became available in previous centuries, the need for specialists to synthesize and explain it to nonspecialists increased. So computers will probably create a greater dependency on experts.
questions.questionStem: The dialogue most strongly supports the claim that Mary and Joyce disagree with each other about whether

answerChoices.A: computers will contribute only negligibly to the increasing dissemination of knowledge in society
answerChoices.B: computers will increase the need for ordinary people seeking knowledge to turn to experts
answerChoices.C: computers will make more information available to ordinary people
answerChoices.D: dependency on computers will increase with the increase of knowledge
answerChoices.E: synthesizing knowledge and explaining it to ordinary people can be accomplished only by computer experts

questions.stimulus: Solicitor: Loux named Zembaty executor of her will. Her only beneficiary was her grandson, of whom she was very fond. Prior to distributing the remainder to the beneficiary, Zembaty was legally required to choose which properties in the estate should be sold to clear the estate's heavy debts. Loux never expressed any particular desire about the Stoke Farm, which includes the only farmland in her estate. Thus, it is unlikely that Loux would have had any objection to Zembaty's having sold it rather than having transferred it to her grandson.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the solicitor's argument?

answerChoices.A: The estate's debts could not have been cleared without selling the Stoke Farm.
answerChoices.B: Loux repeatedly told her grandson that she would take care of him in her will.
answerChoices.C: Loux was well aware of the legal requirements the executor of her will would have to satisfy.
answerChoices.D: The Stoke Farm was the main cause of the estate's debts.
answerChoices.E: Loux's grandson had repeatedly expressed his desire to own a farm.

questions.stimulus: Government official: A satisfactory way of eliminating chronic food shortages in our country is not easily achievable. Direct aid from other countries in the form of food shipments tends to undermine our prospects for long-term agricultural self-sufficiency. If external sources of food are delivered effectively by external institutions, local food producers and suppliers are forced out of business. On the other hand, foreign capital funneled to long-term development projects would inject so much cash into our economy that inflation would drive the price of food beyond the reach of most of our citizens.
questions.questionStem: The claim that foreign capital funneled into the economy would cause inflation plays which one of the following roles in the government official's argument?

answerChoices.A: It supports the claim that the official's country must someday be agriculturally self-sufficient.
answerChoices.B: It supports the claim that there is no easy solution to the problem of chronic food shortages in the official's country.
answerChoices.C: It is supported by the claim that the official's country must someday be agriculturally self-sufficient.
answerChoices.D: It supports the claim that donations of food from other countries will not end the chronic food shortages in the official's country.
answerChoices.E: It is supported by the claim that food producers and suppliers in the official's country may be forced out of business by donations of food from other countries.

questions.stimulus: Medical doctor: Sleep deprivation is the cause of many social ills, ranging from irritability to potentially dangerous instances of impaired decision making. Most people today suffer from sleep deprivation to some degree. Therefore we should restructure the workday to allow people flexibility in scheduling their work hours.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most strengthen the medical doctor's argument?

answerChoices.A: The primary cause of sleep deprivation is overwork.
answerChoices.B: Employees would get more sleep if they had greater latitude in scheduling their work hours.
answerChoices.C: Individuals vary widely in the amount of sleep they require.
answerChoices.D: More people would suffer from sleep deprivation today than did in the past if the average number of hours worked per week had not decreased.
answerChoices.E: The extent of one's sleep deprivation is proportional to the length of one's workday.

questions.stimulus: Essayist: Knowledge has been defined as a true belief formed by a reliable process. This definition has been criticized on the grounds that if someone had a reliable power of clairvoyance, we would not accept that person's claim to know certain things on the basis of this power. I agree that we would reject such claims, but we would do so because we really do not believe in clairvoyance as a reliable process. Were we to believe in clairvoyance, we would accept knowledge claims made on the basis of it.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the essayist's method of defending the definition against the objection?

answerChoices.A: asserting that the objection is based on a belief about the reliability of clairvoyance rather than on the nature of knowledge or its definition
answerChoices.B: asserting that the case of clairvoyance is one of knowledge even though we do not really believe in clairvoyance as a reliable process
answerChoices.C: arguing against the assumption that clairvoyance is unreliable
answerChoices.D: explaining that the definition of knowledge is a matter of personal choice
answerChoices.E: demonstrating that the case of clairvoyance is not a case of knowledge and does not fit the definition of knowledge

questions.stimulus: I agree that Hogan's actions resulted in grievous injury to Winters. And I do not deny that Hogan fully realized the nature of his actions and the effects that they would have. Indeed, I would not disagree if you pointed out that intentionally causing such effects is reprehensible, other things being equal. But in asking you to concur with me that Hogan's actions not be wholly condemned I emphasize again that Hogan mistakenly believed Winters to be the robber who had been terrorizing west-side apartment buildings for the past several months.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the conclusion of the argument?

answerChoices.A: Hogan should not be considered responsible for the injuries sustained by Winters.
answerChoices.B: The robber who had been terrorizing west-side apartment buildings should be considered to be as responsible for Winters's injuries as Hogan.
answerChoices.C: The actions of Hogan that seriously injured Winters are not completely blameworthy.
answerChoices.D: Hogan thought that Winters was the person who had been terrorizing west-side apartment buildings for the last few months.
answerChoices.E: The actions of Hogan that seriously injured Winters were reprehensible, other things being equal.

questions.stimulus:
Peter: Because the leaves of mildly drought-stressed plants are tougher in texture than the leaves of abundantly watered plants, insects prefer to feed on the leaves of abundantly watered plants. Therefore, to minimize crop damage, farmers should water crops only just enough to ensure that there is no substantial threat, from a lack of water, to either the growth or the yield of the crops.
Jennifer: Indeed. In fact, a mildly drought-stressed plant will divert a small amount of its resources from normal growth to the development of pesticidal toxins, but abundantly watered plants will not.
questions.questionStem: Jennifer's comment is related to Peter's argument in which one of the following ways?

answerChoices.A: It offers information that supports each of the claims that Peter makes in his argument.
answerChoices.B: It supports Peter's argument by supplying a premise without which Peter's conclusion cannot properly be drawn.
answerChoices.C: It supports Peter's argument by offering an explanation of all of Peter's premises.
answerChoices.D: It supports one of Peter's premises although it undermines Peter's conclusion.
answerChoices.E: It supports the conclusion of Peter's argument by offering independent grounds for that conclusion.

questions.stimulus:
Peter: Because the leaves of mildly drought-stressed plants are tougher in texture than the leaves of abundantly watered plants, insects prefer to feed on the leaves of abundantly watered plants. Therefore, to minimize crop damage, farmers should water crops only just enough to ensure that there is no substantial threat, from a lack of water, to either the growth or the yield of the crops.
Jennifer: Indeed. In fact, a mildly drought-stressed plant will divert a small amount of its resources from normal growth to the development of pesticidal toxins, but abundantly watered plants will not.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens Peter's argument?

answerChoices.A: The leaves of some crop plants are much larger, and therefore absorb more water, than the leaves of some other crop plants.
answerChoices.B: In industrialized nations there are more crops that are abundantly watered than there are crops grown under mild drought stress.
answerChoices.C: Insect damage presents a greater threat to crop plants than does mild drought stress.
answerChoices.D: Farmers are not always able to control the amount of water that their crops receive when, for instance, there are rainstorms in the areas where their crops are growing.
answerChoices.E: Mexican bean beetles are more likely to feed on the leaves of slightly drought-stressed soybeans than oak lace bugs are to feed on the leaves of abundantly watered soybeans.

questions.stimulus: Vague laws set vague limits on people's freedom, which makes it impossible for them to know for certain whether their actions are legal. Thus, under vague laws people cannot feel secure.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: People can feel secure only if they know for certain whether their actions are legal.
answerChoices.B: If people do not know for certain whether their actions are legal, then they might not feel secure.
answerChoices.C: If people know for certain whether their actions are legal, they can feel secure.
answerChoices.D: People can feel secure if they are governed by laws that are not vague.
answerChoices.E: Only people who feel secure can know for certain whether their actions are legal.

questions.stimulus: While it was once believed that the sort of psychotherapy appropriate for the treatment of neuroses caused by environmental factors is also appropriate for schizophrenia and other psychoses, it is now known that these latter, more serious forms of mental disturbance are best treated by biochemical-that is, medicinal-means. This is conclusive evidence that psychoses, unlike neuroses, have nothing to do with environmental factors but rather are caused by some sort of purely organic condition, such as abnormal brain chemistry or brain malformations.
questions.questionStem: The argument is vulnerable to criticism because it ignores the possibility that

answerChoices.A: the organic conditions that result in psychoses can be caused or exacerbated by environmental factors
answerChoices.B: the symptoms of mental disturbance caused by purely organic factors can be alleviated with medicine
answerChoices.C: organic illnesses that are nonpsychological in nature may be treatable without using biochemical methods
answerChoices.D: the nature of any medical condition can be inferred from the nature of the treatment that cures that condition
answerChoices.E: organic factors having little to do with brain chemistry may be at least partially responsible for neuroses

questions.stimulus: We learn to use most of the machines in our lives through written instructions, without knowledge of the machines' inner workings, because most machines are specifically designed for use by nonexperts. So, in general, attaining technological expertise would prepare students for tomorrow's job market no better than would a more traditional education stressing verbal and quantitative skills.
questions.questionStem: The argument depends on assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Fewer people receive a traditional education stressing verbal and quantitative skills now than did 20 years ago.
answerChoices.B: Facility in operating machines designed for use by nonexperts is almost never enhanced by expert knowledge of the machines' inner workings.
answerChoices.C: Most jobs in tomorrow's job market will not demand the ability to operate many machines that are designed for use only by experts.
answerChoices.D: Students cannot attain technological expertise and also receive an education that does not neglect verbal and quantitative skills.
answerChoices.E: When learning to use a machine, technological expertise is never more important than verbal and quantitative skills.

questions.stimulus: Environmentalists who seek stricter governmental regulations controlling water pollution should be certain to have their facts straight. For if it turns out, for example, that water pollution is a lesser threat than they proclaimed, then there will be a backlash and the public will not listen to them even when dire threats exist.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following best illustrates the principle illustrated by the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Middle-level managers who ask their companies to hire additional employees should have strong evidence that doing so will benefit the company; otherwise, higher-level managers will refuse to follow their suggestions to hire additional employees even when doing so really would benefit the company.
answerChoices.B: Politicians who defend the rights of unpopular constituencies ought to see to it that they use cool, dispassionate rhetoric in their appeals. Even if they have their facts straight, inflammatory rhetoric can cause a backlash that results in more negative reactions to these constituencies, whether or not they are deserving of more rights.
answerChoices.C: People who are trying to convince others to take some sort of action should make every effort to present evidence that is emotionally compelling. Such evidence is invariably more persuasive than dry, technical data, even when the data strongly support their claims.
answerChoices.D: Whoever wants to advance a political agenda ought to take the time to convince legislators that their own political careers are at stake in the matter at hand; otherwise, the agenda will simply be ignored.
answerChoices.E: Activists who want to prevent excessive globalization of the economy should assign top priority to an appeal to the economic self-interest of those who would be adversely affected by it, for if they fail in such an appeal, extreme economic globalization is inevitable.

questions.stimulus: Herpetologist: Some psychologists attribute complex reasoning to reptiles, claiming that simple stimulus-response explanations of some reptiles' behaviors, such as food gathering, cannot account for the complexity of such behavior. But since experiments show that reptiles are incapable of making major alterations in their behavior, for example, when faced with significant changes in their environment, these animals must be incapable of complex reasoning.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the herpetologist's argument?

answerChoices.A: Animals could make major changes in their behavior only if they were capable of complex reasoning.
answerChoices.B: Simple stimulus-response explanations can in principle account for all reptile behaviors.
answerChoices.C: Reptile behavior appears more complex in the field than laboratory experiments reveal it to be.
answerChoices.D: If reptiles were capable of complex reasoning, they would sometimes be able to make major changes in their behavior.
answerChoices.E: Complex reasoning and responses to stimuli cannot both contribute to the same behavior.

questions.stimulus: The purpose of a general theory of art is to explain every aesthetic feature that is found in any of the arts. Premodern general theories of art, however, focused primarily on painting and sculpture. Every premodern general theory of art, even those that succeed as theories of painting and sculpture, fails to explain some aesthetic feature of music.
questions.questionStem: The statements above, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Any general theory of art that explains the aesthetic features of painting also explains those of sculpture.
answerChoices.B: A general theory of art that explains every aesthetic feature of music will achieve its purpose.
answerChoices.C: Any theory of art that focuses primarily on sculpture and painting cannot explain every aesthetic feature of music.
answerChoices.D: No premodern general theory of art achieves its purpose unless music is not art.
answerChoices.E: No premodern general theory of art explains any aesthetic features of music that are not shared with painting and sculpture.

questions.stimulus: It is said that people should accept themselves as they are instead of being dissatisfied with their own abilities. But this is clearly a bad principle if the goal is a society whose citizens are genuinely happy, for no one can be genuinely happy if he or she is not pursuing personal excellence and is unwilling to undergo personal change of any kind.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: Those who are willing to change will probably find genuine happiness.
answerChoices.B: People who are not dissatisfied with themselves are less likely than others to pursue personal excellence.
answerChoices.C: Personal excellence cannot be acquired by those who lack genuine confidence in their own abilities.
answerChoices.D: People are justified in feeling content with themselves when they have achieved some degree of personal excellence.
answerChoices.E: Happiness is not genuine unless it is based on something that is painful to obtain.

questions.stimulus: My father likes turnips, but not potatoes, which he says are tasteless. So it is not true that whoever likes potatoes likes turnips.
questions.questionStem: The flawed reasoning in the argument above most closely resembles that in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: This book is not a paperback, but it is expensive. So it is not true that some paperbacks are expensive.
answerChoices.B: Although this recently published work of fiction has more than 75 pages, it is not a novel. Thus, it is not the case that all novels have more than 75 pages.
answerChoices.C: All ornate buildings were constructed before the twentieth century. This house is ornate, so it must be true that it was built before the twentieth century.
answerChoices.D: Erica enjoys studying physics, but not pure mathematics, which she says is boring. So it is not true that whoever enjoys studying physics enjoys studying pure mathematics.
answerChoices.E: People who do their own oil changes are car fanatics. My next-door neighbors are car fanatics, so it follows that they do their own oil changes.

questions.stimulus: Critic: Although some people claim it is inconsistent to support freedom of speech and also support legislation limiting the amount of violence in TV programs, it is not. We can limit TV program content because the damage done by violent programs is more harmful than the decrease in freedom of speech that would result from the limitations envisioned by the legislation.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the critic's reasoning?

answerChoices.A: In evaluating legislation that would impinge on a basic freedom, we should consider the consequences of not passing the legislation.
answerChoices.B: One can support freedom of speech while at the same time recognizing that it can sometimes be overridden by other interests.
answerChoices.C: When facing a choice between restricting freedom of speech or not, we must decide based on what would make the greatest number of people the happiest.
answerChoices.D: If the exercise of a basic freedom leads to some harm, then the exercise of that freedom should be restricted.
answerChoices.E: In some circumstances, we should tolerate regulations that impinge on a basic freedom.

questions.stimulus:
Sandy: I play the Bigbucks lottery—that's the one where you pick five numbers and all the players who have picked the five numbers drawn at the end of the week share the money pot. But it's best to play only after there have been a few weeks with no winners, because the money pot increases each week that there is no winner.
Alex: No, you're more likely to win the lottery when the money pot is small, because that's when the fewest other people are playing.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a mistake in the reasoning of one of the two speakers?

answerChoices.A: Sandy holds that the chances of anyone's winning are unaffected by the number of times that person plays.
answerChoices.B: Alex holds that the chances of Sandy's winning are affected by the number of other people playing.
answerChoices.C: Sandy holds that the chances of anyone's winning are unaffected by the size of the pot.
answerChoices.D: Alex holds that the chances of Sandy's winning in a given week are unaffected by whether anyone has won the week before.
answerChoices.E: Sandy holds that the chances of there being a winner go up if no one has won the lottery for quite a while.

questions.stimulus: The retail price of decaffeinated coffee is considerably higher than that of regular coffee. However, the process by which coffee beans are decaffeinated is fairly simple and not very costly. Therefore, the price difference cannot be accounted for by the greater cost of providing decaffeinated coffee to the consumer.
questions.questionStem: The argument relies on assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Processing regular coffee costs more than processing decaffeinated coffee.
answerChoices.B: Price differences between products can generally be accounted for by such factors as supply and demand, not by differences in production costs.
answerChoices.C: There is little competition among companies that process decaffeinated coffee.
answerChoices.D: Retail coffee-sellers do not expect that consumers are content to pay more for decaffeinated coffee than for regular coffee.
answerChoices.E: The beans used for producing decaffeinated coffee do not cost much more before processing than the beans used for producing regular coffee.

questions.stimulus: A newspaper article on Britain's unions argued that their strength was declining. The article's evidence was the decreasing number and size of strikes, as if the reason for the unions' existence was to organize strikes. Surely, in a modern industrial society, the calling of a strike is evidence that the negotiating position of the union was too weak. Strong unions do not need to call strikes. They can concentrate their efforts on working with others in the labor market to achieve common goals, such as profitable and humane working conditions.
questions.questionStem: The argument criticizing the newspaper article is directed toward establishing which one of the following as its main conclusion?

answerChoices.A: The negotiating position of a union is weak if the only means it has of achieving its end is a strike or the threat of a strike.
answerChoices.B: Although unions represent the interests of their members, that does not preclude them from having interests in common with other participants in the labor market.
answerChoices.C: There is no reason to believe, on the basis of what the newspaper article said, that union strength in Britain is declining.
answerChoices.D: The reason for unions' existence is to work for goals such as profitable and humane working conditions by organizing strikes.
answerChoices.E: With strong unions it is possible for a modern industrial society to achieve profitable and humane working conditions, but without them it would be impossible.

questions.stimulus: A newspaper article on Britain's unions argued that their strength was declining. The article's evidence was the decreasing number and size of strikes, as if the reason for the unions' existence was to organize strikes. Surely, in a modern industrial society, the calling of a strike is evidence that the negotiating position of the union was too weak. Strong unions do not need to call strikes. They can concentrate their efforts on working with others in the labor market to achieve common goals, such as profitable and humane working conditions.
questions.questionStem: The argument criticizing the newspaper article employs which one of the following strategies?

answerChoices.A: questioning the accuracy of the statistical evidence that the newspaper article uses
answerChoices.B: detailing historical changes that make the newspaper article's analysis outdated
answerChoices.C: reinterpreting evidence that the newspaper article uses as indicating the opposite of what the newspaper concludes
answerChoices.D: arguing that the newspaper article's conclusion is motivated by a desire to change the role of unions
answerChoices.E: pointing to common interests among unions and management which the newspaper article ignores

questions.stimulus: Anthropologist: All music is based on a few main systems of scale building. Clearly, if the popularity of a musical scale were a result of social conditioning, we would expect, given the diversity of social systems, a diverse mixture of diatonic and nondiatonic scales in the world's music. Yet diatonic scales have always dominated the music of most of the world. Therefore, the popularity of diatonic music can be attributed only to innate dispositions of the human mind.
questions.questionStem: The anthropologist's argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it fails to

answerChoices.A: consider the possibility that some people appreciate nondiatonic music more than they do diatonic music
answerChoices.B: explain how innate dispositions increase appreciation of nondiatonic music
answerChoices.C: explain the existence of diatonic scales as well as the existence of nondiatonic scales
answerChoices.D: consider that innate dispositions and social conditioning could jointly affect the popularity of a type of music
answerChoices.E: consider whether any appreciation of nondiatonic music is demonstrated by some nonhuman species of animals

questions.stimulus: Before 1986 physicists believed they could describe the universe in terms of four universal forces. Experiments then suggested, however, a fifth universal force of mutual repulsion between particles of matter. This fifth force would explain the occurrence in the experiments of a smaller measurement of the gravitational attraction between bodies than the established theory predicted.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument that there is a fifth universal force?

answerChoices.A: The extremely sophisticated equipment used for the experiments was not available to physicists before the 1970s.
answerChoices.B: No previously established scientific results are incompatible with the notion of a fifth universal force.
answerChoices.C: Some scientists have suggested that the alleged fifth universal force is an aspect of gravity rather than being fundamental in itself.
answerChoices.D: The experiments were conducted by physicists in remote geological settings in which factors affecting the force of gravity could not be measured with any degree of precision.
answerChoices.E: The fifth universal force was postulated at a time in which many other exciting and productive ideas in theoretical physics were developed.

questions.stimulus: A government ought to protect and encourage free speech, because free speech is an activity that is conducive to a healthy nation and thus is in the best interest of its people.
questions.questionStem: The main conclusion above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: An activity that is in the best interest of the people ought to be protected and encouraged by a nation's government.
answerChoices.B: Basic, inalienable rights of the people ought to be protected and encouraged by government.
answerChoices.C: An activity that helps a government to govern ought to be protected and encouraged by it.
answerChoices.D: A government ought to protect and encourage an activity that is conducive to the interests of that government.
answerChoices.E: Universal human rights that are in the best interest of the people ought to be protected and encouraged by a nation's government.

questions.stimulus: The current theory about earthquakes holds that they are caused by adjoining plates of rock sliding past each other; the plates are pressed together until powerful forces overcome the resistance. As plausible as this may sound, at least one thing remains mysterious on this theory. The overcoming of such resistance should create enormous amounts of heat. But so far no increases in temperature unrelated to weather have been detected following earthquakes.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the argument?

answerChoices.A: No increases in temperature have been detected following earthquakes.
answerChoices.B: The current theory does not fully explain earthquake data.
answerChoices.C: No one will ever be sure what the true cause of earthquakes is.
answerChoices.D: Earthquakes produce enormous amounts of heat that have so far gone undetected.
answerChoices.E: Contrary to the current theory, earthquakes are not caused by adjoining plates of rock sliding past one another.

questions.stimulus: Legal theorist: It is unreasonable to incarcerate anyone for any other reason than that he or she is a serious threat to the property or lives of other people. The breaking of a law does not justify incarceration, for lawbreaking proceeds either from ignorance of the law or of the effects of one's actions, or from the free choice of the lawbreaker. Obviously mere ignorance cannot justify incarcerating a lawbreaker, and even free choice on the part of the lawbreaker fails to justify incarceration, for free choice proceeds from the desires of an agent, and the desires of an agent are products of genetics and environmental conditioning, neither of which is controlled by the agent.
questions.questionStem: The claim in the first sentence of the passage plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It is offered as a premise that helps to show that no actions are under the control of the agent.
answerChoices.B: It is offered as background information necessary to understand the argument.
answerChoices.C: It is offered as the main conclusion that the argument is designed to establish.
answerChoices.D: It is offered as evidence for the stated claim that protection of life and property is more important than retribution for past illegal acts.
answerChoices.E: It is offered as evidence for the stated claim that lawbreaking proceeds from either ignorance of the law, or ignorance of the effects of one's actions, or free choice.

questions.stimulus: A certain gene can be stimulated by chemicals in cigarette smoke, causing lung cells to metabolize the chemicals in a way that makes the cells cancerous. Yet smokers in whom this gene is not stimulated have as high a risk of developing lung cancer from smoking as other smokers do.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, it can be concluded on the basis of them that

answerChoices.A: stimulation of the gene by chemicals in cigarette smoke is not the only factor affecting the risk for smokers of developing lung cancer
answerChoices.B: nonsmokers have as high a risk of developing lung cancer as do smokers in whom the gene has not been stimulated
answerChoices.C: smokers in whom the gene has been stimulated are more likely to develop lung cancer than are other smokers
answerChoices.D: the gene is more likely to be stimulated by chemicals in cigarette smoke than by other chemicals
answerChoices.E: smokers are less likely to develop lung cancer if they do not have the gene

questions.stimulus: In a poll of eligible voters conducted on the eve of a mayoral election, more of those polled stated that they favored Panitch than stated that they favored any other candidate. Despite this result, another candidate, Yeung, defeated Panitch by a comfortable margin.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, contributes to a resolution of the discrepancy described above except:

answerChoices.A: Of Yeung's supporters, a smaller percentage were eligible to vote than the percentage of Panitch's supporters who were eligible to vote.
answerChoices.B: A third candidate, Mulhern, conducted a press conference on the morning of the election and withdrew from the race.
answerChoices.C: The poll's questions were designed by staff members of Panitch's campaign.
answerChoices.D: Of the poll respondents supporting Yeung, 70 percent described the election as "important" or "very important," while 30 percent of respondents supporting Panitch did the same.
answerChoices.E: The poll, conducted on a Monday, surveyed persons in the downtown area, and the percentage of Yeung's supporters who work downtown is lower than that of Panitch's supporters.

questions.stimulus: Commissioner: Budget forecasters project a revenue shortfall of a billion dollars in the coming fiscal year. Since there is no feasible way to increase the available funds, our only choice is to decrease expenditures. The plan before you outlines feasible cuts that would yield savings of a billion dollars over the coming fiscal year. We will be able to solve the problem we face, therefore, only if we adopt this plan.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the commissioner's argument is flawed because this argument

answerChoices.A: relies on information that is far from certain
answerChoices.B: confuses being an adequate solution with being a required solution
answerChoices.C: inappropriately relies on the opinions of experts
answerChoices.D: inappropriately employs language that is vague
answerChoices.E: takes for granted that there is no way to increase available funds

questions.stimulus: Critic: Emily Dickinson's poetry demonstrates that meaning cannot reside entirely within a poem itself, but is always the unique result of an interaction between a reader's system of beliefs and the poem; and, of course, any two readers from different cultures or eras have radically different systems of beliefs.
questions.questionStem: If the critic's statements are true, each of the following could be true except:

answerChoices.A: A reader's interpretation of a poem by Dickinson is affected by someone else's interpretation of it.
answerChoices.B: A modern reader and a nineteenth-century reader interpret one of Shakespeare's sonnets in the same way.
answerChoices.C: A reader's interpretation of a poem evolves over time.
answerChoices.D: Two readers from the same era arrive at different interpretations of the same poem.
answerChoices.E: A reader's enjoyment of a poem is enhanced by knowing the poet's interpretation of it.

questions.stimulus: Archaeologist: The fact that the ancient Egyptians and the Maya both built pyramids is often taken as evidence of a historical link between Old- and New-World civilizations that is earlier than any yet documented. But while these buildings are similar to each other, there are important differences in both design and function. The Egyptian pyramids were exclusively tombs for rulers, whereas the Mayan pyramids were used as temples. This shows conclusively that there was no such link between Old- and New-World civilizations.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a flaw in the archaeologist's argument?

answerChoices.A: The argument equivocates with respect to the term "evidence."
answerChoices.B: The argument appeals to emotion rather than to reason.
answerChoices.C: The argument assumes the conclusion it is trying to prove.
answerChoices.D: The argument incorrectly relies on words whose meanings are vague or imprecise.
answerChoices.E: The argument presumes that no other evidence is relevant to the issue at hand.

questions.stimulus: Manuscripts written by first-time authors generally do not get serious attention by publishers except when these authors happen to be celebrities. My manuscript is unlikely to be taken seriously by publishers for I am a first-time author who is not a celebrity.
questions.questionStem: The structure of which one of the following arguments is most similar to the structure of the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Challengers generally do not win elections unless the incumbent has become very unpopular. The incumbent in this election has become very unpopular. Therefore, the challenger may win.
answerChoices.B: Fruit salad that contains bananas is ordinarily a boring dish unless it contains two or more exotic fruits. This fruit salad has bananas in it, and the only exotic fruit it has is guava. Thus, it will probably be boring.
answerChoices.C: Thursday's city council meeting is likely to be poorly attended. Traditionally, council meetings are sparsely attended if zoning issues are the only ones on the agenda. The agenda for Thursday is exclusively devoted to zoning.
answerChoices.D: The bulk of an estate generally goes to the spouse, if surviving, and otherwise goes to the surviving children. In this case there is no surviving spouse; hence the bulk of the estate is likely to go to the surviving children.
answerChoices.E: Normally about 40 percent of the deer population will die over the winter unless it is extremely mild. The percentage of the deer population that died over the recent winter was the normal 40 percent. I conclude that the recent winter was not unusually mild.

questions.stimulus: Twelve healthy volunteers with the Apo-A-IV-1 gene and twelve healthy volunteers who instead have the Apo-A-IV-2 gene each consumed a standard diet supplemented daily by a high-cholesterol food. A high level of cholesterol in the blood is associated with an increased risk of heart disease. After three weeks, the blood cholesterol levels of the subjects in the second group were unchanged, whereas the blood cholesterol levels of those with the Apo-A-IV-1 gene rose 20 percent.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Approximately half the population carries a gene that lowers cholesterol levels.
answerChoices.B: Most of those at risk of heart disease may be able to reduce their risk by adopting a low-cholesterol diet.
answerChoices.C: The bodies of those who have the Apo-A-IV-2 gene excrete cholesterol when blood cholesterol reaches a certain level.
answerChoices.D: The presence of the Apo-A-IV-1 gene seems to indicate that a person has a lower risk of heart disease.
answerChoices.E: The presence of the Apo-A-IV-2 gene may inhibit the elevation of blood cholesterol.

questions.stimulus: High school students who feel that they are not succeeding in school often drop out before graduating and go to work. Last year, however, the city's high school dropout rate was significantly lower than the previous year's rate. This is encouraging evidence that the program instituted two years ago to improve the morale of high school students has begun to take effect to reduce dropouts.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true about the last year, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: There was a recession that caused a high level of unemployment in the city.
answerChoices.B: The morale of students who dropped out of high school had been low even before they reached high school.
answerChoices.C: As in the preceding year, more high school students remained in school than dropped out.
answerChoices.D: High schools in the city established placement offices to assist their graduates in obtaining employment.
answerChoices.E: The antidropout program was primarily aimed at improving students' morale in those high schools with the highest dropout rates.

questions.stimulus: The television show Henry was not widely watched until it was scheduled for Tuesday evenings immediately after That's Life, the most popular show on television. During the year after the move, Henry was consistently one of the ten most-watched shows on television. Since Henry's recent move to Wednesday evenings, however, it has been watched by far fewer people. We must conclude that Henry was widely watched before the move to Wednesday evenings because it followed That's Life and not because people especially liked it.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Henry has been on the air for three years, but That's Life has been on the air for only two years.
answerChoices.B: The show that replaced Henry on Tuesdays has persistently had a low number of viewers in the Tuesday time slot.
answerChoices.C: The show that now follows That's Life on Tuesdays has double the number of viewers it had before being moved.
answerChoices.D: After its recent move to Wednesday, Henry was aired at the same time as the second most popular show on television.
answerChoices.E: That's Life was not widely watched during the first year it was aired.

questions.stimulus:
Joseph: My encyclopedia says that the mathematician Pierre de Fermat died in 1665 without leaving behind any written proof for a theorem that he claimed nonetheless to have proved. Probably this alleged theorem simply cannot be proved, since as the article points out no one else has been able to prove it. Therefore it is likely that Fermat was either lying or else mistaken when he made his claim.
Laura: Your encyclopedia is out of date. Recently someone has in fact proved Fermat's theorem. And since the theorem is provable, your claim— that Fermat was lying or mistaken—clearly is wrong.
questions.questionStem: Joseph's statement that "this alleged theorem simply cannot be proved" plays which one of the following roles in his argument?

answerChoices.A: an assumption for which no support is offered
answerChoices.B: a subsidiary conclusion on which his argument's main conclusion is based
answerChoices.C: a potential objection that his argument anticipates and attempts to answer before it is raised
answerChoices.D: the principal claim that his argument is structured to refute
answerChoices.E: background information that neither supports nor undermines his argument's conclusion

questions.stimulus:
Joseph: My encyclopedia says that the mathematician Pierre de Fermat died in 1665 without leaving behind any written proof for a theorem that he claimed nonetheless to have proved. Probably this alleged theorem simply cannot be proved, since as the article points out no one else has been able to prove it. Therefore it is likely that Fermat was either lying or else mistaken when he made his claim.
Laura: Your encyclopedia is out of date. Recently someone has in fact proved Fermat's theorem. And since the theorem is provable, your claim— that Fermat was lying or mistaken—clearly is wrong.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a reasoning error in Laura's argument?

answerChoices.A: It purports to establish its conclusion by making a claim that, if true, would actually contradict that conclusion.
answerChoices.B: It mistakenly assumes that the quality of a person's character can legitimately be taken to guarantee the accuracy of the claims that person has made.
answerChoices.C: It mistakes something that is necessary for its conclusion to follow for something that ensures that the conclusion follows.
answerChoices.D: It uses the term "provable" without defining it.
answerChoices.E: It fails to distinguish between a true claim that has mistakenly been believed to be false and a false claim that has mistakenly been believed to be true.

questions.stimulus: It is not good for a university to have class sizes that are very large or very small, or to have professors with teaching loads that are very light or very heavy. After all, crowded classes and overworked faculty cripple the institution's ability to recruit and retain both qualified students and faculty.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if added as a premise to the argument, most helps to justify its conclusion?

answerChoices.A: Professors who have very light teaching loads tend to focus their remaining time on research.
answerChoices.B: Classes that have very low numbers of students tend to have a lot of classroom discussion.
answerChoices.C: Very small class sizes or very light teaching loads indicate incompetence in classroom instruction.
answerChoices.D: Very small class sizes or very light teaching loads are common in the worst and the best universities.
answerChoices.E: Professors with very light teaching loads have no more office hours for students than professors with normal teaching loads.

questions.stimulus:
Sales manager: The highest priority should be given to the needs of the sales department, because without successful sales the company as a whole would fail.
Shipping manager: There are several departments other than sales that also must function successfully for the company to succeed. It is impossible to give the highest priority to all of them.
questions.questionStem: The shipping manager criticizes the sales manager's argument by pointing out

answerChoices.A: that the sales department taken by itself is not critical to the company's success as a whole
answerChoices.B: the ambiguity of the term "highest priority"
answerChoices.C: that departments other than sales are more vital to the company's success
answerChoices.D: an absurd consequence of its apparent assumption that a department's necessity earns it the highest priority
answerChoices.E: that the sales manager makes a generalization from an atypical case

questions.stimulus: Researchers have found that people who drink five or more cups of coffee a day have a risk of heart disease 2.5 times the average after corrections are made for age and smoking habits. Members of the research team say that, on the basis of their findings, they now limit their own daily coffee intake to two cups.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, indicates that the researchers' precaution might not have the result of decreasing their risk of heart disease?

answerChoices.A: The study found that for people who drank three or more cups of coffee daily, the additional risk of heart disease increased with each extra daily cup.
answerChoices.B: Per capita coffee consumption has been declining over the past 20 years because of the increasing popularity of soft drinks and also because of health worries.
answerChoices.C: The study did not collect information that would show whether variations in level of coffee consumption are directly related to variations in level of stress, a major causal factor in heart disease.
answerChoices.D: Subsequent studies have consistently shown that heavy smokers consume coffee at about 3 times the rate of nonsmokers.
answerChoices.E: Subsequent studies have shown that heavy coffee consumption tends to cause an elevated blood-cholesterol level, an immediate indicator of increased risk of heart disease.

questions.stimulus: People who have political power tend to see new technologies as a means of extending or protecting their power, whereas they generally see new ethical arguments and ideas as a threat to it. Therefore, technical ingenuity usually brings benefits to those who have this ingenuity, whereas ethical inventiveness brings only pain to those who have this inventiveness.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Those who offer new ways of justifying current political power often reap the benefits of their own innovations.
answerChoices.B: Politically powerful people tend to reward those who they believe are useful to them and to punish those who they believe are a threat.
answerChoices.C: Ethical inventiveness and technical ingenuity are never possessed by the same individuals.
answerChoices.D: New technologies are often used by people who strive to defeat those who currently have political power.
answerChoices.E: Many people who possess ethical inventiveness conceal their novel ethical arguments for fear of retribution by the politically powerful.

questions.stimulus: Birds need so much food energy to maintain their body temperatures that some of them spend most of their time eating. But a comparison of a bird of a seed-eating species to a bird of a nectar-eating species that has the same overall energy requirement would surely show that the seed-eating bird spends more time eating than does the nectar-eating bird, since a given amount of nectar provides more energy than does the same amount of seeds.
questions.questionStem: The argument relies on which one of the following questionable assumptions?

answerChoices.A: Birds of different species do not generally have the same overall energy requirements as each other.
answerChoices.B: The nectar-eating bird does not sometimes also eat seeds.
answerChoices.C: The time it takes for the nectar-eating bird to eat a given amount of nectar is not longer than the time it takes the seed-eating bird to eat the same amount of seeds.
answerChoices.D: The seed-eating bird does not have a lower body temperature than that of the nectar-eating bird.
answerChoices.E: The overall energy requirements of a given bird do not depend on factors such as the size of the bird, its nest-building habits, and the climate of the region in which it lives.

questions.stimulus: Consumer advocate: The introduction of a new drug into the marketplace should be contingent upon our having a good understanding of its social impact. However, the social impact of the newly marketed antihistamine is far from clear. It is obvious, then, that there should be a general reduction in the pace of bringing to the marketplace new drugs that are now being tested.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: The social impact of the new antihistamine is much better understood than that of most new drugs being tested.
answerChoices.B: The social impact of some of the new drugs being tested is poorly understood.
answerChoices.C: The economic success of some drugs is inversely proportional to how well we understand their social impact.
answerChoices.D: The new antihistamine is chemically similar to some of the new drugs being tested.
answerChoices.E: The new antihistamine should be on the market only if most new drugs being tested should be on the market also.

questions.stimulus:
Tina: For centuries oceans and human eccentricity have been linked in the literary and artistic imagination. Such linkage is probably due to the European Renaissance practice of using ships as asylums for the socially undesirable.
Sergio: No. Oceans have always been viewed as mysterious and unpredictable—qualities that people have invariably associated with eccentricity.
questions.questionStem: Tina's and Sergio's statements lend the most support to the claim that they disagree about which one of the following statements?

answerChoices.A: Eccentric humans were considered socially undesirable during the European Renaissance.
answerChoices.B: Oceans have always been viewed as mysterious and unpredictable.
answerChoices.C: The linkage between oceans and eccentricity explains the European Renaissance custom of using ships as asylums.
answerChoices.D: People have never attributed the same qualities to oceans and eccentrics.
answerChoices.E: The linkage between oceans and eccentricity predates the European Renaissance.

questions.stimulus: In a recent study, a group of subjects had their normal daily caloric intake increased by 25 percent. This increase was entirely in the form of alcohol. Another group of similar subjects had alcohol replace nonalcoholic sources of 25 percent of their normal daily caloric intake. All subjects gained body fat over the course of the study, and the amount of body fat gained was the same for both groups.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Alcohol is metabolized more quickly by the body than are other foods or drinks.
answerChoices.B: In the general population, alcohol is the primary cause of gains in body fat.
answerChoices.C: An increased amount of body fat does not necessarily imply a weight gain.
answerChoices.D: Body fat gain is not dependent solely on the number of calories one consumes.
answerChoices.E: The proportion of calories from alcohol in a diet is more significant for body fat gain than are the total calories from alcohol.

questions.stimulus: When investigators discovered that the director of a local charity had repeatedly overstated the number of people his charity had helped, the director accepted responsibility for the deception. However, the investigators claimed that journalists were as much to blame as the director was for inflating the charity's reputation, since they had naïvely accepted what the director told them, and simply reported as fact the numbers he gave them.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the investigators' claim?

answerChoices.A: Anyone who works for a charitable organization is obliged to be completely honest about the activities of that organization.
answerChoices.B: Anyone who knowingly aids a liar by trying to conceal the truth from others is also a liar.
answerChoices.C: Anyone who presents as factual a story that turns out to be untrue without first attempting to verify that story is no less responsible for the consequences of that story than anyone else is.
answerChoices.D: Anyone who lies in order to advance his or her own career is more deserving of blame than someone who lies in order to promote a good cause.
answerChoices.E: Anyone who accepts responsibility for a wrongful act that he or she committed is less deserving of blame than someone who tries to conceal his or her own wrongdoing.

questions.stimulus: Telephone companies are promoting "voice mail" as an alternative to the answering machine. By recording messages from callers when a subscriber does not have access to his or her telephone, voice mail provides a service similar to that of an answering machine. The companies promoting this service argue that it will soon make answering machines obsolete, since it is much more convenient, more flexible, and less expensive than an answering machine.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most calls into question the argument made by the companies promoting voice mail?

answerChoices.A: Unlike calls made to owners of answering machines, all telephone calls made to voice-mail subscribers are completed, even if the line called is in use at the time of the call.
answerChoices.B: The surge in sales of answering machines occurred shortly after they were first introduced to the electronics market.
answerChoices.C: Once a telephone customer decides to subscribe to voice mail, that customer can cancel the service at any time.
answerChoices.D: Answering machines enable the customer to hear who is calling before the customer decides whether to answer the telephone, a service voice mail does not provide.
answerChoices.E: The number of messages a telephone answering machine can record is limited by the length of the magnetic tape on which calls are recorded.

questions.stimulus: The judgment that an artist is great always rests on assessments of the work the artist has produced. A series of great works is the only indicator of greatness. Therefore, to say that an artist is great is just to summarize the quality of his or her known works, and the artist's greatness can provide no basis for predicting the quality of the artist's unknown or future works.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following contains questionable reasoning most similar to that in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: The only way of knowing whether someone has a cold is to observe symptoms. Thus, when a person is said to have a cold, this means only that he or she has displayed the symptoms of a cold, and no prediction about the patient's future symptoms is justified.
answerChoices.B: Although colds are very common, there are some people who never or only very rarely catch colds. Clearly these people must be in some way physiologically different from people who catch colds frequently.
answerChoices.C: Someone who has a cold is infected by a cold virus. No one can be infected by the same cold virus twice, but there are indefinitely many different cold viruses. Therefore, it is not possible to predict from a person's history of infection how susceptible he or she will be in the future.
answerChoices.D: The viruses that cause colds are not all the same, and they differ in their effects. Therefore, although it may be certain that a person has a cold, it is impossible to predict how the cold will progress.
answerChoices.E: Unless a person displays cold symptoms, it cannot properly be said that the person has a cold. But each of the symptoms of a cold is also the symptom of some other disease. Therefore, one can never be certain that a person has a cold.

questions.stimulus: Company president: Grievance procedures should allow the grievant and the respondent to select a mediator who will attempt to work out a resolution. Grievances are costly and mediation could help to resolve many of them. However, beginning mediation fairly late in the process, as our human resources department proposes, would be relatively ineffective.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to justify the company president's criticism of the human resources department's proposal?

answerChoices.A: People who file grievances are unreasonable and would resist listening to a mediator.
answerChoices.B: Many disagreements are already being solved without the intervention of a mediator.
answerChoices.C: Adversaries' positions tend to harden as a dispute wears on, making compromise less likely.
answerChoices.D: Respondents tend to be supervisors who cannot give in to employees without losing authority.
answerChoices.E: The mediation process itself is likely to cost as much in time and money as the present grievance procedures.

questions.stimulus: The solidity of bridge piers built on pilings depends largely on how deep the pilings are driven. Prior to 1700, pilings were driven to "refusal," that is, to the point at which they refused to go any deeper. In a 1588 inquiry into the solidity of piers for Venice's Rialto Bridge, it was determined that the bridge's builder, Antonio Da Ponte, had met the contemporary standard for refusal: he had caused the pilings to be driven until additional penetration into the ground was no greater than two inches after twenty-four hammer blows.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following can properly be inferred from the passage?

answerChoices.A: The Rialto Bridge was built on unsafe pilings.
answerChoices.B: The standard of refusal was not sufficient to ensure the safety of a bridge.
answerChoices.C: Da Ponte's standard of refusal was less strict than that of other bridge builders of his day.
answerChoices.D: After 1588, no bridges were built on pilings that were driven to the point of refusal.
answerChoices.E: It is possible that the pilings of the Rialto Bridge could have been driven deeper even after the standard of refusal had been met.

questions.stimulus: Joan got A's on all her homework assignments, so if she had gotten an A on her term paper, she could pass the course even without doing the class presentation. Unfortunately, she did not get an A on her term paper, so it is obvious that she will have to do the class presentation to pass the course.
questions.questionStem: The argument's reasoning is questionable because the argument

answerChoices.A: ignores the possibility that Joan must either have an A on her term paper or do the class presentation to pass the course
answerChoices.B: presupposes without justification that Joan's not getting an A on her term paper prevents her from passing the course without doing the class presentation
answerChoices.C: overlooks the importance of class presentations to a student's overall course grade
answerChoices.D: ignores the possibility that if Joan has to do the class presentation to pass the course, then she did not get an A on her term paper
answerChoices.E: fails to take into account the possibility that some students get A's on their term papers but do not pass the course

questions.stimulus: Compared to us, people who lived a century ago had very few diversions to amuse them. Therefore, they likely read much more than we do today.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Many of the books published a century ago were of low literary quality.
answerChoices.B: On average, people who lived a century ago had considerably less leisure time than we do today.
answerChoices.C: The number of books sold today is larger than it was a century ago.
answerChoices.D: On the average, books today cost slightly less in relation to other goods than they did a century ago.
answerChoices.E: One of the popular diversions of a century ago was horse racing.

questions.stimulus: Although consciousness seems to arise from physical processes, physical theories can explain only why physical systems have certain physical structures and how these systems perform various physical functions. Thus, no strictly physical theory can explain consciousness.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion of the argument follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Physical theories can explain only physical phenomena.
answerChoices.B: An explanation of consciousness must encompass more than an explanation of physical structures and functions.
answerChoices.C: The physical structures and functions of consciousness are currently unknown.
answerChoices.D: Consciousness arises from processes that are entirely explainable by physical theories.
answerChoices.E: An explanation of physical structures and functions must be formulated in strictly physical terms.

questions.stimulus: Advertisement: At most jewelry stores, the person assessing the diamond is the person selling it, so you can see why an assessor might say that a diamond is of higher quality than it really is. But because all diamonds sold at Gem World are certified in writing, you're assured of a fair price when purchasing a diamond from Gem World.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the advertisement would be most strengthened if which one of the following were true?

answerChoices.A: Many jewelry stores other than Gem World also provide written certification of the quality of their diamonds.
