answerChoices.D: One deserves praise for advancing one's own interests only if one also advances the interests of others.
answerChoices.E: It is the motives rather than the consequences of one's actions that determine whether one deserves praise for them.

questions.stimulus: Political theorist: Newly enacted laws need a period of immunity during which they can be repealed only if circumstances are dire. This is because the short-term consequences of any statutory change are likely to be painful, since people are not accustomed to it, while its long-term benefits are initially obscure, because people require time to learn how to take advantage of it.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the political theorist's argument?

answerChoices.A: Whether a law should be retained is independent of what the voters think its consequences will be.
answerChoices.B: Whether a law should be retained depends primarily on the long-term consequences of its enactment.
answerChoices.C: The repeal of a law should be at least as difficult as the passage of a law.
answerChoices.D: The short-term consequences of a law's repeal should be considered more carefully than the short-term consequences of its passage.
answerChoices.E: The long-term consequences of the enactment of a law should be more beneficial than its short-term consequences.

questions.stimulus: The druid stones discovered in Ireland are very, very old. But this particular druid stone was discovered in Scotland; hence, it must be of more recent vintage.
questions.questionStem: The argument is flawed because it

answerChoices.A: allows a key term to shift in meaning from one use to the next
answerChoices.B: takes the fact that most members of a group have a certain property to constitute evidence that all members of the group have that property
answerChoices.C: takes for granted the very claim that it sets out to establish
answerChoices.D: presumes without justification that what was true of the members of a group in the past will continue to be true of them in the future
answerChoices.E: takes the fact that all members of a group have a certain property to constitute evidence that the members of the group are the only things with that property

questions.stimulus:
Robert: Speed limits on residential streets in Crownsbury are routinely ignored by drivers. People crossing those streets are endangered by speeding drivers, yet the city does not have enough police officers to patrol every street. So the city should install speed bumps and signs warning of their presence on residential streets to slow down traffic.
Sheila: That is a bad idea. People who are driving too fast can easily lose control of their vehicles when they hit a speed bump.
questions.questionStem: Sheila's response depends on the presupposition that

answerChoices.A: problems of the kind that Robert describes are worse in Crownsbury than they are in other cities
answerChoices.B: Robert's proposal is intended to address a problem that Robert does not in fact intend it to address
answerChoices.C: with speed bumps and warning signs in place, there would still be drivers who would not slow down to a safe speed
answerChoices.D: most of the people who are affected by the problem Robert describes would be harmed by the installation of speed bumps and warning signs
answerChoices.E: problems of the kind that Robert describes do not occur on any nonresidential streets in Crownsbury

questions.stimulus:
Robert: Speed limits on residential streets in Crownsbury are routinely ignored by drivers. People crossing those streets are endangered by speeding drivers, yet the city does not have enough police officers to patrol every street. So the city should install speed bumps and signs warning of their presence on residential streets to slow down traffic.
Sheila: That is a bad idea. People who are driving too fast can easily lose control of their vehicles when they hit a speed bump.
questions.questionStem: The relationship of Sheila's statement to Robert's argument is that Sheila's statement

answerChoices.A: raises the objection that the problem with which Robert is concerned may not be as serious as he takes it to be
answerChoices.B: argues that the solution Robert advocates is likely to have undesirable side effects of its own
answerChoices.C: defends an alternative course of action as more desirable than the one advocated by Robert
answerChoices.D: concedes that the solution advocated by Robert would be effective, but insists that the reasons for this are not those given by Robert
answerChoices.E: charges that Robert's proposal would have no net effect on the problem he describes

questions.stimulus: In ancient Mesopotamia, prior to 2900 B.C., wheat was cultivated in considerable quantities, but after 2900 B.C. production of that grain began to decline as the production of barley increased sharply. Some historians who study ancient Mesopotamia contend that the decline in wheat production was due to excessive irrigation, lack of drainage, and the consequent accumulation of salt residues in the soil.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to support the historians' contention concerning the reasons for the decline in wheat production in ancient Mesopotamia?

answerChoices.A: The cultivation of barley requires considerably less water than does the cultivation of wheat.
answerChoices.B: Barley has much greater resistance to the presence of salt in soil than does wheat.
answerChoices.C: Prior to 2900 B.C., barley was cultivated along with wheat, but the amount of barley produced was far less than the amount of wheat produced.
answerChoices.D: Around 2900 B.C., a series of wheat blights occurred, destroying much of the wheat crop year after year.
answerChoices.E: Literary and archaeological evidence indicates that in the period following 2900 B.C., barley became the principal grain in the diet of most of the inhabitants of Mesopotamia.

questions.stimulus: Physician: In itself, exercise does not cause heart attacks; rather, a sudden increase in an exercise regimen can be a cause. When people of any physical condition suddenly increase their amount of exercise, they also increase their risk of heart attack. As a result, there will be an increased risk of heart attack among employees of this company due to the new health program.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion drawn by the physician follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Employees will abruptly increase their amount of exercise as a result of the new health program.
answerChoices.B: The exercises involved in the new health program are more strenuous than those in the previous health program.
answerChoices.C: The new health program will force employees of all levels of health to exercise regularly.
answerChoices.D: The new health program constitutes a sudden change in the company's policy.
answerChoices.E: All employees, no matter what their physical condition, will participate in the new health program.

questions.stimulus: Last month OCF, Inc., announced what it described as a unique new product: an adjustable computer workstation. Three days later ErgoTech unveiled an almost identical product. The two companies claim that the similarities are coincidental and occurred because the designers independently reached the same solution to the same problem. The similarities are too fundamental to be mere coincidence, however. The two products not only look alike, but they also work alike. Both are oddly shaped with identically placed control panels with the same types of controls. Both allow the same types of adjustments and the same types of optional enhancements.
questions.questionStem: The main point of the argument is that

answerChoices.A: the two products have many characteristics in common
answerChoices.B: ErgoTech must have copied the design of its new product from OCF's design
answerChoices.C: the similarities between the two products are not coincidental
answerChoices.D: product designers sometimes reach the same solution to a given problem without consulting each other
answerChoices.E: new products that at first appear to be unique are sometimes simply variations of other products

questions.stimulus: An anthropologist hypothesized that a certain medicinal powder contained a significant amount of the deadly toxin T. When the test she performed for the presence of toxin T was negative, the anthropologist did not report the results. A chemist who nevertheless learned about the test results charged the anthropologist with fraud. The anthropologist, however, countered that those results were invalid because the powder had inadvertently been tested in an acidic solution.
questions.questionStem: In the absence of the anthropologist's reply, which one of the following principles, if established, would most support the chemist's charge?

answerChoices.A: Reporting results for an experiment that was not conducted and reporting a false result for an actual experiment are both instances of scientific fraud.
answerChoices.B: Scientists can commit fraud and yet report some disconfirmations of their hypotheses.
answerChoices.C: Scientists can neglect to report some disconfirmations of their hypotheses and yet be innocent of fraud.
answerChoices.D: Scientists commit fraud whenever they report as valid any test result they know to be invalid.
answerChoices.E: Scientists who neglect to report any experiment that could be interpreted as disconfirming their hypotheses have thereby committed fraud.

questions.stimulus: An anthropologist hypothesized that a certain medicinal powder contained a significant amount of the deadly toxin T. When the test she performed for the presence of toxin T was negative, the anthropologist did not report the results. A chemist who nevertheless learned about the test results charged the anthropologist with fraud. The anthropologist, however, countered that those results were invalid because the powder had inadvertently been tested in an acidic solution.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the anthropologist's counterargument?

answerChoices.A: The anthropologist had evidence from field work that the medicinal powder was typically prepared using toxin T.
answerChoices.B: The activity level of toxin T tends to decline if the powder is stored for a long time.
answerChoices.C: When it is put into an acidic solution, toxin T becomes undetectable.
answerChoices.D: A fresh batch of powder for a repeat analysis was available at the time of the test.
answerChoices.E: The type of analysis used was insensitive to very small amounts of toxin T.

questions.stimulus:
Naima: The proposed new computer system, once we fully implemented it, would operate more smoothly and efficiently than the current system. So we should devote the resources necessary to accomplish the conversion as soon as possible.
Nakai: We should keep the current system for as long as we can. The cost in time and money of converting to the new system would be greater than any predicted benefits.
questions.questionStem: Naima and Nakai disagree with each other over whether

answerChoices.A: the predicted benefits of the new computer system will be realized
answerChoices.B: it is essential to have the best computer system available
answerChoices.C: accomplishing the conversion is technically impossible
answerChoices.D: the current computer system does not work well enough to do what it is supposed to do
answerChoices.E: the conversion to a new computer system should be delayed

questions.stimulus: Every year, new reports appear concerning the health risks posed by certain substances, such as coffee and sugar. One year an article claimed that coffee is dangerous to one's health. The next year, another article argued that coffee has some benefits for one's health. From these contradictory opinions, we see that experts are useless for guiding one's decisions about one's health.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a flaw in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: The argument takes for granted that coffee is dangerous to one's health.
answerChoices.B: The argument presumes, without providing warrant, that one always wants expert guidance in making decisions about one's health.
answerChoices.C: The argument fails to consider the nature of expert opinion in areas other than health.
answerChoices.D: The argument presumes, without providing justification, that because expert opinion is trustworthy in one case, it must therefore be trustworthy in all cases.
answerChoices.E: The argument fails to consider that coffee may be harmful to one's health in some respects and beneficial in others.

questions.stimulus: Because people are generally better at detecting mistakes in others' work than in their own, a prudent principle is that one should always have one's own work checked by someone else.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following provides the best illustration of the principle above?

answerChoices.A: The best elementary school math teachers are not those for whom math was always easy. Teachers who had to struggle through math themselves are better able to explain math to students.
answerChoices.B: One must make a special effort to clearly explain one's views to someone else; people normally find it easier to understand their own views than to understand others' views.
answerChoices.C: Juries composed of legal novices, rather than panels of lawyers, should be the final arbiters in legal proceedings. People who are not legal experts are in a better position to detect good legal arguments by lawyers than are other lawyers.
answerChoices.D: People should always have their writing proofread by someone else. Someone who does not know in advance what is meant to be said is in a better position to spot typographical errors.
answerChoices.E: Two people going out for dinner will have a more enjoyable meal if they order for each other. By allowing someone else to choose, one opens oneself up to new and exciting dining experiences.

questions.stimulus: Pundit: The only airline providing service for our town announced that because the service is unprofitable it will discontinue this service next year. Town officials have urged the community to use the airline's service more frequently so that the airline will change its decision. There is no reason to comply with their recommendation, however, for just last week these same officials drove to an out-of-town conference instead of flying.
questions.questionStem: The pundit's reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it presumes, without providing justification, that

answerChoices.A: increasing the number of tickets sold without increasing ticket prices will be sufficient to make continued air service economically feasible
answerChoices.B: suspending service and losing money by continuing service are the airline's only options
answerChoices.C: the town officials paid for their trip with taxpayers' money rather than their own money
answerChoices.D: ground transportation is usually no less expensive than airplane transportation
answerChoices.E: if the town officials did not follow their own advice then that advice is not worth following

questions.stimulus: Some scientists believe that 65 million years ago an asteroid struck what is now the Yucatán Peninsula, thereby causing extinction of the dinosaurs. These scientists have established that such a strike could have hurled enough debris into the atmosphere to block sunlight and cool the atmosphere. Without adequate sunlight, food sources for herbivorous dinosaurs would have disappeared, and no dinosaurs could have survived a prolonged period of low temperatures. These same scientists, however, have also established that most debris launched by the asteroid would have settled to the ground within six months, too soon for the plants to disappear or the dinosaurs to freeze.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy between the scientists' beliefs and the scientists' results, as described above?

answerChoices.A: Loss of the herbivorous dinosaurs would have deprived the carnivorous dinosaurs of their food source.
answerChoices.B: Dinosaurs inhabited most landmasses on the planet but were not especially abundant in the area of the asteroid strike.
answerChoices.C: A cloud of debris capable of diminishing sunlight by 20 percent would have cooled the earth's surface by 7 to 10 degrees Celsius.
answerChoices.D: The asteroid was at least 9.6 km in diameter, large enough for many dinosaurs to be killed by the strike itself and by subsequent tidal waves.
answerChoices.E: Dinosaurs were susceptible to fatal respiratory problems caused by contamination of the air by asteroid debris.

questions.stimulus:
Bernard: For which language, and thus which frequency distribution of letters and letter sequences, was the standard typewriter keyboard designed?
Cora: To ask this question, you must be making a mistaken assumption: that typing speed was to be maximized. The real danger with early typewriters was that operators would hit successive keys too quickly, thereby crashing typebars into each other, bending connecting wires, and so on. So the idea was to slow the operator down by making the most common letter sequences awkward to type.
Bernard: This is surely not right! These technological limitations have long since vanished, yet the keyboard is still as it was then.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, could be used by Cora to counter Bernard's rejection of her explanation?

answerChoices.A: Typewriters and word-processing equipment are typically sold to people who have learned to use the standard keyboard and who, therefore, demand it in equipment they buy.
answerChoices.B: Typewriters have been superseded in most offices by word-processing equipment, which has inherited the standard keyboard from typewriters.
answerChoices.C: The standard keyboard allows skilled operators to achieve considerable typing speeds, though it makes acquiring such skills relatively difficult.
answerChoices.D: A person who has learned one keyboard layout can readily learn to use a second one in place of the first, but only with difficulty learn to use a second one alongside the first.
answerChoices.E: It is now possible to construct typewriters and word-processing equipment in which a single keyboard can accommodate two or even more different keyboard layouts, each accessible to the operator at will.

questions.stimulus: Some teachers claim that students would not learn curricular content without the incentive of grades. But students with intense interest in the material would learn it without this incentive, while the behavior of students lacking all interest in the material is unaffected by such an incentive. The incentive of grades, therefore, serves no essential academic purpose.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: takes for granted that the only purpose of school is to convey a fixed body of information to students
answerChoices.B: takes for granted that students who are indifferent to the grades they receive are genuinely interested in the curricular material
answerChoices.C: fails to consider that the incentive of grades may serve some useful nonacademic purpose
answerChoices.D: ignores the possibility that students who lack interest in the curricular material would be quite interested in it if allowed to choose their own curricular material
answerChoices.E: fails to consider that some students may be neither fascinated by nor completely indifferent to the subject being taught

questions.stimulus: Economist: Technology now changes so rapidly that workers need periodic retraining. Such retraining can be efficient only if it allows individual companies to meet their own short-term needs. Hence, large governmental job retraining programs are no longer a viable option in the effort to retrain workers efficiently.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the economist's argument?

answerChoices.A: Workers did not need to be retrained when the pace of technological change was slower than it is currently.
answerChoices.B: Large job retraining programs will be less efficient than smaller programs if the pace of technological change slows.
answerChoices.C: No single type of retraining program is most efficient at retraining technological workers.
answerChoices.D: Large governmental job retraining programs do not meet the short-term needs of different individual companies.
answerChoices.E: Technological workers are more likely now than in the past to move in order to find work for which they are already trained.

questions.stimulus: Recent research indicates that increased consumption of fruits and vegetables by middle-aged people reduces their susceptibility to stroke in later years. The researchers speculate that this may be because fruits and vegetables are rich in folic acid. Low levels of folic acid are associated with high levels of homocysteine, an amino acid that contributes to blocked arteries.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: An increased risk of stroke is correlated with low levels of homocysteine.
answerChoices.B: A decreased risk of stroke is correlated with increased levels of folic acid.
answerChoices.C: An increased propensity for blocked arteries is correlated with decreased levels of homocysteine.
answerChoices.D: A decreased propensity for blocked arteries is correlated with low levels of folic acid.
answerChoices.E: Stroke is prevented by ingestion of folic acid in quantities sufficient to prevent a decline in the levels of homocysteine.

questions.stimulus: Thirty years ago, the percentage of the British people who vacationed in foreign countries was very small compared with the large percentage of the British population who travel abroad for vacations now. Foreign travel is, and always has been, expensive from Britain. Therefore, British people must have, on average, more money to spend on vacations now than they did 30 years ago.
questions.questionStem: The argument requires assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: If foreign travel had been less expensive 30 years ago, British people would still not have had enough money to take vacations abroad.
answerChoices.B: If travel to Britain were less expensive, more people of other countries would travel to Britain for their vacations.
answerChoices.C: If the percentage of British people vacationing abroad was lower 30 years ago, then the British people of 30 years ago must have spent more money on domestic vacations.
answerChoices.D: If more of the British people of 30 years ago had had enough money to vacation abroad, more would have done so.
answerChoices.E: If British people are now wealthier than they were 30 years ago, then they must have more money to spend on vacations now than they did 30 years ago.

questions.stimulus: Mystery stories often feature a brilliant detective and the detective's dull companion. Clues are presented in the story, and the companion wrongly infers an inaccurate solution to the mystery using the same clues that the detective uses to deduce the correct solution. Thus, the author's strategy of including the dull companion gives readers a chance to solve the mystery while also diverting them from the correct solution.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Most mystery stories feature a brilliant detective who solves the mystery presented in the story.
answerChoices.B: Mystery readers often solve the mystery in a story simply by spotting the mistakes in the reasoning of the detective's dull companion in that story.
answerChoices.C: Some mystery stories give readers enough clues to infer the correct solution to the mystery.
answerChoices.D: The actions of the brilliant detective in a mystery story rarely divert readers from the actions of the detective's dull companion.
answerChoices.E: The detective's dull companion in a mystery story generally uncovers the misleading clues that divert readers from the mystery's correct solution.

questions.stimulus: Policy analyst: Increasing the size of a police force is only a stopgap method of crime prevention; it does not get at the root causes of crime. Therefore, city officials should not respond to rising crime rates by increasing the size of their city's police force.
questions.questionStem: The flawed reasoning in which one of the following arguments most closely resembles the flawed reasoning in the policy analyst's argument?

answerChoices.A: Some people think that rules with higher standards than people can live up to, such as those enjoining total honesty, prevent some immoral behavior by giving people a guide to self-improvement. But such rules actually worsen behavior by making people cynical about rules. Thus, societies should not institute overly demanding rules.
answerChoices.B: Swamps play an important role in allaying the harsh effects of floods because they absorb a great deal of water. Although dams prevent many floods, they worsen the effects of the greatest floods by drying up swamps. Thus dams should not be built.
answerChoices.C: Although less effective in preventing theft than security guards, burglar alarm systems are more affordable to maintain. Because the greater loss from theft when alarms are used is outweighed by their lower cost, companies are advised always to use burglar alarm systems.
answerChoices.D: Because taking this drug does not cure the disease for which it is prescribed, but only reduces the disease's most harmful effects, doctors should not continue to prescribe this drug.
answerChoices.E: We will never fully understand what causes people to engage in criminal activity. Therefore, we should investigate other ways to improve society's ability to combat crime.

questions.stimulus: In order to determine automobile insurance premiums for a driver, insurance companies calculate various risk factors; as the risk factors increase, so does the premium. Certain factors, such as the driver's age and past accident history, play an important role in these calculations. Yet these premiums should also increase with the frequency with which a person drives. After all, a person's chance of being involved in a mishap increases in proportion to the number of times that person drives.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most undermines the argument?

answerChoices.A: People who drive infrequently are more likely to be involved in accidents that occur on small roads than in highway accidents.
answerChoices.B: People who drive infrequently are less likely to follow rules for safe driving than are people who drive frequently.
answerChoices.C: People who drive infrequently are less likely to violate local speed limits than are people who drive frequently.
answerChoices.D: People who drive frequently are more likely to make long-distance trips in the course of a year than are people who drive infrequently.
answerChoices.E: People who drive frequently are more likely to become distracted while driving than are people who drive infrequently.

questions.stimulus: In order to determine automobile insurance premiums for a driver, insurance companies calculate various risk factors; as the risk factors increase, so does the premium. Certain factors, such as the driver's age and past accident history, play an important role in these calculations. Yet these premiums should also increase with the frequency with which a person drives. After all, a person's chance of being involved in a mishap increases in proportion to the number of times that person drives.
questions.questionStem: The claim that insurance premiums should increase as the frequency with which a driver drives increases plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

answerChoices.A: a premise of the argument
answerChoices.B: the conclusion of the argument
answerChoices.C: evidence offered in support of one of the premises
answerChoices.D: an assertion phrased to preclude an anticipated objection
answerChoices.E: a clarification of a key term in the argument

questions.stimulus: Essayist: Only happiness is intrinsically valuable; other things are valuable only insofar as they contribute to happiness. Some philosophers argue that the fact that we do not approve of a bad person’s being happy shows that we value happiness only when it is deserved. This supposedly shows that we find something besides happiness to be intrinsically valuable. But the happiness people deserve is determined by the amount of happiness they bring to others. Therefore, _______.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most logically completes the final sentence of the essayist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: the notion that people can be deserving of happiness is ultimately incoherent
answerChoices.B: people do not actually value happiness as much as they think they do
answerChoices.C: the judgment that a person deserves to be happy is itself to be understood in terms of happiness
answerChoices.D: the only way to be assured of happiness is to bring happiness to those who have done something to deserve it
answerChoices.E: a truly bad person cannot actually be very happy

questions.stimulus: Sociologist: Climate and geology determine where human industry can be established. Drastic shifts in climate always result in migrations, and migrations bring about the intermingling of ideas necessary for rapid advances in civilization.
questions.questionStem: The sociologist's statements, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Climate is the primary cause of migration.
answerChoices.B: All shifts in climate produce a net gain in human progress.
answerChoices.C: A population remains settled only where the climate is fairly stable.
answerChoices.D: Populations settle in every place where human industry can be established.
answerChoices.E: Every migration is accompanied by rapid advances in civilization.

questions.stimulus: Some educators claim that it is best that school courses cover only basic subject matter, but cover it in depth. These educators argue that if students achieve a solid grasp of the basic concepts and investigatory techniques in a subject, they will be able to explore the breadth of that subject on their own after the course is over. But if they simply learn a lot of factual information, without truly understanding its significance, they will not be well equipped for further study on their own.
questions.questionStem: The educators' reasoning provides grounds for accepting which one of the following statements?

answerChoices.A: It is easier to understand how plants and animals are classified after learning how plants and animals can be useful.
answerChoices.B: It is more difficult to recall the details of a dull and complicated lecture than of a lively and interesting one.
answerChoices.C: It is easier to remember new ideas explained personally by a teacher than ideas that one explores independently.
answerChoices.D: It is easier to understand any Greek tragedy after one has analyzed a few of them in detail.
answerChoices.E: It is easier to learn many simple ideas well than to learn a few complicated ideas well.

questions.stimulus: Damming the Merv River would provide irrigation for the dry land in its upstream areas; unfortunately, a dam would reduce agricultural productivity in the fertile land downstream by reducing the availability and quality of the water there. The productivity loss in the downstream area would be greater than the productivity gain upstream, so building a dam would yield no overall gain in agricultural productivity in the region as a whole.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above most closely parallels that in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Disease-causing bacteria in eggs can be destroyed by overcooking the eggs, but the eggs then become much less appetizing; health is more important than taste, however, so it is better to overcook eggs than not to do so.
answerChoices.B: Increasing the price of transatlantic telephone calls will discourage many private individuals from making them. But since most transatlantic telephone calls are made by businesses, not by private individuals, a rate increase will not reduce telephone company profits.
answerChoices.C: A new highway will allow suburban commuters to reach the city more quickly, but not without causing increased delays within the city that will more than offset any time saved on the highway. Therefore, the highway will not reduce suburban commuters' overall commuting time.
answerChoices.D: Doctors can prescribe antibiotics for many minor illnesses, but antibiotics are expensive, and these illnesses can often be cured by rest alone. Therefore, it is better to rest at home than to see a doctor for these illnesses.
answerChoices.E: A certain chemical will kill garden pests that damage tomatoes, but that chemical will damage certain other plants more severely than the pests damage the tomatoes, so the only gardens that will benefit from the use of the chemical are those in which only tomatoes are grown.

questions.stimulus: Activist: Food producers irradiate food in order to prolong its shelf life. Five animal studies were recently conducted to investigate whether this process alters food in a way that could be dangerous to people who eat it. The studies concluded that irradiated food is safe for humans to eat. However, because these studies were subsequently found by a panel of independent scientists to be seriously flawed in their methodology, it follows that irradiated food is not safe for human consumption.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the activist's argument is flawed because that argument

answerChoices.A: treats a failure to prove a claim as constituting proof of the denial of that claim
answerChoices.B: treats methodological flaws in past studies as proof that it is currently not possible to devise methodologically adequate alternatives
answerChoices.C: fails to consider the possibility that even a study whose methodology has no serious flaws nonetheless might provide only weak support for its conclusion
answerChoices.D: fails to consider the possibility that what is safe for animals might not always be safe for human beings
answerChoices.E: fails to establish that the independent scientists know more about food irradiation than do the people who produced the five studies

questions.stimulus: One-year-olds ordinarily prefer the taste of sweet food to that of salty food. Yet if one feeds a one-year-old salty food rather than sweet food, then over a period of about a year he or she will develop a taste for the salty flavor and choose to eat salty food rather than sweet food. Thus, a young child's taste preferences can be affected by the type of food he or she has been exposed to.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: Two-year-olds do not naturally prefer salty food to sweet food.
answerChoices.B: A child's taste preferences usually change between age one and age two.
answerChoices.C: Two-year-olds do not naturally dislike salty food so much that they would not choose it over some other foods.
answerChoices.D: The salty food fed to infants in order to change their taste preferences must taste pleasant.
answerChoices.E: Sweet food is better for infant development than is salty food.

questions.stimulus: Journalist: One reason many people believe in extrasensory perception (ESP) is that they have heard of controlled experiments in which ESP is purportedly demonstrated. However, ESP is a myth and the public is deluded by these experiments, for a prominent researcher has admitted to falsifying data on psychic phenomena in order to obtain additional grants.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the journalist's argument is flawed because this argument

answerChoices.A: uses an irrelevant personal attack on the integrity of someone
answerChoices.B: infers that something must be a myth from the fact that the general public believes it
answerChoices.C: presupposes that, in general, only evidence from experiments can support beliefs
answerChoices.D: implies that all scientists who depend on grants to support their research are unreliable
answerChoices.E: overgeneralizes from the example of one deceptive researcher

questions.stimulus: One way kidney stones can form is when urine produced in the kidneys is overly concentrated with calcium or oxalate. Reducing dietary calcium has been thought, therefore, to decrease the likelihood that calcium will concentrate and form additional stones. Oddly enough, for many people the chances of recurrence are decreased by increasing calcium intake.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy described above?

answerChoices.A: Laboratory studies on animals with kidney stones reveal that they rarely get additional stones once calcium supplements are added to the diet.
answerChoices.B: Increasing dietary oxalate while reducing dietary calcium does not reduce the chances of kidney stone recurrence.
answerChoices.C: Kidney stone development is sometimes the result of an inherited disorder that can result in excessive production of calcium and oxalate.
answerChoices.D: Increasing calcium intake increases the amount of calcium eliminated through the intestines, which decreases the amount to be filtered by the kidneys.
answerChoices.E: Some kidney stones are composed of uric acid rather than a combination of calcium and oxalate.

questions.stimulus:
David: Forbidding companies from hiring permanent replacements for striking employees would be profoundly unfair. Such companies would have little leverage in their negotiations with strikers.
Lin: No, the companies would still have sufficient leverage in negotiations if they hired temporary replacements.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements is most strongly supported by the exchange between David and Lin?

answerChoices.A: David does not believe that the freedom to hire temporary replacements gives companies any leverage in their negotiations with strikers.
answerChoices.B: David and Lin believe that companies should be allowed as much leverage in negotiations as the striking employees.
answerChoices.C: David and Lin disagree over the amount of leverage companies lose in their negotiations with strikers by not being able to hire permanent replacements.
answerChoices.D: David and Lin disagree over how much leverage should be accorded companies in their negotiations with strikers.
answerChoices.E: Lin believes it is unfair to forbid companies from hiring permanent replacements for their striking employees.

questions.stimulus: A favorable biography of a politician omits certain incriminating facts about the politician that were available to anyone when the book was written. The book's author claims that, because he was unaware of these facts when he wrote the book, he is not accountable for the fact that readers were misled by this omission. In a biographer, however, ignorance of this kind cannot be used to evade blame for misleading readers.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if established, does most to justify the position advanced by the passage?

answerChoices.A: An author of a biography should not be blamed for whether the book is perceived to be favorable or unfavorable by readers of the biography.
answerChoices.B: An author of a biography should be blamed for readers' misperceptions only when facts are omitted deliberately in order to mislead the readers.
answerChoices.C: An author of a biography should not be blamed for omitting facts if those facts would have supported the author's view.
answerChoices.D: An author of a biography should be blamed for misleading readers only if facts are omitted to which the author alone had access when the biography was written.
answerChoices.E: An author of a biography should be blamed for readers' misperceptions caused by omitting facts that were widely available when the biography was written.

questions.stimulus: Logician: I have studied and thoroughly mastered the laws of logic. So to argue that I sometimes violate the laws of logic in ordinary conversation would be like arguing that some physicist circumvents the laws of physics in everyday life.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the logician's argument is questionable because this argument

answerChoices.A: ignores the fact that our conception of physical laws undergoes constant change
answerChoices.B: presents no evidence that physics is as difficult to master as logic
answerChoices.C: fails to rule out the possibility that some physicist could circumvent the laws of physics in everyday life
answerChoices.D: treats two kinds of things that differ in important respects as if they do not differ
answerChoices.E: has a conclusion that contradicts what is asserted in its premise

questions.stimulus: One thousand people in Denmark were questioned about their views on banning cigarette advertising. The sample comprised adults who are representative of the general population, and who, ten years previously, had been questioned on the same issue. Interestingly, their opinions changed little. Results show that 31 percent are in favor of such a ban, 24 percent are against it, 38 percent are in favor, but only for certain media, and 7 percent have no opinion.
questions.questionStem: The survey results in the passage best support which one of the following conclusions?

answerChoices.A: People's opinions never change very much.
answerChoices.B: A minority of Denmark's population feels that banning cigarette advertising would set a bad precedent.
answerChoices.C: Most of Denmark's population is not seriously concerned about cigarette advertising.
answerChoices.D: Most of Denmark's population favors some sort of ban on cigarette advertising.
answerChoices.E: Most of Denmark's population does not smoke cigarettes.

questions.stimulus: Passenger volume in the airline industry has declined dramatically over the past two years, and thus fewer travelers and fewer planes are using airports. Since airport expansion can be warranted only by increases in air traffic volume, and since it will probably be at least five years before passenger volume returns to and then exceeds its previous level, it seems surprising that now is the time that airports are going ahead with plans to expand their passenger terminal facilities.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, provides the best reason in favor of the airports' timing of their planned expansions?

answerChoices.A: It is generally more difficult to finance major construction projects when the economy is in a period of decline.
answerChoices.B: Low volume in passenger air travel permits airport expansion with relatively little inconvenience to the public.
answerChoices.C: A rise in fuel costs that is expected in the near future will drive up the cost of all forms of transportation, including airline travel.
answerChoices.D: When passenger volume begins to grow again after a period of decline, most airlines can, initially, absorb the increase without adding new routes or new planes.
answerChoices.E: A sustained decline in passenger travel could lead to the failure of many airlines and the absorption of their routes by those airlines that survive.

questions.stimulus: Books updating the classification systems used by many libraries are not free—in fact they are very expensive. The only way to sell copies of them is to make the potential buyers believe they need to adopt the most recent system. Thus, these frequent changes in the classification systems are just a ploy by the publishers to make libraries buy their products.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning above is most vulnerable to criticism because it

answerChoices.A: claims without providing warrant that the books are unreasonably expensive
answerChoices.B: concludes that a possible ulterior motive must be the only motive
answerChoices.C: fails to consider that there may be potential buyers of these books other than libraries
answerChoices.D: concludes that there is no need ever to change classification systems
answerChoices.E: fails to consider that the libraries cannot afford to buy every book they want

questions.stimulus: During the three months before and the three months after a major earthquake in California, students at a college there happened to be keeping a record of their dreams. After experiencing the earthquake, half of the students reported dreaming about earthquakes. During the same six months, a group of college students in Ontario who had never experienced an earthquake also recorded their dreams. Almost none of the students in Ontario reported dreaming about earthquakes. So it is clear that experiencing an earthquake can cause people to dream about earthquakes.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Before the California earthquake, no more of the students in California than of those in Ontario recorded dreams about earthquakes.
answerChoices.B: The students in California were members of a class studying dreams and dream recollection, but the students in Ontario were not.
answerChoices.C: Before they started keeping records of their dreams, many of the students in California had experienced at least one earthquake.
answerChoices.D: The students in Ontario reported having more dreams overall, per student, than the students in California did.
answerChoices.E: The students in Ontario who reported having dreams about earthquakes recorded the dreams as having occurred after the California earthquake.

questions.stimulus: It is wrong to waste our natural resources, and it is an incredible waste of resources to burn huge amounts of trash in incinerators. When trash is recycled, fewer resources are wasted. Because less trash will be recycled if an incinerator is built, the city should not build an incinerator.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the statements above?

answerChoices.A: All of the city's trash that is not recycled goes into incinerators.
answerChoices.B: By recycling more trash, the city can stop wasting resources entirely.
answerChoices.C: The most effective way to conserve resources is to recycle trash.
answerChoices.D: If the city is to avoid wasting resources, huge amounts of trash cannot be burned in any city incinerator.
answerChoices.E: If the city does not burn trash, it will not waste resources.

questions.stimulus: Human intelligence is not possible without human emotions. A computer is something that can never have emotions, so for that reason alone a computer will never be able to display intelligence.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: A computer could have emotions only if it could display intelligence.
answerChoices.B: Computer technology will not greatly advance beyond its current state.
answerChoices.C: Someone or something is intelligent only if it can identify its emotions.
answerChoices.D: The greater the capacity to feel emotions, the more intelligence there is.
answerChoices.E: Being intelligent requires the capacity to have emotions.

questions.stimulus: Several recent studies establish that most people would want to be informed if they had any serious medical condition. In each study, over 80 percent of the people surveyed indicated that they would want to be told.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, weakens the argument except:

answerChoices.A: In another recent study, most of the people surveyed indicated that they would not want to be told if they had a serious medical condition.
answerChoices.B: People often do not indicate their true feelings when responding to surveys.
answerChoices.C: Some of the researchers conducting the studies had no background in medicine.
answerChoices.D: Some questions asked in the studies suggested that reasonable people would want to be told if they had a serious medical condition.
answerChoices.E: The people surveyed in the studies were all young students in introductory psychology courses.

questions.stimulus: Historian: Political regimes that routinely censor various forms of expression on the grounds that they undermine public morality inevitably attempt to expand the categories of proscribed expression to include criticisms that these regimes perceive to threaten their power. Accordingly, many totalitarian regimes classify as blasphemous or pornographic those writings that would, if widely influential, reduce public passivity.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the historian's reasoning depends?

answerChoices.A: Unless a piece of writing expresses something that is widely believed, it is unlikely to be very popular.
answerChoices.B: Not all political regimes that routinely censor forms of expression on the grounds that they erode public morality are totalitarian regimes.
answerChoices.C: A totalitarian regime can perceive loss of public passivity as a threat to its power.
answerChoices.D: Widespread public passivity is usually needed for a regime to retain political power.
answerChoices.E: Most writings that totalitarian regimes label blasphemous or pornographic would, if widely influential, reduce public passivity.

questions.stimulus: Ethicist: Both ASA and TPA are clot-dissolving agents. Recent studies show that the more expensive agent, TPA, would save at most two more lives than would ASA out of every 50 cardiac patients to whom they are postoperatively administered. However, since the relatives of the patients who die simply because they were given the less expensive medicine would be particularly grieved, the financial saving involved in using ASA over TPA must also be weighed against such considerations.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the conclusion of the ethicist's argument?

answerChoices.A: ASA should never be given to postoperative cardiac patients in place of TPA.
answerChoices.B: TPA is a slightly more effective clot-dissolving agent than ASA.
answerChoices.C: The extra expense of TPA cannot be weighed simply against the few additional lives saved.
answerChoices.D: ASA is a less expensive clot-dissolving agent than TPA.
answerChoices.E: Relatives of a patient who has died grieve more if the patient received ASA rather than TPA.

questions.stimulus:
Ashley: Words like "of" and "upon," unlike "pencil" and "shirt," do not refer to anything.
Joshua: I agree; and since such words are meaningless, they should be abandoned.
questions.questionStem: Joshua's remarks indicate that he interpreted Ashley's statement to imply that

answerChoices.A: only words that refer to something have meaning
answerChoices.B: words that are not useful are meaningless
answerChoices.C: words that refer to something are meaningful
answerChoices.D: if a word is not useful, it should be abandoned
answerChoices.E: all words that refer to something are useful

questions.stimulus: Ethicist: Some would ban cloning on the grounds that clones would be subpeople, existing to indulge the vanity of their "originals." It is not illegal, however, to use one person as a vehicle for the ambitions of another. Some people push their children to achieve in academics or athletics. You do not have to have been born in a test tube to be an extension of someone else's ego.
questions.questionStem: The assertion that it is not illegal to use one person as a vehicle for another's ambitions is used in the ethicist's argument in which one of the following ways?

answerChoices.A: It supports the ethicist's view that society does not value individuality as much as many opponents of cloning think it does.
answerChoices.B: It supports the conclusion that forcing children to pursue academic success is not objectionable.
answerChoices.C: It is implied by the ethicist's conviction that clones are not subpeople.
answerChoices.D: It supports the ethicist's view that vanity's being the motivation for cloning is not enough of a reason to ban cloning.
answerChoices.E: It describes a legal position that the ethicist argues should be changed.

questions.stimulus:
Selena: Asteroid impact on the Earth caused the extinction of the dinosaurs by raising vast clouds of dust, thus blocking the Sun's rays and cooling the planet beyond the capacity of the dinosaurs, or perhaps the vegetation that supported them, to adapt. A worldwide dust layer provides evidence of asteroid impact at approximately the correct time, and a huge crater exists on the edge of the Yucatán peninsula in Mexico.
Trent: That asteroid crater is not large enough for the requisite amount of dust to have been produced. Besides, the extinction of dinosaur species took many years, not just one or two. So the extinctions must have been due not to asteroid impact on the Earth but to some other kind of cause.
questions.questionStem: Trent’s argument assumes that

answerChoices.A: any collision of an asteroid with the Earth would have occurred on a land area rather than an ocean
answerChoices.B: dinosaurs in the neighborhood of an asteroid impact but not within the zone of direct impact would have survived such an impact
answerChoices.C: any event that takes place over a long period of time has many different kinds of causes
answerChoices.D: dust from the impact of an asteroid on the Earth would not have had any cooling effect on the climate
answerChoices.E: no more than one large asteroid struck the Earth during the period when the dinosaurs were becoming extinct

questions.stimulus: It is impossible to do science without measuring. It is impossible to measure without having first selected units of measurement. Hence, science is arbitrary, since the selection of a unit of measurement—kilometer, mile, fathom, etc.—is always arbitrary.
questions.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most similar to that in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Long hours of practice are necessary for developing musical skill. One must develop one's musical skill in order to perform difficult music. But long hours of practice are tedious. So performing difficult music is tedious.
answerChoices.B: You have to advertise to run an expanding business, but advertising is expensive. Hence, it is expensive to run a business.
answerChoices.C: It is permissible to sit on the park benches. To sit on the park benches one must walk to them. One way to walk to them is by walking on the grass. So it is permissible to walk on the grass.
answerChoices.D: It is impossible to be a manager without evaluating people. The process of evaluation is necessarily subjective. Thus, people resent managers because they resent being evaluated subjectively.
answerChoices.E: Some farming on the plains requires irrigation. This irrigation now uses water pumped from aquifers. But aquifers have limited capacity and continued pumping will eventually exhaust them. Thus, a new source of water will have to be found in order for such farming to continue indefinitely.

questions.stimulus:
Professor Beckstein: American Sign Language is the native language of many North Americans. Therefore, it is not a foreign language, and for that reason alone, no student should be permitted to satisfy the university's foreign language requirement by learning it.
Professor Sedley: According to your argument, students should not be allowed to satisfy the university's foreign language requirement by learning French or Spanish either, since they too are the native languages of many North Americans. Yet many students currently satisfy the requirement by studying French or Spanish, and it would be ridiculous to begin prohibiting them from doing so.
questions.questionStem: Their statements commit Professors Beckstein and Sedley to disagreeing about which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: whether American Sign Language is the native language of a significant number of North Americans
answerChoices.B: whether any North American whose native language is not English should be allowed to fulfill the university's foreign language requirement by studying his or her own native language
answerChoices.C: whether the university ought to retain a foreign language requirement
answerChoices.D: whether any other universities in North America permit their students to fulfill a foreign language requirement by learning American Sign Language
answerChoices.E: whether the fact that a language is the native language of many North Americans justifies prohibiting its use to fulfill the university's foreign language requirement

questions.stimulus:
Professor Beckstein: American Sign Language is the native language of many North Americans. Therefore, it is not a foreign language, and for that reason alone, no student should be permitted to satisfy the university's foreign language requirement by learning it.
Professor Sedley: According to your argument, students should not be allowed to satisfy the university's foreign language requirement by learning French or Spanish either, since they too are the native languages of many North Americans. Yet many students currently satisfy the requirement by studying French or Spanish, and it would be ridiculous to begin prohibiting them from doing so.
questions.questionStem: Professor Sedley uses which one of the following strategies of argumentation in responding to Professor Beckstein's argument?

answerChoices.A: attempting to demonstrate that the reasoning used to reach a certain conclusion leads to another conclusion that is undesirable
answerChoices.B: trying to show that a certain conclusion contradicts some of the evidence used to support it
answerChoices.C: questioning an opponent's authority to address the issue under discussion
answerChoices.D: offering an alternative explanation of the facts used to arrive at a specific conclusion
answerChoices.E: agreeing with the conclusion of a particular argument while rejecting the evidence used to support the conclusion

questions.stimulus: So-called “engineered foods," usually in powder or liquid form, consist of protein that is distilled from natural sources and supplemented with vitamins and minerals. Although the amino acids contained in such products stimulate the production of growth hormones, these hormones produce growth in connective tissue rather than in muscle mass; this does not improve muscle strength. Hence, athletes, who need to improve their muscular strength, should not consume engineered foods.
questions.questionStem: The argument depends on assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: An increase in muscle mass produces an increase in strength.
answerChoices.B: People who are not athletes require neither stronger connective tissue nor muscle strength.
answerChoices.C: If an engineered food does not improve muscle strength, there is no other substantial advantage to athletes from consuming it.
answerChoices.D: Consuming engineered foods that provide nutrients that can be obtained more easily elsewhere is unhealthy.
answerChoices.E: Growth of muscle mass enhances muscle strength only when accompanied by growth of connective tissue.

questions.stimulus: Some types of organisms originated through endosymbiosis, the engulfing of one organism by another so that a part of the former becomes a functioning part of the latter. An unusual nucleomorph, a structure that contains DNA and resembles a cell nucleus, has been discovered within a plant known as a chlorarachniophyte. Two versions of a particular gene have been found in the DNA of this nucleomorph, and one would expect to find only a single version of this gene if the nucleomorph were not the remains of an engulfed organism's nucleus.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Only organisms of types that originated through endosymbiosis contain nucleomorphs.
answerChoices.B: A nucleomorph within the chlorarachniophyte holds all of the genetic material of some other organism.
answerChoices.C: Nucleomorphs originated when an organism endosymbiotically engulfed a chlorarachniophyte.
answerChoices.D: Two organisms will not undergo endosymbiosis unless at least one of them contains a nucleomorph.
answerChoices.E: Chlorarachniophytes emerged as the result of two organisms having undergone endosymbiosis.

questions.stimulus: Reviewer: Although finalism—the view that there are purposes in nature—has been universally rejected, this book launches another attack on that view. Its arguments are based on a complete misunderstanding of the operation of pure chance in nature and so it fails as a critique of finalism. Finalism, therefore, is clearly more plausible than people have thought.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most closely parallel in its flawed reasoning to the flawed reasoning in the reviewer's argument?

answerChoices.A: No literary historian still believes the claim that a single author wrote every word of this collection of works. Evidence on which that claim is based can be shown to be false by manuscript dating techniques, but these dating results have not been cited before. Therefore, it is quite likely that a single author did write every word of this collection of works.
answerChoices.B: Few botanists deny that a recently discovered fern is the same species represented in ancient fossils. The botanists who first discovered this specimen deny that it is the same species as the ancient one, but they have spent little time studying the specimen. Therefore, the specimen is likely to be the same species represented in the ancient fossils.
answerChoices.C: Bicycle engineers no longer believe that aluminum is as good a frame material as titanium. An engineer at Ace Bicycles has argued that aluminum is not as good as titanium because it breaks under pressure. But he is confused about the kind of pressure exerted on bicycles. Therefore, the claim that aluminum is as good a frame material as titanium makes more sense than bicycle engineers believe.
answerChoices.D: Experts agree that red wines from France's Bordeaux region are the best in the world, and five are on this year's list of the world's top ten red wines. However, the best currently available Bordeaux wines are more than one year old, whereas other countries' best are not. Therefore, it is false that Bordeaux red wines are the best in the world this year.
answerChoices.E: Sociologists agree that the psychological development of children may be impaired by watching too much television, though researchers argued recently that the quality of the parent-child relationship is more developmentally significant than television viewing. These researchers did not consider the long-term impact of television on children, so it is quite likely that the psychological development of children is impaired by watching too much television.

questions.stimulus: Appliance dealer: Appliance manufacturers commonly modify existing models without giving the modified versions new model names. Some people have complained that this practice makes it impossible for consumers to be certain that the appliance they are about to purchase is identical to the one they may have seen at a neighbor's or read about in a consumer magazine. Yet manufacturers' modifications to existing models are invariably improvements that benefit the buyer. Therefore, consumers have little reason to object to this practice.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the dealer's argument?

answerChoices.A: Appliances are generally purchased with the expectation that they will continue to be used for several years.
answerChoices.B: Appliances usually carry a model number that provides substantially more detailed information about the product than does the model name.
answerChoices.C: Appliance manufacturers frequently sell identical products under several different model names.
answerChoices.D: Improved versions of appliances typically become available before vendors have stopped selling the older versions of the appliance with the same model name.
answerChoices.E: The high cost of product advertising makes appliance manufacturers generally reluctant to change model names to reflect modifications to their products.

questions.stimulus: In our solar system only one of the nine planets—Earth— qualifies as fit to sustain life. Nonetheless, using this ratio, and considering the astonishingly large number of planetary systems in the universe, we must conclude that the number of planets fit to sustain some form of life is extremely large.
questions.questionStem: The argument is questionable because it presumes which one of the following without providing justification?

answerChoices.A: If a planet is Earthlike, then life will arise on it.
answerChoices.B: Our solar system is similar to many other planetary systems in the universe.
answerChoices.C: The conditions necessary for life to begin are well understood.
answerChoices.D: Life similar to Earth's could evolve under conditions very different from those on Earth.
answerChoices.E: Most other planetary systems in the universe have nine planets.

questions.stimulus: Sociologist: Suggestions for improved efficiency that derive from employers are unlikely to elicit positive responses from employees, who tend to resent suggestions they did not generate. An employer should therefore engage the employee in a nonthreatening dialogue that emphasizes the positive contributions of the employee to the development of such ideas. Then the ideas employers want to try will be implemented more quickly and effectively.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the sociologist's reasoning?

answerChoices.A: Employees are more likely to accept suggestions for improved efficiency when these suggestions are not obviously directed at them.
answerChoices.B: Employees are more likely to carry out ideas for improved efficiency that they believe they have participated in generating.
answerChoices.C: Employees are more likely to implement ideas for improved efficiency that derive from a dialogue in which they have participated than from a dialogue in which they have not participated.
answerChoices.D: Employees are more likely to generate good ideas for improved efficiency when they do not feel resentment about the process that attempts to formulate such ideas.
answerChoices.E: Employees are more likely to resent employers who attempt to implement the employers' rather than the employees' ideas for improved efficiency.

questions.stimulus: The following passage is used for Section 4, questions 1 through 2. Ms. Smith: I am upset that my son’s entire class lost two days of recess because some of the children were throwing raisins in the cafeteria. He was not throwing raisins, and it was clear to everyone just who the culprits were. Principal: I’m sorry you’re upset, Ms. Smith, but your son’s situation is like being caught in a traffic jam caused by an accident. People who aren’t involved in the accident nevertheless have to suffer by sitting there in the middle of it.
questions.questionStem: 1. If the principal is speaking sincerely, then it can be inferred from what the principal says that the principal believes that

answerChoices.A: many children were throwing raisins in the cafeteria
answerChoices.B: Ms. Smith’s son might not have thrown raisins in the cafeteria
answerChoices.C: after an accident the resulting traffic jams are generally caused by police activity
answerChoices.D: Ms. Smith’s son knows who it was that threw raisins in the cafeteria
answerChoices.E: losing two days of recess will deter future disruptions

questions.stimulus: The following passage is used for Section 4, questions 1 through 2. Ms. Smith: I am upset that my son’s entire class lost two days of recess because some of the children were throwing raisins in the cafeteria. He was not throwing raisins, and it was clear to everyone just who the culprits were. Principal: I’m sorry you’re upset, Ms. Smith, but your son’s situation is like being caught in a traffic jam caused by an accident. People who aren’t involved in the accident nevertheless have to suffer by sitting there in the middle of it.
questions.questionStem: 2. The principal’s response to Ms. Smith’s complaint is most vulnerable to criticism on which one of the following grounds?

answerChoices.A: It makes a generalization about all the children in the class which is not justified by the facts.
answerChoices.B: It suggests that throwing raisins in the cafeteria produces as much inconvenience as does being caught in a traffic jam.
answerChoices.C: It does not acknowledge the fact that a traffic jam following an accident is unavoidable while the mass punishment was avoidable.
answerChoices.D: It assumes that Ms. Smith’s son is guilty when there is evidence to the contrary which the principal has disregarded.
answerChoices.E: It attempts to confuse the point at issue by introducing irrelevant facts about the incident.

questions.stimulus: Journalist: Obviously, though some animals are purely carnivorous, none would survive without plants. But the dependence is mutual. Many plant species would never have come to be had there been no animals to pollinate, fertilize, and broadcast their seeds. Also, plants’ photosynthetic activity would deplete the carbon dioxide in Earth’s atmosphere were it not constantly being replenished by the exhalation of animals, engine fumes, and smoke from fires, many set by human beings.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the journalist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The photosynthetic activity of plants is necessary for animal life, but animal life is also necessary for the occurrence of photosynthesis in plants.
answerChoices.B: Some purely carnivorous animals would not survive without plants.
answerChoices.C: The chemical composition of Earth and its atmosphere depends, at least to some extent, on the existence and activities of the animals that populate Earth.
answerChoices.D: Human activity is part of what prevents plants from depleting the oxygen in Earth’s atmosphere on which plants and animals alike depend.
answerChoices.E: Just as animals are dependent on plants for their survival, plants are dependent on animals for theirs.

questions.stimulus: The government-owned gas company has begun selling stoves and other gas appliances to create a larger market for its gas. Merchants who sell such products complain that the competition will hurt their businesses. That may well be; however, the government-owned gas company is within its rights. After all, the owner of a private gas company might well decide to sell such appliances and surely there would be nothing wrong with that.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: Government-owned companies have the right to do whatever private businesses have the right to do.
answerChoices.B: A government should always take seriously the complaints of merchants.
answerChoices.C: Private businesses have no right to compete with government monopolies.
answerChoices.D: There is nothing wrong with a government-owned company selling products so long as owners of private companies do not complain.
answerChoices.E: There is nothing wrong with private companies competing against each other.

questions.stimulus: Toxicologist: A survey of oil-refinery workers who work with MBTE, an ingredient currently used in some smog-reducing gasolines, found an alarming incidence of complaints about headaches, fatigue, and shortness of breath. Since gasoline containing MBTE will soon be widely used, we can expect an increased incidence of headaches, fatigue, and shortness of breath.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, strengthens the toxicologist’s argument except:

answerChoices.A: Most oil-refinery workers who do not work with MBTE do not have serious health problems involving headaches, fatigue, and shortness of breath.
answerChoices.B: Headaches, fatigue, and shortness of breath are among the symptoms of several medical conditions that are potentially serious threats to public health.
answerChoices.C: Since the time when gasoline containing MBTE was first introduced in a few metropolitan areas, those areas reported an increase in the number of complaints about headaches, fatigue, and shortness of breath.
answerChoices.D: Regions in which only gasoline containing MBTE is used have a much greater incidence of headaches, fatigue, and shortness of breath than do similar regions in which only MBTE-free gasoline is used.
answerChoices.E: The oil-refinery workers surveyed were carefully selected to be representative of the broader population in their medical histories prior to exposure to MBTE, as well as in other relevant respects.

questions.stimulus: In any field, experience is required for a proficient person to become an expert. Through experience, a proficient person gradually develops a repertory of model situations that allows an immediate, intuitive response to each new situation. This is the hallmark of expertise, and for this reason computerized “expert systems” cannot be as good as human experts. Although computers have the ability to store millions of bits of information, the knowledge of human experts, who benefit from the experience of thousands of situations, is not stored within their brains in the form of rules and facts.
questions.questionStem: The argument requires the assumption of which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Computers can show no more originality in responding to a situation than that built into them by their designers.
answerChoices.B: The knowledge of human experts cannot be adequately rendered into the type of information that a computer can store.
answerChoices.C: Human experts rely on information that can be expressed by rules and facts when they respond to new situations.
answerChoices.D: Future advances in computer technology will not render computers capable of sorting through greater amounts of information.
answerChoices.E: Human experts rely heavily on intuition while they are developing a repertory of model situations.

questions.stimulus: When drivers are deprived of sleep there are definite behavioral changes, such as slower responses to stimuli and a reduced ability to concentrate, but people’s self-awareness of these changes is poor. Most drivers think they can tell when they are about to fall asleep, but they cannot.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following illustrates the principle that the passage illustrates except:

answerChoices.A: People who have been drinking alcohol are not good judges of whether they are too drunk to drive.
answerChoices.B: Elementary school students who dislike arithmetic are not good judges of whether multiplication tables should be included in the school’s curriculum.
answerChoices.C: Industrial workers who have just been exposed to noxious fumes are not good judges of whether they should keep working.
answerChoices.D: People who have just donated blood and have become faint are not good judges of whether they are ready to walk out of the facility.
answerChoices.E: People who are being treated for schizophrenia are not good judges of whether they should continue their medical treatments.

questions.stimulus: Politician: My opponent says our zoning laws too strongly promote suburban single-family dwellings and should be changed to encourage other forms of housing like apartment buildings. Yet he lives in a house in the country. His lifestyle contradicts his own argument, which should therefore not be taken seriously.
questions.questionStem: The politician’s reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that

answerChoices.A: its characterization of the opponent’s lifestyle reveals the politician’s own prejudice against constructing apartment buildings
answerChoices.B: it neglects the fact that apartment buildings can be built in the suburbs just as easily as in the center of the city
answerChoices.C: it fails to mention the politician’s own living situation
answerChoices.D: its discussion of the opponent’s lifestyle is irrelevant to the merits of the opponent’s argument
answerChoices.E: it ignores the possibility that the opponent may have previously lived in an apartment building

questions.stimulus: Consumers are deeply concerned about the quantity of plastic packaging on the market and have spurred manufacturers to find ways to recycle plastic materials. Despite their efforts, however, only 6.5 percent of plastic is now being recycled, as compared to 33 percent of container glass.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, helps to explain the relatively low rate of plastic recycling except:

answerChoices.A: Many factories are set up to accept and make economical use of recycled glass, whereas there are few factories that make products out of recycled plastic.
answerChoices.B: Many plastic products are incompatible and cannot be recycled together, whereas most containers made of glass are compatible.
answerChoices.C: The manufacture of new plastic depletes oil reserves, whereas the manufacture of new glass uses renewable resources.
answerChoices.D: Unlike glass, which can be heated to thousands of degrees during the recycling process to burn off contaminants, recycled plastic cannot be heated enough to sterilize it.
answerChoices.E: Plastic polymers tend to break down during the recycling process and weaken the resulting product, whereas glass does not break down.

questions.stimulus: Technological progress makes economic growth and widespread prosperity possible; it also makes a worker’s particular skills less crucial to production. Yet workers’ satisfaction in their work depends on their believing that their work is difficult and requires uncommon skills. Clearly, then, technological progress _______.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most logically completes the argument?

answerChoices.A: decreases the quality of most products
answerChoices.B: provides benefits only to those whose work is not directly affected by it
answerChoices.C: is generally opposed by the workers whose work will be directly affected by it
answerChoices.D: causes workers to feel less satisfaction in their work
answerChoices.E: eliminates many workers’ jobs

questions.stimulus: Environmentalist: The complex ecosystem of the North American prairie has largely been destroyed to produce cattle feed. But the prairie ecosystem once supported 30 to 70 million bison, whereas North American agriculture now supports about 50 million cattle. Since bison yield as much meat as cattle, and the natural prairie required neither pesticides, machinery, nor government subsidies, returning as much land as possible to an uncultivated state could restore biodiversity without a major decrease in meat production.
