Elaine: The purpose of art museums is to preserve artworks and make them available to the public. Museums, therefore, should seek to acquire and display the best examples of artworks from each artistic period and genre, even if some of these works are not recognized by experts as masterpieces.
Frederick: Art museums ought to devote their limited resources to acquiring the works of recognized masters in order to ensure the preservation of the greatest artworks.
questions.questionStem: Elaine's and Frederick's statements provide the most support for the claim that they would disagree about whether

answerChoices.A: many artistic masterpieces are not recognized as such by art experts
answerChoices.B: museums should seek to represent all genres of art in their collections
answerChoices.C: art museums should seek to preserve works of art
answerChoices.D: an art museum ought to acquire an unusual example of a period or genre if more characteristic examples are prohibitively expensive
answerChoices.E: all of the artworks that experts identify as masterpieces are actually masterpieces

questions.stimulus: Science columnist: It is clear why humans have so many diseases in common with cats. Many human diseases are genetically based, and cats are genetically closer to humans than are any other mammals except nonhuman primates. Each of the genes identified so far in cats has an exact counterpart in humans.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the science columnist's explanation for the claim that humans have so many diseases in common with cats?

answerChoices.A: Cats have built up resistance to many of the diseases they have in common with humans.
answerChoices.B: Most diseases that humans have in common with cats have no genetic basis.
answerChoices.C: Cats have more diseases in common with nonhuman primates than with humans.
answerChoices.D: Many of the diseases humans have in common with cats are mild and are rarely diagnosed.
answerChoices.E: Humans have more genes in common with nonhuman primates than with cats.

questions.stimulus: This region must find new ways to help business grow. After all, shoe manufacturing used to be a major local industry, but recently has experienced severe setbacks due to overseas competition, so there is a need for expansion into new manufacturing areas. Moreover, our outdated public policy generally inhibits business growth.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion drawn in the argument?

answerChoices.A: The region needs to find new ways to enhance business growth.
answerChoices.B: Shoe manufacturing is no longer a major source of income in the region.
answerChoices.C: Shoe manufacturing in the region has dramatically declined due to overseas competition.
answerChoices.D: Business in the region must expand into new areas of manufacturing.
answerChoices.E: Outdated public policy inhibits business growth in the region.

questions.stimulus: As a result of modern medicine, more people have been able to enjoy long and pain-free lives. But the resulting increase in life expectancy has contributed to a steady increase in the proportion of the population that is of advanced age. This population shift is creating potentially devastating financial problems for some social welfare programs.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following propositions is most precisely exemplified by the situation presented above?

answerChoices.A: Technical or scientific innovation cannot be the solution to all problems.
answerChoices.B: Implementing technological innovations should be delayed until the resulting social changes can be managed.
answerChoices.C: Every enhancement of the quality of life has unavoidable negative consequences.
answerChoices.D: All social institutions are affected by a preoccupation with prolonging life.
answerChoices.E: Solving one set of problems can create a different set of problems.

questions.stimulus: Since Jackie is such a big fan of Moral Vacuum's music, she will probably like The Cruel Herd's new album. Like Moral Vacuum, The Cruel Herd on this album plays complex rock music that employs the acoustic instrumentation and harmonic sophistication of early sixties jazz. The Cruel Herd also has very witty lyrics, full of puns and sardonic humor, like some of Moral Vacuum's best lyrics.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Jackie has not previously cared for The Cruel Herd, but on the new album The Cruel Herd's previous musical arranger has been replaced by Moral Vacuum's musical arranger.
answerChoices.B: Though The Cruel Herd's previous albums' production quality was not great, the new album is produced by one of the most widely employed producers in the music industry.
answerChoices.C: Like Moral Vacuum, The Cruel Herd regularly performs in clubs popular with many students at the university that Jackie attends.
answerChoices.D: All of the music that Jackie prefers to listen to on a regular basis is rock music.
answerChoices.E: Jackie's favorite Moral Vacuum songs have lyrics that are somber and marked by a strong political awareness.

questions.stimulus: Superconductors are substances that conduct electricity without resistance at low temperatures. Their use, however, will never be economically feasible, unless there is a substance that superconducts at a temperature above minus 148 degrees Celsius. If there is such a substance, that substance must be an alloy of niobium and germanium. Unfortunately, such alloys superconduct at temperatures no higher than minus 160 degrees Celsius.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

answerChoices.A: The use of superconductors will never be economically feasible.
answerChoices.B: If the alloys of niobium and germanium do not superconduct at temperatures above minus 148 degrees Celsius, then there are other substances that will do so.
answerChoices.C: The use of superconductors could be economically feasible if there is a substance that superconducts at temperatures below minus 148 degrees Celsius.
answerChoices.D: Alloys of niobium and germanium do not superconduct at temperatures below minus 160 degrees Celsius.
answerChoices.E: No use of alloys of niobium and germanium will ever be economically feasible.

questions.stimulus: Doctor: In three separate studies, researchers compared children who had slept with night-lights in their rooms as infants to children who had not. In the first study, the children who had slept with night-lights proved more likely to be nearsighted, but the later studies found no correlation between night-lights and nearsightedness. However, the children in the first study were younger than those in the later studies. This suggests that if night-lights cause nearsightedness, the effect disappears with age.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most weaken the doctor's argument?

answerChoices.A: A fourth study comparing infants who were currently sleeping with night-lights to infants who were not did not find any correlation between night-lights and nearsightedness.
answerChoices.B: On average, young children who are already very nearsighted are no more likely to sleep with night-lights than young children who are not already nearsighted.
answerChoices.C: In a study involving children who had not slept with night-lights as infants but had slept with night-lights when they were older, most of the children studied were not nearsighted.
answerChoices.D: The two studies in which no correlation was found did not examine enough children to provide significant support for any conclusion regarding a causal relationship between night-lights and nearsightedness.
answerChoices.E: In a fourth study involving 100 children who were older than those in any of the first three studies, several of the children who had slept with night-lights as infants were nearsighted.

questions.stimulus: Global surveys estimate the earth's population of nesting female leatherback turtles has fallen by more than two-thirds in the past 15 years. Any species whose population declines by more than two-thirds in 15 years is in grave danger of extinction, so the leatherback turtle is clearly in danger of extinction.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption that the argument requires?

answerChoices.A: The decline in the population of nesting female leatherback turtles is proportional to the decline in the leatherback turtle population as a whole.
answerChoices.B: If the global population of leatherback turtles falls by more than two-thirds over the next 15 years, the species will eventually become extinct.
answerChoices.C: The global population of leatherback turtles consists in roughly equal numbers of females and males.
answerChoices.D: Very few leatherback turtles exist in captivity.
answerChoices.E: The only way to ensure the continued survival of leatherback turtles in the wild is to breed them in captivity.

questions.stimulus: Public health experts have waged a long-standing educational campaign to get people to eat more vegetables, which are known to help prevent cancer. Unfortunately, the campaign has had little impact on people's diets. The reason is probably that many people simply dislike the taste of most vegetables. Thus, the campaign would probably be more effective if it included information on ways to make vegetables more appetizing.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: The campaign to get people to eat more vegetables has had little impact on the diets of most people who love the taste of vegetables.
answerChoices.B: Some ways of making vegetables more appetizing diminish vegetables' ability to help prevent cancer.
answerChoices.C: People who find a few vegetables appetizing typically do not eat substantially more vegetables than do people who dislike the taste of most vegetables.
answerChoices.D: People who dislike the taste of most vegetables would eat many more vegetables if they knew how to make them more appetizing.
answerChoices.E: The only way to make the campaign to get people to eat more vegetables more effective would be to ensure that anyone who at present dislikes the taste of certain vegetables learns to find those vegetables appetizing.

questions.stimulus: Pure science—research with no immediate commercial or technological application—is a public good. Such research requires a great amount of financial support and does not yield profits in the short term. Since private corporations will not undertake to support activities that do not yield short-term profits, a society that wants to reap the benefits of pure science ought to use public funds to support such research.
questions.questionStem: The claim about private corporations serves which one of the following functions in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It expresses the conclusion of the argument.
answerChoices.B: It explains what is meant by the expression "pure research" in the context of the argument.
answerChoices.C: It distracts attention from the point at issue by introducing a different but related goal.
answerChoices.D: It supports the conclusion by ruling out an alternative way of achieving the benefits mentioned.
answerChoices.E: It illustrates a case where unfortunate consequences result from a failure to accept the recommendation offered.

questions.stimulus:
Melinda: Hazard insurance decreases an individual's risk by judiciously spreading the risk among many policyholders.
Jack: I disagree. It makes sense for me to buy fire insurance for my house, but I don't see how doing so lessens the chances that my house will burn down.
questions.questionStem: Jack's response most clearly trades on an ambiguity in which one of the following expressions used by Melinda?

answerChoices.A: judiciously spreading
answerChoices.B: many policyholders
answerChoices.C: risk
answerChoices.D: decreases
answerChoices.E: hazard insurance

questions.stimulus: Some doctors believe that a certain drug reduces the duration of episodes of vertigo, claiming that the average duration of vertigo for people who suffer from it has decreased since the drug was introduced. However, during a recent three-month shortage of the drug, there was no significant change in the average duration of vertigo. Thus, we can conclude that the drug has no effect on the duration of vertigo.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: If a drug made a difference in the duration of vertigo, a three-month shortage of that drug would have caused a significant change in the average duration of vertigo.
answerChoices.B: If there were any change in the average duration of vertigo since the introduction of the drug, it would have demonstrated that the drug has an effect on the duration of vertigo.
answerChoices.C: A period of time greater than three months would not have been better to use in judging whether the drug has an effect on the duration of vertigo.
answerChoices.D: Changes in diet and smoking habits are not responsible for any change in the average duration of vertigo since the introduction of the drug.
answerChoices.E: There are various significant factors other than drugs that decrease the duration of vertigo for many people who suffer from it.

questions.stimulus: It has been suggested that a television set should be thought of as nothing more than "a toaster with pictures" and that since we let market forces determine the design of kitchen appliances we can let them determine what is seen on television. But that approach is too simple. Some governmental control is needed, since television is so important politically and culturally. It is a major source of commercial entertainment. It plays an important political role because it is the primary medium through which many voters obtain information about current affairs. It is a significant cultural force in that in the average home it is on for more than five hours a day.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the role played in the argument by the claim that television is so important politically and culturally?

answerChoices.A: It states a view that the argument as a whole is designed to discredit.
answerChoices.B: It is an intermediate conclusion that is offered in support of the claim that a television set should be thought of as nothing more than "a toaster with pictures" and for which the claim that we can let market forces determine what is seen on television is offered as support.
answerChoices.C: It is a premise that is offered in support of the claim that we let market forces determine the design of kitchen appliances.
answerChoices.D: It is an intermediate conclusion that is offered in support of the claim that some governmental control of television is needed and for which the claim that the television is on for more than five hours a day in the average home is offered as partial support.
answerChoices.E: It is a premise that is offered in support of the claim that television is the primary medium through which many voters obtain information about current affairs.

questions.stimulus: Earthworms, vital to the health of soil, prefer soil that is approximately neutral on the acid-to-alkaline scale. Since decomposition of dead plants makes the top layer of soil highly acidic, application of crushed limestone, which is highly alkaline, to the soil's surface should make the soil more attractive to earthworms.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: As far as soil health is concerned, aiding the decomposition of dead plants is the most important function performed by earthworms.
answerChoices.B: After its application to the soil's surface, crushed limestone stays in the soil's top layer long enough to neutralize some of the top layer's acidity.
answerChoices.C: Crushed limestone contains available calcium and magnesium, both of which are just as vital as earthworms to healthy soil.
answerChoices.D: By itself, acidity of soil does nothing to hasten decomposition of dead plants.
answerChoices.E: Alkaline soil is significantly more likely to benefit from an increased earthworm population than is highly acidic soil.

questions.stimulus: Jurist: A nation's laws must be viewed as expressions of a moral code that transcends those laws and serves as a measure of their adequacy. Otherwise, a society can have no sound basis for preferring any given set of laws to all others. Thus, any moral prohibition against the violation of statutes must leave room for exceptions.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the jurist's statements?

answerChoices.A: Those who formulate statutes are not primarily concerned with morality when they do so.
answerChoices.B: Sometimes criteria other than the criteria derived from a moral code should be used in choosing one set of laws over another.
answerChoices.C: Unless it is legally forbidden ever to violate some moral rules, moral behavior and compliance with laws are indistinguishable.
answerChoices.D: There is no statute that a nation's citizens have a moral obligation to obey.
answerChoices.E: A nation's laws can sometimes come into conflict with the moral code they express.

questions.stimulus: An association between two types of conditions does not establish that conditions of one type cause conditions of the other type. Even persistent and inviolable association is inconclusive; such association is often due to conditions of both types being effects of the same kind of cause.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following judgments most closely conforms to the principle stated above?

answerChoices.A: Some people claim that rapid growth of the money supply is what causes inflation. But this is a naive view. What these people do not realize is that growth in the money supply and inflation are actually one and the same phenomenon.
answerChoices.B: People who have high blood pressure tend to be overweight. But before we draw any inferences, we should consider that an unhealthy lifestyle can cause high blood pressure, and weight gain can result from living unhealthily.
answerChoices.C: In some areas, there is a high correlation between ice cream consumption and the crime rate. Some researchers have proposed related third factors, but we cannot rule out that the correlation is purely coincidental.
answerChoices.D: People's moods seem to vary with the color of the clothes they wear. Dark colors are associated with gloomy moods, and bright colors are associated with cheerful moods. This correlation resolves nothing, however. We cannot say whether it is the colors that cause the moods or the converse.
answerChoices.E: Linguists propose that the similarities between Greek and Latin are due to their common descent from an earlier language. But how are we to know that the similarities are not actually due to the two languages having borrowed structures from one another, as with the languages Marathi and Telegu?

questions.stimulus: Salesperson: When a salesperson is successful, it is certain that that person has been in sales for at least three years. This is because to succeed as a salesperson, one must first establish a strong client base, and studies have shown that anyone who spends at least three years developing a client base can eventually make a comfortable living in sales.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the salesperson's argument is vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it fails to consider the possibility that

answerChoices.A: salespeople who have spent three years developing a client base might not yet be successful in sales
answerChoices.B: some salespeople require fewer than three years in which to develop a strong client base
answerChoices.C: a salesperson who has not spent three years developing a client base may not succeed in sales
answerChoices.D: it takes longer than three years for a salesperson to develop a strong client base
answerChoices.E: few salespeople can afford to spend three years building a client base

questions.stimulus: People who have habitually slept less than six hours a night and then begin sleeping eight or more hours a night typically begin to feel much less anxious. Therefore, most people who sleep less than six hours a night can probably cause their anxiety levels to fall by beginning to sleep at least eight hours a night.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in which one of the following arguments is most similar to that in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: When a small company first begins to advertise on the Internet, its financial situation generally improves. This shows that most small companies that have never advertised on the Internet can probably improve their financial situation by doing so.
answerChoices.B: Certain small companies that had never previously advertised on the Internet have found that their financial situations began to improve after they started to do so. So most small companies can probably improve their financial situations by starting to advertise on the Internet.
answerChoices.C: It must be true that any small company that increases its Internet advertising will improve its financial situation, since most small companies that advertise on the Internet improved their financial situations soon after they first began to do so.
answerChoices.D: Usually, the financial situation of a small company that has never advertised on the Internet will improve only if that company starts to advertise on the Internet. Therefore, a typical small company that has never advertised on the Internet can probably improve its financial situation by doing so.
answerChoices.E: A small company's financial situation usually improves soon after that company first begins to advertise on the Internet. Thus, most small companies that have never advertised on the Internet could probably become financially strong.

questions.stimulus: Biologist: Lions and tigers are so similar to each other anatomically that their skeletons are virtually indistinguishable. But their behaviors are known to be quite different: tigers hunt only as solitary individuals, whereas lions hunt in packs. Thus, paleontologists cannot reasonably infer solely on the basis of skeletal anatomy that extinct predatory animals, such as certain dinosaurs, hunted in packs.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion is properly drawn if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: The skeletons of lions and tigers are at least somewhat similar in structure in certain key respects to the skeletons of at least some extinct predatory animals.
answerChoices.B: There have existed at least two species of extinct predatory dinosaurs that were so similar to each other that their skeletal anatomy is virtually indistinguishable.
answerChoices.C: If skeletal anatomy alone is ever an inadequate basis for inferring a particular species' hunting behavior, then it is never reasonable to infer, based on skeletal anatomy alone, that a species of animals hunted in packs.
answerChoices.D: If any two animal species with virtually indistinguishable skeletal anatomy exhibit quite different hunting behaviors, then it is never reasonable to infer, based solely on the hunting behavior of those species, that the two species have the same skeletal anatomy.
answerChoices.E: If it is unreasonable to infer, solely on the basis of differences in skeletal anatomy, that extinct animals of two distinct species differed in their hunting behavior, then the skeletal remains of those two species are virtually indistinguishable.

questions.stimulus: The trees always blossom in May if April rainfall exceeds 5 centimeters. If April rainfall exceeds 5 centimeters, then the reservoirs are always full on May 1. The reservoirs were not full this May 1 and thus the trees will not blossom this May.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following exhibits a flawed pattern of reasoning most similar to the flawed pattern of reasoning in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: If the garlic is in the pantry, then it is still fresh. And the potatoes are on the basement stairs if the garlic is in the pantry. The potatoes are not on the basement stairs, so the garlic is not still fresh.
answerChoices.B: The jar reaches optimal temperature if it is held over the burner for 2 minutes. The contents of the jar liquefy immediately if the jar is at optimal temperature. The jar was held over the burner for 2 minutes, so the contents of the jar must have liquefied immediately.
answerChoices.C: A book is classified "special" if it is more than 200 years old. If a book was set with wooden type, then it is more than 200 years old. This book is not classified "special," so it is not printed with wooden type.
answerChoices.D: The mower will operate only if the engine is not flooded. The engine is flooded if the foot pedal is depressed. The foot pedal is not depressed, so the mower will operate.
answerChoices.E: If the kiln is too hot, then the plates will crack. If the plates crack, then the artisan must redo the order. The artisan need not redo the order. Thus, the kiln was not too hot.

questions.stimulus: Doctor: Being overweight has long been linked with a variety of health problems, such as high blood pressure and heart disease. But recent research conclusively shows that people who are slightly overweight are healthier than those who are considerably underweight. Therefore, to be healthy, it suffices to be slightly overweight.
questions.questionStem: The argument's reasoning is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: ignores medical opinions that tend to lead to a conclusion contrary to the one drawn
answerChoices.B: never adequately defines what is meant by "healthy"
answerChoices.C: does not take into account the fact that appropriate weight varies greatly from person to person
answerChoices.D: holds that if a person lacks a property that would suffice to make the person unhealthy, then that person must be healthy
answerChoices.E: mistakes a merely relative property for one that is absolute

questions.stimulus: Robust crops not only withstand insect attacks more successfully than other crops, they are also less likely to be attacked in the first place, since insects tend to feed on weaker plants. Killing insects with pesticides does not address the underlying problem of inherent vulnerability to damage caused by insect attacks. Thus, a better way to reduce the vulnerability of agricultural crops to insect pest damage is to grow those crops in good soil soil with adequate nutrients, organic matter, and microbial activity.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: The application of nutrients and organic matter to farmland improves the soil's microbial activity.
answerChoices.B: Insects never attack crops grown in soil containing adequate nutrients, organic matter, and microbial activity.
answerChoices.C: The application of pesticides to weak crops fails to reduce the extent to which they are damaged by insect pests.
answerChoices.D: Crops that are grown in good soil tend to be more robust than other crops.
answerChoices.E: Growing crops without the use of pesticides generally produces less robust plants than when pesticides are used.

questions.stimulus: People perceive color by means of certain photopigments in the retina that are sensitive to certain wavelengths of light. People who are color-blind are unable to distinguish between red and green, for example, due to an absence of certain photopigments. What is difficult to explain, however, is that in a study of people who easily distinguish red from green, 10 to 20 percent failed to report distinctions between many shades of red that the majority of the subjects were able to distinguish.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, helps to explain the result of the study cited above except:

answerChoices.A: People with abnormally low concentrations of the photopigments for perceiving red can perceive fewer shades of red than people with normal concentrations.
answerChoices.B: Questions that ask subjects to distinguish between different shades of the same color are difficult to phrase with complete clarity.
answerChoices.C: Some people are uninterested in fine gradations of color and fail to notice or report differences they do not care about.
answerChoices.D: Some people are unable to distinguish red from green due to an absence in the retina of the photopigment sensitive to green.
answerChoices.E: Some people fail to report distinctions between certain shades of red because they lack the names for those shades.

questions.stimulus: Occultist: The issue of whether astrology is a science is easily settled: it is both an art and a science. The scientific components are the complicated mathematics and the astronomical knowledge needed to create an astrological chart. The art is in the synthesis of a multitude of factors and symbols into a coherent statement of their relevance to an individual.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the occultist's argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: presumes, without providing justification, that any science must involve complicated mathematics
answerChoices.B: incorrectly infers that a practice is a science merely from the fact that the practice has some scientific components
answerChoices.C: denies the possibility that astrology involves components that are neither artistic nor scientific
answerChoices.D: incorrectly infers that astronomical knowledge is scientific merely from the fact that such knowledge is needed to create an astrological chart
answerChoices.E: presumes, without providing justification, that any art must involve the synthesis of a multitude of factors and symbols

questions.stimulus: The water of Lake Laberge, in Canada, currently contains high levels of the pesticide toxaphene. Authorities are puzzled because toxaphene was banned in North America in the early 1980s and now is used only in a few other parts of the world.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, does most to explain why the water of Lake Laberge currently contains high levels of toxaphene?

answerChoices.A: Levels of pesticides in the environment often continue to be high for decades after their use ends.
answerChoices.B: Lake Laberge's water contains high levels of other pesticides besides toxaphene.
answerChoices.C: Toxic chemicals usually do not travel large distances in the atmosphere.
answerChoices.D: North American manufacturers opposed banning toxaphene.
answerChoices.E: Toxic chemicals become more readily detectable once they enter organisms the size of fish.

questions.stimulus: Although Samantha likes both oolong and green tea, none of her friends likes both. However, all of her friends like black tea.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, each of the following could be true except:

answerChoices.A: Samantha likes black tea.
answerChoices.B: None of Samantha's friends likes green tea.
answerChoices.C: Samantha's friends like exactly the same kinds of tea as each other.
answerChoices.D: One of Samantha's friends likes neither oolong nor green tea.
answerChoices.E: One of Samantha's friends likes all the kinds of teas that Samantha likes.

questions.stimulus: Because it permits a slower and more natural rhythm of life, living in the country is supposed to be more healthy and relaxed than living in the city. But surveys show that people living in the country become ill as often and as seriously as people living in the city, and that they experience an equal amount of stress.
questions.questionStem: The statements above, if true, provide the most support for which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Living in the country is neither healthier nor more relaxing than living in the city.
answerChoices.B: Living in the country does not in fact permit a slower and more natural rhythm of life than living in the city.
answerChoices.C: People whose rhythm of life is slow and natural recover quickly from illness.
answerChoices.D: Despite what people believe, a natural rhythm of life is unhealthy.
answerChoices.E: The amount of stress a person experiences depends on that person's rhythm of life.

questions.stimulus: Industrialist: Environmentalists contend that emissions from our factory pose a health risk to those living downwind. The only testimony presented in support of this contention comes from residents of the communities surrounding the factory. But only a trained scientist can determine whether or not these emissions are dangerous, and none of the residents are scientists. Hence our factory's emissions present no health risk.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the industrialist's argument is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: impugns the motives of the residents rather than assessing the reasons for their contention
answerChoices.B: does not consider the safety of emissions from other sources in the area
answerChoices.C: presents no testimony from scientists that the emissions are safe
answerChoices.D: fails to discuss the benefits of the factory to the surrounding community
answerChoices.E: equivocates between two different notions of the term "health risk"

questions.stimulus: In the city of Glasgow, Scotland, trade doubled between 1750, when the first bank opened there, and 1765, when government regulations on banking were first implemented in Scotland.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, could contribute to an explanation of the doubling described above except:

answerChoices.A: The technological revolution that started in the early eighteenth century in England resulted in increased trade between England and Scotland.
answerChoices.B: Reductions in tariffs on foreign goods in 1752 led to an increase in imports to Glasgow.
answerChoices.C: The establishment of banking in Glasgow encouraged the use of paper money, which made financial transactions more efficient.
answerChoices.D: Improvements in Scottish roads between 1750 and 1758 facilitated trade between Glasgow and the rest of Scotland.
answerChoices.E: The initial government regulation of Scottish banks stimulated Glasgow's economy.

questions.stimulus: Some argue that laws are instituted at least in part to help establish a particular moral fabric in society. But the primary function of law is surely to help order society so that its institutions, organizations, and citizenry can work together harmoniously, regardless of any further moral aims of the law. Indeed, the highest courts have on occasion treated moral beliefs based on conscience or religious faith as grounds for making exceptions in the application of laws.
questions.questionStem: The statements above, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: The manner in which laws are applied sometimes takes into account the beliefs of the people governed by those laws.
answerChoices.B: The law has as one of its functions the ordering of society but is devoid of moral aims.
answerChoices.C: Actions based on religious belief or on moral conviction tend to receive the protection of the highest courts.
answerChoices.D: The way a society is ordered by law should not reflect any moral convictions about the way society ought to be ordered.
answerChoices.E: The best way to promote cooperation among a society's institutions, organizations, and citizenry is to institute order in that society by means of law.

questions.stimulus: In Western economies, more energy is used to operate buildings than to operate transportation. Much of the decline in energy consumption since the oil crisis of 1973 is due to more efficient use of energy in homes and offices. New building technologies, which make lighting, heating, and ventilation systems more efficient, have cut billions of dollars from energy bills in the West. Since energy savings from these efficiencies save several billion dollars per year today, we can conclude that 50 to 100 years from now they will save more than $200 billion per year (calculated in current dollars).
questions.questionStem: On which one of the following assumptions does the argument rely?

answerChoices.A: Technology used to make buildings energy efficient will not become prohibitively expensive over the next century.
answerChoices.B: Another oil crisis will occur in the next 50 to 100 years.
answerChoices.C: Buildings will gradually become a less important consumer of energy than transportation.
answerChoices.D: Energy bills in the West will be $200 billion lower in the next 50 to 100 years.
answerChoices.E: Energy-efficient technologies based on new scientific principles will be introduced in the next 50 to 100 years.

questions.stimulus: Travel writer: A vacationer should choose an airline that has had an accident in the past 5 years. Though this may seem counterintuitive, studies show that the average airline has 1 accident every 5 years. So if an airline has had no accident during the past 5 years, the chances that the airline will have a crash are increased.
questions.questionStem: The flawed reasoning in the travel writer's argument is most similar to that in which one of the following arguments?

answerChoices.A: A tossed coin has come up heads 100 times in a row. It is therefore reasonable to believe that the coin is not fair, and thus that it is more likely to come up heads than tails when it is flipped again.
answerChoices.B: If there are 10 adult male baboons in a troop, the chance of an average adult male baboon ascending to dominance in any given year is 1 in 10. Thus, if an adult male baboon has been in the troop more than 10 years and has never ascended to dominance, then the chance of his doing so is now better than 1 in 10.
answerChoices.C: On a given day, an average resident's chance of being involved in a traffic accident in a certain city is 1 in 10,000. Therefore, the chance of Marty, a 5-year-old resident, being involved in a traffic accident in the city on any given day is also 1 in 10,000.
answerChoices.D: The average adolescent who works full-time in a certain country makes about 76 cents for every dollar that an adult who works full-time there makes. Therefore, since in this country the average adolescent who works part-time makes less than the average adolescent who works full-time, the average adolescent who works part-time makes less than 76 cents for every dollar made by an employed adult.
answerChoices.E: Though until recently this chess grandmaster had responded to opening move X with move Y half of the time, in the current tournament he has responded to move X with move Y 90 percent of the time. Thus, in the next game of the current tournament, he is 90 percent likely to respond to move X with move Y.

questions.stimulus:
Phoebe: There have been many reported sightings of strange glowing lights, but a number of these sightings have a straightforward, natural explanation. They occurred clustered in time and location around the epicenters of three earthquakes, and so were almost certainly earthquake lights, a form of ball lightning caused by stresses in the ground.
Quincy: I am skeptical that the association between the lights and the earthquakes is anything more than a coincidence. The theory that ground stresses related to earthquakes can cause any kind of lightning is extremely speculative.
questions.questionStem: In responding to Phoebe, Quincy

answerChoices.A: takes a correlation to be a causal relation
answerChoices.B: challenges the accuracy of the data about sightings that Phoebe takes for granted
answerChoices.C: criticizes Phoebe's explanation as unsubstantiated
answerChoices.D: offers an explanation of the glowing lights different from Phoebe's
answerChoices.E: accuses Phoebe of introducing irrelevant information

questions.stimulus: Those who have the ability to fully concentrate are always of above-average intelligence. Also, being successfully trained in speed-reading will usually be accompanied by an increased ability to concentrate.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, then each of the following could be true except:

answerChoices.A: Some people can speed-read, and are able to fully concentrate, but are of below-average intelligence.
answerChoices.B: All people who can speed-read are of above-average intelligence.
answerChoices.C: Many people of above-average intelligence are unable to fully concentrate.
answerChoices.D: Some people with little ability to concentrate are of below-average intelligence, but can speed-read.
answerChoices.E: All people who can speed-read are able to concentrate to some extent.

questions.stimulus: In order to maintain a high standard of living, a nation must maintain a functioning infrastructure. Major investment in the improvement of its infrastructure will, over time, reward a nation with a corresponding rise in its standard of living. Hence a nation whose standard of living is on the rise can be safely assumed to be a nation that has invested heavily in improving its infrastructure.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed because the argument fails to take into account that

answerChoices.A: a nation that fails to invest in its infrastructure need not experience any resulting decline in its standard of living
answerChoices.B: many nations are unable to make the needed investments in infrastructure
answerChoices.C: the rise in a nation's standard of living that is prompted by investment in its infrastructure may take a long time to occur
answerChoices.D: a rise in a nation's standard of living need not be the result of major investments in its infrastructure
answerChoices.E: nations often experience short-term crises that require that resources be diverted to purposes other than the maintenance and improvement of infrastructure

questions.stimulus:
Yang: Yeast has long been known to be a leaven, that is, a substance used in baking to make breads rise. Since biblical evidence ties the use of leavens to events dating back to 1200 B.C., we can infer that yeast was already known to be a leaven at that time.
Campisi: I find your inference unconvincing; several leavens other than yeast could have been known in 1200 B.C.
questions.questionStem: Campisi counters Yang's argument by

answerChoices.A: suggesting that an alternative set of evidence better supports Yang's conclusion
answerChoices.B: questioning the truth of a presumption underlying Yang's argument
answerChoices.C: denying the truth of Yang's conclusion without considering the reason given for that conclusion
answerChoices.D: pointing out that the premises of Yang's argument more strongly support a contrary conclusion
answerChoices.E: calling into question the truth of the evidence presented in Yang's argument

questions.stimulus: Researcher: People with certain personality disorders have more theta brain waves than those without such disorders. But my data show that the amount of one's theta brain waves increases while watching TV. So watching too much TV increases one's risk of developing personality disorders.
questions.questionStem: A questionable aspect of the reasoning above is that it

answerChoices.A: uses the phrase "personality disorders" ambiguously
answerChoices.B: fails to define the phrase "theta brain waves"
answerChoices.C: takes correlation to imply a causal connection
answerChoices.D: draws a conclusion from an unrepresentative sample of data
answerChoices.E: infers that watching TV is a consequence of a personality disorder

questions.stimulus: The authorship of the Iliad and the Odyssey has long been debated. Some traditional evidence suggests that Homer created both works, or at least large portions of them, but there is equally forceful evidence that he had nothing to do with either. Since there is no overwhelming evidence for either claim, we ought to accept the verdict of tradition that Homer is the principal author of both works.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the principle underlying the argumentation above?

answerChoices.A: If there is no overwhelming evidence for or against a hypothesis, then one should suspend judgment as to its truth.
answerChoices.B: If a hypothesis goes against tradition, one should not accept the hypothesis without overwhelming evidence.
answerChoices.C: If there is no overwhelming evidence for or against a hypothesis, one should believe it.
answerChoices.D: One should accept the authority of tradition only if one has nontraditional evidence for the traditional hypothesis.
answerChoices.E: One should defer to the authority of tradition if two or more hypotheses conflict with it.

questions.stimulus: Midlevel managers at large corporations are unlikely to suggest reductions in staff in their own departments even when these departments are obviously overstaffed.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, supports the claim above except:

answerChoices.A: The compensation paid to midlevel managers is greater when they supervise more workers.
answerChoices.B: Midlevel managers have less work to do when their departments are overstaffed.
answerChoices.C: Staff morale and productivity often suffer when workers are laid off.
answerChoices.D: Departmental workloads at most large corporations increase and decrease significantly and unpredictably.
answerChoices.E: Many large corporations allow managers to offer early retirement as a means of reducing staff.

questions.stimulus: Editorialist: Some people propose that, to raise revenues and encourage conservation, our country's taxes on oil, gasoline, and coal should be increased. Such a tax increase, however, would do more harm than good. By raising energy costs, the tax increase would decrease our competitiveness with other countries. Many families would be unfairly burdened with higher transportation costs. Finally, by reducing the demand for energy, the tax increase would reduce the number of energy production jobs.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, would weaken the editorialist's argument except:

answerChoices.A: The editorialist's country's budget deficit will decrease if the energy tax increase is implemented, thus benefiting the economy.
answerChoices.B: Higher gasoline prices tend to lead to a cleaner environment, because people do less nonessential driving.
answerChoices.C: The proposed tax increase would be larger for some energy sources than for others.
answerChoices.D: Higher gasoline prices will encourage people to carpool, which will reduce individual transportation costs.
answerChoices.E: The government would use the increase in tax revenue to create many more jobs than would be lost in the energy production sector.

questions.stimulus: Reporter: A team of scientists has recently devised a new test that for the first time accurately diagnoses autism in children as young as 18 months old. When used to evaluate 16,000 children at their 18-month checkup, the test correctly diagnosed all 10 children later confirmed to be autistic, though it also wrongly identified 2 children as autistic. Autistic children can therefore now benefit much earlier in life than before from the treatments already available.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the reporter's argument depends?

answerChoices.A: No test intended for diagnosing autism at such an early age existed before the new test was devised.
answerChoices.B: A diagnostic test that sometimes falsely gives a positive diagnosis can still provide a reasonable basis for treatment decisions.
answerChoices.C: The new test can be used to evaluate all children, regardless of the level of development of their verbal skills.
answerChoices.D: Those children incorrectly identified as autistic will not be adversely affected by treatments aimed at helping autistic children.
answerChoices.E: There was no reliable evidence that autism could affect children so young until the advent of the new test.

questions.stimulus: Tallulah: The columnist attributes the decline of interest in novels to consumerism, technology, and the laziness of people who prefer watching television to reading a novel. However, in reaching this conclusion, the columnist has overlooked important evidence. It is surely relevant that contemporary fiction is frequently of poor quality indeed, much of it is meaningless and depressing-whereas many good newspapers, magazines, professional journals, and books of other types are currently available.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of Tallulah's argument?

answerChoices.A: Contemporary fiction is unpopular because it is meaningless, depressing, and of poor overall quality.
answerChoices.B: The columnist's claim that novels are being displaced by consumerism, technology, and television is false.
answerChoices.C: The view expressed by the columnist was formed without considering all of the pertinent evidence.
answerChoices.D: People read as much as they used to, but most of the works they now read are not novels.
answerChoices.E: A large number of high-quality newspapers, magazines, professional journals, and nonfiction books are currently published.

questions.stimulus: Renting cars from dealerships is less expensive than renting cars from national rental firms. But to take advantage of dealership rates, tourists must determine which local dealerships offer rentals, and then pay for long taxi rides between the airport and those dealerships. So renting from dealerships rather than national rental firms is generally more worthwhile for local residents than for tourists.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, strengthens the argument except:

answerChoices.A: To encourage future business, many car dealerships drop off and pick up rental cars for local residents at no charge.
answerChoices.B: Tourists renting cars from national rental firms almost never need to pay for taxi rides to or from the airport.
answerChoices.C: Travel agents generally are unable to inform tourists of which local car dealerships offer rentals.
answerChoices.D: Many local residents know of local car dealerships that offer low-priced rentals.
answerChoices.E: For local residents, taxi rides to car dealerships from their homes or workplaces are usually no less expensive than taxi rides to national rental firms.

questions.stimulus: On some hot days the smog in Hillview reaches unsafe levels, and on some hot days the wind blows into Hillview from the east. Therefore, on some days when the wind blows into Hillview from the east, the smog in Hillview reaches unsafe levels.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed in that the argument

answerChoices.A: mistakes a condition that sometimes accompanies unsafe levels of smog for a condition that necessarily accompanies unsafe levels of smog
answerChoices.B: fails to recognize that one set might have some members in common with each of two others even though those two other sets have no members in common with each other
answerChoices.C: uses the key term "unsafe” in one sense in a premise and in another sense in the conclusion
answerChoices.D: contains a premise that is implausible unless the conclusion is presumed to be true
answerChoices.E: infers a particular causal relation from a correlation that could be explained in a variety of other ways

questions.stimulus: Labor representative: Social historians have shown conclusively that if workers strike when the working conditions at their jobs are poor, those conditions usually significantly improve after five years. Although workers in this industry are familiar with this fact, they nonetheless refuse to strike even though their working conditions are poor.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy described by the labor representative?

answerChoices.A: Until recently it was widely believed that strikes do not generally improve working conditions.
answerChoices.B: Most factories in this industry change ownership every two years.
answerChoices.C: Working conditions in many other industries are worse than conditions in this industry.
answerChoices.D: Workers typically plan to work in this industry only three years.
answerChoices.E: Wages in this industry have increased each year.

questions.stimulus: Paleontologists recently discovered teeth from several woolly mammoths on an isolated Arctic island where no mammoth fossils had previously been found. The teeth were 25 percent smaller on average than adult mammoth teeth that have been found elsewhere, but they are clearly adult mammoth teeth. Therefore, provided that the teeth are representative of their respective populations, woolly mammoths that lived on the island were smaller on average than those that lived elsewhere.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, would allow the conclusion to be properly drawn?

answerChoices.A: Neither tooth size nor overall body size is completely uniform among adult members of most species, including woolly mammoths.
answerChoices.B: The tooth wear that naturally occurs in many animals over the course of their adult years did not result in a significant change in tooth size among adult woolly mammoths as they aged.
answerChoices.C: Unusually small mammoth teeth found at locations other than the island have always been those of juvenile mammoths rather than adult mammoths.
answerChoices.D: Tooth size among adult woolly mammoths was always directly proportional to the overall size of those mammoths.
answerChoices.E: Woolly mammoths of the kind that lived on the island had the same number and variety of teeth as mammoths that lived elsewhere had.

questions.stimulus: Diplomat: Every major war in the last 200 years has been preceded by a short, sharp increase in the acquisition of weapons by the nations that subsequently became participants in those conflicts. Clearly, therefore, arms control agreements will preserve peace.
questions.questionStem: Of the following, which one most accurately describes a reasoning flaw in the diplomat's argument?

answerChoices.A: The argument infers, merely from the claim that events of one type have for a long time consistently preceded events of a second type, that an event of the second type will not occur unless an event of the first type occurs.
answerChoices.B: The argument reasons that, simply because weapons are used in war, a rapid, dramatic increase in the acquisition of weapons will always lead to war.
answerChoices.C: The argument draws a conclusion that simply restates a claim presented in support of that conclusion.
answerChoices.D: The argument fails to consider that a short, sharp increase in the acquisition of weapons by a nation may be a response to the increased armament of neighboring nations.
answerChoices.E: The argument fails to consider that some of the minor wars that have occurred in the last 200 years may have been preceded by rapid increases in the acquisition of weapons by the nations that subsequently became participants in those wars.

questions.stimulus: Newscaster: In order for the public to participate in a meaningful way in the current public policy debate, one requirement is that the issues be stated in terms the public can understand. The mayor's speech has just stated these issues in such terms, so now the public at least might be able to participate in a meaningful way in the current public policy debate.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most closely parallels the newscaster's argument in its reasoning?

answerChoices.A: One must know Russian if one is to read Dostoyevski's original text of Crime and Punishment. Rachel has never learned Russian; therefore she cannot read the original text of Crime and Punishment.
answerChoices.B: In order to reach one's goals, one must be able to consider these goals carefully. Laura has reached her goals, so she must have been able to consider those goals carefully.
answerChoices.C: One cannot confuse the majority of one's students if one wants to be a good teacher. Hugo wants to be a good teacher; therefore, he might be able to avoid confusing the majority of his students.
answerChoices.D: In order to discover the meaning of certain seldom-used words, one must use a good dictionary. Paul has used a good dictionary, so Paul must have discovered the meaning of those words.
answerChoices.E: One must at least have warm clothing if one is to survive in a very cold climate. Jerome has obtained warm clothing; therefore, he might be able to survive in a very cold climate.

questions.stimulus: Most serious students are happy students, and most serious students go to graduate school. Furthermore, all students who go to graduate school are overworked.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the statements above?

answerChoices.A: Most overworked students are happy students.
answerChoices.B: Some happy students are overworked.
answerChoices.C: All overworked students are serious students.
answerChoices.D: Some unhappy students go to graduate school.
answerChoices.E: All serious students are overworked.

questions.stimulus: Editorialist: Some people argue that highway speed limits should be increased to reflect the actual average speeds of highway drivers, which are currently 10 to 20 percent higher than posted speed limits. Any such increase would greatly decrease highway safety, however; as past experience teaches, higher average highway speeds would result, since even though most drivers who currently violate posted speed limits would obey higher ones, almost all drivers who obey current speed limits would likely increase their speed.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the editorialist's argument?

answerChoices.A: Some drivers who obey current speed limits would not change their speeds after the introduction of the new speed limits.
answerChoices.B: Uniformity of speeds among vehicles is more important for highway safety than is a low average highway speed.
answerChoices.C: Most drivers who drive 10 to 20 percent faster than current speed limits have never been involved in a highway accident.
answerChoices.D: Some drivers who violate current speed limits would also violate higher speed limits.
answerChoices.E: Most drivers who violate current speed limits determine their speeds by what they believe to be safe in the situation.

questions.stimulus: At many electronics retail stores, the consumer has the option of purchasing product warranties that extend beyond the manufacturer's warranty. However, consumers are generally better off not buying extended warranties. Most problems with electronic goods occur within the period covered by the manufacturer's warranty.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Problems with electronic goods that occur after the manufacturer's warranty expires are generally inexpensive to fix in comparison with the cost of an extended warranty.
answerChoices.B: Because problems are so infrequent after the manufacturer's warranty expires, extended warranties on electronic goods are generally inexpensive.
answerChoices.C: Most of those who buy extended warranties on electronic goods do so because special circumstances make their item more likely to break than is usually the case.
answerChoices.D: Some extended warranties on electronic goods cover the product for the period covered by the manufacturer's warranty as well as subsequent years.
answerChoices.E: Retail stores sell extended warranties in part because consumers who purchase them are likely to purchase other products from the same store.

questions.stimulus: Since the 1970s, environmentalists have largely succeeded in convincing legislators to enact extensive environmental regulations. Yet, as environmentalists themselves not only admit but insist, the condition of the environment is worsening, not improving. Clearly, more environmental regulations are not the solution to the environment's problems.
questions.questionStem: The argument's reasoning is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: attacks the environmentalists themselves instead of their positions
answerChoices.B: presumes, without providing warrant, that only an absence of environmental regulations could prevent environmental degradation
answerChoices.C: fails to consider the possibility that the condition of the environment would have worsened even more without environmental regulations
answerChoices.D: fails to justify its presumption that reducing excessive regulations is more important than preserving the environment
answerChoices.E: fails to consider the views of the environmentalists' opponents

questions.stimulus: Although it is unwise to take a developmental view of an art like music as if Beethoven were an advance over Josquin, or Miles Davis an advance over Louis Armstrong-there are ways in which it makes sense to talk about musical knowledge growing over time. We certainly know more about certain sounds than was known five centuries ago; that is, we understand how sounds that earlier composers avoided can be used effectively in musical compositions. For example, we now know how the interval of the third, which is considered dissonant, can be used in compositions to create consonant musical phrases.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

answerChoices.A: Sounds that were never used in past musical compositions are used today.
answerChoices.B: Sounds that were once considered dissonant are more pleasing to modern listeners.
answerChoices.C: It is inappropriate to take a developmental view of music.
answerChoices.D: It is unwise to say that one composer is better than another.
answerChoices.E: Our understanding of music can improve over the course of time.

questions.stimulus: A recent test of an electric insect control device discovered that, of the more than 300 insects killed during one 24-hour period, only 12 were mosquitoes. Thus this type of device may kill many insects, but will not significantly aid in controlling the potentially dangerous mosquito population.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: A careful search discovered no live mosquitoes in the vicinity of the device after the test.
answerChoices.B: A very large proportion of the insects that were attracted to the device were not mosquitoes.
answerChoices.C: The device is more likely to kill beneficial insects than it is to kill harmful insects.
answerChoices.D: Many of the insects that were killed by the device are mosquito-eating insects.
answerChoices.E: The device does not succeed in killing all of the insects that it attracts.

questions.stimulus: Brain-scanning technology provides information about processes occurring in the brain. For this information to help researchers understand how the brain enables us to think, however, researchers must be able to rely on the accuracy of the verbal reports given by subjects while their brains are being scanned. Otherwise brain-scan data gathered at a given moment might not contain information about what the subject reports thinking about at that moment, but instead about some different set of thoughts.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

answerChoices.A: It is unlikely that brain-scanning technology will ever enable researchers to understand how the brain enables us to think.
answerChoices.B: There is no way that researchers can know for certain that subjects whose brains are being scanned are accurately reporting what they are thinking.
answerChoices.C: Because subjects whose brains are being scanned may not accurately report what they are thinking, the results of brain-scanning research should be regarded with great skepticism.
answerChoices.D: Brain scans can provide information about the accuracy of the verbal reports of subjects whose brains are being scanned.
answerChoices.E: Information from brain scans can help researchers understand how the brain enables us to think only if the verbal reports of those whose brains are being scanned are accurate.

questions.stimulus: Ornithologist: This bird species is widely thought to subsist primarily on vegetation, but my research shows that this belief is erroneous. While concealed in a well-camouflaged blind, I have observed hundreds of these birds every morning over a period of months, and I estimate that over half of what they ate consisted of insects and other animal food sources.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the ornithologist's argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: assumes, without providing justification, that the feeding behavior of the birds observed was not affected by the ornithologist's act of observation
answerChoices.B: fails to specify the nature of the animal food sources, other than insects, that were consumed by the birds
answerChoices.C: adopts a widespread belief about the birds' feeding habits without considering the evidence that led to the belief
answerChoices.D: neglects the possibility that the birds have different patterns of food consumption during different parts of the day and night
answerChoices.E: fails to consider the possibility that the birds' diet has changed since the earlier belief about their diet was formed

questions.stimulus: Educator: Only those students who are genuinely curious about a topic can successfully learn about that topic. They find the satisfaction of their curiosity intrinsically gratifying, and appreciate the inherent rewards of the learning process itself. However, almost no child enters the classroom with sufficient curiosity to learn successfully all that the teacher must instill. A teacher’s job, therefore, _______.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most logically completes the educator’s argument?

answerChoices.A: requires for the fulfillment of its goals the stimulation as well as the satisfaction of curiosity
answerChoices.B: necessitates the creative use of rewards that are not inherent in the learning process itself
answerChoices.C: is to focus primarily on those topics that do not initially interest the students
answerChoices.D: is facilitated by students' taking responsibility for their own learning
answerChoices.E: becomes easier if students realize that some learning is not necessarily enjoyable

questions.stimulus: Environmentalist: When bacteria degrade household cleaning products, vapors that are toxic to humans are produced. Unfortunately, household cleaning products are often found in landfills. Thus, the common practice of converting landfills into public parks is damaging human health.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption the environmentalist's argument requires?

answerChoices.A: In at least some landfills that have been converted into public parks there are bacteria that degrade household cleaning products.
answerChoices.B: Converting a landfill into a public park will cause no damage to human health unless toxic vapors are produced in that landfill and humans are exposed to them.
answerChoices.C: If a practice involves the exposure of humans to vapors from household cleaning products, then it causes at least some damage to human health.
answerChoices.D: When landfills are converted to public parks, measures could be taken that would prevent people using the parks from being exposed to toxic vapors.
answerChoices.E: If vapors toxic to humans are produced by the degradation of household cleaning products by bacteria in any landfill, then the health of at least some humans will suffer.

questions.stimulus: Tea made from camellia leaves is a popular beverage. However, studies show that regular drinkers of camellia tea usually suffer withdrawal symptoms if they discontinue drinking the tea. Furthermore, regular drinkers of camellia tea are more likely than people in general to develop kidney damage. Regular consumption of this tea, therefore, can result in a heightened risk of kidney damage.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Several other popular beverages contain the same addictive chemical that is found in camellia tea.
answerChoices.B: Addictive chemicals are unlikely to cause kidney damage solely by virtue of their addictive qualities.
answerChoices.C: Some people claim that regular consumption of camellia tea helps alleviate their stress.
answerChoices.D: Most people who regularly drink camellia tea do not develop kidney damage.
answerChoices.E: Many people who regularly consume camellia tea also regularly consume other beverages suspected of causing kidney damage.

questions.stimulus: Artist: Avant-garde artists intend their work to challenge a society's mainstream beliefs and initiate change. And some art collectors claim that an avant-garde work that becomes popular in its own time is successful. However, a society's mainstream beliefs do not generally show any significant changes over a short period of time. Therefore, when an avant-garde work becomes popular it is a sign that the work is not successful, since it does not fulfil the intentions of its creator.
questions.questionStem: The reference to the claim of certain art collectors plays which one of the following roles in the artist's argument?

answerChoices.A: It serves to bolster the argument's main conclusion.
answerChoices.B: It identifies a view that is ultimately disputed by the argument.
answerChoices.C: It identifies a position supported by the initial premise in the argument.
answerChoices.D: It provides support for the initial premise in the argument.
answerChoices.E: It provides support for a counterargument to the initial premise.

questions.stimulus: A recent epidemiological study found that businesspeople who travel internationally on business are much more likely to suffer from chronic insomnia than are businesspeople who do not travel on business. International travelers experience the stresses of dramatic changes in climate, frequent disruption of daily routines, and immersion in cultures other than their own, stresses not commonly felt by those who do not travel. Thus, it is likely that these stresses cause the insomnia.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following would, if true, most strengthen the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: Most international travel for the sake of business occurs between countries with contiguous borders.
answerChoices.B: Some businesspeople who travel internationally greatly enjoy the changes in climate and immersion in another culture.
answerChoices.C: Businesspeople who already suffer from chronic insomnia are no more likely than businesspeople who do not to accept assignments from their employers that require international travel.
answerChoices.D: Experiencing dramatic changes in climate and disruption of daily routines through international travel can be beneficial to some people who suffer from chronic insomnia.
answerChoices.E: Some businesspeople who once traveled internationally but no longer do so complain of various sleep-related ailments.

questions.stimulus: Many mountain climbers regard climbing Mount Everest as the ultimate achievement. But climbers should not attempt this climb since the risk of death or serious injury in an Everest expedition is very high. Moreover, the romantic notion of gaining "spiritual discovery" atop Everest is dispelled by climbers' reports that the only profound experiences they had at the top were of exhaustion and fear.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: Projects undertaken primarily for spiritual reasons ought to be abandoned if the risks are great.
answerChoices.B: Dangerous activities that are unlikely to result in significant spiritual benefits for those undertaking them should be avoided.
answerChoices.C: Activities that are extremely dangerous ought to be legally prohibited unless they are necessary to produce spiritual enlightenment.
answerChoices.D: Profound spiritual experiences can be achieved without undergoing the serious danger involved in mountain climbing.
answerChoices.E: Mountain climbers and other athletes should carefully examine the underlying reasons they have for participating in their sports.

questions.stimulus: Each of the smallest particles in the universe has an elegantly simple structure. Since these particles compose the universe, we can conclude that the universe itself has an elegantly simple structure.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following arguments exhibits flawed reasoning similar to that in the argument above except:

answerChoices.A: Each part of this car is nearly perfectly engineered. Therefore this car is nearly perfect, from an engineering point of view.
answerChoices.B: Each part of this desk is made of metal. Therefore this desk is made of metal.
answerChoices.C: Each brick in this wall is rectangular. Therefore this wall is rectangular.
answerChoices.D: Each piece of wood in this chair is sturdy. Therefore this chair is sturdy.
answerChoices.E: Each sentence in this novel is well constructed. Therefore this is a well-constructed novel.

questions.stimulus: Criminologist: A judicial system that tries and punishes criminals without delay is an effective deterrent to violent crime. Long, drawn-out trials and successful legal maneuvering may add to criminals' feelings of invulnerability. But if potential violent criminals know that being caught means prompt punishment, they will hesitate to break the law.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the criminologist's argument?

answerChoices.A: It is in the nature of violent crime that it is not premeditated.
answerChoices.B: About one-fourth of all suspects first arrested for a crime are actually innocent.
answerChoices.C: Many violent crimes are committed by first-time offenders.
answerChoices.D: Everyone accused of a crime has the right to a trial.
answerChoices.E: Countries that promptly punish suspected lawbreakers have lower crime rates than countries that allow long trials.

questions.stimulus: Journalist: Many people object to mandatory retirement at age 65 as being arbitrary, arguing that people over 65 make useful contributions. However, if those who reach 65 are permitted to continue working indefinitely, we will face unacceptable outcomes. First, young people entering the job market will not be able to obtain decent jobs in the professions for which they were trained, resulting in widespread dissatisfaction among the young. Second, it is not fair for those who have worked 40 or more years to deprive others of opportunities. Therefore, mandatory retirement should be retained.
questions.questionStem: The journalist's argument depends on assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Anyone who has worked 40 years is at least 65 years old.
answerChoices.B: All young people entering the job market are highly trained professionals.
answerChoices.C: It is unfair for a person not to get a job in the profession for which that person was trained.
answerChoices.D: If people are forced to retire at age 65, there will be much dissatisfaction among at least some older people.
answerChoices.E: If retirement ceases to be mandatory at age 65, at least some people will choose to work past age 65.

questions.stimulus: Editorial: Contrary to popular belief, teaching preschoolers is not especially difficult, for they develop strict systems (e.g., for sorting toys by shape), which help them to learn, and they are always intensely curious about something new in their world.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the editorial's argument?

answerChoices.A: Preschoolers have a tendency to imitate adults, and most adults follow strict routines.
answerChoices.B: Children intensely curious about new things have very short attention spans.
answerChoices.C: Some older children also develop strict systems that help them learn.
answerChoices.D: Preschoolers ask as many creative questions as do older children.
answerChoices.E: Preschool teachers generally report lower levels of stress than do other teachers.

questions.stimulus: Lawyer: A body of circumstantial evidence is like a rope, and each item of evidence is like a strand of that rope. Just as additional pieces of circumstantial evidence strengthen the body of evidence, adding strands to the rope strengthens the rope. And if one strand breaks, the rope is not broken nor is its strength much diminished. Thus, even if a few items of a body of circumstantial evidence are discredited, the overall body of evidence retains its basic strength.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the lawyer's argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: takes for granted that no items in a body of circumstantial evidence are significantly more critical to the strength of the evidence than other items in that body
answerChoices.B: presumes, without providing justification, that the strength of a body of evidence is less than the sum of the strengths of the parts of that body
answerChoices.C: fails to consider the possibility that if many items in a body of circumstantial evidence were discredited, the overall body of evidence would be discredited
answerChoices.D: offers an analogy in support of a conclusion without indicating whether the two types of things compared share any similarities
answerChoices.E: draws a conclusion that simply restates a claim presented in support of that conclusion

questions.stimulus: Ethicist: Many environmentalists hold that the natural environment is morally valuable for its own sake, regardless of any benefits it provides us. However, even if nature has no moral value, nature can be regarded as worth preserving simply on the grounds that people find it beautiful. Moreover, because it is philosophically disputable whether nature is morally valuable but undeniable that it is beautiful, an argument for preserving nature that emphasizes nature's beauty will be less vulnerable to logical objections than one that emphasizes its moral value.
questions.questionStem: The ethicist's reasoning most closely conforms to which one of the following principles?

answerChoices.A: An argument in favor of preserving nature will be less open to logical objections if it avoids the issue of what makes nature worth preserving.
answerChoices.B: If an argument for preserving nature emphasizes a specific characteristic of nature and is vulnerable to logical objections, then that characteristic does not provide a sufficient reason for preserving nature.
answerChoices.C: If it is philosophically disputable whether nature has a certain characteristic, then nature would be more clearly worth preserving if it did not have that characteristic.
