answerChoices.A: Greeting one's coworkers must be a polite thing to do, because people who are considered polite always greet their coworkers. The proof that these people really are polite is that they are consistently polite in their daily lives.
answerChoices.B: This card game must be intellectually challenging, because it is played by highly intelligent people, who play only intellectually challenging card games. In fact, these players' intelligence is demonstrated by the fact that they play this game.
answerChoices.C: When coffee is being chosen, Brand Z is the coffee chosen by people with highly developed taste in coffee. These people showed their highly developed taste in coffee by correctly distinguishing eight brands of coffee from each other in a taste test.
answerChoices.D: That jacket must have been made for a very short person, because only very short people were able to fit into it. We know that they were very short because we saw them before they tried on the jacket.
answerChoices.E: This painting is a poor imitation, because only people with poor eyesight mistook it for the original. That these people have poor eyesight is demonstrated by the fact that they also mistook a vase of flowers in the painting for a peacock.

questions.stimulus: A study of 86 patients, all of whom suffered from disease T and received the same standard medical treatment, divided the patients into 2 equal groups. One group's members all attended weekly support group meetings, but no one from the other group attended support group meetings. After 10 years, 41 patients from each group had died. Clearly, support group meetings do not help patients with disease T live longer.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Of the 4 patients who survived more than 10 years, the 2 who had attended weekly support group meetings lived longer than the 2 who had not.
answerChoices.B: For many diseases, attending weekly support group meetings is part of the standard medical treatment.
answerChoices.C: The members of the group that attended weekly support group meetings lived 2 years longer, on average, than the members of the other group.
answerChoices.D: Some physicians have argued that attending weekly support group meetings gives patients less faith in the standard treatment for disease T.
answerChoices.E: Everyone in the group whose members attended weekly support group meetings reported after 1 year that those meetings had helped them to cope with the disease.

questions.stimulus: Astronomer: I have asserted that our solar system does not contain enough meteoroids and other cosmic debris to have caused the extensive cratering on the far side of the moon. My opponents have repeatedly failed to demonstrate the falsity of this thesis. Their evidence is simply inconclusive; thus they should admit that my thesis is correct.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the astronomer's argument is flawed because this argument

answerChoices.A: criticizes the astronomer's opponents rather than their arguments
answerChoices.B: infers the truth of the astronomer's thesis from the mere claim that it has not been proven false
answerChoices.C: ignores the possibility that alternative explanations may exist for the cratering
answerChoices.D: presumes that the astronomer's thesis should not be subject to rational discussion and criticism
answerChoices.E: fails to precisely define the key word “meteoroids"

questions.stimulus: Many newborn babies have a yellowish tinge to their skin because their blood contains a high level of the pigment bilirubin. One group of doctors treats newborns to reduce high levels of bilirubin, since bilirubin, if it enters the brain, might cause the tetanus that sometimes occurs in newborns. However, a second group of doctors argues for allowing bilirubin levels in newborn babies to remain high, since the brain’s own natural defenses normally prevent bilirubin from entering.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to support the position of the second group of doctors?

answerChoices.A: The treatment that most effectively reduces high levels of bilirubin in newborns has no known negative side effects.
answerChoices.B: Some diseases that occur in newborns can weaken the brain’s natural defenses and allow bilirubin to enter.
answerChoices.C: In newborns the pigment bilirubin, like other pigments, occurs not only in the blood but also in fluids involved in digestion.
answerChoices.D: Bilirubin neutralizes certain potentially damaging substances to which newborns are exposed at birth.
answerChoices.E: Among doctors who recommend treating newborns to reduce high levels of bilirubin, there is general agreement about what levels should be considered excessively high.

questions.stimulus: Economist: Some sociologists argue that because capitalism intrinsically involves competition, it weakens the ties between the people of a community. Although this may formerly have been true, modern capitalism requires that there be large corporations. Thus, modern capitalism promotes, rather than weakens, communal ties.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the economist’s argument depends?

answerChoices.A: Few economic systems are more successful than modern capitalism in fostering communal ties between citizens.
answerChoices.B: Modern capitalism is designed primarily to distribute goods and services, not to create communal ties between people.
answerChoices.C: Corporations that compete with each other must develop some ties to each other in order to reach agreement on the rules of the competition.
answerChoices.D: Having large corporations in a modern capitalist system promotes the strength of communal ties.
answerChoices.E: An economic system that does not encourage large corporations will be less successful economically than one that does.

questions.stimulus: Teacher: Participating in organized competitive athletics may increase a child’s strength and coordination. As critics point out, however, it also instills in those children who are not already well developed in these respects a feeling of inferiority that never really disappears. Yet, since research has shown that adults with feelings of inferiority become more successful than those free of such anxieties, funding for children’s athletic programs should not be eliminated.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the role played in the teacher’s argument by the assertion that participating in organized competitive athletics may increase a child’s strength and coordination?

answerChoices.A: It is mentioned as one possible reason for adopting a policy for which the teacher suggests an additional reason.
answerChoices.B: It is a claim that the teacher attempts to refute with counterarguments.
answerChoices.C: It is a hypothesis for which the teacher offers additional evidence.
answerChoices.D: It is cited as an insufficient reason for eliminating funding for children’s athletic programs.
answerChoices.E: It is cited as an objection that has been raised to the position that the teacher is supporting.

questions.stimulus: Columnist: Donating items to charity may be a sign of generosity, but any generosity it may demonstrate is rarely a permanent virtue, since most donors make donations only intermittently.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a flaw in the columnist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The argument takes for granted that truly generous people are the most virtuous.
answerChoices.B: The argument attacks the character of those whose values are different from those of the columnist.
answerChoices.C: The argument takes for granted that a character trait is present only when manifested.
answerChoices.D: The argument generalizes from too small a sample of cases.
answerChoices.E: The argument takes for granted that most people donate out of generosity.

questions.stimulus: Researchers have found that, hours after birth, infants are able to distinguish faces from other images. Infants stare at drawings of faces for longer periods of time than they do at blank ovals or drawings in which facial features are scrambled.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the ability of newborn infants described above?

answerChoices.A: Certain abilities of facial pattern recognition are innate in humans, rather than learned.
answerChoices.B: The longer an infant stares at an object, the more interesting the infant finds that object.
answerChoices.C: Infants learn to associate human faces with the necessities of comfort and nourishment.
answerChoices.D: The less an infant stares at an object, the weaker the preference the infant has for that object.
answerChoices.E: Infants learn to associate the sound of human voices with the images of human faces.

questions.stimulus: Violent crime in this town is becoming a serious problem. Compared to last year, local law enforcement agencies have responded to 17 percent more calls involving violent crimes, showing that the average citizen of this town is more likely than ever to become a victim of a violent crime.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: The town’s overall crime rate appears to have risen slightly this year compared to the same period last year.
answerChoices.B: In general, persons under the age of 65 are less likely to be victims of violent crimes than persons over the age of 65.
answerChoices.C: As a result of the town’s community outreach programs, more people than ever are willing to report violent crimes to the proper authorities.
answerChoices.D: In response to worries about violent crime, the town has recently opened a community center providing supervised activities for teenagers.
answerChoices.E: Community officials have shown that a relatively small number of repeat offenders commit the majority of violent crimes in the town.

questions.stimulus: Two different dates have been offered as the approximate end point of the last ice age in North America. The first date was established by testing insect fragments found in samples of sediments to determine when warmth-adapted open-ground beetles replaced cold-adapted arctic beetles. The second date was established by testing pollen grains in those same samples to determine when ice masses yielded to spruce forests. The first date is more than 500 years earlier than the second.
questions.questionStem: The statements above, if true, most strongly support which one of the following conclusions about the last ice age and its aftermath in North America?

answerChoices.A: Toward the end of the ice age, warmth-adapted open-ground beetles ceased to inhabit areas where the predominant tree cover consisted of spruce forests.
answerChoices.B: Among those sediments deposited toward the end of the ice age, those found to contain cold-adapted arctic beetle fragments can also be expected to contain spruce-pollen grains.
answerChoices.C: Ice masses continued to advance through North America for several hundred years after the end of the ice age.
answerChoices.D: The species of cold-adapted arctic beetle that inhabited areas covered by ice masses died out toward the end of the last ice age.
answerChoices.E: Toward the end of the ice age, warmth-adapted open-ground beetles colonized the new terrain opened to them faster than soil changes and seed dispersion established new spruce forests.

questions.stimulus: When presented with the evidence against him, Ellison freely admitted to engaging in illegal transactions using company facilities. However, the company obtained the evidence by illegally recording Ellison’s conversations. Therefore, although the company may demand that he immediately cease, it cannot justifiably take any punitive measures against him.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following judgments best illustrates the principle illustrated by the argument above?

answerChoices.A: After Price confessed to having stolen money from Long over a period of several years, Long began stealing from Price. Despite Price’s guilt, Long was not justified in taking illegal action against him.
answerChoices.B: Shakila’s secretary has admitted that he is illegally receiving cable television without paying for it. Shakila would not be justified in reporting him, though, since she once did the same thing.
answerChoices.C: After Takashi told Sarah’s parents that he had seen her at the movies on Tuesday, Sarah confessed to sneaking out that day. On Monday, however, Takashi had violated the local curfew for minors. Hence Sarah’s parents cannot justifiably punish her in this case.
answerChoices.D: After a conservation officer discovered them, Kuttner admitted that he had set the illegal animal traps on his land. But, because she was trespassing at the time, the conservation officer cannot justifiably punish Kuttner in this case.
answerChoices.E: Ramirez was forced by the discovery of new evidence to admit that she lied about her role in managing the chief of staff’s financial affairs. Nevertheless, the board of directors cannot justifiably take action against Ramirez, because in past instances it has pardoned others guilty of similar improprieties.

questions.stimulus: In a recent study, each member of two groups of people, Group A (composed of persons sixty-five to seventy-five years old) and Group B (composed of college students), was required to make a telephone call to a certain number at a specified time. The time when each call was initiated was recorded electronically. Group A proved far better at remembering to make a telephone call precisely at a specified time than did Group B. There were fourteen lapses in Group B but only one lapse in Group A. Clearly, at least one type of memory does not suffer as a person ages.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if all of them are true, is least helpful in establishing that the conclusion above is properly drawn?

answerChoices.A: There was the same number of people in each group.
answerChoices.B: The same group of researchers answered the calls made by the callers in both study groups.
answerChoices.C: Among the college students there were no persons more than forty years old.
answerChoices.D: Both groups had unrestricted access to telephones for making the required calls.
answerChoices.E: The members of the two groups received their instructions approximately the same amount of time before they were to make their telephone calls.

questions.stimulus: Prediction, the hallmark of the natural sciences, appears to have been made possible by reducing phenomena to mathematical expressions. Some social scientists also want the power to predict accurately and assume they ought to perform the same reduction. But this would be a mistake; it would neglect data that are not easily mathematized and thereby would only distort the social phenomena.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

answerChoices.A: The social sciences do not have as much predictive power as the natural sciences.
answerChoices.B: Mathematics plays a more important role in the natural sciences than it does in the social sciences.
answerChoices.C: There is a need in the social sciences to improve the ability to predict.
answerChoices.D: Phenomena in the social sciences should not be reduced to mathematical formulas.
answerChoices.E: Prediction is responsible for the success of the natural sciences.

questions.stimulus: Studies have shown that the more high-stress points a bridge has, the more likely it is to fracture eventually. This might lead one to expect fractures to develop at high-stress points. Surprisingly, however, fractures develop not at high-stress points but elsewhere on the bridge.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, contributes most to an explanation of why bridges fracture elsewhere than at high-stress points?

answerChoices.A: In many structures other than bridges, such as ship hulls and airplane bodies, fractures do not develop at high-stress points.
answerChoices.B: Fractures do not develop at high-stress points, because bridges are reinforced at those points; however, stress is transferred to other points on the bridge where it causes fractures.
answerChoices.C: In many structures, the process of fracturing often causes high-stress points to develop.
answerChoices.D: Structures with no high-stress points can nonetheless have a high probability of fracturing.
answerChoices.E: Improper bridge construction, e.g., low-quality welding or the use of inferior steel, often leads both to the development of high-stress points and to an increased probability of fracturing.

questions.stimulus: Many people say that the press should not pry into the personal lives of private individuals. But the press has the right to publish any story of interest to the public unless that story is libelous. So, if a story about a private individual is not libelous, the press has an obligation to publish it, for such information is clearly of interest to the public.
questions.questionStem: The argument’s reasoning is vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument presumes, without giving warrant, that

answerChoices.A: the press can publish nonlibelous stories about private individuals without prying into their personal lives
answerChoices.B: one’s having a right to do something entails one’s having an obligation to do it
answerChoices.C: the publishing of information about the personal lives of private individuals cannot be libelous
answerChoices.D: if one has an obligation to do something then one has a right to do it
answerChoices.E: the press’s right to publish always outweighs the individual’s right not to be libeled

questions.stimulus: Consumer advocate: A recent study concluded that top-loading washing machines are superior overall to front-loaders. But front-loaders have the controls and access in front. This is more convenient for wheelchair users, some of whom find it highly inconvenient to remove laundry from top-loaders. So for some consumers front-loaders are superior.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption upon which the consumer advocate’s argument depends?

answerChoices.A: For some consumers the convenience of front-loaders outweighs the advantages of top-loaders in assessing which is superior.
answerChoices.B: Washing machines of a given type should be compared only with washing machines of that type.
answerChoices.C: Convenience is the only important factor in determining which type of washing machine is superior.
answerChoices.D: Retrieving clothes from a top-loader is convenient for people who do not use wheelchairs.
answerChoices.E: Retrieving clothes from front-loaders is inconvenient for people who are not wheelchair users.

questions.stimulus: Over 90 percent of the human brain currently serves no purpose, as is evident from the fact that many people with significant brain damage show no discernible adverse effects. So once humans begin to tap into this tremendous source of creativity and innovation, many problems that today seem insurmountable will be within our ability to solve.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a flaw in the argument?

answerChoices.A: The argument presumes, without providing justification, that the effects of brain damage are always easily detectable.
answerChoices.B: The argument presumes, without providing justification, that the only reason that any problem remains unsolved is a lack of creativity and innovation.
answerChoices.C: The argument infers that certain parts of the brain do nothing merely on the basis of the assertion that we do not know what they do.
answerChoices.D: The argument infers that problems will be solved merely on the basis of the claim that they will be within our ability to solve.
answerChoices.E: The argument presumes, without providing justification, that the currently unused parts of the brain are a potential source of tremendous creativity and innovation.

questions.stimulus: Some scientists have expressed reservations about quantum theory because of its counterintuitive consequences. But despite rigorous attempts to show that quantum theory’s predictions were inaccurate, they were shown to be accurate within the generally accepted statistical margin of error. These results, which have not been equaled by quantum theory’s competitors, warrant acceptance of quantum theory.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles most helps to justify the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: A scientific theory should be accepted if it has fewer counterintuitive consequences than do its competitors.
answerChoices.B: A scientific theory should be accepted if it has been subjected to serious attempts to disprove it and has withstood all of them.
answerChoices.C: The consequences of a scientific theory should not be considered counterintuitive if the theory’s predictions have been found to be accurate.
answerChoices.D: A theory should not be rejected until it has been subjected to serious attempts to disprove it.
answerChoices.E: A theory should be accepted only if its predictions have not been disproved by experiment.

questions.stimulus: Psychologist: The obligation to express gratitude cannot be fulfilled anonymously. However much society may have changed over the centuries, human psychology is still driven primarily by personal interaction. Thus, the important social function of positively reinforcing those behaviors that have beneficial consequences for others can be served only if the benefactor knows the source of the gratitude.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the role played in the psychologist’s argument by the claim that the obligation to express gratitude cannot be fulfilled anonymously?

answerChoices.A: It is an illustration of a premise that is used to support the argument’s conclusion.
answerChoices.B: It is used to counter a consideration that might be taken to undermine the argument’s conclusion.
answerChoices.C: It is used to support indirectly a claim that the argument in turn uses to support directly the conclusion.
answerChoices.D: It is used to identify the social benefit with which the argument is concerned.
answerChoices.E: It is the conclusion that the argument is intended to support.

questions.stimulus: Curator: Our museum displays only twentieth-century works, which are either on loan from private collectors or in the museum’s permanent collection. Prints of all of the latter works are available in the museum store. The museum store also sells prints of some works that are not part of the museum’s permanent collection, such as Hopper’s Nighthawks.
questions.questionStem: If the curator’s statements are true, which one of the following must be true?

answerChoices.A: Every print in the museum store is of a work that is either on loan to the museum from a private collector or part of the museum’s permanent collection.
answerChoices.B: Every print that is sold in the museum store is a copy of a twentieth-century work.
answerChoices.C: There are prints in the museum store of every work that is displayed in the museum and not on loan from a private collector.
answerChoices.D: Hopper’s Nighthawks is both a twentieth-century work and a work on loan to the museum from a private collector.
answerChoices.E: Hopper’s Nighthawks is not displayed in the museum.

questions.stimulus: Nutritionist: Because humans have evolved very little since the development of agriculture, it is clear that humans are still biologically adapted to a diet of wild foods, consisting mainly of raw fruits and vegetables, nuts and seeds, lean meat, and seafood. Straying from this diet has often resulted in chronic illness and other physical problems. Thus, the more our diet consists of wild foods, the healthier we will be.
questions.questionStem: The claim that humans are still biologically adapted to a diet of wild foods plays which one of the following roles in the nutritionist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: It is a conclusion for which the only support offered is the claim that straying from a diet of wild foods has often resulted in chronic illness and other physical problems.
answerChoices.B: It is a premise for which no justification is provided, but which is used to support the argument’s main conclusion.
answerChoices.C: It is a phenomenon for which the main conclusion of the nutritionist’s argument is cited as an explanation.
answerChoices.D: It is an intermediate conclusion for which one claim is offered as support, and which is used in turn to support the argument’s main conclusion.
answerChoices.E: It is a premise offered in support of the claim that humans have evolved very little since the development of agriculture.

questions.stimulus: Editorialist: Some people argue that we have an obligation not to cut down trees. However, there can be no obligation to an entity unless that entity has a corresponding right. So if we have an obligation toward trees, then trees have rights. But trees are not the sort of things that can have rights. Therefore, we have no obligation not to cut down trees.
questions.questionStem: The editorialist’s argument depends on assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: If an entity has a right to certain treatment, we have an obligation to treat it that way.
answerChoices.B: Any entity that has rights also has obligations.
answerChoices.C: Only conscious entities are the sort of things that can have rights.
answerChoices.D: Avoiding cutting down trees is not an obligation owed to some entity other than trees.
answerChoices.E: One does not always have the right to cut down the trees on one’s own property.

questions.stimulus: A recent study suggests that consuming three glasses of wine daily substantially decreases the risk of stroke. Critics of the study, defending earlier research recommending one glass of wine daily, claim that binge drinkers (who drink once a week or less, but drink three or more drinks when they do drink) are the people most likely to drink three glasses of wine in one day and are more likely to die from sudden heart attacks than are other drinkers. According to these critics, drinking three glasses of wine daily would not benefit health overall, since the decrease in the risk of stroke associated with that level of consumption is negated by its associated increased risk of sudden heart attack.
questions.questionStem: The critics’ argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it

answerChoices.A: inappropriately attributes the consequences of binge drinking to persons whose regular consumption of wine is three glasses a day
answerChoices.B: confuses the risk of sudden alcohol-induced heart attacks with other health risks
answerChoices.C: presumes, without providing justification, that there is no significant difference between wine and other alcoholic beverages in terms of health benefits and risks
answerChoices.D: fails to address specifically the reduction in risk of stroke conferred by the level of consumption in the recent study
answerChoices.E: overlooks the difference between strokes that result in death and less severe strokes

questions.stimulus: Scientist: Isaac Newton’s Principia, the seventeenth-century work that served as the cornerstone of physics for over two centuries, could at first be understood by only a handful of people, but a basic understanding of Newton’s ideas eventually spread throughout the world. This shows that the barriers to communication between scientists and the public are not impermeable. Thus recent scientific research, most of which also can be described only in language that seems esoteric to most contemporary readers, may also become part of everyone’s intellectual heritage.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the role played in the scientist’s argument by the claim that recent scientific research can often be described only in language that seems esoteric to most contemporary readers?

answerChoices.A: It is raised as a potential objection to the argument’s main conclusion, but its truth is called into doubt by the preceding statements.
answerChoices.B: It is a premise that supports the argument’s main conclusion by suggesting that the results of recent scientific research are only superficially different from claims made in Newton’s Principia.
answerChoices.C: It is cited as further evidence for the conclusion that the barriers to communication between scientists and the public are not impermeable.
answerChoices.D: It is a claim that serves mainly to help establish the relevance of the preceding statements to the argument’s final conclusion.
answerChoices.E: It serves to cast doubt on an alleged similarity between Newton’s Principia and recent scientific research.

questions.stimulus: Only a minority of those who engage in political action do so out of a sense of social justice. Therefore, some people who have a sense of social justice do not engage in political action.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following uses flawed reasoning most similar to that used in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Most scholars are not motivated by a desire to win prestigious academic prizes. Thus, some of those who want to win prestigious academic prizes are not scholars.
answerChoices.B: Only foolish politicians disregard the wishes of most voters. Thus, most voters deserve to be represented by foolish politicians.
answerChoices.C: Some corporations only feign a concern for the environment when they advertise a product as environmentally friendly. Thus, no corporation has a genuine concern for the environment.
answerChoices.D: Some parents show no interest in the curricula used in the schools that their children attend. Thus, some of the decisions regarding school curricula should be made without regard for the wishes of the children’s parents.
answerChoices.E: Only a small percentage of the profits that companies make are directly attributable to good management decisions. Thus, even companies that are managed badly will usually turn a profit.

questions.stimulus:
Columnist: Even if the primary purpose of university education is to make students employable, such education should emphasize the liberal arts rather than the more narrow kind of technical training that prepares one for a particular sort of job. This is because the reasoning
skills one acquires from a liberal arts education allow one to adapt to new intellectual challenges and thus to perform jobs for which one has received no specialized training.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the columnist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: It is better for people to have good educations than good jobs.
answerChoices.B: Many people with narrow technical training manage to find jobs.
answerChoices.C: Having a series of different jobs is more interesting than having only one job.
answerChoices.D: Having a general understanding of life is more important than possessing practical skills.
answerChoices.E: Technical training does not help students acquire reasoning skills.

questions.stimulus: Provinces and states with stringent car safety requirements, including required use of seat belts and annual safety inspections, have on average higher rates of accidents per kilometer driven than do provinces and states with less stringent requirements. Nevertheless, most highway safety experts agree that more stringent requirements do reduce accident rates.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to reconcile the safety experts’ belief with the apparently contrary evidence described above?

answerChoices.A: Annual safety inspections ensure that car tires are replaced before they grow old.
answerChoices.B: Drivers often become overconfident after their cars have passed a thorough safety inspection.
answerChoices.C: The roads in provinces and states with stringent car safety requirements are far more congested and therefore dangerous than in other provinces and states.
answerChoices.D: Psychological studies show that drivers who regularly wear seat belts often come to think of themselves as serious drivers, which for a few people discourages reckless driving.
answerChoices.E: Provinces and states with stringent car safety requirements have, on average, many more kilometers of roads than do other provinces and states.

questions.stimulus: It is difficult to grow cacti in a humid climate. It is difficult to raise orange trees in a cold climate. In most parts of a certain country, it is either easy to grow cacti or easy to raise orange trees.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must be false?

answerChoices.A: Half of the country is both humid and cold.
answerChoices.B: Most of the country is hot.
answerChoices.C: Some parts of the country are neither cold nor humid.
answerChoices.D: It is not possible to raise cacti in the country.
answerChoices.E: Most parts of the country are humid.

questions.stimulus: Essayist: Common sense, which is always progressing, is nothing but a collection of theories that have been tested over time and found useful. When alternative theories that prove even more useful are developed, they gradually take the place of theories already embodied in common sense. This causes common sense to progress, but, because it absorbs new theories slowly, it always contains some obsolete theories.
questions.questionStem: If all of the essayist’s statements are true, then which one of the following must be true?

answerChoices.A: At least some new theories that have not yet been found to be more useful than any theory currently part of common sense will never be absorbed into the body of common sense.
answerChoices.B: Of the useful theories within the body of common sense, the older ones are generally less useful than the newer ones.
answerChoices.C: The frequency with which new theories are generated prevents their rapid absorption into the body of common sense.
answerChoices.D: Each theory within the body of common sense is eventually replaced with a new theory that is more useful.
answerChoices.E: At least some theories that have been tested over time and found useful are less useful than some other theories that have not been fully absorbed into the body of common sense.

questions.stimulus: This region’s swimmers generally swim during the day because they are too afraid of sharks to swim after dark but feel safe swimming during daylight hours. Yet all recent shark attacks on swimmers in the area have occurred during the day, indicating that, contrary to popular opinion, it is not more dangerous to swim here at night than during the day.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it

answerChoices.A: overlooks the possibility that some sharks are primarily nocturnal hunters
answerChoices.B: bases its conclusion on evidence from an unreliable source
answerChoices.C: overlooks the possibility that swimmers might feel anxiety caused by not being able to see one’s surroundings in the dark
answerChoices.D: presumes, without providing justification, that swimmers cannot be the most knowledgeable about which times of day are safest for swimming
answerChoices.E: fails to take into account the possibility that the number of shark attacks at night would increase dramatically if more people swam at night

questions.stimulus: Denise: Crime will be reduced only when punishment is certain and is sufficiently severe to give anyone considering committing a crime reason to decide against doing so. Reshmi: No, crime will be most effectively reduced if educational opportunities are made readily available to everyone, so that those who once viewed criminal activity as the only means of securing a comfortable lifestyle will choose a different path.
questions.questionStem: Their dialogue provides the most support for the claim that Denise and Reshmi agree that

answerChoices.A: people are capable of choosing whether or not to commit crimes
answerChoices.B: crime is the most important issue facing modern society
answerChoices.C: reducing crime requires fair and consistent responses to criminal behavior
answerChoices.D: crimes are committed in response to economic need
answerChoices.E: reducing crime requires focusing on assured punishments

questions.stimulus: Acme Corporation offers unskilled workers excellent opportunities for advancement. As evidence, consider the fact that the president of the company, Ms. Garon, worked as an assembly line worker, an entry-level position requiring no special skills, when she first started at Acme.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most weakens the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: Acme’s vice president of operations also worked as an assembly line worker when he first started at Acme.
answerChoices.B: Acme regularly hires top graduates of business schools and employs them briefly in each of a succession of entry-level positions before promoting them to management.
answerChoices.C: Acme promotes its own employees to senior management positions much more frequently than it hires senior managers from other companies.
answerChoices.D: Ms. Garon worked at Acme for more than 20 years before she was promoted to president.
answerChoices.E: Acme pays entry-level employees slightly higher wages than most other businesses in the same industry.

questions.stimulus: The song of the yellow warbler signals to other yellow warblers that a particular area has been appropriated by the singer as its own feeding territory. Although the singing deters other yellow warblers from taking over the feeding territory of the singer, other yellow warblers may range for food within a portion of the singer’s territory. However, a warbler sings a special song when it molts (sheds its feathers). Other yellow warblers will not enter the smaller core territory of a yellow warbler singing its molting song. Therefore yellow warblers, which can only fly short distances during molting, have no competition for the food supply within the range of their restricted flying.
questions.questionStem: The argument makes which one of the following assumptions?

answerChoices.A: The core areas contain just enough food to sustain one yellow warbler while it molts.
answerChoices.B: Warblers are the only molting birds that lay claim to core areas of feeding territories by singing.
answerChoices.C: There are no birds other than yellow warblers that compete with yellow warblers for food.
answerChoices.D: Warblers often share their feeding areas with other kinds of birds, which often do not eat the same insects or seeds as warblers do.
answerChoices.E: The core areas of each feeding territory are the same size for each molting warbler.

questions.stimulus: Chinh: Television producers should not pay attention to the preferences of the viewing public when making creative decisions. Great painters do not consider what the museum-going public wants to see. Lana: But television is expressly for the viewing public. So a producer is more like a CEO than like an artist. Just as a company would be foolhardy not to consider consumers’ tastes when developing products, the TV producer must consider viewers’ preferences.
questions.questionStem: According to Lana, Chinh’s argument is flawed in that it

answerChoices.A: is circular
answerChoices.B: relies on a sample of consumers that is unrepresentative of consumers in general
answerChoices.C: infers from the effect produced by an action that the action is intended to produce that effect
answerChoices.D: fails to consider the possibility that painters may in fact try to please the museum-going public
answerChoices.E: offers a faulty analogy

questions.stimulus: Dietitian: High consumption of sodium increases some people’s chances of developing heart disease. To maintain cardiac health without lowering sodium consumption, therefore, these people should eat fresh, rather than canned or frozen, fruit and vegetables, since the potassium in plant foods helps to prevent sodium’s malign effects.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the dietitian’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Fresh fruits and vegetables contain more potassium than sodium.
answerChoices.B: Food processing businesses often add sodium to foods being canned or frozen.
answerChoices.C: Potassium is the only mineral that helps to prevent sodium’s malign effects.
answerChoices.D: Potassium in fruits and vegetables has few negative side effects.
answerChoices.E: Fresh fruits and vegetables contain more potassium than do canned or frozen ones.

questions.stimulus: Dana intentionally watered the plant every other day. But since the plant was a succulent, and needed dry soil, the frequent watering killed the plant. Therefore Dana intentionally killed the plant.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments exhibits a flawed pattern of reasoning most similar to the flawed pattern of reasoning exhibited in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Jack stole $10 from Kelly and bet it on a race. The bet returned $100 to Jack. Therefore Jack really stole $100 from Kelly.
answerChoices.B: Celeste knows that coffee is grown in the mountains in Peru and that Peru is in South America. Therefore Celeste should know that coffee is grown in South America.
answerChoices.C: The restaurant owner decided to take an item off her restaurant’s menu. This decision disappointed Jerry because that item was his favorite dish. Therefore the restaurant owner decided to disappoint Jerry.
answerChoices.D: The heavy rain caused the dam to break, and the breaking of the dam caused the fields downstream to be flooded. Therefore the heavy rain caused the flooding of the fields.
answerChoices.E: The power plant raised the water temperature, and whatever raised the water temperature is responsible for the decrease in fish. Therefore the power plant is responsible for the decrease in fish.

questions.stimulus: This boulder is volcanic in origin and yet the rest of the rock in this area is sedimentary. Since this area was covered by southward-moving glaciers during the last ice age, this boulder was probably deposited here, hundreds of miles from its geological birthplace, by a glacier.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the conclusion drawn in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Most boulders that have been moved by glaciers have not been moved more than 100 miles.
answerChoices.B: The closest geological source of volcanic rock is 50 miles south of this boulder.
answerChoices.C: The closest geological source of volcanic rock is 50 miles north of this boulder.
answerChoices.D: There are no geological sources of volcanic rock north of this boulder.
answerChoices.E: No other boulders of volcanic origin exist within 50 miles of this boulder.

questions.stimulus: Rifka: We do not need to stop and ask for directions. We would not need to do that unless, of course, we were lost. Craig: The fact that we are lost is precisely why we need to stop.
questions.questionStem: In the exchange above, the function of Craig’s comment is to

answerChoices.A: contradict the conclusion of Rifka’s argument without offering any reason to reject any of Rifka’s implicit premises
answerChoices.B: deny one of Rifka’s implicit premises and thereby arrive at a different conclusion
answerChoices.C: imply that Rifka’s argument is invalid by accepting the truth of its premises while rejecting its conclusion
answerChoices.D: provide a counterexample to Rifka’s generalization
answerChoices.E: affirm the truth of the stated premise of Rifka’s argument while remaining noncommittal about its conclusion

questions.stimulus: Critic: The idealized world portrayed in romance literature is diametrically opposed to the debased world portrayed in satirical literature. Nevertheless, the major characters in both types of works have moral qualities that reflect the worlds in which they are presented. Comedy and tragedy, meanwhile, require that the moral qualities of major characters change during the course of the action. Therefore, neither tragedy nor comedy can be classified as satirical literature or romance literature.
questions.questionStem: The critic’s conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Some characters in comedies and tragedies are neither debased nor idealized.
answerChoices.B: The visions of the world portrayed in works of tragedy and works of comedy change during the course of the action.
answerChoices.C: If a character in a tragedy is idealized at the beginning of the action depicted in the tragedy, he or she must be debased at the end.
answerChoices.D: In romance literature and satirical literature, characters’ moral qualities do not change during the course of the action.
answerChoices.E: Both comedy and tragedy require that the moral qualities of minor characters change during the course of the action.

questions.stimulus: Lance: If experience teaches us nothing else, it teaches us that every general rule has at least one exception. Frank: What you conclude is itself a general rule. If we assume that it is true, then there is at least one general rule that has no exceptions. Therefore, you must withdraw your conclusion.
questions.questionStem: Frank’s argument is an attempt to counter Lance’s conclusion by

answerChoices.A: demonstrating that Lance assumes the very thing he sets out to prove
answerChoices.B: showing that Lance’s conclusion involves him in a contradiction
answerChoices.C: showing that no general rule can have exceptions
answerChoices.D: establishing that experience teaches us the opposite of what Lance concludes
answerChoices.E: showing that it has no implications for any real cases

questions.stimulus: Throughout a certain nation, electricity has actually become increasingly available to people in urban areas while energy production has been subsidized to help residents of rural areas gain access to electricity. However, even with the subsidy, many of the most isolated rural populations still have no access to electricity. Thus, the energy subsidy has failed to achieve its intended purpose.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: takes for granted that the subsidy’s intended purpose could have been achieved if the subsidy had not existed
answerChoices.B: takes for granted that if a subsidy has any benefit for those whom it was not intended to benefit, then that subsidy has failed to achieve its intended purpose
answerChoices.C: presumes, without providing justification, that the intended purpose of the subsidy was to benefit not only rural populations in the nation who have no electricity, but other people in the nation as well
answerChoices.D: overlooks the possibility that even many of the people in the nation who live in urban areas would have difficulty gaining access to electricity without the subsidy
answerChoices.E: fails to take into account that the subsidy could have helped many of the rural residents in the nation gain access to electricity even if many other rural residents in the nation were not helped in this way

questions.stimulus: Heart attacks are most likely to occur on Mondays. The accepted explanation is that because Monday is the first day of the workweek, people feel more stress on Mondays than on other days. However, research shows that even unemployed retired people are more likely to have heart attacks on Mondays than on other days.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the increased likelihood that an unemployed retiree will have a heart attack on a Monday?

answerChoices.A: Because they associate Monday with work, retired people are more likely to begin large projects on Mondays.
answerChoices.B: Many retired people take up part-time jobs after they retire from their careers.
answerChoices.C: People seldom change their dietary and other health habits after retirement.
answerChoices.D: Stress is the major factor influencing the risk of heart attack.
answerChoices.E: Unemployed retired people are even more likely to have heart attacks than are people who have jobs.

questions.stimulus: Psychologist: We asked 100 entrepreneurs and 100 business managers to answer various questions and rate how confident they were that their responses were correct. While members of each group were overconfident, in general the entrepreneurs were much more so than the business managers. This indicates that people who are especially overconfident are more likely to attempt to start a business in spite of the enormous odds against success than people who are less confident.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, lends the most support to the psychologist’s conclusion?

answerChoices.A: The questions asked of the entrepreneurs and business managers included personal, political, and business questions.
answerChoices.B: At least some of the entrepreneurs surveyed had accurately determined before attempting to start their businesses what the odds were against their attempts being successful.
answerChoices.C: Another survey showed that degree of confidence was highly correlated with success in business.
answerChoices.D: The business managers who were most overconfident were found to have attempted to start businesses in the past.
answerChoices.E: How confident each person surveyed was that his or her answers to the questions asked were correct corresponded closely to that person’s confidence in his or her business acumen.

questions.stimulus: If Agnes’s research proposal is approved, the fourth-floor lab must be cleaned out for her use. Immanuel’s proposal, on the other hand, requires less space. So if his proposal is approved, he will continue to work in the second-floor lab. Only those proposals the director supports will be approved. So since the director will support both proposals, the fourth-floor lab must be cleaned out.
questions.questionStem: The argument’s reasoning is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: presumes, without providing justification, that the fourth-floor lab is bigger than the second-floor lab
answerChoices.B: fails to consider the possibility that a proposal will be rejected even with the director’s support
answerChoices.C: presumes, without providing justification, that the director will support both proposals with equal enthusiasm
answerChoices.D: fails to consider the possibility that Immanuel will want to move to a bigger lab once his proposal is approved
answerChoices.E: presumes, without providing justification, that no lab other than the fourth-floor lab would be adequate for Agnes’s research

questions.stimulus: In order to expand its mailing lists for e-mail advertising, the Outdoor Sports Company has been offering its customers financial incentives if they provide the e-mail addresses of their friends. However, offering such incentives is an unethical business practice, because it encourages people to exploit their personal relationships for profit, which risks damaging the integrity of those relationships.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It is unethical for people to exploit their personal relationships for profit if in doing so they risk damaging the integrity of those relationships.
answerChoices.B: If it would be unethical to use information that was gathered in a particular way, then it is unethical to gather that information in the first place.
answerChoices.C: It is an unethical business practice for a company to deliberately damage the integrity of its customers’ personal relationships in any way.
answerChoices.D: It is unethical to encourage people to engage in behavior that could damage the integrity of their personal relationships.
answerChoices.E: Providing a friend’s personal information to a company in exchange for a financial reward will almost certainly damage the integrity of one’s personal relationship with that friend.

questions.stimulus: Glen: An emphasis on law’s purely procedural side produces a concern with personal rights that leads to the individual’s indifference to society’s welfare. Law’s primary role should be to create virtuous citizens. Sara: But such a role would encourage government to decide which modes of life are truly virtuous; that would be more dangerous than government’s being overprotective of individuals’ rights.
questions.questionStem: The dialogue provides the most support for the claim that Glen and Sara disagree about whether

answerChoices.A: citizens can be assumed to be capable of making good choices without governmental interference
answerChoices.B: virtuousness on the part of citizens is more important than the protection of citizens’ rights
answerChoices.C: there is an inherent danger in allowing government to decide what constitutes virtuous behavior among citizens
answerChoices.D: an emphasis on law’s purely procedural side results in government’s being overprotective of citizens’ rights
answerChoices.E: the cultivation of virtue among citizens should be the primary role of law

questions.stimulus: Some credit card companies allow cardholders to skip payments for up to six months under certain circumstances, but it is almost never in a cardholder’s interest to do so. Finance charges accumulate during the skipped-payment period, and the cost to the cardholder is much greater in the long run.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments illustrates a principle most similar to the principle underlying the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Although insecticides are effective in ridding the environment of insect pests, they often kill beneficial insects at the same time. Since these beneficial insects are so important, we must find other ways to combat insect pests.
answerChoices.B: Increasing the base salary of new employees is good for a company. Although the company’s payroll will increase, it will be easier for the company to recruit new employees.
answerChoices.C: It is unwise to use highway maintenance funds for construction of new roads. There is some immediate benefit from new roads, but if these funds are not used for maintenance, the total maintenance cost will be greater in the long run.
answerChoices.D: It is better to invest in a used piece of equipment than to purchase a new one. Although used equipment requires more repairs and is sometimes more costly in the long run, buying a new machine requires a far greater initial outlay of capital.
answerChoices.E: Sports cars are impractical for most drivers. While there is undoubtedly a certain thrill associated with driving these cars, their small size makes them incapable of transporting any but the smallest amounts of cargo.

questions.stimulus: None of the students taking literature are taking physics, but several of the students taking physics are taking art. In addition, none of the students taking rhetoric are taking physics.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements follows logically from the statements above?

answerChoices.A: There are students who are taking art but not literature.
answerChoices.B: None of the students taking literature are taking art.
answerChoices.C: There are students who are taking rhetoric but not literature.
answerChoices.D: None of the students taking rhetoric are taking literature.
answerChoices.E: There are students who are taking both art and literature.

questions.stimulus: Psychologist: Psychotherapists who attempt to provide psychotherapy on radio or television talk shows are expected to do so in ways that entertain a broad audience. However, satisfying this demand is nearly always incompatible with providing high-quality psychological help. For this reason, psychotherapists should never provide psychotherapy on talk shows.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles must be assumed in order for the psychologist’s conclusion to be properly drawn?

answerChoices.A: It is never appropriate for psychotherapists to attempt to entertain a broad audience.
answerChoices.B: The context in which psychological help is presented has a greater impact on its quality than the nature of the advice that is given.
answerChoices.C: Psychotherapy should never be provided in a context in which there is any chance that the therapy might be of less than high quality.
answerChoices.D: Most members of radio and television talk show audiences are seeking entertainment rather than high-quality psychological help.
answerChoices.E: Psychotherapists should never attempt to provide psychological help in a manner that makes it unlikely to be of high quality.

questions.stimulus: Tania: A good art critic is not fair in the ordinary sense; it is only about things that do not interest one that one can give a truly unbiased opinion. Since art is a passion, good criticism of art cannot be separated from emotion. Monique: Art is not simply a passion. The best art critics passionately engage with the artwork, but render their criticism only after shedding all of their biases and consulting general principles of aesthetics.
questions.questionStem: The dialogue most strongly supports the claim that Tania and Monique disagree about whether

answerChoices.A: art is not simply a passion
answerChoices.B: good art criticism is sometimes unbiased
answerChoices.C: art critics should not feel emotion toward artworks
answerChoices.D: fairness generally requires minimizing the influence of bias
answerChoices.E: the passionate engagement of the art critic with the artwork is the most important aspect of art criticism

questions.stimulus: The writing styles in works of high literary quality are not well suited to the avoidance of misinterpretation. For this reason, the writing in judicial decisions, which are primarily intended as determinations of law, is rarely of high literary quality. However, it is not uncommon to find writing of high literary quality in dissenting opinions, which are sometimes included in written decisions in cases heard by a panel of judges.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the statements above?

answerChoices.A: It is not uncommon for more than one judge to have an influence on the way a dissenting opinion is written.
answerChoices.B: Unlike literary works, legal opinions rely heavily on the use of technical terminology.
answerChoices.C: The law is not to any great extent determined by dissenting opinions.
answerChoices.D: Judges spend much more time reading judicial decisions than reading works of high literary quality.
answerChoices.E: Judicial decisions issued by panels of judges are likely to be more widely read than are judicial decisions issued by a single judge who hears a case alone.

questions.stimulus: Ecologist: Without the intervention of conservationists, squirrel monkeys will become extinct. But they will survive if large tracts of second-growth forest habitat are preserved for them. Squirrel monkeys flourish in second-growth forest because of the plentiful supply of their favorite insects and fruit.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the ecologist’s statements?

answerChoices.A: No habitat other than second-growth forest contains plentiful supplies of squirrel monkeys’ favorite insects and fruit.
answerChoices.B: At least some of the conservationists who intervene to help the squirrel monkeys survive will do so by preserving second-growth forest habitat for the monkeys.
answerChoices.C: Without plentiful supplies of their favorite insects and fruit, squirrel monkeys will become extinct.
answerChoices.D: If conservationists intervene to help squirrel monkeys survive, then the squirrel monkeys will not become extinct.
answerChoices.E: Without the intervention of conservationists, large tracts of second-growth forest habitat will not be preserved for squirrel monkeys.

questions.stimulus: Over 40,000 lead seals from the early Byzantine Empire remain today. Apart from the rare cases where the seal authenticated a document of special importance, most seals had served their purpose when the document was opened. Lead was not expensive, but it was not free: most lead seals would have been recast once they had served their purpose. Thus the number of early Byzantine documents sealed in such a fashion must have been many times the number of remaining lead seals.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Most of the lead seals produced during the early Byzantine Empire were affixed to documents that were then opened during that period.
answerChoices.B: Most of the lead seals produced during the early Byzantine Empire were affixed to documents that have since been destroyed.
answerChoices.C: The amount of lead available for seals in the early Byzantine Empire was much greater than the amount of lead that remains in the seals today.
answerChoices.D: During the time of the early Byzantine Empire there were at most 40,000 documents of enough importance to prevent the removing and recycling of the seal.
answerChoices.E: During the time of the early Byzantine Empire there were fewer than 40,000 seals affixed to documents at any given time.

questions.stimulus: Farmer: In the long run, it is counterproductive for farmers to use insecticides. Because insects’ resistance to insecticides increases with insecticide use, farmers have to use greater and greater amounts of costly insecticides to control insect pests.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the role played in the farmer’s argument by the proposition that farmers have to use greater and greater amounts of costly insecticides to control insect pests?

answerChoices.A: It is the argument’s main conclusion, but not its only conclusion.
answerChoices.B: It is a claim for which a causal explanation is provided and which itself is used as direct support for the argument’s only conclusion.
answerChoices.C: It is the argument’s only conclusion.
answerChoices.D: It is a claim that is used as direct support for an intermediary conclusion, which in turn is used as direct support for the argument’s main conclusion.
answerChoices.E: It identifies a phenomenon for which the argument’s main conclusion offers a causal explanation.

questions.stimulus: Anna: Did you know that rainbows always occur opposite the sun, appearing high in the sky when the sun is low, and low in the sky when the sun is high? The Roman scholar Pliny the Elder claimed that this was so, in the first century A.D. William: His claim cannot be correct. After all, Pliny the Elder wrote that there are tribes of dog-headed people and beings with no heads or necks but with eyes on their shoulders, and said that smearing snails on your forehead cures headaches!
questions.questionStem: William’s argument against Anna’s claims about rainbows is most vulnerable to criticism because it

answerChoices.A: inappropriately distorts Anna’s conclusion, making it appear more extreme than it really is
answerChoices.B: takes for granted that Pliny the Elder was in bad faith when he reported about unheard-of creatures
answerChoices.C: illicitly infers that, because Pliny the Elder made some incorrect assertions, Pliny the Elder’s assertions about rainbows are also incorrect
answerChoices.D: accepts the assertions of an ancient scholar without presenting contemporary verification of that scholar’s views
answerChoices.E: implies that Pliny the Elder’s writings are too outdated to be of any value

questions.stimulus: Shareholder: The company’s current operations are time-proven successes. The move into food services may siphon off funds needed by these other operations. Also, the food service industry is volatile, with a higher inherent risk than with, for instance, pharmaceuticals, another area into which the company has considered expanding.
questions.questionStem: If the shareholder’s statements are true, which one of the following is most strongly supported by them?

answerChoices.A: The company’s present operations require increased funding.
answerChoices.B: Investment into pharmaceuticals would not siphon off money from other operations.
answerChoices.C: The company will lose money as it expands into the food service industry.
answerChoices.D: Only if the company expands its operations into pharmaceuticals are increased profits possible.
answerChoices.E: The company has a greater chance of losing money in food services than in pharmaceuticals.

questions.stimulus: Mariah: Joanna has argued that Adam should not judge the essay contest because several of his classmates have entered the contest. However, the essays are not identified by author to the judge and, moreover, none of Adam’s friends are classmates of his. Still, Adam has no experience in critiquing essays. Therefore, I agree with Joanna that Adam should not judge the contest.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify Mariah’s argument?

answerChoices.A: A suspicion of bias is insufficient grounds on which to disqualify someone from judging a contest.
answerChoices.B: Expertise should be the primary prerequisite for serving as a contest judge.
answerChoices.C: The ability of a judge to make objective decisions is more important than that judge’s content expertise.
answerChoices.D: In selecting a contest judge, fairness concerns should override concern for the appropriate expertise.
answerChoices.E: A contest judge, no matter how well qualified, cannot judge properly if the possibility of bias exists.

questions.stimulus: The manufacturers of NoSmoke claim that their product reduces smokers’ cravings for cigarettes. However, in a recent study, smokers given the main ingredient in NoSmoke reported no decrease in cravings for cigarettes. Thus, since NoSmoke has only two ingredients, if similar results are found for the second ingredient, we can conclude that NoSmoke does not reduce smokers’ cravings.
questions.questionStem: The argument above is flawed in that it

answerChoices.A: illicitly presumes that a whole must lack a certain quality if all of its parts lack that quality
answerChoices.B: confuses a mere correlation with a cause
answerChoices.C: relies on a sample that is likely to be unrepresentative
answerChoices.D: overlooks the possibility that NoSmoke helps people to quit smoking in ways other than by reducing smokers’ cravings for cigarettes
answerChoices.E: illicitly presumes that a claim must be false because the people making the claim are biased

questions.stimulus: Gardener: Researchers encourage us to allow certain kinds of weeds to grow among garden vegetables because they can repel caterpillars from the garden. While it is wise to avoid unnecessary use of insecticides, the researchers’ advice is premature. For all we know, those kinds of weeds can deplete the soil of nutrients and moisture that garden crops depend on, and might even attract other kinds of damaging pests.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the gardener’s argument?

answerChoices.A: To the extent that it is possible to do so, we should eliminate the use of insecticides in gardening.
answerChoices.B: Allowing certain kinds of weeds to grow in vegetable gardens may contribute to a net increase in unwanted garden pests.
answerChoices.C: Allowing the right kinds of weeds to grow in vegetable gardens can help toward controlling caterpillars without the use of insecticides.
answerChoices.D: We should be cautious about the practice of allowing certain kinds of weeds to grow among garden vegetables.
answerChoices.E: We should be skeptical about the extent to which certain kinds of weeds can reduce the presence of caterpillars in gardens.

questions.stimulus: Executive: We recently ran a set of advertisements in the print version of a travel magazine and on that magazine’s website. We were unable to get any direct information about consumer response to the print ads. However, we found that consumer response to the ads on the website was much more limited than is typical for website ads. We concluded that consumer response to the print ads was probably below par as well.
questions.questionStem: The executive’s reasoning does which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: bases a prediction of the intensity of a phenomenon on information about the intensity of that phenomenon’s cause
answerChoices.B: uses information about the typical frequency of events of a general kind to draw a conclusion about the probability of a particular event of that kind
answerChoices.C: infers a statistical generalization from claims about a large number of specific instances
answerChoices.D: uses a case in which direct evidence is available to draw a conclusion about an analogous case in which direct evidence is unavailable
answerChoices.E: bases a prediction about future events on facts about recent comparable events

questions.stimulus: Conservation officers justified their decision to remove a pack of ten coyotes from a small island by claiming that the coyotes, which preyed on wild cats and plover, were decimating the plover population and would soon wipe it out. After the coyotes were removed, however, the plover population plummeted dramatically, and within two years plover could no longer be found on the island.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following would, if true, most help explain the phenomenon described above?

answerChoices.A: Plover are ground-nesting birds, which makes them easy prey for coyotes.
answerChoices.B: Wild cat and plover populations tend to fluctuate together.
answerChoices.C: Coyotes are not susceptible to any of the diseases that commonly infect plover or wild cats.
answerChoices.D: The wild cat population on the island was once significantly larger than it is currently.
answerChoices.E: The coyotes preyed mainly on wild cats, and wild cats prey on plover.

questions.stimulus: Economist: During a recession, a company can cut personnel costs either by laying off some employees without reducing the wages of remaining employees or by reducing the wages of all employees without laying off anyone. Both damage morale, but layoffs damage it less, since the aggrieved have, after all, left. Thus, when companies must reduce personnel costs during recessions, they are likely to lay off employees.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the economist’s reasoning?

answerChoices.A: Employee morale is usually the primary concern driving companies’ decisions about whether to lay off employees or to reduce their wages.
answerChoices.B: In general, companies increase wages only when they are unable to find enough qualified employees.
answerChoices.C: Some companies will be unable to make a profit during recessions no matter how much they reduce personnel costs.
answerChoices.D: When companies cut personnel costs during recessions by reducing wages, some employees usually resign.
answerChoices.E: Some companies that have laid off employees during recessions have had difficulty finding enough qualified employees once economic growth resumed.

questions.stimulus: There are far fewer independent bookstores than there were 20 years ago, largely because chain bookstores prospered and multiplied during that time. Thus, chain bookstores’ success has been to the detriment of book consumers, for the shortage of independent bookstores has prevented the variety of readily available books from growing as much as it otherwise would have.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument relies?

answerChoices.A: Book consumers would be better off if there were a greater variety of readily available books than there currently is.
answerChoices.B: Independent bookstores typically do not sell the kinds of books that are available in chain bookstores.
answerChoices.C: The average bookstore today is larger than the average bookstore of 20 years ago.
answerChoices.D: The average bookstore today is smaller than the average bookstore of 20 years ago.
answerChoices.E: Some book consumers value low prices more highly than wide selection.

questions.stimulus: Concert promoter: Some critics claim that our concert series lacks popular appeal. But our income from the sales of t-shirts and other memorabilia at the concerts is equal to or greater than that for similar sales at comparable series. So those critics are mistaken.
questions.questionStem: The concert promoter’s argument is flawed in that it

answerChoices.A: attacks the critics on the basis of emotional considerations rather than factual ones
answerChoices.B: takes for granted that income from sales of memorabilia is the sole indicator of popular appeal
answerChoices.C: takes for granted that the comparable series possess popular appeal
answerChoices.D: draws a conclusion about the popularity of a series based on a comparison with other, dissimilar events
answerChoices.E: fails to adequately distinguish the series as a whole from individual concerts in it

questions.stimulus: The sun emits two types of ultraviolet radiation that damage skin: UV-A, which causes premature wrinkles, and UV-B, which causes sunburn. Until about ten years ago, sunscreens protected against UV-B radiation but not against UV-A radiation.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is best supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Since about ten years ago, the percentage of people who wear sunscreen every time they spend time in the sun has increased.
answerChoices.B: Most people whose skin is prematurely wrinkled have spent a large amount of time in the sun without wearing sunscreen.
answerChoices.C: The specific cause of premature skin wrinkling was not known until about ten years ago.
answerChoices.D: People who wear sunscreen now are less likely to become sunburned than were people who spent the same amount of time in the sun wearing sunscreen ten years ago.
answerChoices.E: Until about ten years ago, people who wore sunscreen were no less likely to have premature wrinkles than were people who spent the same amount of time in the sun without wearing sunscreen.

questions.stimulus: Advice columnist: Several scientific studies have shown that, when participating in competitive sports, those people who have recently been experiencing major stress in their lives are several times more likely to suffer serious injuries than are other participants in competitive sports. Since risking serious injury is unwise, no sports activity should be used as a method for coping with stress.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning in the advice columnist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: If people recently under stress should avoid a subset of activities of a certain type, they should avoid all activities of that type.
answerChoices.B: A method for coping with stress should be used only if it has been subjected to scientific study.
answerChoices.C: People who have not been experiencing major stress in their lives should participate in competitive sports.
answerChoices.D: When people have been under considerable stress, they should engage in competitive activities in order to relieve the stress.
answerChoices.E: People with a history of sports injuries should not engage in sports activities if they have recently been under stress.

questions.stimulus: Tent caterpillars’ routes between their nests and potential food sources are marked with chemical traces called pheromones that the caterpillars leave behind. Moreover, routes from food sources back to the nest are marked more heavily than are merely exploratory routes that have failed to turn up a food source. Thus, tent caterpillars are apparently among the insect species that engage in communal foraging, which consists in the conveying of information concerning the location of food to other members of the colony, nest, or hive.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, adds the most support to the argument?

answerChoices.A: A hungry tent caterpillar is more likely to follow heavily marked routes than lightly marked routes.
answerChoices.B: Tent caterpillars can detect the presence but not the concentration of pheromones.
answerChoices.C: Sometimes individual tent caterpillars will not return to the nest until a food source is located.
answerChoices.D: The pheromones left by tent caterpillars are different from the pheromones left by other animals.
answerChoices.E: The pheromones that tent caterpillars leave behind are detectable by certain other species of caterpillars.

questions.stimulus: Many movies starring top actors will do well at the box office because the actors are already well known and have a loyal following. Movies starring unknown actors are therefore unlikely to do well.
questions.questionStem: The flawed reasoning in the argument above is most similar to that in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Many animals must devote most of their energy to locating food, or they will not get enough food to maintain optimal energy levels. Thus, if immediate survival requires such an animal to devote most of its energy to some other purpose, optimal energy levels generally will not be maintained.
answerChoices.B: Often the presence of the flower bee balm in a garden will attract bumblebees that pollinate the plants and enable the garden to produce an abundant crop. So, gardens that lack bee balm usually do not produce abundant crops.
answerChoices.C: A person’s ability to keep confidences is a large part of being a friend, since frequently such an ability enables a high degree of openness in communication. Thus, a high degree of openness in communication is an essential feature of friendship.
answerChoices.D: Visual aids can be very useful in effectively teaching math skills, because they generally allow vivid conceptualization of math principles. If such visual aids were never employed, therefore, teaching math skills might sometimes be more difficult.
answerChoices.E: An understanding of the rules of perspective is necessary for achieving success as a painter, since it is the understanding of these most basic rules that allows the painter to paint realistically. Thus, painters with an understanding of the rules of perspective will achieve success.

questions.stimulus: As part of a new trend in the writing of history, an emphasis on the details of historical events and motivations has replaced the previous emphasis on overarching historical trends and movements, with the result that the latter are often overlooked. In consequence, the ominous parallels that may exist between historical trends and current trends are also overlooked, which lessens our ability to learn from history.
questions.questionStem: The statements above, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?
