answerChoices.C: It is a premise in support of the claim that the quality of human relations in technologically advanced societies is extremely poor.
answerChoices.D: It is a generalization based on the claim that the more people resist technological innovations, the more difficult it is for them to adjust to those innovations.
answerChoices.E: It is an example presented to illustrate the claim that resistance to technological innovations deeply affects the quality of human relations.

questions.stimulus: To win democratic elections that are not fully subsidized by the government, nonwealthy candidates must be supported by wealthy patrons. This makes plausible the belief that these candidates will compromise their views to win that support. But since the wealthy are dispersed among the various political parties in roughly equal proportion to their percentage in the overall population, this belief is false.
questions.questionStem: The argument is vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it fails to consider that

answerChoices.A: the primary function of political parties in democracies whose governments do not subsidize elections might not be to provide a means of negating the influence of wealth on elections
answerChoices.B: in democracies in which elections are not fully subsidized by the government, positions endorsed by political parties might be much less varied than the positions taken by candidates
answerChoices.C: in democracies, government-subsidized elections ensure that the views expressed by the people who run for office might not be overly influenced by the opinions of the wealthiest people in those countries
answerChoices.D: in democracies in which elections are not fully subsidized by the government, it might be no easier for a wealthy person to win an election than it is for a nonwealthy person to win an election
answerChoices.E: a democracy in which candidates do not compromise their views in order to be elected to office might have other flaws

questions.stimulus: In modern "brushless" car washes, cloth strips called mitters have replaced brushes. Mitters are easier on most cars' finishes than brushes are. This is especially important with the new clear-coat finishes found on many cars today, which are more easily scratched than older finishes are.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the statements above, if those statements are true?

answerChoices.A: When car washes all used brushes rather than mitters, there were more cars on the road with scratched finishes than there are today.
answerChoices.B: Modern "brushless" car washes were introduced as a direct response to the use of clear-coat finishes on cars.
answerChoices.C: Modern "brushless" car washes usually do not produce visible scratches on cars with older finishes.
answerChoices.D: Brushes are more effective than mitters and are preferred for cleaning cars with older finishes.
answerChoices.E: More cars in use today have clear-coat finishes rather than older finishes.

questions.stimulus: It is widely believed that lancelets—small, primitive sea animals—do not have hearts. Each lancelet has a contracting vessel, but this vessel is considered an artery rather than a heart. However, this vessel is indeed a heart. After all, it strongly resembles the structure of the heart of certain other sea animals. Moreover, the muscular contractions in the lancelet's vessel closely resemble the muscular contractions of other animals' hearts.
questions.questionStem: The argument's conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Only animals that have contracting vessels have hearts.
answerChoices.B: Some primitive animals other than lancelets have what is widely held to be a heart.
answerChoices.C: A vessel whose structure and actions closely resemble those of other animal hearts is a heart.
answerChoices.D: For a vessel in an animal to be properly considered a heart, that vessel must undergo muscular contractions.
answerChoices.E: No animal that has a heart lacks an artery.

questions.stimulus: Manager: I recommend that our company reconsider the decision to completely abandon our allegedly difficult-to-use computer software and replace it companywide with a new software package advertised as more flexible and easier to use. Several other companies in our region officially replaced the software we currently use with the new package, and while their employees can all use the new software, unofficially many continue to use their former software as much as possible.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the manager's statements?

answerChoices.A: The current company software is as flexible as the proposed new software package.
answerChoices.B: The familiarity that employees have with a computer software package is a more important consideration in selecting software than flexibility or initial ease of use.
answerChoices.C: The employees of the manager's company would find that the new software package lacks some of the capabilities of the present software.
answerChoices.D: Adopting the new software package would create two classes of employees, those who can use it and those who cannot.
answerChoices.E: Many of the employees in the manager's company would not prefer the new software package to the software currently in use.

questions.stimulus: Commentator: Although the present freshwater supply is adequate for today's patterns of water use, the human population will increase substantially over the next few decades, drastically increasing the need for freshwater. Hence, restrictions on water use will be necessary to meet the freshwater needs of humankind in the not-too-distant future.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: Humans will adapt to restrictions on the use of water without resorting to wasteful use of other natural resources.
answerChoices.B: The total supply of freshwater has not diminished in recent years.
answerChoices.C: The freshwater supply will not increase sufficiently to meet the increased needs of humankind.
answerChoices.D: No attempt to synthesize water will have an appreciable effect on the quantity of freshwater available.
answerChoices.E: No water conservation measure previously attempted yielded an increase in the supply of freshwater available for human use.

questions.stimulus: Psychologist: The best way to recall a certain word or name that one is having trouble remembering is to occupy one's mind with other things, since often the more we strive to remember a certain word or name that we can't think of, the less likely it becomes that the word will come to mind.
questions.questionStem: The principle that underlies the psychologist's argument underlies which one of the following arguments?

answerChoices.A: Often, the best way to achieve happiness is to pursue other things besides wealth and fame, for there are wealthy and famous people who are not particularly happy, which suggests that true happiness does not consist in wealth and fame.
answerChoices.B: The best way to succeed in writing a long document is not to think about how much is left to write but only about the current paragraph, since on many occasions thinking about what remains to be done will be so discouraging that the writer will be tempted to abandon the project.
answerChoices.C: The best way to overcome a serious mistake is to continue on confidently as though all is well. After all, one can overcome a serious mistake by succeeding in new challenges, and dwelling on one's errors usually distracts one's mind from new challenges.
answerChoices.D: The best way to fall asleep quickly is to engage in some mental diversion like counting sheep, because frequently the more one concentrates on falling asleep the lower the chance of falling asleep quickly.
answerChoices.E: The best way to cope with sorrow or grief is to turn one's attention to those who are experiencing even greater hardship, for in many circumstances this will make our own troubles seem bearable by comparison.

questions.stimulus: Letter to the editor: The Planning Department budget increased from $100,000 in 2001 to $524,000 for this year. However, this does not justify your conclusion in yesterday's editorial that the department now spends five times as much money as it did in 2001 to perform the same duties.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to support the claim made in the letter regarding the justification of the editorial's conclusion?

answerChoices.A: Departments other than the Planning Department have had much larger budget increases since 2001.
answerChoices.B: Since 2001, the Planning Department has dramatically reduced its spending on overtime pay.
answerChoices.C: In some years between 2001 and this year, the Planning Department budget did not increase.
answerChoices.D: The budget figures used in the original editorial were adjusted for inflation.
answerChoices.E: A restructuring act, passed in 2003, broadened the duties of the Planning Department.

questions.stimulus: At mock trials in which jury instructions were given in technical legal jargon, jury verdicts tended to mirror the judge's own opinions. Jurors had become aware of the judge's nonverbal behavior: facial expressions, body movements, tone of voice. Jurors who viewed the same case but were given instruction in clear, nontechnical language, however, were comparatively more likely to return verdicts at odds with the judge's opinion.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is best illustrated by the example described above?

answerChoices.A: Technical language tends to be more precise than nontechnical language.
answerChoices.B: A person's influence is proportional to that person's perceived status.
answerChoices.C: Nonverbal behavior is not an effective means of communication.
answerChoices.D: Real trials are better suited for experimentation than are mock trials.
answerChoices.E: The way in which a judge instructs a jury can influence the jury's verdict.

questions.stimulus: Doctor: While a few alternative medicines have dangerous side effects, some, such as many herbs, have been proven safe to consume. Thus, though there is little firm evidence of medicinal effect, advocates of these herbs as remedies for serious illnesses should always be allowed to prescribe them, since their patients will not be harmed, and might be helped, by the use of these products.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the doctor's argument?

answerChoices.A: Many practitioners and patients neglect more effective conventional medicines in favor of herbal remedies.
answerChoices.B: Many herbal remedies are marketed with claims of proven effectiveness when in fact their effectiveness is unproven.
answerChoices.C: Some patients may have allergic reactions to certain medicines that have been tolerated by other patients.
answerChoices.D: The vast majority of purveyors of alternative medicines are driven as much by the profit motive as by a regard for their patients' health.
answerChoices.E: Any pain relief or other benefits of many herbs have been proven to derive entirely from patients' belief in the remedy, rather than from its biochemical properties.

questions.stimulus: When a nation is on the brink of financial crisis, its government does not violate free-market principles if, in order to prevent economic collapse, it limits the extent to which foreign investors and lenders can withdraw their money. After all, the right to free speech does not include the right to shout "Fire!" in a crowded theatre, and the harm done as investors and lenders rush madly to get their money out before everyone else does can be just as real as the harm resulting from a stampede in a theatre.
questions.questionStem: The argument does which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: tries to show that a set of principles is limited in a specific way by using an analogy to a similar principle that is limited in a similar way
answerChoices.B: infers a claim by arguing that the truth of that claim would best explain observed facts
answerChoices.C: presents numerous experimental results as evidence for a general principle
answerChoices.D: attempts to demonstrate that an explanation of a phenomenon is flawed by showing that it fails to explain a particular instance of that phenomenon
answerChoices.E: applies an empirical generalization to reach a conclusion about a particular case

questions.stimulus: Although many political candidates object to being made the target of advertising designed to cast them in an adverse light, such advertising actually benefits its targets because most elections have been won by candidates who were the targets of that kind of advertising.
questions.questionStem: The pattern of flawed reasoning in the argument most closely parallels that in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Although many people dislike physical exercise, they should exercise because it is a good way to improve their overall health.
answerChoices.B: Although many actors dislike harsh reviews of their work, such reviews actually help their careers because most of the really prestigious acting awards have gone to actors who have had performances of theirs reviewed harshly.
answerChoices.C: Although many students dislike studying, it must be a good way to achieve academic success because most students who study pass their courses.
answerChoices.D: Although many film critics dislike horror films, such films are bound to be successful because a large number of people are eager to attend them.
answerChoices.E: Although many people dislike feeling sleepy as a result of staying up late the previous night, such sleepiness must be acceptable to those who experience it because most people who stay up late enjoy doing so.

questions.stimulus: Working residents of Springfield live, on average, farther from their workplaces than do working residents of Rorchester. Thus, one would expect that the demand for public transportation would be greater in Springfield than in Rorchester. However, Springfield has only half as many bus routes as Rorchester.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, contributes to a resolution of the apparent discrepancy described above except:

answerChoices.A: Three-fourths of the Springfield workforce is employed at the same factory outside the city limits.
answerChoices.B: The average number of cars per household is higher in Springfield than in Rorchester.
answerChoices.C: Rorchester has fewer railway lines than Springfield.
answerChoices.D: Buses in Springfield run more frequently and on longer routes than in Rorchester.
answerChoices.E: Springfield has a larger population than Rorchester does.

questions.stimulus: People who need to reduce their intake of fat and to consume fewer calories often turn to fat substitutes, especially those with zero calories such as N5. But studies indicate that N5 is of no use to such people. Subjects who ate foods prepared with N5 almost invariably reported feeling hungrier afterwards than after eating foods prepared with real fat and consequently they ate more, quickly making up for the calories initially saved by using N5.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument fails to consider the possibility that

answerChoices.A: many foods cannot be prepared with N5
answerChoices.B: N5 has mild but unpleasant side effects
answerChoices.C: not everyone who eats foods prepared with N5 pays attention to caloric intake
answerChoices.D: people who know N5 contains zero calories tend to eat more foods prepared with N5 than do people who are unaware that N5 is calorie-free
answerChoices.E: the total fat intake of people who eat foods prepared with N5 tends to decrease even if their caloric intake does not

questions.stimulus: Music historian: Some critics lament the fact that impoverished postwar recording studios forced early bebop musicians to record extremely short solos, thus leaving a misleading record of their music. But these musicians' beautifully concise playing makes the recordings superb artistic works instead of mere representations of their live solos. Furthermore, the conciseness characteristic of early bebop musicians' recordings fostered a compactness in their subsequent live playing, which the playing of the next generation lacks.
questions.questionStem: The music historian's statements, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Representations of live solos generally are not valuable artistic works.
answerChoices.B: The difficult postwar recording conditions had some beneficial consequences for bebop.
answerChoices.C: Short bebop recordings are always superior to longer ones.
answerChoices.D: The music of the generation immediately following early bebop is of lower overall quality than early bebop.
answerChoices.E: Musicians will not record extremely short solos unless difficult recording conditions force them to do so.

questions.stimulus: Recent studies indicate a correlation between damage to human chromosome number six and adult schizophrenia. We know, however, that there are people without damage to this chromosome who develop adult schizophrenia and that some people with damage to chromosome number six do not develop adult schizophrenia. So there is no causal connection between damage to human chromosome number six and adult schizophrenia.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a reasoning flaw in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: The argument ignores the possibility that some but not all types of damage to chromosome number six lead to schizophrenia.
answerChoices.B: The argument presumes, without providing evidence, that schizophrenia is caused solely by chromosomal damage.
answerChoices.C: The argument makes a generalization based on an unrepresentative sample population.
answerChoices.D: The argument mistakes a cause for an effect.
answerChoices.E: The argument presumes, without providing warrant, that correlation implies causation.

questions.stimulus: City councilperson: Many city residents oppose the city art commission's proposed purchase of an unusual stone edifice, on the grounds that art critics are divided over whether the edifice really qualifies as art. But I argue that the purpose of art is to cause experts to debate ideas, including ideas about what constitutes art itself. Since the edifice has caused experts to debate what constitutes art itself, it does qualify as art.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, enables the conclusion of the city councilperson's argument to be properly inferred?

answerChoices.A: Nothing qualifies as art unless it causes debate among experts.
answerChoices.B: If an object causes debate among experts, no expert can be certain whether that object qualifies as art.
answerChoices.C: The purchase of an object that fulfills the purpose of art should not be opposed.
answerChoices.D: Any object that fulfills the purpose of art qualifies as art.
answerChoices.E: The city art commission should purchase the edifice if it qualifies as art.

questions.stimulus: It is a given that to be an intriguing person, one must be able to inspire the perpetual curiosity of others. Constantly broadening one's abilities and extending one's intellectual reach will enable one to inspire that curiosity. For such a perpetual expansion of one's mind makes it impossible to be fully comprehended, making one a constant mystery to others.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the conclusion drawn in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: To be an intriguing person, one must be able to inspire the perpetual curiosity of others.
answerChoices.B: If one constantly broadens one's abilities and extends one's intellectual reach, one will be able to inspire the perpetual curiosity of others.
answerChoices.C: If one's mind becomes impossible to fully comprehend, one will always be a mystery to others.
answerChoices.D: To inspire the perpetual curiosity of others, one must constantly broaden one's abilities and extend one's intellectual reach.
answerChoices.E: If one constantly broadens one's abilities and extends one's intellectual reach, one will always have curiosity.

questions.stimulus: Theater managers will not rent a film if they do not believe it will generate enough total revenue—including food-and-beverage concession revenue—to yield a profit. Therefore, since film producers want their films to be shown as widely as possible, they tend to make films that theater managers consider attractive to younger audiences.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: Adults consume less of the sort of foods and beverages sold at movie concession stands than do either children or adolescents.
answerChoices.B: Movies of the kinds that appeal to younger audiences almost never also appeal to older audiences.
answerChoices.C: Food-and-beverage concession stands in movie theaters are usually more profitable than the movies that are shown.
answerChoices.D: Theater managers generally believe that a film that is attractive to younger audiences is more likely to be profitable than other films.
answerChoices.E: Films that have an appeal to older audiences almost never generate a profit for theaters that show them.

questions.stimulus: Almost all advances in genetic research give rise to ethical dilemmas. Government is the exclusive source of funding for most genetic research; those projects not funded by government are funded solely by corporations. One or the other of these sources of funding is necessary for any genetic research.
questions.questionStem: If all the statements above are true, then which one of the following must be true?

answerChoices.A: Most advances in genetic research occur in projects funded by government rather than by corporations.
answerChoices.B: Most genetic research funded by government results in advances that give rise to ethical dilemmas.
answerChoices.C: At least some advances in genetic research occur in projects funded by corporations.
answerChoices.D: No ethical dilemmas resulting from advances in genetic research arise without government or corporate funding.
answerChoices.E: As long as government continues to fund genetic research, that research will give rise to ethical dilemmas.

questions.stimulus: Corporate businesses, like species, must adapt to survive. Businesses that are no longer efficient will become extinct. But sometimes a business cannot adapt without changing its core corporate philosophy. Hence, sometimes a business can survive only by becoming a different corporation.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: No business can survive without changing its core corporate philosophy.
answerChoices.B: As a business becomes less efficient, it invariably surrenders its core corporate philosophy.
answerChoices.C: Different corporations have different core corporate philosophies.
answerChoices.D: If a business keeps its core corporate philosophy intact, it will continue to exist.
answerChoices.E: A business cannot change its core corporate philosophy without becoming a different corporation.

questions.stimulus: A survey taken ten years ago of residents of area L showed that although living conditions were slightly below their country's average, most residents of L reported general satisfaction with their living conditions. However, this year the same survey found that while living conditions are now about the same as the national average, most residents of L report general dissatisfaction with their living conditions.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most help to resolve the apparent conflict between the results of the surveys described above?

answerChoices.A: Residents of area L typically value aspects of living conditions different from the aspects of living conditions that are valued by residents of adjacent areas.
answerChoices.B: Between the times that the two surveys were conducted, the average living conditions in L's country had substantially declined.
answerChoices.C: Optimal living conditions were established in the survey by taking into account governmental policies and public demands on three continents.
answerChoices.D: Living conditions in an area generally improve only if residents perceive their situation as somehow in need of improvement.
answerChoices.E: Ten years ago the residents of area L were not aware that their living conditions were below the national average.

questions.stimulus: Travel agent: Although most low-fare airlines have had few, if any, accidents, very few such airlines have been in existence long enough for their safety records to be reliably established. Major airlines, on the other hand, usually have long-standing records reliably indicating their degree of safety. Hence, passengers are safer on a major airline than on one of the newer low-fare airlines.
questions.questionStem: Of the following, which one is the criticism to which the reasoning in the travel agent's argument is most vulnerable?

answerChoices.A: The argument fails to address adequately the possibility that the average major airline has had a total number of accidents as great as the average low-fare airline has had.
answerChoices.B: The argument draws a general conclusion about how safe passengers are on different airlines on the basis of safety records that are each from too brief a period to adequately justify such a conclusion.
answerChoices.C: The argument fails to consider the possibility that long-standing and reliable records documenting an airline's degree of safety may indicate that the airline is unsafe.
answerChoices.D: The argument takes for granted that airlines that are the safest are also the most reliable in documenting their safety.
answerChoices.E: The argument fails to address adequately the possibility that even airlines with long-standing, reliable records indicating their degree of safety are still likely to have one or more accidents.

questions.stimulus: Economist: Our economy's weakness is the direct result of consumers' continued reluctance to spend, which in turn is caused by factors such as high-priced goods and services. This reluctance is exacerbated by the fact that the average income is significantly lower than it was five years ago. Thus, even though it is not a perfect solution, if the government were to lower income taxes, the economy would improve.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the economist's argument?

answerChoices.A: Increasing consumer spending will cause prices for goods and services to decrease.
answerChoices.B: If consumer spending increases, the average income will increase.
answerChoices.C: If income taxes are not lowered, consumers' wages will decline even further.
answerChoices.D: Consumers will be less reluctant to spend money if income taxes are lowered.
answerChoices.E: Lowering income taxes will have no effect on government spending.

questions.stimulus: A person with a type B lipid profile is at much greater risk of heart disease than a person with a type A lipid profile. In an experiment, both type A volunteers and type B volunteers were put on a low-fat diet. The cholesterol levels of the type B volunteers soon dropped substantially, although their lipid profiles were unchanged. The type A volunteers, however, showed no benefit from the diet, and 40 percent of them actually shifted to type B profiles.
questions.questionStem: If the information above is true, which one of the following must also be true?

answerChoices.A: In the experiment, most of the volunteers had their risk of heart disease reduced at least marginally as a result of having been put on the diet.
answerChoices.B: People with type B lipid profiles have higher cholesterol levels, on average, than do people with type A lipid profiles.
answerChoices.C: Apart from adopting the low-fat diet, most of the volunteers did not substantially change any aspect of their lifestyle that would have affected their cholesterol levels or lipid profiles.
answerChoices.D: The reduction in cholesterol levels in the volunteers is solely responsible for the change in their lipid profiles.
answerChoices.E: For at least some of the volunteers in the experiment, the risk of heart disease increased after having been put on the low-fat diet.

questions.stimulus: Columnist: Although there is and should be complete freedom of thought and expression, that does not mean that there is nothing wrong with exploiting depraved popular tastes for the sake of financial gain.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following judgments conforms most closely to the principle cited by the columnist?

answerChoices.A: The government should grant artists the right to create whatever works of art they want to create so long as no one considers those works to be depraved.
answerChoices.B: People who produce depraved movies have the freedom to do so, but that means that they also have the freedom to refrain from doing so.
answerChoices.C: There should be no laws restricting what books are published, but publishing books that pander to people with depraved tastes is not thereby morally acceptable.
answerChoices.D: The public has the freedom to purchase whatever recordings are produced, but that does not mean that the government may not limit the production of recordings deemed to be depraved.
answerChoices.E: One who advocates complete freedom of speech should not criticize others for saying things that he or she believes to exhibit depraved tastes.

questions.stimulus: When a society undergoes slow change, its younger members find great value in the advice of its older members. But when a society undergoes rapid change, young people think that little in the experience of their elders is relevant to them, and so do not value their advice. Thus, we may measure the rate at which a society is changing by measuring the amount of deference its younger members show to their elders.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: A society's younger members can often accurately discern whether that society is changing rapidly.
answerChoices.B: How much deference young people show to their elders depends on how much of the elders' experience is practically useful to them.
answerChoices.C: The deference young people show to their elders varies according to how much the young value their elders' advice.
answerChoices.D: The faster a society changes, the less relevant the experience of older members of the society is to younger members.
answerChoices.E: Young people value their elders' advice just insofar as the elders' experience is practically useful to them.

questions.stimulus: Politician: We should impose a tariff on imported fruit to make it cost consumers more than domestic fruit. Otherwise, growers from other countries who can grow better fruit more cheaply will put domestic fruit growers out of business. This will result in farmland's being converted to more lucrative industrial uses and the consequent vanishing of a unique way of life.
questions.questionStem: The politician's recommendation most closely conforms to which one of the following principles?

answerChoices.A: A country should put its own economic interest over that of other countries.
answerChoices.B: The interests of producers should always take precedence over those of consumers.
answerChoices.C: Social concerns should sometimes take precedence over economic efficiency.
answerChoices.D: A country should put the interests of its own citizens ahead of those of citizens of other countries.
answerChoices.E: Government intervention sometimes creates more economic efficiency than free markets.

questions.stimulus: The Kiffer Forest Preserve, in the northernmost part of the Abbimac Valley, is where most of the bears in the valley reside. During the eight years that the main road through the preserve has been closed the preserve's bear population has nearly doubled. Thus, the valley's bear population will increase if the road is kept closed.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most undermines the argument?

answerChoices.A: Most of the increase in the preserve's bear population over the past eight years is due to migration.
answerChoices.B: Only some of the increase in the preserve's bear population over the past eight years is due to migration of bears from other parts of the Abbimac Valley.
answerChoices.C: Only some of the increase in the preserve's bear population over the past eight years is due to migration of bears from outside the Abbimac Valley.
answerChoices.D: The bear population in areas of the Abbimac Valley outside the Kiffer Forest Preserve has decreased over the past eight years.
answerChoices.E: The bear population in the Abbimac Valley has remained about the same over the past eight years.

questions.stimulus: If a wig has any handmade components, it is more expensive than one with none. Similarly, a made-to-measure wig ranges from medium-priced to expensive. Handmade foundations are never found on wigs that do not use human hair. Furthermore, any wig that contains human hair should be dry-cleaned. So all made-to-measure wigs should be dry-cleaned.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion of the argument follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Any wig whose price falls in the medium-priced to expensive range has a handmade foundation.
answerChoices.B: If a wig's foundation is handmade, then it is more expensive than one whose foundation is not handmade.
answerChoices.C: A wig that has any handmade components should be dry-cleaned.
answerChoices.D: If a wig's foundation is handmade, then its price is at least in the medium range.
answerChoices.E: Any wig that should be dry-cleaned has a foundation that is handmade.

questions.stimulus: Philosopher: Wolves do not tolerate an attack by one wolf on another if the latter wolf demonstrates submission by baring its throat. The same is true of foxes and domesticated dogs. So it would be erroneous to deny that animals have rights on the grounds that only human beings are capable of obeying moral rules.
questions.questionStem: The philosopher's argument proceeds by attempting to

answerChoices.A: provide counterexamples to refute a premise on which a particular conclusion is based
answerChoices.B: establish inductively that all animals possess some form of morality
answerChoices.C: cast doubt on the principle that being capable of obeying moral rules is a necessary condition for having rights
answerChoices.D: establish a claim by showing that the denial of that claim entails a logical contradiction
answerChoices.E: provide evidence suggesting that the concept of morality is often applied too broadly

questions.stimulus: Students in a first-year undergraduate course were divided into two groups. All the students in both groups were given newspaper articles identical in every respect, except for the headline, which was different for each group. When the students were later asked questions about the contents of the article, the answers given by the two groups were markedly different, though within each group the answers were similar.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Readers base their impressions of what is in a newspaper on headlines alone.
answerChoices.B: Newspaper headlines hamper a reader's ability to comprehend the corresponding articles.
answerChoices.C: Careless reading is more common among firstyear undergraduates than among more senior students.
answerChoices.D: Newspaper headlines tend to be highly misleading.
answerChoices.E: Newspaper headlines influence a reader's interpretation of the corresponding articles.

questions.stimulus: All works of art are beautiful and have something to teach us. Thus, since the natural world as a whole is both beautiful and instructive, it is a work of art.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: uses the inherently vague term "beautiful" without providing an explicit definition of that term
answerChoices.B: attempts to establish an evaluative conclusion solely on the basis of claims about factual matters
answerChoices.C: concludes, simply because an object possesses two qualities that are each common to all works of art, that the object is a work of art
answerChoices.D: presumes, without providing justification, that only objects that are beautiful are instructive
answerChoices.E: fails to consider the possibility that there are many things that are both beautiful and instructive but are not part of the natural world

questions.stimulus: When Copernicus changed the way we think about the solar system, he did so not by discovering new information, but by looking differently at information already available. Edward Jenner's discovery of a smallpox vaccine occurred when he shifted his focus to disease prevention from the then more common emphasis on cure. History is replete with breakthroughs of this sort.
questions.questionStem: The examples provided above illustrate which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Many valuable intellectual accomplishments occur by chance.
answerChoices.B: Shifting from earlier modes of thought can result in important advances.
answerChoices.C: The ability to look at information from a different point of view is rare.
answerChoices.D: Understanding is advanced less often by better organization of available information than it is by the accumulation of new information.
answerChoices.E: Dramatic intellectual breakthroughs are more easily accomplished in fields in which the amount of information available is relatively small.

questions.stimulus: Politician: Suppose censorship is wrong in itself, as modern liberals tend to believe. Then an actor's refusing a part in a film because the film glamorizes a point of view abhorrent to the actor would be morally wrong. But this conclusion is absurd. It follows that censorship is not, after all, wrong in itself.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the politician's argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that this argument

answerChoices.A: presumes, without providing justification, that actors would subscribe to any tenet of modern liberalism
answerChoices.B: uses the term "liberal" in order to discredit opponents' point of view
answerChoices.C: takes for granted that there is a moral obligation to practice one's profession
answerChoices.D: draws a conclusion that is inconsistent with a premise it accepts
answerChoices.E: presumes, without providing justification, that declining a film role constitutes censorship in the relevant sense

questions.stimulus: Motor oil serves to lubricate engines and thus retard engine wear. A study was conducted to assess the effectiveness of various brands of motor oil by using them in taxicabs over a 6,000-mile test period. All the oils did equally well in retarding wear on pistons and cylinders, the relevant parts of the engine. Hence, cheaper brands of oil are the best buys.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Cheaper brands of motor oil are often used by knowledgeable automobile mechanics for their own cars.
answerChoices.B: Tests other than of the ability to reduce engine wear also can reliably gauge the quality of motor oil.
answerChoices.C: The lubricating properties of all motor oils deteriorate over time, and the rate of deterioration is accelerated by heat.
answerChoices.D: The engines of some individual cars that have had their oil changed every 3,000 miles, using only a certain brand of oil, have lasted an extraordinarily long time.
answerChoices.E: Ability to retard engine wear is not the only property of motor oil important to the running of an engine.

questions.stimulus:
Elena: The best form of government is one that fosters the belief among its citizens that they have a say in how the government is run. Thus, democracy is the best form of government.
Marsha: But there are many forms of government under which citizens can be manipulated into believing they have a say when they don't.
questions.questionStem: Marsha's claim that it is possible for governments to manipulate people into thinking that they have a say when they do not is used to

answerChoices.A: concur with Elena's claim that democracy is the best form of government
answerChoices.B: support Marsha's unstated conclusion that the best form of government is one that appears to be democratic but really is not
answerChoices.C: suggest that the premise Elena uses to support her conclusion could be used to support a conflicting conclusion
answerChoices.D: support Marsha's unstated conclusion that most people seek only the appearance of democracy rather than democracy itself
answerChoices.E: reject Elena's conclusion that the best form of government is democracy

questions.stimulus: Researcher: The use of the newest drug in treating this disease should be discontinued. The treatment usually wreaks havoc with the normal functioning of the human body, causing severe side effects such as total loss of hair, debilitating nausea, and intense pain in the joints.
questions.questionStem: The argument's reasoning is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: fails to specify what is meant by "normal functioning of the human body"
answerChoices.B: fails to consider the consequences of not administering the treatment
answerChoices.C: presumes that every patient with the disease is treated with the drug
answerChoices.D: does not consider the length of time needed for the treatment to begin taking effect
answerChoices.E: does not acknowledge that the effects of the treatment may not be of the same severity in all cases

questions.stimulus:
Otis: Aristotle's principle of justice says that we should treat relevantly similar cases similarly. Therefore, it is wrong for a dentist to schedule an after-hours appointment to suit a family friend but refuse to do it for anyone else.
Tyra: I accept Aristotle's principle of justice, but it's human nature to want to do special favors for friends. Indeed, that's what friends are—those for whom you would do special favors. It's not unjust for dentists to do that.
questions.questionStem: It can be inferred on the basis of their statements that Otis and Tyra disagree about whether

answerChoices.A: Aristotle's principle of justice is widely applicable
answerChoices.B: situations involving friends and situations involving others should be considered relevantly similar cases
answerChoices.C: human nature makes it impossible to treat relevantly similar cases similarly
answerChoices.D: dentists should be willing to schedule an after-hours appointment for anyone who asks
answerChoices.E: Aristotle recognizes that friendship sometimes morally outweighs justice

questions.stimulus: Typically, people who have diets high in saturated fat have an increased risk of heart disease. Those who replace saturated fat in their diets with unsaturated fat decrease their risk of heart disease. Therefore, people who eat a lot of saturated fat can lower their risk of heart disease by increasing their intake of unsaturated fat.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, most helps to justify the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: People who add unsaturated fat to their diets will eat less food that is high in saturated fat.
answerChoices.B: Adding unsaturated fat to a diet brings health benefits other than a reduced risk of heart disease.
answerChoices.C: Diet is the most important factor in a person's risk of heart disease.
answerChoices.D: Taking steps to prevent heart disease is one of the most effective ways of increasing life expectancy.
answerChoices.E: It is difficult to move from a diet that is high in saturated fat to a diet that includes very little fat.

questions.stimulus: Only people who are willing to compromise should undergo mediation to resolve their conflicts. Actual litigation should be pursued only when one is sure that one's position is correct. People whose conflicts are based on ideology are unwilling to compromise.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, then which one of the following must be true?

answerChoices.A: People who do not undergo mediation to resolve their conflicts should be sure that their positions are correct.
answerChoices.B: People whose conflicts are not based on ideology should attempt to resolve their conflicts by means of litigation.
answerChoices.C: People whose conflicts are based on ideology are not always sure that their positions are correct.
answerChoices.D: People who are sure of the correctness of their positions are not people who should undergo mediation to resolve their conflicts.
answerChoices.E: People whose conflicts are based on ideology are not people who should undergo mediation to resolve their conflicts.

questions.stimulus: Scientists have long thought that omega-3 fatty acids in fish oil tend to lower blood cholesterol and strongly suspected that a diet that includes a modest amount of fish would provide substantial health benefits. Now these views have acquired strong support from a recent study showing that middle-aged people who eat fish twice a week are nearly 30 percent less likely to develop heart disease than are those who do not eat fish.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: The test subjects in the recent study who did not eat fish were not vegetarians.
answerChoices.B: The test subjects in the recent study who ate fish twice a week did not have a diet that was otherwise conducive to the development of heart disease.
answerChoices.C: The test subjects in the recent study who did not eat fish were significantly more likely to eat red meat several times per week than were those who did eat fish.
answerChoices.D: The test subjects in the recent study who ate fish twice a week were not significantly more likely than those who did not to engage regularly in activities known to augment cardiorespiratory health.
answerChoices.E: The test subjects in the recent study who ate fish twice a week were no more likely than those who did not to have sedentary occupations.

questions.stimulus: Researcher: A number of studies have suggested that, on average, clients in short-term psychotherapy show similar levels of improvement regardless of the kind of psychotherapy they receive. So any client improvement in short-term psychotherapy must be the result of some aspect or aspects of therapy that are common to all psychotherapies—for example, the presence of someone who listens and gives attention to the client.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most weaken the researcher's argument?

answerChoices.A: The methods by which the studies measured whether clients improved primarily concerned immediate symptom relief and failed to address other important kinds of improvement.
answerChoices.B: On average, clients improve more dramatically when they receive long-term psychotherapy, a year or longer in duration, than when clients receive short-term psychotherapy.
answerChoices.C: The studies found that psychotherapy by a trained counselor does not result in any greater improvement, on average, among clients than does simple counseling by an untrained layperson.
answerChoices.D: The specific techniques and interventions used by therapists practicing different kinds of psychotherapy differ dramatically.
answerChoices.E: More-experienced therapists tend to use a wider range of techniques and interventions in psychotherapy than do inexperienced therapists.

questions.stimulus: Journalists sometimes use historical photographs to illustrate articles about current events. But this recycling of old photographs overstates the similarities between past and present, and thereby denies the individual significance of those current events. Hence, the use of historical photographs in this manner by journalists distorts public understanding of the present by presenting current events as mere repetitions of historical incidents.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, enables the conclusion of the argument to be properly inferred?

answerChoices.A: Any practice by which journalists present current events as mere repetitions of historical incidents overstates the similarities between past and present.
answerChoices.B: If the work of a journalist overstates the similarities between past and present, then it distorts public understanding of the present by presenting current events as mere repetitions of historical incidents.
answerChoices.C: If a journalistic practice distorts public understanding of the present by overstating the similarities between past and present, then it denies the individual significance of any articles about current events.
answerChoices.D: No article about a current event treats that event as merely a repetition of historical incidents unless it uses historical photographs to illustrate that article.
answerChoices.E: If journalists believe current events to be mere repetitions of historical incidents, then public understanding of the present will be distorted.

questions.stimulus: If Juan went to the party, it is highly unlikely that Maria would have enjoyed the party. But in fact it turned out that Maria did enjoy the party; therefore, it is highly unlikely that Juan was at the party.
questions.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in the argument above is most similar to that in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: According to the newspaper, all eight teams in the soccer tournament have an equal chance of winning it. If so, then we will probably lose our goalie, since if we do lose our goalie we will probably not win the tournament.
answerChoices.B: Kapinski, our new neighbor, is probably friendly, for Kapinski sells insurance and most people who sell insurance are friendly.
answerChoices.C: If the lottery were fair, the person who won the lottery would not have been likely to win it. Thus, since this person would have been likely to win the lottery if it were unfair, the lottery was probably unfair.
answerChoices.D: If Clarissa missed the bus today, it is quite unlikely that she would have gotten to work on time. So, it is quite unlikely that Clarissa missed the bus, since she actually was at work on time today.
answerChoices.E: This year's election will probably be fair. But Popov probably will not win unless the election is unfair. So, Popov will not win the election.

questions.stimulus: Sonya: Anyone who lives without constant awareness of the fragility and precariousness of human life has a mind clouded by illusion. Yet those people who are perpetually cognizant of the fragility and precariousness of human life surely taint their emotional outlook on existence.
questions.questionStem: Sonya's statements, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Anyone who places a higher priority on maintaining a positive emotional outlook than on dispelling illusion will be completely unaware of the fragility and precariousness of human life.
answerChoices.B: Either no one has a tainted emotional outlook on existence, or no one has a mind clouded by illusion.
answerChoices.C: It is impossible for anyone to live without some degree of self-deception.
answerChoices.D: Everyone whose emotional outlook on existence is untainted has a mind clouded by illusion.
answerChoices.E: It is better to be aware of the fragility and precariousness of human life than to have an untainted emotional outlook on existence.

questions.stimulus: In a study, shoppers who shopped in a grocery store without a shopping list and bought only items that were on sale for half price or less spent far more money on a comparable number of items than did shoppers in the same store who used a list and bought no sale items.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the apparent paradox in the study's results?

answerChoices.A: Only the shoppers who used a list used a shopping cart.
answerChoices.B: The shoppers who did not use lists bought many unnecessary items.
answerChoices.C: Usually, only the most expensive items go on sale in grocery stores.
answerChoices.D: The grocery store in the study carries many expensive items that few other grocery stores carry.
answerChoices.E: The grocery store in the study places relatively few items on sale.

questions.stimulus: A group of mountain climbers was studied to determine how they were affected by diminished oxygen in the air at high altitudes. As they climbed past 6,100 meters above sea level, the climbers slurred words, took longer to understand simple sentences, and demonstrated poor judgment. This combination of worsened performances disproves the theory that the area of the brain controlling speech is distinct from that controlling other functions.
questions.questionStem: The argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it overlooks the possibility that

answerChoices.A: the climbers' performance in speech, comprehension, and reasoning was impaired because oxygen deprivation affected their entire brains
answerChoices.B: the climbers' performance in speech, comprehension, and reasoning was better than average before they were studied
answerChoices.C: the climbers showed different levels of impairment in their performance in speech, comprehension, and reasoning
answerChoices.D: some of the effects described were apparent just before the climbers reached 6,100 meters
answerChoices.E: many of the climbers had engaged in special training before the climb because they wanted to improve the efficiency with which their bodies use oxygen

questions.stimulus: It was once thought that pesticide TSX-400 was extremely harmful to the environment but that pesticides Envirochem and Zanar were environmentally harmless. TSX-400 was banned; Envirochem and Zanar were not. However, according to recent studies, Envirochem and Zanar each cause greater environmental harm than does TSX-400. If these studies are accurate, then either Envirochem and Zanar should be banned or TSX-400 should be legalized.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the argumentation?

answerChoices.A: Two pesticides should not both be legal if one is measurably more harmful to the environment than the other is.
answerChoices.B: Two pesticides should both be legal only if neither is harmful to the environment.
answerChoices.C: Two pesticides should both be illegal only if both are harmful to the environment.
answerChoices.D: One pesticide should be legal and another illegal only if the former is less harmful to the environment than is the latter.
answerChoices.E: One pesticide should be legal and another illegal if the former is harmless to the environment and the latter is harmful to it.

questions.stimulus: Recent studies have demonstrated that smokers are more likely than nonsmokers to develop heart disease. Other studies have established that smokers are more likely than others to drink caffeinated beverages. Therefore, even though drinking caffeinated beverages is not thought to be a cause of heart disease, there is a positive correlation between drinking caffeinated beverages and the development of heart disease.
questions.questionStem: The argument's reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument fails to take into account the possibility that

answerChoices.A: smokers who drink caffeinated beverages are less likely to develop heart disease than are smokers who do not drink caffeinated beverages
answerChoices.B: something else, such as dietary fat intake, may be a more important factor in the development of heart disease than are the factors cited in the argument
answerChoices.C: drinking caffeinated beverages is more strongly correlated with the development of heart disease than is smoking
answerChoices.D: it is only among people who have a hereditary predisposition to heart disease that caffeine consumption is positively correlated with the development of heart disease
answerChoices.E: there is a common cause of both the development of heart disease and behaviors such as drinking caffeinated beverages and smoking

questions.stimulus: The layouts of supermarkets are not accidental: they are part of a plan designed to make customers walk all the way to the back of the store just to pick up a loaf of bread, passing tempting displays the whole way. But supermarkets can alienate customers by placing popular items in the rear; surveys list inconvenience as shoppers' top reason for disliking supermarkets.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following propositions does the passage most precisely illustrate?

answerChoices.A: Supermarkets should focus on customers who want to purchase many items in a single trip.
answerChoices.B: Alienation of customers is not good for business.
answerChoices.C: Even well-thought-out plans can fail.
answerChoices.D: Distracting customers is not good for business.
answerChoices.E: Manipulation of people can have unwelcome consequences.

questions.stimulus: Doctor: Medication to reduce blood pressure often has unhealthy side effects. However, lifestyle changes such as exercising more and avoiding fatty foods reduce blood pressure just as effectively as taking medication does. Therefore, it is healthier to rely on these lifestyle changes than on medication to reduce blood pressure.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption that the doctor's argument requires?

answerChoices.A: Other than medication, the only way to reduce blood pressure is by making lifestyle changes such as exercising more and avoiding fatty foods.
answerChoices.B: If it is healthier to rely on a lifestyle change than on medication to reduce blood pressure, then that lifestyle change reduces blood pressure at least as effectively as medication does.
answerChoices.C: The side effects, if any, of exercising more and avoiding fatty foods in order to reduce blood pressure are less unhealthy than those of taking medication to reduce blood pressure.
answerChoices.D: If an alternative to medication relieves a medical condition just as effectively as medication does, then it is always healthier to rely on that alternative than on medication to relieve that medical condition.
answerChoices.E: If two different methods of treating a medical condition have similar side effects, then it is healthier to rely on the more effective method.

questions.stimulus: Columnist: Several recent studies show, and insurance statistics confirm, that more pedestrians are killed every year in North American cities when crossing with the light than when crossing against it. Crossing against the light in North American cities is therefore less dangerous than crossing with the light.
questions.questionStem: The columnist's reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it

answerChoices.A: relies on sources that are likely to be biased in their reporting
answerChoices.B: presumes, without providing justification, that because two things are correlated there must be a causal relationship between them
answerChoices.C: does not adequately consider the possibility that a correlation between two events may be explained by a common cause
answerChoices.D: ignores the possibility that the effects of the types of actions considered might be quite different in environments other than the ones studied
answerChoices.E: ignores possible differences in the frequency of the two actions whose risk is being assessed

questions.stimulus: Many scientific studies have suggested that taking melatonin tablets can induce sleep. But this does not mean that melatonin is helpful in treating insomnia. Most of the studies examined only people without insomnia, and in many of the studies, only a few of the subjects given melatonin appeared to be significantly affected by it.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: A weaker correlation between taking melatonin and the inducement of sleep was found in the studies that included people with insomnia than in the studies that did not.
answerChoices.B: None of the studies that suggested that taking melatonin tablets can induce sleep examined a fully representative sample of the human population.
answerChoices.C: In the studies that included subjects with insomnia, only subjects without insomnia were significantly affected by doses of melatonin.
answerChoices.D: Several people who were in control groups and only given placebos claimed that the tablets induced sleep.
answerChoices.E: If melatonin were helpful in treating insomnia, then every person with insomnia who took doses of melatonin would appear to be significantly affected by it.

questions.stimulus: The asteroid that hit the Yucatán Peninsula 65 million years ago caused both long-term climatic change and a tremendous firestorm that swept across North America. We cannot show that it was this fire that caused the extinction of the triceratops, a North American dinosaur in existence at the time of the impact of the asteroid. Nor can we show that the triceratops became extinct due to the climatic changes resulting from the asteroid's impact. Hence, we cannot attribute the triceratops's extinction to the asteroid's impact.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following has flawed reasoning most similar to the flawed reasoning in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: I know that one cannot move this piano unless one can lift at least 150 kilograms. I doubt that either Leon or Pam can lift 150 kilograms alone. So I doubt that either Leon or Pam can move this piano alone. Thus, I doubt that Leon and Pam can move this piano together.
answerChoices.B: Since we are quite sure that Cheng and Lin are the only candidates in the mayoral election, we can be quite sure that either Cheng or Lin will win the election. Therefore, either we know that Cheng will win or we know that Lin will win.
answerChoices.C: It has not been conclusively proven that the accident was caused by John's driving at excessive speeds. Nor has it been conclusively proven that the accident was the result of John's weaving out of his lane. Hence, it has been conclusively proven that the cause of the accident was neither John's driving at excessive speeds nor John's weaving out of his lane.
answerChoices.D: The flooding in the basement caused damage to the furnace and also caused a short in the electrical system. Fire investigators could not show that the damage to the furnace caused the fire that resulted shortly after the flooding, nor could they show that the fire was caused by the short in the electrical system. Therefore, we cannot claim that the flooding in the basement caused the fire.
answerChoices.E: We have good reason to believe that the cause of the flooding along the coast was the unusually high tides. We also have good reason to believe that the cause of the unusually high tides was either the sun or the moon. So it is reasonable to maintain that the cause of the flooding was either the sun or the moon.

questions.stimulus: Economist: Although obviously cuts in personal income tax rates for the upper income brackets disproportionately benefit the wealthy, across-the-board cuts for all brackets tend to have a similar effect. Personal income tax rates are progressive (i.e., graduated), and if total revenue remains constant, then across-the-board cuts in these taxes require increasing the amount of revenue generated through nonprogressive taxes, thereby favoring the wealthy. Yet if nonprogressive taxes are not increased to compensate for the cuts, then the budget deficit will increase, requiring more government borrowing and driving up interest rates. This favors those who have money to lend, once again benefiting primarily the wealthy.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the economist's argument?

answerChoices.A: Cuts in personal income tax rates for upper income brackets benefit the wealthy more than they benefit others.
answerChoices.B: Across-the-board cuts in personal income tax rates do not generate enough additional economic activity to prevent a net loss of revenue.
answerChoices.C: It is the wealthy who are favored by generating a high amount of revenue through nonprogressive taxes.
answerChoices.D: It is primarily the wealthy who benefit from increases in the budget deficit, which drive up interest rates.
answerChoices.E: Across-the-board personal income tax rate cuts generally benefit the wealthy more than they benefit others.

questions.stimulus: Automated flight technology can guide an aircraft very reliably, from navigation to landing. Yet this technology, even when functioning correctly, is not a perfect safeguard against human error.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the situation described above?

answerChoices.A: Automated flight technology does not always function correctly.
answerChoices.B: Smaller aircraft do not always have their automated flight technology updated regularly.
answerChoices.C: If a plane’s automated flight technology malfunctions, crew members have to operate the plane manually.
answerChoices.D: Some airplane crashes are due neither to human error nor to malfunction of automated flight technology.
answerChoices.E: Automated flight technology invariably executes exactly the commands that humans give it.

questions.stimulus: To keep one’s hands warm during the winter, one never needs gloves or mittens. One can always keep one’s hands warm simply by putting on an extra layer of clothing, such as a thermal undershirt or a sweater. After all, keeping one’s vital organs warm can keep one’s hands warm as well.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Maintaining the temperature of your hands is far less important, physiologically, than maintaining the temperature of your torso.
answerChoices.B: Several layers of light garments will keep one’s vital organs warmer than will one or two heavy garments.
answerChoices.C: Wearing an extra layer of clothing will not keep one’s hands warm at temperatures low enough to cause frostbite.
answerChoices.D: Keeping one’s hands warm by putting on an extra layer of clothing is less effective than turning up the heat.
answerChoices.E: The physical effort required to put on an extra layer of clothing does not stimulate circulation enough to warm your hands.

questions.stimulus: The reason music with a simple recurring rhythm exerts a strong primordial appeal is that it reminds us of the womb environment. After all, the first sound heard within the womb is the comforting sound of the mother’s regular heartbeat. So in taking away from us the warmth and security of the womb, birth also takes away a primal and constant source of comfort. Thus it is extremely natural that in seeking sensations of warmth and security throughout life, people would be strongly drawn toward simple recurring rhythmic sounds.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion drawn in the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: The explanation of the strong primordial appeal of music with a simple recurring rhythm is that it reminds us of the womb environment.
answerChoices.B: The comforting sound of the mother’s regular heartbeat is the first sound that is heard inside the womb.
answerChoices.C: Birth deprives us of a primal and constant source of comfort when it takes away the warmth and security of the womb.
answerChoices.D: People seek sensations of warmth and security throughout life because birth takes away the warmth and security of the womb.
answerChoices.E: The comforting sound of the mother’s regular heartbeat is a simple recurring rhythmic sound.

questions.stimulus: Linguist: Most people can tell whether a sequence of words in their own dialect is grammatical. Yet few people who can do so are able to specify the relevant grammatical rules.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following best illustrates the principle underlying the linguist’s statements?

answerChoices.A: Some people are able to write cogent and accurate narrative descriptions of events. But these people are not necessarily also capable of composing emotionally moving and satisfying poems.
answerChoices.B: Engineers who apply the principles of physics to design buildings and bridges must know a great deal more than do the physicists who discover these principles.
answerChoices.C: Some people are able to tell whether any given piece of music is a waltz. But the majority of these people cannot state the defining characteristics of a waltz.
answerChoices.D: Those travelers who most enjoy their journeys are not always those most capable of vividly describing the details of those journeys to others.
answerChoices.E: Quite a few people know the rules of chess, but only a small number of them can play chess very well.

questions.stimulus: Company president: For the management consultant position, we shall interview only those applicants who have worked for management consulting firms generally recognized as in the top 1 percent of firms worldwide. When we finally select somebody, then, we can be sure to have selected one of the best management consultants available.
questions.questionStem: The company president’s reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it

answerChoices.A: takes for granted that only the best management consultants have worked for the top management consulting firms
answerChoices.B: generalizes from too small a sample of management consulting firms worldwide
answerChoices.C: takes for granted that if something is true of each member of a collection, then it is also true of the collection as a whole
answerChoices.D: presumes, without providing warrant, that persons who have worked for the top companies will accept a job offer
answerChoices.E: presumes, without providing justification, that highly competent management consultants are highly competent at every task

questions.stimulus: Beginners typically decide each chess move by considering the consequences. Expert players, in contrast, primarily use pattern-recognition techniques. That is, such a player recognizes having been in a similar position before and makes a decision based on information recalled about the consequences of moves chosen on that prior occasion.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Beginning chess players are better at thinking through the consequences of chess moves than experts are.
answerChoices.B: A beginning chess player should use pattern-recognition techniques when deciding what move to make.
answerChoices.C: One’s chess skills will improve only if one learns to use pattern-recognition techniques.
answerChoices.D: In playing chess, an expert player relies crucially on his or her memory.
answerChoices.E: Any chess player who played other games that require pattern-recognition skills would thereby improve his or her chess skills.

questions.stimulus: Farmer: Because water content is what makes popcorn pop, the kernels must dry at just the right speed to trap the correct amount of water. The best way to achieve this effect is to have the sun dry the corn while the corn is still in the field, but I always dry the ears on a screen in a warm, dry room.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy between the farmer’s theory and practice?

answerChoices.A: The region in which the farmer grows popcorn experiences a long, cloudy season that begins shortly before the popcorn in fields would begin to dry.
answerChoices.B: Leaving popcorn to dry on its stalks in the field is the least expensive method of drying it.
answerChoices.C: Drying popcorn on its stalks in the field is only one of several methods that allow the kernels’ water content to reach acceptable levels.
answerChoices.D: When popcorn does not dry sufficiently, it will still pop, but it will take several minutes to do so, even under optimal popping conditions.
answerChoices.E: If popcorn is allowed to dry too much, it will not pop.

questions.stimulus: Factory manager: One reason the automobile parts this factory produces are expensive is that our manufacturing equipment is outdated and inefficient. Our products would be more competitively priced if we were to refurbish the factory completely with new, more efficient equipment. Therefore, since to survive in today’s market we have to make our products more competitively priced, we must completely refurbish the factory in order to survive.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the factory manager’s argument is flawed because this argument

answerChoices.A: fails to recognize that the price of a particular commodity can change over time
answerChoices.B: shifts without justification from treating something as one way of achieving a goal to treating it as the only way of achieving that goal
answerChoices.C: argues that one thing is the cause of another when the evidence given indicates that the second thing may in fact be the cause of the first
answerChoices.D: recommends a solution to a problem without first considering any possible causes of that problem
answerChoices.E: fails to make a definite recommendation and instead merely suggests that some possible course of action might be effective

questions.stimulus: Two months ago a major shipment of pythons arrived from Africa, resulting in a great number of inexpensive pythons in pet stores. Anyone interested in buying a python, however, should beware: many pythons hatched in Africa are afflicted with a deadly liver disease. Although a few pythons recently hatched in North America have this disease, a much greater proportion of African-hatched pythons have it. The disease is difficult to detect in its early stages, and all pythons die within six months of contracting the disease.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements can be properly inferred from the statements above?

answerChoices.A: Some pythons hatched in North America may appear fine but will die within six months as a result of the liver disease.
answerChoices.B: Pythons that hatch in Africa are more susceptible to the liver disease than are pythons that hatch in North America.
answerChoices.C: Any python that has not died by the age of six months does not have the liver disease.
answerChoices.D: The pythons are inexpensively priced because many of them suffer from the liver disease.
answerChoices.E: Pythons hatched in neither Africa nor North America are not afflicted with the liver disease.

questions.stimulus: Nutritionists believe that a person’s daily requirement for vitamins can readily be met by eating five servings of fruits and vegetables daily. However, most people eat far less than this. Thus, most people need to take vitamin pills.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Even five servings of fruits and vegetables a day is insufficient unless the intake is varied to ensure that different vitamins are consumed.
answerChoices.B: Certain commonly available fruits and vegetables contain considerably more nutrients than others.
answerChoices.C: Nutritionists sometimes disagree on how much of a fruit or vegetable constitutes a complete serving.
answerChoices.D: Many commonly consumed foods that are neither fruits nor vegetables are fortified by manufacturers with the vitamins found in fruits and vegetables.
answerChoices.E: Fruits and vegetables are also important sources of fiber, in forms not found in vitamin pills.

questions.stimulus: Researcher: This fall I returned to a research site to recover the armadillos I had tagged there the previous spring. Since a large majority of the armadillos I recaptured were found within a few hundred yards of the location of their tagging last spring, I concluded that armadillos do not move rapidly into new territories.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the researcher’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Of the armadillos living in the area of the tagging site last spring, few were able to avoid being tagged by the researcher.
answerChoices.B: Most of the armadillos tagged the previous spring were not recaptured during the subsequent fall.
answerChoices.C: Predators did not kill any of the armadillos that had been tagged the previous spring.
answerChoices.D: The tags identifying the armadillos cannot be removed by the armadillos, either by accident or deliberately.
answerChoices.E: A large majority of the recaptured armadillos did not move to a new territory in the intervening summer and then move back to the old territory by the fall.

questions.stimulus: Sahira: To make a living from their art, artists of great potential would have to produce work that would gain widespread popular acclaim, instead of their best work. That is why governments are justified in subsidizing artists. Rahima: Your argument for subsidizing art depends on claiming that to gain widespread popular acclaim, artists must produce something other than their best work; but this need not be true.
questions.questionStem: In her argument, Rahima

answerChoices.A: disputes an implicit assumption of Sahira’s
answerChoices.B: presents independent support for Sahira’s argument
answerChoices.C: accepts Sahira’s conclusion, but for reasons different from those given by Sahira
answerChoices.D: uses Sahira’s premises to reach a conclusion different from that reached by Sahira
answerChoices.E: argues that a standard that she claims Sahira uses is self-contradictory

questions.stimulus: Adult frogs are vulnerable to dehydration because of their highly permeable skins. Unlike large adult frogs, small adult frogs have such a low ratio of body weight to skin surface area that they cannot survive in arid climates. The animals’ moisture requirements constitute the most important factor determining where frogs can live in the Yucatán peninsula, which has an arid climate in the north and a wet climate in the south.
questions.questionStem: The information above most strongly supports which one of the following conclusions about frogs in the Yucatán peninsula?

answerChoices.A: Large adult frogs cannot coexist with small adult frogs in the wet areas.
answerChoices.B: Frogs living in wet areas weigh more on average than frogs in the arid areas.
answerChoices.C: Large adult frogs can live in more of the area than small adult frogs can.
answerChoices.D: Fewer small adult frogs live in the south than do large adult frogs.
answerChoices.E: Small adult frogs in the south have less permeable skins than small adult frogs in the north.
