answerChoices.C: It is unclear whether the company’s venture succeeded, because the criteria for its success are undefined. But if the venture had had a measurable goal, then it would have been possible to judge its success.
answerChoices.D: A teacher is someone who teaches. In addition, there are people who teach but are not called teachers. So while the number of those called teachers is large, the number of those who teach is even larger.
answerChoices.E: Because someone intervened in the conflict, the effects of that intervention can be discerned. But since no one can investigate what does not happen, it is impossible to discern what would have happened had someone not intervened.

questions.stimulus: Families with underage children make up much of the population, but because only adults can vote, lawmakers in democracies pay too little attention to the interests of these families. To remedy this, parents should be given additional votes to cast on behalf of their underage children. Families with underage children would thus receive fair representation.
questions.questionStem: The argument requires assuming which one of the following principles?

answerChoices.A: The amount of attention that lawmakers give to a group’s interests should be directly proportional to the number of voters in that group.
answerChoices.B: Parents should not be given responsibility for making a decision on their child’s behalf unless their child is not mature enough to decide wisely.
answerChoices.C: The parents of underage children should always consider the best interests of their children when they vote.
answerChoices.D: It is not fair for lawmakers to favor the interests of people who have the vote over the interests of people who do not have the vote.
answerChoices.E: A group of people can be fairly represented in a democracy even if some members of that group can vote on behalf of others in that group.

questions.stimulus: Critic: The Gazette-Standard newspaper recently increased its editorial staff to avoid factual errors. But this clearly is not working. Compared to its biggest competitor, the Gazette-Standard currently runs significantly more corrections acknowledging factual errors.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the critic’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The Gazette-Standard pays its editorial staff lower salaries than its biggest competitor pays its editorial staff.
answerChoices.B: The Gazette-Standard has been in business considerably longer than has its biggest competitor.
answerChoices.C: The Gazette-Standard more actively follows up reader complaints about errors in the paper than does its biggest competitor.
answerChoices.D: The Gazette-Standard’s articles are each checked by more editors than are the articles of its biggest competitor.
answerChoices.E: The increase in the Gazette-Standard’s editorial staff has been offset by a decrease in the reporting staff at the newspaper.

questions.stimulus: For the first few weeks after birth, the dunnart has such poor control over its respiratory muscles that it cannot use them to breathe. Instead, this tiny marsupial breathes through its thin skin, which gradually thickens as the dunnart matures inside its mother’s pouch. The dunnart is unique among warm-blooded animals, the rest of which need thick skin throughout their lives to maintain body temperature and reduce water loss.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps explain how newborn dunnarts manage to survive despite their thin skins?

answerChoices.A: The dunnart’s respiratory muscles begin to develop a few days after birth.
answerChoices.B: The dunnart’s body temperature is higher than that of many other warm-blooded animals.
answerChoices.C: Adult dunnarts experience more heat and water loss through their skin than other adult marsupials do.
answerChoices.D: Its mother’s pouch keeps a newborn dunnart warm and reduces water loss through its skin.
answerChoices.E: Some dunnarts live where daytime temperatures are high and the climate is dry.

questions.stimulus: Successful stand-up comedians are able to keep the attention of a large audience for a few hours, in such a way that the audience remembers long afterwards what the comedian said. And in their routines, many comedians make interesting points about serious topics. Unsurprisingly, humor is the means through which comedians are able to accomplish all of this. University professors hope to achieve much the same in their lectures. Thus, _______.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most logically completes the argument?

answerChoices.A: stand-up comedians and university professors have the same skill set
answerChoices.B: incorporating humor into lectures can help professors to achieve the goals they have for those lectures
answerChoices.C: university professors can achieve the goals they have for their lectures only if they incorporate humor into them
answerChoices.D: there is no reason to suppose that a lecture lasting several hours cannot hold an audience’s attention
answerChoices.E: university professors should treat even the most serious topics in a humorous way

questions.stimulus: Reviewer: Almost all books that offer management advice are written from the perspective of the CEO. But most managers aren’t CEOs and don’t have the same perspective as CEOs. So the advice in management books is of limited use for most managers.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion of the reviewer’s argument can be properly drawn if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Advice books rarely take the perspective of their intended audience.
answerChoices.B: Most people who read management advice books aspire to be CEOs.
answerChoices.C: Almost all CEOs have experience as lower-level managers.
answerChoices.D: Advice is of limited use unless it is offered from the perspective of the recipient.
answerChoices.E: Most managers prefer to read books that they think will be useful to them in their work.

questions.stimulus: The mayor has been accused of taking a bribe based on the fact that a consultant that does business with the city paid for improvements to the mayor’s vacation house. In his own defense, the mayor has said that he paid every bill for those improvements that was presented to him.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most undermines the mayor’s defense?

answerChoices.A: Authorities are investigating the consultant for taking bribes from officials of other cities.
answerChoices.B: The mayor was aware that many of the bills were being presented to the consultant rather than to the mayor.
answerChoices.C: The building contractor in charge of the improvements to the mayor’s house had done business with the city in the past.
answerChoices.D: The improvements to the mayor’s house were done with expensive materials and involved thousands of hours of labor.
answerChoices.E: The amount of money that the city paid the consultant over the last year greatly exceeded the cost of the improvements to the mayor’s house.

questions.stimulus: Archaeologist: The earliest evidence of controlled fire use in Europe dates to just 400,000 years ago. This casts doubt on the commonly held view that, because of Europe’s cold winter climate, mastery of fire was a necessary prerequisite for humans’ migration there.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: The humans who first mastered fire used it for heat but not for cooking.
answerChoices.B: The climate in Europe was significantly colder 400,000 years ago than it is today.
answerChoices.C: Prior to 400,000 years ago, humans occasionally took advantage of naturally occurring fires.
answerChoices.D: Humans would not have mastered fire were it not for the need for heat in a cold climate.
answerChoices.E: There were humans inhabiting Europe prior to 400,000 years ago.

questions.stimulus: Astronomer: This country’s space agency is currently building a new space telescope that is, unfortunately, way over budget. Some people argue that the project should be canceled. But that would be a mistake. If we cancel it now, all the money that has already been spent—which is more than the additional cost required to complete the project—would be wasted.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, would most help to justify the astronomer’s argument?

answerChoices.A: A government agency should not cancel a partially completed project unless the amount of money already spent on the project is small relative to the agency’s overall budget.
answerChoices.B: If more than half of the total cost of a project has already been spent, then the project should be completed.
answerChoices.C: If it becomes clear that the total cost of a project will be more than twice the amount originally budgeted, then the project should be canceled.
answerChoices.D: One should not commit additional funding to a project just because one has spent considerable money on it in the past.
answerChoices.E: In determining which scientific projects to fund, governments should give priority to the projects that are most likely to lead to important new discoveries.

questions.stimulus: Naturalist: Different nonhuman primate species exhibit many contrasts in behavior. If a zookeeper leaves a screwdriver within reach of a chimpanzee, the animal is likely to examine and play with it for a time, and then move on to something else. In the same circumstances, an orangutan is likely to pretend to ignore the tool at first; later, in the zookeeper’s absence, the orangutan may use the screwdriver to try to dismantle its cage.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the naturalist’s statements?

answerChoices.A: Orangutans are the most intelligent of nonhuman primates.
answerChoices.B: Orangutans have better memories than chimpanzees have.
answerChoices.C: Some nonhuman primates are capable of deception.
answerChoices.D: Orangutans dislike being caged more than chimpanzees do.
answerChoices.E: Not all nonhuman primates understand tool use.

questions.stimulus: Manager: The only employees who should receive bonuses this year are those who were exceptionally productive over the past year. Liang is an excellent account executive, but she works in a corporate division that has failed to meet its productivity goals for the year. Thus Liang should not receive a bonus this year.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the manager’s argument is flawed in that the argument

answerChoices.A: fails to take into account the possibility that the standards by which productivity is judged might vary across different divisions of a corporation
answerChoices.B: overlooks the possibility that a corporation as a whole can have a profitable year even though one division of the corporation does not
answerChoices.C: fails to justify its use of one group’s performance as the basis for a conclusion about a wholly different group
answerChoices.D: reaches a conclusion about the performance of one member of a group merely on the basis of the performance of the group as a whole
answerChoices.E: takes for granted that an employee who has an unproductive year will not be exceptionally productive in subsequent years

questions.stimulus: Even though she thought the informant was untrustworthy, the journalist promised not to reveal his identity so long as the information he provided did not turn out to be false. However, she will publicly reveal the informant’s identity if she is ordered to do so by a judge or her editor. After all, the information concerns safety violations at the power plant. Thus, the journalist will surely reveal the informant’s identity even if the information is accurate.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion of the argument follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: The information that the informant provided is known to be false.
answerChoices.B: The journalist’s editor will not order her to reveal the informant’s identity unless the information is accurate and concerns public safety.
answerChoices.C: If the information concerns safety at the power plant, a judge will order the journalist to reveal her informant’s identity.
answerChoices.D: The truth of the information provided by the informant can be verified only if the informant’s identity is publicly revealed.
answerChoices.E: The informant understood, at the time the journalist promised him confidentiality, that she would break this promise if ordered to do so by a judge.

questions.stimulus: One who has borrowed an item from someone and promised to return it by a certain date should do so if it would not be difficult to return it on time and the person from whom one has borrowed it has not given permission to return the item late.
questions.questionStem: The principle stated above most helps to justify the reasoning in which one of the following arguments?

answerChoices.A: Christopher told Sumi that the book she borrowed from him need not be returned by Friday. Thus, it would be wrong for Sumi to return the book earlier than Friday.
answerChoices.B: Nick promised Wanda that he would return the bicycle he borrowed from her by tomorrow. Thus, if Wanda did not give Nick permission to return it late, he ought to return it by tomorrow even if doing so is difficult.
answerChoices.C: Val should return Ted’s car to him today, because although he told her that she could return it late, she promised that she would return it today and it would not be difficult for her to do so.
answerChoices.D: Yesenia borrowed Mike’s computer, and he has just requested that she return it to him by tomorrow. Although Yesenia has not promised to return it by tomorrow, she should return it by then since it would not be difficult for her to do so.
answerChoices.E: Oliver borrowed Madeline’s guitar from her yesterday and promised to bring it back today. So, since it would be easy for Oliver to return the guitar today, and Madeline has not given him permission to return it late, he should return it today.

questions.stimulus: Human skin gives off an array of gaseous substances, including carbon dioxide and lactic acid, both of which attract mosquitoes. However, neither of these two substances, whether alone or combined with one another, will attract mosquitoes as much as a bare human arm will, even in complete darkness, where a mosquito has no visual cues. Therefore, some other gaseous substance given off by human skin also attracts mosquitoes.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument requires which one of the following assumptions?

answerChoices.A: Mosquitoes do not communicate with one another.
answerChoices.B: Mosquitoes are not attracted to humans by body heat.
answerChoices.C: Human skin gives off gaseous substances in greater amounts during the day than during the night.
answerChoices.D: Mosquitoes are no more successful in finding a bare human arm in darkness than in light.
answerChoices.E: Human skin never gives off any gaseous substances that repel mosquitoes.

questions.stimulus: A 1955 analysis of paint samples from an Italian painting found evidence of cobalt, suggesting the use of cobalt blue, a pigment not used in Europe before 1804. The painting was thus deemed to have been produced sometime after 1804. A 2009 analysis also found cobalt, but that analysis suggested that the painting might have been produced before 1804.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

answerChoices.A: The 2009 analysis revealed that cobalt was located only in the topmost paint layer, which was possibly applied to conceal damage to original paint layers.
answerChoices.B: The 2009 analysis used sophisticated scientific equipment that can detect much smaller amounts of cobalt than could the equipment used for the 1955 analysis.
answerChoices.C: The 2009 analysis took more samples from the painting than the 1955 analysis did, though those samples were smaller.
answerChoices.D: Many experts, based on the style and the subject matter of the painting, have dated the painting to the 1700s.
answerChoices.E: New information that came to light in the 1990s suggested that cobalt blue was used only rarely in Italy in the years immediately following 1804.

questions.stimulus: A six-month public health campaign sought to limit the spread of influenza by encouraging people to take precautions such as washing their hands frequently and avoiding public places when they experience influenza symptoms. Since the incidence of influenza was much lower during those months than experts had predicted, the public evidently heeded the campaign.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: The incidence of food-borne illnesses, which can be effectively controlled by frequent hand washing, was markedly lower than usual during the six-month period.
answerChoices.B: During the six-month period, the incidence of the common cold, which has many of the same symptoms as influenza, was about the same as usual.
answerChoices.C: There were fewer large public gatherings than usual during the six-month period.
answerChoices.D: Independently of the public health campaign, the news media spread the message that one’s risk of contracting influenza can be lessened by frequent hand washing.
answerChoices.E: In a survey completed before the campaign began, many people admitted that they should do more to limit the spread of influenza.

questions.stimulus: A study at a company found that most meetings showed diminishing returns after 30 minutes, and little could be expected after 60 minutes. Moreover, the most productive meetings were those for which a clear time frame was established. For a meeting at the company to achieve maximum productivity, then, it needs to have a clear time frame and be no more than 30 minutes long.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the conclusion drawn in the argument?

answerChoices.A: In general, a meeting at the company that is no more than 30 minutes long and has a clear time frame will achieve maximum productivity.
answerChoices.B: Most meetings at the company show diminishing returns after 30 minutes, according to a study.
answerChoices.C: A meeting at the company will be maximally productive only if it has a clear time frame and lasts no more than 30 minutes.
answerChoices.D: According to a study, meetings at the company were the most productive when they had clear time frames.
answerChoices.E: A study of meetings at the company says that little productivity should be expected after the 60-minute mark.

questions.stimulus: Nutritionist: Most fad diets prescribe a single narrow range of nutrients for everyone. But because different foods contain nutrients that are helpful for treating or preventing different health problems, dietary needs vary widely from person to person. However, everyone should eat plenty of fruits and vegetables, which protect against a wide range of health problems.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the nutritionist’s statements?

answerChoices.A: Most fad diets require that everyone following them eat plenty of fruits and vegetables.
answerChoices.B: Fruits and vegetables are the only foods that contain enough different nutrients to protect against a wide range of health problems.
answerChoices.C: Any two people have different health problems and thus different dietary needs.
answerChoices.D: Most fad diets fail to satisfy the dietary needs of some people.
answerChoices.E: There are very few if any nutrients that are contained in every food other than fruits and vegetables.

questions.stimulus: The caffeine in coffee stimulates the production of irritating acid in the stomach. But darker roasts of coffee, produced by roasting the coffee beans longer, contain more N-methylpyridinium (NMP) than lighter roasts, and NMP tends to suppress production of acid in the stomach. Therefore if you drink caffeinated coffee, darker roasts will irritate your stomach less than lighter roasts.
questions.questionStem: The answer to which one of the following questions most helps in evaluating the argument?

answerChoices.A: Does extending the roasting time of coffee beans increase the amount of caffeine present in the brewed coffee?
answerChoices.B: Does a reduction in acid production in the stomach have an adverse effect on stomach function?
answerChoices.C: Would coffee drinkers who drink caffeinated coffee increase their coffee consumption if the coffee they drank contained less caffeine?
answerChoices.D: Do some coffee drinkers who switch from lighter to darker roasts of coffee increase their daily coffee consumption?
answerChoices.E: Do lighter roasts of coffee have any important health benefits that darker roasts of coffee lack?

questions.stimulus: Film historians often find it difficult to determine typical audience members’ responses to particular films, especially those from the early twentieth century. Box office figures help little, for they indicate only a film’s financial success or failure; they do not show what audiences found funny, or frightening, or moving. These historians also find that newspaper and magazine reviews fail to provide much insight.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the statements above?

answerChoices.A: Newspaper and magazine reviews of films are usually written in advance of a film’s general release.
answerChoices.B: Typical audience members’ responses to films from the latter part of the twentieth century are easy to determine.
answerChoices.C: The box office success of a film does not depend on its viewers finding it funny, frightening, or moving.
answerChoices.D: Film historians do not believe that film reviews in newspapers and magazines reveal typical film audience members’ views.
answerChoices.E: Films from the early part of the twentieth century were not usually reviewed in newspapers or magazines.

questions.stimulus: The consensus among astronomers, based upon observations of the surfaces of pulsars, is that pulsars are spinning balls of neutrons compressed into a sphere some 10 kilometers in diameter with a mass roughly equal to that of our sun. However, their observed properties are also consistent with some pulsars actually being filled with quarks, the building blocks of neutrons. Because the core of a quark-filled pulsar, unlike a neutron-filled one, would have an overall positive charge, it would attract a layer of negatively charged particles that could support a crust of neutrons.
questions.questionStem: The statement that the core of a quark-filled pulsar would have an overall positive charge plays which one of the following roles in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: It helps explain how pulsars could have neutrons on their surface even if they were not entirely made up of neutrons.
answerChoices.B: It forms part of a challenge to the claim that some pulsars may be made up of quarks.
answerChoices.C: It helps explain why some pulsars would not be readily recognized as such by astronomers.
answerChoices.D: It presents a new finding that challenges the consensus view of the structure of pulsars.
answerChoices.E: It points out a problem with the view that pulsars have a mass roughly equal to that of our sun.

questions.stimulus: Analyst: Any new natural-gas-powered electrical generation station needs to be located close to a natural-gas pipeline, a large body of water for cooling, and transmission lines. It also must be situated in a region where residents will not oppose construction. Our country has an extensive system of transmission lines, but our natural-gas pipelines run in the vicinity of only three of our large bodies of water, and residents would oppose any significant construction projects near these bodies of water.
questions.questionStem: The analyst’s statements, if true, most strongly support which one of the following statements about the analyst’s country?

answerChoices.A: Future electrical needs will have to be met by alternatives to natural-gas-powered generation.
answerChoices.B: If a new natural-gas-powered electrical station is built in a region, many residents will move away from that region.
answerChoices.C: No site would be suitable for constructing a natural-gas-powered electrical station unless the existing system of natural-gas pipelines is expanded.
answerChoices.D: There currently is no natural-gas-powered electrical generation station near any of the three largest bodies of water.
answerChoices.E: Many residents who would oppose the construction of a new natural-gas-powered electrical station in their region would not oppose the construction of new transmission lines there.

questions.stimulus: Voting records regularly show that people over 65 vote in the highest percentages while young adults are least likely to vote. This indicates that citizens are becoming increasingly disconnected from the political system with each passing generation.
questions.questionStem: The argument’s reasoning is questionable in that the argument

answerChoices.A: compares an early stage of one generation to a later stage of another
answerChoices.B: fails to take into account the relative sizes of the generations compared
answerChoices.C: provides evidence for a phenomenon without providing an explanation of the phenomenon
answerChoices.D: confuses the cause of an effect with the effect itself
answerChoices.E: overlooks the possibility that voting patterns among age groups will change in the future

questions.stimulus: A local marsh would need to be drained before the proposed office complex could be built. Such marshes often play crucial roles in purifying groundwater and there has been no scientific assessment of the marsh’s role in maintaining the quality of the city’s well water. The city should therefore block the proposed office complex pending such an assessment.
questions.questionStem: The principle underlying the argument above is most similar to the principle underlying which one of the following arguments?

answerChoices.A: A new highway cannot be built in the lake district unless an environmental impact assessment is first carried out. An environmental impact assessment would cost more than the projected economic benefit of the highway. The proposal for a new highway in the lake district should therefore be rejected.
answerChoices.B: Defective products can cost an appliance manufacturer millions of dollars because of product recalls and lawsuits. Yova Corporation’s new line of appliances has not yet been thoroughly tested for defects. Thus, Yova should not bring its new line to market at this time.
answerChoices.C: A laboratory safety check of a portable grill requires a week of uninterrupted testing. The new portable grill has been at the testing lab for a week, but the testing could not begin until the paperwork arrived three days later. Therefore, no report on the results of the safety check should be released at this time.
answerChoices.D: Building the new highway along the proposed northern route would inevitably damage an adjoining wilderness area. The highway would also cause environmental damage if it follows the proposed southern route, but it would not harm any wilderness areas. Thus, if the highway is built, it should be built on the southern route.
answerChoices.E: Building a light rail line to serve the downtown core could involve cost overruns and expensive delays, but traffic congestion will become intolerable within ten years without a light rail line. A light rail line should therefore be built.

questions.stimulus: In a recent study, one group of participants watched video recordings of themselves running on treadmills, and a second group watched recordings of other people running on treadmills. When contacted later, participants in the first group reported exercising, on average, 1 hour longer each day than did the other participants. This shows that watching a recording of yourself exercising can motivate you to exercise more.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: In another study, people who watched recordings of themselves lifting weights exercised for more time each day than did people who watched recordings of themselves running.
answerChoices.B: Another study’s members exhibited an increased willingness to give to charity after hearing stories in which people with whom they identified did so.
answerChoices.C: Participants who were already highly motivated to exercise did not report exercising for any longer each day than they had before the study.
answerChoices.D: In studies of identical twins, participants who observed their twin reading overreported by a significant amount how much time they themselves spent reading in the days that followed.
answerChoices.E: A third group of participants who watched recordings of themselves sitting on couches afterwards reported being sedentary for more time each day than did the other participants.

questions.stimulus: Environmentalist: Efforts to attain an overall reduction in carbon use by convincing people to focus on their personal use of fossil fuels cannot achieve that goal. Even if most people changed their behavior, changes in personal use of fossil fuels cannot produce the needed reductions in carbon use. Only government policies can produce change on the required scale.
questions.questionStem: The environmentalist’s argument requires assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Convincing most people to focus on their personal use of fossil fuels would not lead to their successfully pressuring the government into implementing policies that reduce carbon use.
answerChoices.B: The calculations needed to determine how best to minimize one’s personal use of fossil fuels are too difficult for individuals to carry out on their own.
answerChoices.C: Efforts to convince people to focus on reducing their personal use of fossil fuels have been made only by those who are not currently involved in framing government policy.
answerChoices.D: It is easier to convince the government to change its policies on carbon use than to convince people to reduce their personal use of fossil fuels.
answerChoices.E: People who are concerned about environmental issues are more likely to support political candidates who support environmental issues.

questions.stimulus: There are only two plausible views about where the aesthetic value of a painting lies: either in its purely formal qualities or in what the painting means. But there exists no compelling general account of how a painting could derive its value from its purely formal characteristics. Therefore, the aesthetic value of a painting lies in what it means.
questions.questionStem: The pattern of questionable reasoning in the argument above is most similar to that in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: This cardiac patient could be treated with surgery or angioplasty, among other methods. But his weak condition would make recovery from surgery a very long process. Therefore, the doctors ought to perform angioplasty.
answerChoices.B: Should the company be outbid on the new project, it will either have to lay off workers or find new business. But it does not expect to find new business in the foreseeable future. Therefore, it must be expecting to win the bid on the new project.
answerChoices.C: History is driven primarily by economic forces or primarily by political forces. But no historian has shown convincingly that history is driven mainly by economic forces. Therefore, it is driven primarily by political forces.
answerChoices.D: Some analysts are forecasting that if the economy expands, the inflation rate will rise or the unemployment rate will fall. But the unemployment rate promises to remain stable. Therefore, the inflation rate will not change either.
answerChoices.E: If the party does not change its policies, it will lose heavily in the next election. But if it changes its policies, some people who support those policies will be upset and will sit out the next election. Therefore, it is impossible for the party to win in the next election.

questions.stimulus: Substantial economic growth must be preceded by technological innovations that expanding industries incorporate into their production or distribution procedures. Since a worldwide ban on the use of fossil fuels would surely produce many technological innovations, it is obvious that such a ban would be followed by an economic boom rather than by the economic depression forecast by the critics of such a ban.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a flaw in the argument’s reasoning?

answerChoices.A: The argument assumes the truth of the conclusion for which it purports to be providing evidence.
answerChoices.B: The argument attempts to establish the falsehood of a proposition by criticizing the reasoning of those who assert its truth.
answerChoices.C: The argument attempts to establish a conclusion on the basis of stronger evidence than the conclusion requires.
answerChoices.D: The argument confuses a necessary condition for a phenomenon with a sufficient condition for that phenomenon.
answerChoices.E: The argument presumes, without providing warrant, that because certain conditions only sometimes precede a certain phenomenon, these conditions always bring about the phenomenon.

questions.stimulus:
Winston: The rules for awarding Nobel Prizes stipulate that no more than three people can share the same prize. Nobel Prizes in scientific disciplines are generally given in recognition of particular scientific results, however, and many important results are the work of four or more scientists.
Sanjay: Those rules also stipulate that prize winners must be living, but some highly influential scientists died before their work was fully appreciated.
questions.questionStem: The dialogue most strongly supports the claim that Winston and Sanjay agree that

answerChoices.A: the rules that govern the awarding of Nobel Prizes should be changed so that prizes can be awarded to deceased persons
answerChoices.B: the rules that govern the awarding of Nobel Prizes in scientific disciplines should be different from the rules for other Nobel Prizes
answerChoices.C: Nobel Prizes in scientific disciplines should not be given in recognition of particular scientific results
answerChoices.D: the evaluation of individual achievement in science is a highly subjective matter
answerChoices.E: Nobel Prizes are inaccurate indicators of scientists’ contributions to their disciplines

questions.stimulus: A nonprofit organization concerned with a social issue sent out a fund-raising letter to 5,000 people. The letter was accompanied by a survey soliciting recipients’ opinions. Of the 300 respondents, 283 indicated in the survey that they agreed with the organization’s position on the social issue. This suggests that most of the 5,000 people to whom the letter was sent agreed with that position.
questions.questionStem: The argument is most vulnerable to criticism on which one of the following grounds?

answerChoices.A: It draws a conclusion about a population from observations of a subgroup that is quite likely to be unrepresentative of that population in certain relevant respects.
answerChoices.B: It takes for granted that most individuals do not vary significantly in the opinions they would express on a given issue if surveyed regarding that issue on different occasions.
answerChoices.C: It relies on the accuracy of a survey made under conditions in which it is probable that most of the responses to that survey did not correctly reflect the opinions of the respondents.
answerChoices.D: It uses evidence about an opinion held by the majority of a population in an attempt to justify a conclusion regarding the opinion of a small part of that population.
answerChoices.E: It takes for granted that the fund-raising letter had some influence on the opinions of most of the people who received it.

questions.stimulus: An unstable climate was probably a major cause of the fall of the Roman empire. Tree-ring analysis shows that Europe’s climate underwent extreme fluctuations between 250 A.D. and 550 A.D., a period that encompasses Rome’s decline and fall. This highly variable climate surely hurt food production, which made the empire harder to rule and defend.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Political failures within the Roman empire during its last years led to conflicts that hampered agricultural production.
answerChoices.B: The areas of the Roman empire that had the greatest climatic instability between 250 A.D. and 550 A.D. did not experience unusual levels of unrest during that period.
answerChoices.C: Poor farming practices led to depleted soil in many parts of Europe during the last years of the Roman empire.
answerChoices.D: During periods when the Roman empire was thriving, Europe consistently experienced weather that was favorable for agriculture.
answerChoices.E: Total food production in Europe was likely greater in the years around 550 A.D. than in the years around 250 A.D.

questions.stimulus: Sales manager: Having spent my entire career in sales, most of that time as a sales manager for a large computer company, I know that natural superstar salespeople are rare. But many salespeople can perform like superstars if they have a good manager. Therefore, companies should _______.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most logically completes the sales manager’s argument?

answerChoices.A: devote more effort to training than to evaluating salespeople
answerChoices.B: devote more effort to finding good managers than to finding natural superstar salespeople
answerChoices.C: keep to a minimum the number of salespeople for which a manager is responsible
answerChoices.D: promote more natural superstar salespeople to management positions
answerChoices.E: reward superstar performance more than superstar talent

questions.stimulus: According to economists, people’s tendency to purchase a given commodity is inversely proportional to its price. When new techniques produced cheaper steel, more steel was purchased. Nevertheless, once machine-produced lace became available, at much lower prices than the handcrafted variety, lace no longer served to advertise its wearers’ wealth and the lace market collapsed. Obviously, then, there are exceptions to the economists’ general rule.
questions.questionStem: The claim that more steel was purchased when it could be manufactured more cheaply plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It is described as inadequate evidence for the falsity of the argument’s conclusion.
answerChoices.B: It is described as an exception to a generalization for which the argument offers evidence.
answerChoices.C: It is used to illustrate the generalization that, according to the argument, does not hold in all cases.
answerChoices.D: It is the evidence that, according to the argument, led economists to embrace a false hypothesis.
answerChoices.E: It is cited as one of several reasons for modifying a general assumption made by economists.

questions.stimulus: Resident: Data indicates that 30 percent of the houses in our town have inadequate site drainage and 30 percent have structural defects that could make them unsafe. Hence, at least 60 percent of our town’s houses have some kind of problem that threatens their integrity.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the resident’s argument is flawed in that the argument overlooks the possibility that

answerChoices.A: the town has a relatively small number of houses
answerChoices.B: inadequate site drainage can make a house unsafe
answerChoices.C: structural defects are often easier to fix than inadequate site drainage
answerChoices.D: many houses in the town have neither inadequate site drainage nor structural defects that could make them unsafe
answerChoices.E: some of the houses that have structural defects that could make them unsafe also have inadequate site drainage

questions.stimulus: The decisions that one makes can profoundly affect one’s life years later. So one should not regret the missed opportunities of youth, for had one decided instead to seize one’s of these opportunities, one would not have some of the close personal relationships one currently has. And everyone deeply cherishes their close personal relationships.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning in the argument?

answerChoices.A: One should not regret making a decision unless a different decision would have resulted in one having a greater number of close personal relationships.
answerChoices.B: One should not regret making a decision if it helped to bring about something that one cherishes.
answerChoices.C: One should not regret making a decision that had little effect on one’s life.
answerChoices.D: People who regret the missed opportunities of youth should cherish their close personal relationships more deeply.
answerChoices.E: People with few close personal relationships should cherish the ones they have.

questions.stimulus: The Kuna, a people native to several Panamanian islands, generally have a low incidence of high blood pressure. But Kuna who have moved to the Panamanian mainland do not have a low incidence of high blood pressure. Kuna who live on the islands, unlike those who live on the mainland, typically drink several cups of cocoa a day. This cocoa is minimally processed and thus high in flavonoids.
questions.questionStem: Of the following, which one is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Foods high in flavonoids are not readily available on the Panamanian mainland.
answerChoices.B: Kuna who live on the islands drink cocoa because they believe that it is beneficial to their health.
answerChoices.C: The Kuna have a genetic predisposition to low blood pressure.
answerChoices.D: Kuna who live on the Panamanian mainland generally have higher blood pressure than other people who live on the mainland.
answerChoices.E: Drinking several cups of flavonoid-rich cocoa per day tends to prevent high blood pressure.

questions.stimulus: Numerous studies suggest that when scientific evidence is presented in a trial, jurors regard that evidence as more credible than they would if they had encountered the same evidence outside of the courtroom context. Legal theorists have hypothesized that this effect is primarily due to the fact that judges prescreen scientific evidence and allow only credible scientific evidence to be presented in the courtroom.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following would be most useful to know in order to evaluate the legal theorists’ hypothesis?

answerChoices.A: whether jurors typically know that judges have appraised the scientific evidence presented at trial
answerChoices.B: whether jurors’ reactions to scientific evidence presented at trial are influenced by other members of the jury
answerChoices.C: how jurors determine the credibility of an expert witness who is presenting scientific evidence in a trial
answerChoices.D: whether jurors typically draw upon their own scientific knowledge when weighing scientific evidence presented at trial
answerChoices.E: how jurors respond to situations in which different expert witnesses give conflicting assessments of scientific evidence

questions.stimulus: Organized word-of-mouth marketing campaigns are driven by product boosters who extol a product to friends and acquaintances. A study found that these campaigns are more successful when the product booster openly admits to being part of an organized marketing campaign. This is surprising because one of the purported advantages of word-of-mouth campaigns is that consumers take a less skeptical stance toward word-of-mouth messages than toward mass-media advertisements.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the surprising finding?

answerChoices.A: Word-of-mouth marketing campaigns are generally used for specialty products that are not well suited to being marketed through mass-media advertisements.
answerChoices.B: Those who tend to be the most receptive to mass-media marketing campaigns are also the least likely to be influenced by knowledge of a product booster’s affiliation.
answerChoices.C: Most people who work as product boosters in word-of-mouth marketing campaigns have themselves been recruited through a word-of-mouth process.
answerChoices.D: Most word-of-mouth marketing campaigns cost far less than marketing campaigns that rely on mass-media advertisements.
answerChoices.E: When a word-of-mouth product booster admits his or her affiliation, it fosters a more relaxed and in-depth discussion of the marketed product.

questions.stimulus: Consultant: If Whalley sticks with her current platform in the upcoming election, then she will lose to her opponent by a few percentage points among voters under 50, while beating him by a bigger percentage among voters 50 and over. Therefore, sticking with her current platform will allow her to win the election.
questions.questionStem: The consultant’s conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: There is no change Whalley could make to her platform that would win over more voters under 50 than it would lose voters 50 and over.
answerChoices.B: The issues that most concern voters under 50 are different from those that most concern voters 50 and over.
answerChoices.C: If Whalley changes her platform, her opponent will not change his platform in response.
answerChoices.D: There will be more voters in the election who are 50 and over than there will be voters under 50.
answerChoices.E: Whalley would change her platform if she thought it would give her a better chance to win.

questions.stimulus: From 1880 to 2000 Britain’s economy grew fivefold, but emissions of carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas, were the same on a per capita basis in Britain in 2000 as they were in 1880.
questions.questionStem: The claims made above are incompatible with which one of the following generalizations?

answerChoices.A: A decrease in per capita emissions of carbon dioxide never occurs during a period of economic growth.
answerChoices.B: Countries whose economies are growing slowly or not at all usually cannot afford to enact laws restricting carbon dioxide emissions.
answerChoices.C: Economic growth initially leads to increased per capita emissions of greenhouse gases, but eventually new technologies are developed that tend to reduce these emissions.
answerChoices.D: As the world’s population grows, emissions of greenhouse gases will increase proportionately.
answerChoices.E: Economic growth always increases household income and consumption, which inevitably increases per capita emissions of carbon dioxide.

questions.stimulus: Advertisement: When you need a will, consulting a lawyer is much more expensive than using do-it-yourself software. And you get a valid will either way. However, when you’re ill, you aren’t satisfied with simply getting some valid prescription or other; what you pay your doctor for is the doctor’s expert advice concerning your particular illness. Similarly, what you pay a lawyer for is to tailor your will to your particular circumstances. Clearly, when you need a will, a lawyer’s expert advice is always worth paying for.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument presented in the advertisement?

answerChoices.A: A lawyer’s knowledge and level of expertise is at least as complex as that of a doctor.
answerChoices.B: Do-it-yourself software cannot tailor a person’s will to meet that person’s particular circumstances as well as a lawyer can.
answerChoices.C: Many people who prepare their wills using do-it-yourself software are not satisfied with the results.
answerChoices.D: In the majority of cases, valid wills do not adequately meet the needs of the persons for whom the wills were prepared.
answerChoices.E: There is some way for an ill person to get a valid prescription without first consulting a doctor.

questions.stimulus: Pollution is a problem wherever there are people who are indifferent to their environment, and nature’s balance is harmed wherever there is pollution. So wherever there are people who are indifferent to their environment, nature’s balance is harmed.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in which one of the following arguments is most similar to that in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Any dessert with chocolate is high in calories, and any dessert high in calories is fattening. So any dessert with chocolate is fattening.
answerChoices.B: Every dessert with chocolate is high in calories, and every fattening dessert is also high in calories. So any dessert with chocolate is fattening.
answerChoices.C: Any dessert that is high in calories has chocolate in it, and any dessert that is is high in calories is fattening. So every dessert with chocolate is fattening.
answerChoices.D: Every dessert with chocolate is high in calories, and every dessert that is high in calories is fattening. So every fattening dessert has chocolate in it.
answerChoices.E: Any dessert with chocolate is high in calories, and many desserts that are high in calories are fattening. So many desserts with chocolate are fattening.

questions.stimulus: Seventeenth-century proponents of the philosophical school of thought known as mechanism produced numerous arguments that sought to use the principles of mechanism to establish the superiority of monarchies over all other systems of government. This proliferation of arguments has been construed as evidence that the principles of mechanism themselves are in tension with democracy. But it is more likely that the principles of mechanism support democracy and that the arguments multiplied because none of them worked.
questions.questionStem: The claim that the proliferation of arguments has been construed as evidence that the principles of mechanism themselves are in tension with democracy plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It states a principle that the argument seeks to establish.
answerChoices.B: It describes a general phenomenon that the argument seeks to explain.
answerChoices.C: It introduces a hypothesis that the argument challenges.
answerChoices.D: It provides evidence in support of the conclusion of the argument.
answerChoices.E: It expresses the conclusion of the argument.

questions.stimulus: A good manager must understand people and be able to defuse tense situations. But anyone who is able to defuse tense situations must understand people. Since Ishiko is able to defuse tense situations, she must be a good manager.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed in that it

answerChoices.A: confuses a quality that shows an understanding of people with a quality that is necessary for understanding people
answerChoices.B: confuses a quality that usually correlates with being a good manager with a quality that results from being a good manager
answerChoices.C: confuses qualities necessary for being a good manager with qualities that guarantee being a good manager
answerChoices.D: overlooks the possibility that different managers defuse tense situations in different ways
answerChoices.E: takes for granted that because all good managers have a certain quality, Ishiko must have that quality

questions.stimulus: Babblers, a bird species, live in large cooperative groups. Each member attempts to defend the group by sounding a loud barklike call when it spots a predator, inciting the others to bark too. Babblers, however, are extremely well camouflaged and could usually feed safely, unnoticed by predators. These predators, indeed, generally become aware of the presence of babblers only because of their shrill barks, which continue long after most members of the group have been able to take cover and which signal the group’s approximate location to the predators.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most help to explain the babblers’ strange behavior?

answerChoices.A: Babblers fly much faster than the predators that prey upon them.
answerChoices.B: Babblers’ predators are generally intimidated by large numbers of babblers.
answerChoices.C: There is more than one type of predator that preys upon babblers.
answerChoices.D: Babblers’ predators have very good eyesight but relatively weak hearing.
answerChoices.E: Animals that live in close proximity to babblers are also preyed upon by the predators that prey upon babblers.

questions.stimulus: Photographs show an area of Europa, a moon of Jupiter, where the icy surface appears to have buckled as a result of turbulent water moving underneath. This photographic evidence indicates that there is a warm sea beneath Europa’s icy surface. The presence of such a sea is thought by scientists to be a primary factor in the early development of life, so there is reason to believe that there may be life on Europa.
questions.questionStem: The claim that there is a warm sea beneath Europa’s icy surface figures in the argument in which one of the following ways?

answerChoices.A: It is a subsidiary conclusion used by the argument to support its overall conclusion.
answerChoices.B: It is the overall conclusion of the argument.
answerChoices.C: It is used to discredit a theory that the argument disputes.
answerChoices.D: It is the only consideration presented in support of the argument’s overall conclusion.
answerChoices.E: It is presented as support for a subsidiary conclusion drawn in the argument.

questions.stimulus: For consumers, the most enjoyable emotional experience garnered from shopping is feeling lucky. Retailers use this fact to their advantage, but too often they resort to using advertised price cuts to promote their wares. Promotions of this sort might make bargain-minded consumers feel lucky, but they cut into profit margins and undermine customer loyalty.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the overall conclusion drawn in the argument?

answerChoices.A: Feeling lucky is the most enjoyable emotional experience garnered from shopping.
answerChoices.B: Retailers take advantage of the fact that shoppers enjoy feeling lucky.
answerChoices.C: Advertised price cuts are overused as a means of gaining retail sales.
answerChoices.D: Using advertised price cuts to promote retail products reduces profit margins and undermines customer loyalty.
answerChoices.E: Making consumers feel lucky is usually not a good formula for retail success.

questions.stimulus: Jurist: To ensure that a legal system remains just, it is important to guarantee that lawbreaking does not give lawbreakers an unfair advantage over law abiders. Thus, notwithstanding any other goals that criminal punishment may serve, it should certainly attempt to ensure that criminal wrongdoing remains profitless.
questions.questionStem: The jurist’s claim that it is important to guarantee that lawbreaking does not give lawbreakers an unfair advantage over law abiders functions in the argument in which one of the following ways?

answerChoices.A: It states a condition that, if fulfilled, will ensure that a legal system remains just.
answerChoices.B: It expresses a principle that is offered as support for the conclusion.
answerChoices.C: It is a conclusion for which the only support offered is the claim that the legal system serves multiple goals.
answerChoices.D: It is a premise presented as support for the claim that the most important goal of criminal punishment is to ensure that criminal wrongdoing remains profitless.
answerChoices.E: It is presented as refuting an argument that criminal punishment has goals other than guaranteeing that lawbreaking remains profitless.

questions.stimulus: The company president says that significant procedural changes were made before either she or Yeung was told about them. But, according to Grimes, the contract requires that either the company president or any lawyer in the company’s legal department be told about proposed procedural changes before they are made. Thus, unless what Grimes or the company president said is incorrect, the contract was violated.
questions.questionStem: The argument’s conclusion can be properly inferred if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Yeung is a lawyer in the company’s legal department.
answerChoices.B: Neither Grimes nor Yeung was told about the procedural changes until after they were made.
answerChoices.C: No lawyer in the company’s legal department was told about the procedural changes until after they were made.
answerChoices.D: If the company’s president was told about the procedural changes before they were made, then the contract was not violated.
answerChoices.E: If no lawyer in the company’s legal department was told about the procedural changes before they were made, then the contract was violated.

questions.stimulus: Journalist: People whose diets contain a relatively large amount of iron are significantly more likely to develop Parkinson’s disease than are those whose diets contain less of this mineral. Limiting one’s intake of meats, seafood, and other foods rich in iron should thus reduce one’s chances of contracting this disease.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the journalist’s reasoning?

answerChoices.A: Most people who have a genetic predisposition to Parkinson’s disease have no more iron in their diets than people without the predisposition.
answerChoices.B: Many of the vegetables regularly consumed by vegetarians who do not contract Parkinson’s disease are as rich in iron as meat and seafood.
answerChoices.C: Children and adolescents require a much larger amount of iron in their diets than do mature adults.
answerChoices.D: The iron in some foods is much less easily absorbed by the body than the iron contained in other foods.
answerChoices.E: The amounts of iron-rich foods consumed by people starts to decline beginning at age 50.

questions.stimulus: Riverdale’s Modern Party Chairperson: Maples, the Modern Party candidate, would be a better mayor than his opponent, Tannett, who is a member of the Traditionalist Party. Every member of the Modern Party is better qualified to be mayor than is any member of the Traditionalist Party.
questions.questionStem: If the statements of Riverdale’s Modern Party Chairperson are true, each of the following could be true except:

answerChoices.A: Maples has the least seniority of any member of Riverdale’s Modern Party and was recently ousted from the Traditionalist Party.
answerChoices.B: Tannett would be a better mayor than would any other member of Riverdale’s Traditionalist Party.
answerChoices.C: Few residents of Riverdale believe that Maples would be a better mayor than Tannett.
answerChoices.D: Of all the members of Riverdale’s Modern Party, Maples would be the worst mayor.
answerChoices.E: Tannett is better qualified to be mayor than is Riverdale’s Modern Party Chairperson.

questions.stimulus: Businessperson: Because the parking area directly in front of the building was closed for maintenance today, I was late to my meeting. If the maintenance had been done on a different day, I would have gotten to the meeting on time. After finding out that I could not park in that area it took me 15 minutes to find an available parking space, making me a few minutes late.
questions.questionStem: The answer to which one of the following questions would be most useful to know in order to evaluate the reasoning in the businessperson’s argument?

answerChoices.A: What were the reasons for performing maintenance on the parking area directly in front of the building on that particular day?
answerChoices.B: Were any other of the meeting attendees also late to the meeting because they had difficulty finding parking?
answerChoices.C: What are the parking patterns in the building’s vicinity on days when the parking area in front of the building is open?
answerChoices.D: Does the businessperson have a tendency to be late to meetings?
answerChoices.E: Was it particularly important that the businessperson not be late to this meeting?

questions.stimulus: For a work to be rightly thought of as world literature, it must be received and interpreted within the writer’s own national tradition and within external national traditions. A work counts as being interpreted within a national tradition if authors from that tradition use the work in at least one of three ways: as a positive model for the development of their own tradition, as a negative case of a decadent tendency that must be consciously avoided, or as an image of radical otherness that prompts refinement of the home tradition.
questions.questionStem: The statements above, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: A work of literature cannot be well received within an external national tradition if it is not well received within the writer’s own national tradition.
answerChoices.B: A work of world literature offers more to readers within external national traditions than it offers to readers within the writer’s national tradition.
answerChoices.C: A work should not be thought of as world literature if it is more meaningful to readers from the writer’s national tradition than it is to readers from external national traditions.
answerChoices.D: A work of world literature is always influenced by works outside of the writer’s national tradition.
answerChoices.E: A work is not part of world literature if it affects the development of only one national tradition.

questions.stimulus: At Morris University this semester, most of the sociology majors are taking Introduction to Social Psychology, but most of the psychology majors are not. Hence, there must be more sociology majors than psychology majors enrolled in the class.
questions.questionStem: The flawed pattern of reasoning in the argument above is most similar to that in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Most of the paintings on display at the Metro Art Museum are from the twentieth century, but most of the paintings the Metro Art Museum owns are from the nineteenth century. It follows that the museum owns few if any of the twentieth-century paintings it displays.
answerChoices.B: In an opinion poll of Silver Falls residents, more said they were in favor of increased spending on roads than said they were in favor of increased spending on parks. So most Silver Falls residents must be in favor of spending more on roads but opposed to spending more on parks.
answerChoices.C: In the San Felipe city arboretum, most of the trees are of local rather than exotic species. Therefore, in the San Felipe area, there must be more trees of local species than of exotic species.
answerChoices.D: Most of the vegetables available at the Valley Food Co-op are organic, but most of the vegetables available at the Jumbo Supermarket are not. Thus, more organic vegetables are available at Valley Food than are available at Jumbo.
answerChoices.E: The Acme Realty website has photos of most of the houses, but of fewer than half of the condominiums, that Acme is offering for sale. So Acme must have more houses than condominiums for sale.

questions.stimulus: Film director: Although the production costs of my latest film are very high, there is little risk that the film studio will not recover these costs. Even if the film is unpopular, much of the money is being spent to develop innovative special-effects technology that could be used in future films.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Because the film studio owns the new technology, the studio will be able to control its use in any future films.
answerChoices.B: Films that introduce innovative special-effects technologies generally draw large audiences of people who are curious about the new effects.
answerChoices.C: The production costs of this film are so high that, even if the film is popular, it is unlikely that the film’s ticket sales will offset those costs.
answerChoices.D: In the past, many innovative special-effects technologies were abandoned after the films for which they were developed proved to be unpopular.
answerChoices.E: The use of the new special-effects technology would lower the production costs of other films that use it.

questions.stimulus: After a major toll highway introduced a system of electronic toll paying, delays at all of its interchanges declined significantly. Travel time per car trip decreased by an average of 10 percent. Tailpipe pollution for each trip decreased commensurately. Despite this, the total air pollution from vehicles on that highway did not decrease measurably.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

answerChoices.A: The highway began charging higher tolls when it switched to electronic toll paying.
answerChoices.B: Even after the switch to electronic toll paying, there were sometimes long delays at the highway’s interchanges.
answerChoices.C: The prospect of faster, more convenient travel induced more drivers to use the highway.
answerChoices.D: Travel time on the highway for car trips under 30 kilometers (18.6 miles) did not decrease appreciably.
answerChoices.E: Some drivers did not switch to the electronic system but instead continued to use cash to pay their tolls at toll booths.

questions.stimulus: A lack of trust in one’s neighbors leads to their lack of respect for the law. A new study provides compelling evidence for this. Neighborhoods in which people routinely lock their doors have higher burglary rates than neighborhoods in which people do not routinely lock their doors.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed in that the argument

answerChoices.A: treats something that is merely sufficient to produce a result as if it were necessary to produce that result
answerChoices.B: draws a moral conclusion from evidence that could only support a factual conclusion
answerChoices.C: bases its conclusion on data that are contradictory
answerChoices.D: asserts in a premise what it is trying to establish in its conclusion
answerChoices.E: treats what could be the effect of something as if it were the cause of that thing

questions.stimulus: In recent decades, government efforts to fight counterfeiting have been extremely successful, especially efforts to remove counterfeit bills from circulation. Yet counterfeiters are not finding it at all difficult to get away with passing counterfeit bills to merchants and even banks.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

answerChoices.A: Government information campaigns that teach merchants and bank tellers how to detect counterfeit bills are more effective than ever.
answerChoices.B: Governments are continually developing new currency designs with features that are difficult for criminals to counterfeit.
answerChoices.C: Counterfeiters are generally unaware that the percentage of fake bills in circulation is the lowest it has ever been.
answerChoices.D: Government success in removing counterfeit bills from circulation has caused merchants and bank tellers to become lax in checking for counterfeit bills.
answerChoices.E: Governments are spending larger and larger sums of money in their efforts to remove counterfeit bills from circulation.

questions.stimulus: If a civilization as technologically advanced as human civilization existed on another planet and that planet were within 50 light years of Earth, that civilization would have found evidence of intelligent life on Earth and could have easily contacted us. Scientists can thus rule out the possibility of finding a civilization as technologically advanced as our own within 50 light years of Earth.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: Scientists who are searching for evidence of extraterrestrial life forms generally focus their search on evidence of technologically advanced life forms.
answerChoices.B: There is no reason to doubt the possibility that there are technologically advanced civilizations on planets more than 50 light years from Earth.
answerChoices.C: If scientists received a message from a technologically advanced civilization on another planet, they would be able to decipher it fully.
answerChoices.D: A technologically advanced civilization on another planet would want to communicate with intelligent life that it detected on Earth.
answerChoices.E: Intelligent life forms on other planets would be able to recognize all signs of intelligent life on Earth.

questions.stimulus: Recently, many traffic lights and street markings were temporarily removed from a heavily traveled street in a major metropolitan area. Given that this street experiences significant volumes of automobile traffic, the number of accidents on the street was expected to increase. However, even though the street experienced no reduction in traffic, the number of accidents was greatly reduced.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent conflict described above?

answerChoices.A: People often disregard traffic lights and street markings.
answerChoices.B: The lack of traffic lights and street markings caused drivers to drive more cautiously.
answerChoices.C: Most drivers were not aware that traffic lights and street markings had been removed.
answerChoices.D: Traffic lights and street markings are intended to have benefits in addition to those related to safety.
answerChoices.E: Drivers were given advance notice that the traffic lights and street markings would be removed.

questions.stimulus: Some have argued that body size influences mating decisions throughout all societies. Their argument rests largely on self-reports of university-age students and on analyses of personal advertisements in newspapers for dating partners.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument described above is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: concludes that one kind of event causes another kind of event without ruling out the possibility that both kinds of events are the result of a third kind of event
answerChoices.B: bases a conclusion on a sample that may be unrepresentative of the population about which the conclusion is drawn
answerChoices.C: concludes that an effect has only one cause in the face of evidence that the effect has multiple causes
answerChoices.D: uses a claim that applies only to entire societies to draw a conclusion about individual persons
answerChoices.E: draws a universal conclusion on the basis of a very small number of individual cases

questions.stimulus: Journalist: The new mayor is undeniably bold. His assertions are made with utter certainty and confidence. While these kinds of assertions may make him popular with the public, they also demonstrate that he is not an introspective person.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the journalist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Introspective people do not make assertions with utter certainty and confidence.
answerChoices.B: Politicians who make assertions with utter certainty and confidence are popular with the public.
answerChoices.C: People who are bold make public assertions with utter certainty and confidence.
answerChoices.D: People whose assertions are uncertain and lack confidence are introspective.
answerChoices.E: Politicians who are not bold are unpopular with the public.

questions.stimulus: While studying a large colony of macaque monkeys, scientists interacting with baby monkeys under a week old found that the babies would imitate some, but not all, of the scientists’ actions. The babies readily smacked their lips and stuck out their tongues when the scientists did, but stared impassively when the scientists opened and closed their mouths or made hand gestures. Of these four kinds of actions, only lip smacking and sticking out the tongue are used by adult macaques when interacting with babies.
questions.questionStem: The statements above, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Baby macaques under a week old are natural mimics of whatever they see.
answerChoices.B: Baby macaques under a week old cannot imitate hand gestures because they do not yet control the necessary muscles.
answerChoices.C: Adult macaques use lip smacking and sticking out the tongue to entertain infant macaques.
answerChoices.D: Baby macaques under a week old mistake the scientists interacting with them for adult macaques.
answerChoices.E: Baby macaques under a week old only imitate human gestures also used by adult macaques.

questions.stimulus: Some scientists believe that small humanoid skeletons found on an Indonesian island are the remains of human beings with a growth disorder. It is more likely that they represent a distinct human species that became smaller over time due to environmental pressure. These skeletons do not fit the pattern of known growth disorders. And evidence suggests that certain fox and mouse species on the island have evolved into smaller versions of their common counterparts.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the conclusion drawn in the argument?

answerChoices.A: Some scientists believe that the humanoid skeletons are the remains of human beings with a growth disorder.
answerChoices.B: It is more likely that the humanoid skeletons represent a distinct human species than that they are the remains of human beings with a growth disorder.
answerChoices.C: The humanoid skeletons do not fit the pattern of known growth disorders.
answerChoices.D: Certain fox and mouse species on an Indonesian island have evolved into smaller versions of their common counterparts.
answerChoices.E: Environmental pressure can cause species living on islands to become smaller over time.

questions.stimulus: The more sunlight our planet reflects back into space, the cooler the global atmosphere tends to become. Snow and ice reflect much more sunlight back into space than do ocean water or land without snow cover. Therefore, the greater the area of Earth’s surface that is covered with snow and ice, the cooler, on average, the global atmosphere is likely to become.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most strengthen the argument?

answerChoices.A: Low atmospheric temperatures are required for the formation of clouds that result in snow.
answerChoices.B: Other factors besides the reflectivity of ice and snow affect the cooling of Earth’s atmosphere.
answerChoices.C: Ocean water and land heated by sunlight in turn warm Earth’s atmosphere.
answerChoices.D: The atmosphere derives most of its heat from the passage of sunlight through it.
answerChoices.E: Lighter-colored soil reflects more sunlight back into space than does darker-colored soil.

questions.stimulus:
Nick: The Pincus family and their construction company have supported our university financially for decades. The university should not give the contract for building its new library to the family’s main competitor. Doing so would be disloyal to a friend of the university.
Pedro: Accepting a donation does not oblige the university to give the donor any special privileges. If it did, then it wouldn’t really be a charitable contribution. We should award the contract to whatever company makes the most competitive bid.
questions.questionStem: The dialogue provides the most support for the claim that Nick and Pedro disagree over whether

answerChoices.A: loyalty should sometimes be a consideration in making business decisions
answerChoices.B: the Pincus family and their construction company donated money for the purpose of acquiring special privileges from the university
answerChoices.C: the acceptance of donations places a university under a special obligation to the donor
answerChoices.D: the university should be more grateful to donors with a long history of financial support than to new donors
answerChoices.E: the Pincus family’s construction company did not make the most competitive bid

questions.stimulus: Ampicillin and other modern antibiotics kill a much wider variety of bacteria than penicillin does. They also carry higher profit margins, so drug companies now have an incentive to stop manufacturing the older, less profitable antibiotics. This could cause a penicillin shortage, forcing doctors to use the much more powerful new antibiotics in cases where they might otherwise be unnecessary. Thus, these newer antibiotics are likely to result in an outbreak of diseases caused by drug-resistant bacteria, since _______.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion of the argument is most strongly supported if which one of the following completes the passage?

answerChoices.A: drug-resistant bacteria flourish in the absence of competition from a wide variety of other bacteria
answerChoices.B: older antibiotics like penicillin have been widely used for many decades
answerChoices.C: a shortage of penicillin would drive up its price and profit margin
answerChoices.D: treatment of diseases with the powerful new antibiotics is much more expensive than treatment with the older ones
answerChoices.E: most bacteria that are resistant to penicillin are not resistant to ampicillin and other modern antibiotics

questions.stimulus: Weingarten claims that keeping animals in zoos is unethical. He points out that it involves placing animals in unnatural environments merely for the sake of human amusement. However, since Weingarten sees nothing wrong with owning pets, and keeping pets surely involves placing an animal in an unnatural environment merely for human amusement, his claim should be rejected.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed in that the argument

answerChoices.A: takes for granted that Weingarten owns one or more pets
answerChoices.B: inappropriately generalizes from a particular case
answerChoices.C: misrepresents the conclusion of the opposing argument
answerChoices.D: takes a necessary condition for a practice’s being unethical as a sufficient condition for its being so
answerChoices.E: rejects a claim merely on the grounds that its proponent holds another view inconsistent with it

questions.stimulus:
Activist: President Zagel should resign, because she is unable to govern effectively given the widespread belief that she rigged the election.
President Zagel: Over the last decade, scandals have forced two presidents of this country to resign. If I were to resign, the rest of the world would see us as a country whose political system is hopelessly unstable. That would be unacceptable, so I must remain in office.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the activist’s argument in the face of President Zagel’s argument?
