answerChoices.A: A country whose election procedures are resistant to illegitimate manipulation will eventually become politically stable.
answerChoices.B: The leader of a country should resign if doing so is likely to improve that country’s international reputation for political stability.
answerChoices.C: If a president is involved in a scandal that is more serious than scandals that have forced previous leaders to resign, then that president should resign.
answerChoices.D: If it can be conclusively proven that an officeholder rigged an election, then that officeholder should be removed from office.
answerChoices.E: It is more important for a country to have a leader who can govern effectively than it is to be viewed by other countries as having a stable political system.

questions.stimulus: A popular book argues that people who are successful in business have, without exception, benefited from a lot of luck on their way to success. But this is ridiculous. Anyone who has studied successful people knows that success requires a lot of hard work.
questions.questionStem: The argument commits which one of the following errors of reasoning?

answerChoices.A: It mistakes the claim that something is required for a purpose for the claim that it is sufficient for that purpose.
answerChoices.B: It accepts a view as authoritative without establishing the authority of the source of the view.
answerChoices.C: It takes for granted in a premise what it is trying to prove in its conclusion.
answerChoices.D: It treats an effect of something as the cause of that thing.
answerChoices.E: It attacks the source of an argument rather than attacking the substance of that argument.

questions.stimulus: University president: When a faculty member’s falsification of research was uncovered, the media treated it as evidence of the university’s low standards, even though in truth it was a mere case of dishonesty. But since vigilance with respect to academic standards is always necessary, it’s good that standards have become a topic of discussion.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following conforms most closely to the principle illustrated above?

answerChoices.A: The latest government scandal was caused primarily by a lack of oversight, which in turn led to corruption. Since no amount of oversight can eliminate all corruption, it is important that the problems with oversight are not the only topic of discussion.
answerChoices.B: The latest government scandal has been attributed to lack of oversight, although the true cause of the scandal was simple corruption. Nonetheless, this discussion of oversight is welcome, because oversight is important in its own right.
answerChoices.C: The latest government scandal has been attributed to both lack of oversight and corruption. As a result, these important concerns are now being discussed. So, despite the harm that it caused, it is good that the scandal occurred.
answerChoices.D: The latest government scandal has been analyzed as a case of simple corruption, although corruption had little to do with it. Because the true cause of the scandal was lack of oversight, attributing the cause of the scandal to simple corruption is harmful.
answerChoices.E: The latest government scandal has been analyzed as a case of simple corruption, with no mention of the role played by lack of oversight. Nonetheless, the focus on corruption is welcome, because corruption played the largest role in the scandal.

questions.stimulus: Politician: Over the next decade, our city will be replacing all of its street signs with signs that are designed for improved readability. But since no one is complaining about the current signs, installing the new ones is a colossal waste of time and money.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following would be most useful to know in evaluating the politician’s argument?

answerChoices.A: What features of the new street signs improve the readability of the signs?
answerChoices.B: Are the new street signs considerably more expensive to manufacture than the current street signs were?
answerChoices.C: What percentage of its street signs does the city replace annually in the course of ordinary maintenance?
answerChoices.D: Do any other cities plan to replace their street signs with signs designed for improved readability?
answerChoices.E: Were experts consulted when the new street signs were designed?

questions.stimulus: A large survey of scientists found that almost all accept Wang’s Law, and almost all know the results of the Brown-Eisler Experiment. But those results together with Wang’s Law contradict the Minsk Hypothesis. Therefore, most of the scientists surveyed reject the Minsk Hypothesis.
questions.questionStem: The argument requires assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: The scientists surveyed are generally aware that the results of the Brown-Eisler Experiment together with Wang’s Law contradict the Minsk Hypothesis.
answerChoices.B: The scientists in the survey who know the results of the Brown-Eisler Experiment are exactly the same ones who accept Wang’s Law.
answerChoices.C: Almost all of the scientists surveyed are familiar with the way in which the results of the Brown-Eisler Experiment were obtained.
answerChoices.D: The sample is large enough to be representative of scientists in the field.
answerChoices.E: Wang’s Law has in fact been shown to be true.

questions.stimulus: Any literary translation is a compromise between two goals that cannot be entirely reconciled: faithfulness to the meaning of the text and faithfulness to the original author’s style. Thus, even the most skillful translation will be at best a flawed approximation of the original work.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: A translation of a literary work should be entirely faithful to neither the meaning of the text nor the original author’s style.
answerChoices.B: If a literary translation is flawed as an approximation of the original work, it cannot be regarded as a successful compromise between faithfulness to the meaning of the text and faithfulness to the original author’s style.
answerChoices.C: The most skillful literary translation of a work will not necessarily be the most balanced compromise between faithfulness to the meaning of the text and faithfulness to the original author’s style.
answerChoices.D: Any translation that is not entirely faithful to both the meaning of the text and the original author’s style will be at best a flawed approximation of that work.
answerChoices.E: Not even the most skillful literary translation could be faithful to both the literal meaning of the text and the original author’s style.

questions.stimulus: Sociologist: Television, telephones, and other electronic media encourage imprecise, uncritical thinking. Yet critical thinking is the only adequate protection against political demagogues, who seek to exploit people by presenting emotionally loaded language as an objective description of reality.
questions.questionStem: If the sociologist’s statements are true, then each of the following statements could be true except:

answerChoices.A: There are no political demagogues in some highly technological societies.
answerChoices.B: Political demagogues are not the only ones who seek to exploit people by presenting emotionally loaded language as an objective description of reality.
answerChoices.C: Highly emotional people are more easily exploited than less emotional people.
answerChoices.D: The mere presence of an orderly system of government in a society provides adequate protection against political demagogues.
answerChoices.E: The mere presence of electronic communications technology in a society provides adequate protection against the erosion of media freedoms.

questions.stimulus: People with higher-than-average blood levels of a normal dietary by-product called homocysteine are twice as likely to be diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease as are those with average or below-average homocysteine levels. Thus, it is likely that the risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease could be reduced by including in one’s diet large amounts of B vitamins and folic acid, which convert homocysteine into substances known to have no relation to Alzheimer’s disease.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Many Alzheimer’s patients have normal homocysteine levels.
answerChoices.B: The substances into which homocysteine is converted can sometimes have harmful effects unrelated to Alzheimer’s disease.
answerChoices.C: B vitamins and folic acid are not metabolized by the body very efficiently when taken in the form of vitamin-mineral supplements.
answerChoices.D: People whose relatives contracted Alzheimer’s disease are much more likely to develop Alzheimer’s than those whose relatives did not.
answerChoices.E: Alzheimer’s disease tends to increase the levels of homocysteine in the blood.

questions.stimulus: Consumer advocate: Economists reason that price gouging—increasing the price of goods when no alternative seller is available—is efficient because it allocates goods to people whose willingness to pay more shows that they really need those goods. But willingness to pay is not proportional to need. In the real world, some people simply cannot pay as much as others. As a result, a price increase will allocate goods to the people with the most money, not to those with the most need.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the role played in the consumer advocate’s argument by the claim that willingness to pay is not proportional to need?

answerChoices.A: It disputes one explanation in order to make way for an alternative explanation.
answerChoices.B: It is the overall conclusion of the argument.
answerChoices.C: It is a component of reasoning disputed in the argument.
answerChoices.D: It is a general principle whose validity the argument questions.
answerChoices.E: It denies a claim that the argument takes to be assumed in the reasoning that it rejects.

questions.stimulus: Zoologist: Plants preferentially absorb heavy nitrogen from rainwater. Heavy nitrogen consequently becomes concentrated in the tissues of herbivores, and animals that eat meat in turn exhibit even higher concentrations of heavy nitrogen in their bodily tissues. We compared bone samples from European cave bears of the Ice Age with blood samples from present-day bears fed meat-enriched diets, and the levels of heavy nitrogen present in these samples were identical. Thus, the prehistoric European cave bears were not exclusively herbivores.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most strengthen the zoologist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Plants can also absorb heavy nitrogen from a variety of sources other than rainwater.
answerChoices.B: The rate at which heavy nitrogen accumulated in the blood of Ice Age herbivores can be inferred from samples of their bones.
answerChoices.C: The same number of samples was taken from present-day bears as was taken from Ice Age cave bears.
answerChoices.D: Bone samples from present-day bears fed meat-enriched diets exhibit the same levels of heavy nitrogen as do their blood samples.
answerChoices.E: The level of heavy nitrogen in the bones of any bear fed a meat-enriched diet is the same as that in the bones of any other meat-eating bear.

questions.stimulus: Biologist: Some computer scientists imagine that all that is required for making an artificial intelligence is to create a computer program that encapsulates the information contained in the human genome. They are mistaken. The operation of the human brain is governed by the interactions of proteins whose structures are encoded in the human genome.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the biologist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The functions of the human brain are governed by processes that cannot be simulated by a computer.
answerChoices.B: The interactions of the proteins that govern the operation of the human brain are not determined by the information contained in the human genome.
answerChoices.C: The only way to create an artificial intelligence is to model it on the operation of the human brain.
answerChoices.D: The amount of information contained in the human genome is too large to be easily encapsulated by a computer program.
answerChoices.E: It is much more difficult to write a program that encapsulates the interactions of proteins than to write a program that encapsulates the information contained in the human genome.

questions.stimulus: Some advertisers offer certain consumers home computers free of charge. Advertisements play continuously on the computers’ screens whenever they are in use. As consumers use the computers to browse the Internet, information about their browsing patterns is sent to the advertisers, enabling them to transmit to each consumer advertising that accurately reflects his or her individual interests. The advertisers can afford to offer the computers for free because of the increased sales that result from this precise targeting of individual consumers.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: At least some consumers who use a computer offered free of charge by advertisers for browsing the Internet spend more money on purchases from those advertisers than they would if they did not use such a computer to browse the Internet.
answerChoices.B: No advertisers could offer promotions that give away computers free of charge if consumers never used those computers to browse the Internet.
answerChoices.C: There are at least some consumers who browse the Internet using computers offered free of charge by the advertisers and who, if they did not use those computers to browse the Internet, would spend little if any money on purchases from those advertisers.
answerChoices.D: The advertisers would not be able to offer the computers absolutely free of charge if advertisements that accurately reflected the interests of the computers’ users did not play continuously across the computers’ screens whenever they were in use.
answerChoices.E: Consumers who use a computer offered free of charge by the advertisers can sometimes choose to abstain from having information about their browsing patterns sent to the advertisers.

questions.stimulus: Some eloquent speakers impress their audiences with the vividness and clarity of the messages conveyed. Speakers who resort to obscenity, however, are not genuinely eloquent, so none of these speakers impress their audiences.
questions.questionStem: The flawed reasoning in which one of the following is most similar to that in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: A culture without myths will also lack fundamental moral certainties. Thus, this culture must lack fundamental moral certainties, since it is devoid of myth.
answerChoices.B: There are authors who write one page a day and produce one book per year. Serious authors, however, do not write one page per day, so some authors who write one book a year are not serious.
answerChoices.C: Cities that are centers of commerce are always centers of industry as well. It follows that some centers of commerce are small cities, since there are centers of industry that are not small cities.
answerChoices.D: Most farmers like living in rural areas. Since Carla is not a farmer, she probably would not enjoy living in the country.
answerChoices.E: Sculptors sometimes produce significant works of art. But musicians are not sculptors. Hence, musicians never produce significant works of art.

questions.stimulus: Cool weather typically weakens muscle power in cold-blooded creatures. In the veiled chameleon, a cold-blooded animal, the speed at which the animal can retract its tongue declines dramatically as the temperature falls. However, the speed at which this chameleon can extend its tongue does not decline much as the temperature falls.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

answerChoices.A: Most cold-blooded animals are much more active in warmer weather than in cooler weather.
answerChoices.B: Many cold-blooded animals, including the veiled chameleon, have tongues that can extend quite a distance.
answerChoices.C: Veiled chameleons are found in a wide range of habitats, including ones with wide variations in temperature and ones with moderate climates.
answerChoices.D: In the veiled chameleon, tongue retraction is powered by muscles, whereas tongue extension is driven by energy stored in a rubber band-like sheath.
answerChoices.E: Compared with the muscles in the tongues of most cold-blooded animals, the retraction muscles in the veiled chameleon’s tongue are considerably stronger.

questions.stimulus: Acme’s bank loan must be immediately repaid in full if Acme’s earnings fall below $1 million per year. If Acme has to repay the entire loan immediately, it will have to declare bankruptcy. Acme had seemed safe from bankruptcy, having reported annual earnings of well over $1 million in each year it has had the bank loan. However, Acme has now admitted overstating its earnings for last year, so it will have to declare bankruptcy.
questions.questionStem: The argument requires the assumption that

answerChoices.A: Acme’s earnings for last year, when accurately stated, are below $1 million
answerChoices.B: Acme has other debts besides the bank loan
answerChoices.C: last year is not the only year for which Acme overstated earnings
answerChoices.D: Acme’s earnings for the current year will fall below $1 million
answerChoices.E: Acme would be able to avoid bankruptcy if it did not have to repay the bank loan

questions.stimulus: Hospital patients generally have lower infection rates and require shorter hospital stays if they are housed in private rooms rather than semiprivate rooms. Yet in Woodville’s hospital, which has only semiprivate rooms, infection rates and length of stays are typically the same as in several nearby hospitals where most of the rooms are private, even though patients served by these hospitals are very similar to those served by Woodville’s hospital.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent conflict in the information above?

answerChoices.A: Many of the doctors who routinely treat patients in Woodville’s hospital also routinely treat patients in one or more of the nearby hospitals.
answerChoices.B: Most of the nearby hospitals were built within the last 10 years, whereas Woodville’s hospital was built about 50 years ago.
answerChoices.C: Infection is more likely to be spread where people come into close contact with one another than where they do not.
answerChoices.D: Woodville’s hospital has a policy of housing one patient per room in semiprivate rooms whenever possible.
answerChoices.E: Woodville’s hospital is located in its central business district, whereas most of the nearby hospitals are located outside their municipalities’ business districts.

questions.stimulus: Economist: Unemployment will soon decrease. If total government spending significantly increases next year, the economy will be stimulated in the short term and unemployment will decrease. If, on the other hand, total government spending significantly decreases next year, businesses will retain more of their earnings in the short term and employ more workers, thereby decreasing unemployment.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion drawn by the economist is properly inferred if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Either total government spending will significantly decrease next year or else total government spending will significantly increase next year.
answerChoices.B: Government officials are currently implementing policies that are intended to reduce unemployment.
answerChoices.C: If there is a significantly increased demand for workers, then there will be a significant decrease in unemployment.
answerChoices.D: A significant increase in total government spending will slow the economy in the long run.
answerChoices.E: If the economy is not stimulated and businesses do not retain more of their earnings, then unemployment will not decrease.

questions.stimulus:
Marisa: Existing zoning regulations must be loosened; in some places the restrictions on development are now so prohibitive as to reduce the property values of undeveloped areas significantly.
Tyne: I disagree. Though it is true that the recent increase in the stringency of zoning regulations could be seen by developers as merely an activists’ ploy to restrict development further, the value of natural, undisturbed areas can only be better preserved by such regulatory protection.
questions.questionStem: Tyne’s response to Marisa suggests that Tyne has misinterpreted which one of the following words in Marisa’s remarks?

answerChoices.A: regulations
answerChoices.B: development
answerChoices.C: prohibitive
answerChoices.D: values
answerChoices.E: significantly

questions.stimulus: Scientist: Laboratory animals have access to ample food, and they get relatively little exercise. These factors can skew the results of research using animals, since such studies often rely on the assumption that the animal subjects are healthy. For instance, animal studies that purport to show that extreme caloric restriction can extend lifespans take for granted that their subjects were not overfed to begin with.
questions.questionStem: The scientist’s argument requires assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Laboratory animals are healthy if they are fed a carefully restricted diet and get plenty of exercise.
answerChoices.B: Laboratory conditions that provide animals with ample food but relatively little exercise can be unhealthy for the animals.
answerChoices.C: It is not unusual for animals outside of laboratory settings to have access to ample food and get relatively little exercise.
answerChoices.D: Some animal studies take into consideration the differences between the living conditions of laboratory animals and those of other animals.
answerChoices.E: When provided with unlimited food over a long period of time, animals show little day-to-day variation in their eating habits.

questions.stimulus: Trade negotiator: Increasing economic prosperity in a country tends to bring political freedom to its inhabitants. Therefore, it is wrong for any country to adopt trade policies that are likely to seriously hinder growth in the prosperity of any other country.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, would most help to justify the trade negotiator's reasoning?

answerChoices.A: Every country should adopt at least some policies that encourage the development of political freedom in other countries.
answerChoices.B: Both economic prosperity and political freedom can contribute to the overall well-being of any country’s inhabitants.
answerChoices.C: The primary reason that any country seeks economic prosperity is to foster political freedom in that country.
answerChoices.D: A country should not do anything that might hinder the growth of political freedom in any other country.
answerChoices.E: It is wrong for any country to adopt trade policies that might diminish the prosperity of its inhabitants.

questions.stimulus: Whenever an artist endowed with both a high level of artistic skill and a high degree of creativity combines these two abilities in the process of creating an artwork, the resulting product is a great work of art. Moreover, no work of art can be great unless both of these elements are combined in its execution. Thus, great works of art are necessarily rare.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: Not every artist possesses a high level of artistic skill.
answerChoices.B: A high degree of creativity and a high level of artistic skill are seldom combined in the creation of a work of art.
answerChoices.C: An artist endowed with a high degree of creativity and a high level of artistic skill will necessarily produce great works of art.
answerChoices.D: Few artists are endowed with a high degree of creativity.
answerChoices.E: Anyone endowed with both a high level of artistic skill and a high degree of creativity will produce only a few great works of art.

questions.stimulus: Cereal advertisement: Fitness experts say that regular exercise is the most effective way to become physically fit, and studies have shown that adults who eat cereal every day exercise more regularly than adults who do not eat cereal. So by eating Fantastic Flakes every morning, you too will be on the most effective path to physical fitness.
questions.questionStem: The argumentation in the advertisement is flawed in that it

answerChoices.A: infers a cause from a mere correlation
answerChoices.B: presumes, without providing justification, that Fantastic Flakes are more nutritious than other cereals
answerChoices.C: infers that a given factor is the sole predictor of a result merely on the grounds that the factor has been shown to contribute to that result
answerChoices.D: draws a conclusion about all adults from a sample that is too small to be representative
answerChoices.E: infers that some members of a group have a particular characteristic merely from the fact that the group as a whole has it

questions.stimulus: Journalist: Some critics argue that as the entertainment value of news reporting increases, the caliber of that reporting decreases. Yet the greatest journalists have been the most entertaining. So these critics are mistaken.
questions.questionStem: The journalist’s conclusion is properly drawn if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: The news reporting of the greatest journalists has been of the highest caliber.
answerChoices.B: The greatest journalists have been entertainers who report the news.
answerChoices.C: Journalistic greatness involves producing news that is very valuable in some sense.
answerChoices.D: Entertainment and news are not mutually exclusive categories.
answerChoices.E: The worst journalists have been more entertaining than informative.

questions.stimulus: Linguist: Three of the four subfamilies of the so-called “Austronesian” languages are found only among indigenous peoples in Taiwan, whereas the fourth is found on islands over a huge area stretching from Madagascar to the eastern Pacific Ocean. Since these subfamilies all originated in the same language, which must have been originally spoken in a single geographic location, these facts suggest that Taiwan is the homeland where Austronesian languages have been spoken longest and, hence, that Austronesian-speaking peoples originated in Taiwan and later migrated to other islands.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the overall conclusion drawn in the linguist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The Austronesian family of languages has four subfamilies, three of which are found only among indigenous peoples in Taiwan.
answerChoices.B: Wherever most subfamilies of the Austronesian family of languages have been spoken longest is probably the homeland where Austronesian languages originated.
answerChoices.C: Taiwan is probably the homeland where Austronesian languages have been spoken longest.
answerChoices.D: Austronesian-speaking peoples originated in the homeland where Austronesian languages have been spoken longest.
answerChoices.E: Austronesian-speaking peoples probably originated in Taiwan and later migrated to other islands.

questions.stimulus:
West: Of our company’s three quality control inspectors, Haynes is clearly the worst. Of the appliances that were returned to us last year because of quality control defects, half were inspected by Haynes.
Young: But Haynes inspects significantly more than half the appliances we sell each year.
questions.questionStem: Young responds to West’s argument by

answerChoices.A: contending that the argument presupposes what it is trying to prove
answerChoices.B: questioning the relevance of West’s conclusion
answerChoices.C: disputing the accuracy of one of the argument’s stated premises
answerChoices.D: arguing for a less extreme version of West’s conclusion
answerChoices.E: denying one of the argument’s presuppositions

questions.stimulus: While playing a game with a ball, both Emma and John carelessly ignored the danger their game posed to nearby objects. An errant throw by John struck and broke a neighbor’s window. Because his throw broke the window, John, but not Emma, should be required to perform chores for the neighbor as compensation for the damage.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following conforms most closely to the principle illustrated above?

answerChoices.A: While looking after her neighbor’s pets, Laura left the door to her neighbor’s house unlocked. Fortunately, nothing bad happened as a result. But her neighbor should not trust Laura to look after her pets in the future.
answerChoices.B: Gerald hired Linda and Seung to move his furniture to a new residence. Linda and Seung carefully followed Gerald’s instructions, but not all of the furniture fit in the moving truck. Gerald should still be required to pay Linda and Seung for the work they did.
answerChoices.C: Terry and Chris were racing their cars on a public street. Chris lost control of his car and struck a parked car. Chris, but not Terry, should be required to pay to repair the damage.
answerChoices.D: Alexis and Juan rented a boat for the afternoon. Because of improper use by the previous renter, the boat’s engine malfunctioned during their excursion. The boat’s owner should be required to refund Alexis’s and Juan’s rental fees.
answerChoices.E: Susan and Leland disregarded posted warnings in order to skate on a frozen pond. When the ice broke, Susan’s ankle was injured. Susan cannot hold the pond’s owners responsible for her injuries.

questions.stimulus: Psychology researchers observed that parents feel emotion while singing to their infants. The researchers hypothesized that this emotion noticeably affects the sound of the singing. To test this hypothesis the parents were recorded while singing to their infants and while singing with no infant present. They were instructed to make the two renditions as similar as possible. These recordings were then played for psychologists who had not observed the recordings being made. For 80 percent of the recordings, these psychologists were able to correctly identify, by listening alone, which recordings were of parents singing to their children. The researchers concluded that their hypothesis was correct.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most strengthen the researchers’ reasoning?

answerChoices.A: A separate study by the same researchers found that parents feel more emotion when singing to their own children than when singing to other children.
answerChoices.B: Some, but not all, of the parents in the study realized that their song renditions were being recorded.
answerChoices.C: Parents displayed little emotion when singing with no child or adult present.
answerChoices.D: When a person feels emotion, that emotion provokes involuntary physiological responses that affect the vocal cords and lungs.
answerChoices.E: Most of the parents who participated in the study believed that the emotion they felt while singing to their infants affected their singing.

questions.stimulus: Many scholars claim that Shakespeare’s portrayal of Richard III was extremely inaccurate, arguing that he derived that portrayal from propagandists opposed to Richard III. But these claims are irrelevant for appreciating Shakespeare’s work. The character of Richard III as portrayed in Shakespeare’s drama is fascinating and illuminating both aesthetically and morally, regardless of its relation to historical fact.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: In historical drama, the aesthetic value of the work is not necessarily undermined by historical inaccuracies.
answerChoices.B: In dealing with real people, dramatists should reflect their lives accurately.
answerChoices.C: Shakespeare’s historical importance puts him beyond the scope of all literary criticism.
answerChoices.D: History is always told by propagandists from the winning side.
answerChoices.E: Historical inaccuracies should be corrected only when they impugn the reputations of good people.

questions.stimulus: Voter: Our prime minister is evidently seeking a job at an international organization. Anyone seeking a job at an international organization would surely spend a lot of time traveling abroad, and our prime minister has spent more days abroad than at home so far this year.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its flawed reasoning to the voter’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Kao must be a golfer. Kao is planning to run for office, and most people who run for office play golf.
answerChoices.B: Franklin will lose the coming election. The opposing candidate has better policy ideas and brings more relevant experience to the job.
answerChoices.C: Ramirez is evidently able to control the traffic signals. Just now, as Ramirez approached the curb, the traffic signal changed from red to green.
answerChoices.D: Thompson must be negotiating a personal loan. Thompson was at the bank yesterday, and people who are negotiating a personal loan go to the bank to meet with a loan agent.
answerChoices.E: McKinsey must have committed a crime at some point. After all, despite extensive background checks no one has been able to show that McKinsey has never committed a crime.

questions.stimulus: It is pointless to debate the truth of the law of noncontradiction, a fundamental logical principle according to which two statements that contradict each other cannot both be true. For a debate to be productive, participants must hold some basic principles in common. But the principles held in common in a debate over the law of noncontradiction would be much less certain than that law, so it matters little whether the law of noncontradiction can be defended on the basis of those principles.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the overall conclusion drawn in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It is pointless to debate the truth of the law of noncontradiction.
answerChoices.B: Statements that contradict each other cannot both be true.
answerChoices.C: The participants in a productive debate must hold at least some basic principles in common.
answerChoices.D: The law of noncontradiction is a principle that the participants in a productive debate must hold in common.
answerChoices.E: Any principles that could be used to defend the law of noncontradiction are less certain than it is.

questions.stimulus: Pundit: For many high school graduates, attending a university would be of no help in getting a corporate job. The attributes corporations value most in potential employees are initiative, flexibility, and the ability to solve practical problems. Many new high school graduates have these attributes already.
questions.questionStem: The pundit’s argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it

answerChoices.A: fails to establish that university graduates do not have initiative, flexibility, and the ability to solve practical problems
answerChoices.B: overlooks the possibility that corporations may require an attribute that potential employees can obtain only by attending a university
answerChoices.C: provides no justification for the presumption that corporations only hire employees who have initiative, flexibility, and the ability to solve practical problems
answerChoices.D: takes for granted that the only reason that high school graduates go on to attend university is to improve their job prospects
answerChoices.E: takes for granted that initiative, flexibility, and the ability to solve practical problems are attributes that can be acquired through study

questions.stimulus: Archaeologist: Neanderthals, a human-like species living 60,000 years ago, probably preserved meat by smoking it. Burnt lichen and grass have been found in many Neanderthal fireplaces. A fire of lichen and grass produces a lot of smoke but does not produce nearly as much heat or light as a wood fire.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most weaken the archaeologist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: In close proximity to the fireplaces with lichen and grass are other fireplaces that, evidence suggests, burned material that produced more heat than smoke.
answerChoices.B: In the region containing the Neanderthal fireplaces in which lichen and grass were burnt, no plants that could be burned more effectively to produce heat or light were available 60,000 years ago.
answerChoices.C: Some of the fireplaces containing burnt lichen are in regions in which lichen is not believed to have been plentiful and so would have had to have been brought in from some distance.
answerChoices.D: There is clear evidence that at least some groups of Neanderthals living more recently than 60,000 years ago developed methods of preserving meat other than smoking it.
answerChoices.E: The ability to preserve meat through smoking would have made the Neanderthal humans less vulnerable to poor periods of hunting.

questions.stimulus:
Edgar: Some of the pumps supplying water to our region have been ordered shut down in order to protect a species of small fish. But it is absurd to inconvenience thousands of people for the sake of something so inconsequential.
Rafaela: You’re missing the point. The threat to that fish species is a sign of a very serious threat to our water supply.
questions.questionStem: The dialogue provides the most support for the claim that Edgar and Rafaela disagree over whether

answerChoices.A: shutting down the pumps will actually inconvenience a large number of people
answerChoices.B: the survival of the fish species is the only reason for shutting down the pumps
answerChoices.C: species of small fish are inconsequential
answerChoices.D: the order to shut down the pumps was legal
answerChoices.E: shutting down the pumps will be sufficient to protect the fish species

questions.stimulus: Only engineering is capable of analyzing the nature of a machine in terms of the successful working of the whole; physics and chemistry determine the material conditions necessary for this success, but cannot express the notion of purpose. Similarly, only physiology can analyze the nature of an organism in terms of organs’ roles in the body’s healthy functioning. Physics and chemistry cannot ascertain by themselves any of these operational principles.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the analogy?

answerChoices.A: The functioning of the human organism is machine-like in nature.
answerChoices.B: Physics and chemistry determine the material conditions required for good physiological functioning.
answerChoices.C: The notion of purpose used by engineers to judge the success of machinery has an analog in organisms.
answerChoices.D: Physiology as a science is largely independent of physics and chemistry.
answerChoices.E: Biological processes are irreducible to mechanical or chemical processes.

questions.stimulus: After a hepadnavirus inserts itself into a chromosome of an animal, fragments of the virus are passed on to all of that animal’s descendants. A hepadnavirus fragment is present in a chromosome of the zebra finch and in precisely the same location in a corresponding chromosome of the dark-eyed junco. The fact that these two bird species diverged from each other about 25 million years ago therefore means that the hepadnavirus is at least 25 million years old.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Viruses can affect the evolution of an organism and can thereby influence the likelihood of their diverging into two species.
answerChoices.B: The chromosomes of the zebra finch and the dark-eyed junco contain fragments of no virus other than the hepadnavirus.
answerChoices.C: When a virus inserts itself into an animal’s chromosome, the insertion occurs at a random spot.
answerChoices.D: Many bird species other than the zebra finch and the dark-eyed junco contain fragments of the hepadnavirus.
answerChoices.E: The presence of a hepadnavirus in an animal species does not affect the likelihood of that species’ survival.

questions.stimulus: The diet of Heliothis subflexa caterpillars consists entirely of fruit from plants of the genus Physalis. These fruit do not contain linolenic acid, which is necessary to the growth and maturation of many insects other than H. subflexa. Linolenic acid in an insect’s diet is also necessary for the production of a chemical called volicitin. While most caterpillar species have volicitin in their saliva, H. subflexa does not.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the statements above?

answerChoices.A: H. subflexa caterpillars synthesize linolenic acid within their bodies.
answerChoices.B: Most species of caterpillar have sources of linolenic acid in their diets.
answerChoices.C: Any caterpillar that has linolenic acid in its diet has volicitin in its saliva.
answerChoices.D: A food source containing linolenic acid would be poisonous to H. subflexa caterpillars.
answerChoices.E: No caterpillars other than H. subflexa eat fruit from plants of the genus Physalis.

questions.stimulus: Politician: Democracy requires that there be no restrictions on the ability of citizens to share their ideas freely, without fear of reprisal. Therefore the right to have private conversations, unmonitored by the government, is essential to democracy. For a government to monitor conversations on the Internet would thus be a setback for democracy.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the role played in the argument by the claim that democracy depends on the ability of citizens to share their ideas freely, without fear of reprisal?

answerChoices.A: It is a claim for which no support is provided, and which is used to support only the argument’s main conclusion.
answerChoices.B: It is a claim for which no support is provided, and which is used to support a claim that is itself used to support the argument’s main conclusion.
answerChoices.C: It is a claim for which support is provided, and which is in turn used to support the argument’s main conclusion.
answerChoices.D: It is the argument’s main conclusion and is inferred from two other statements in the argument, one of which is used to support the other.
answerChoices.E: It is the argument’s main conclusion and is inferred from two other statements in the argument, neither of which is used to support the other.

questions.stimulus: One way to compare chess-playing programs is to compare how they perform with fixed time limits per move. Given any two computers with which a chess-playing program is compatible, and given fixed time limits per move, such a program will have a better chance of winning on the faster computer. This is simply because the program will be able to examine more possible moves in the time allotted per move.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: If one chess-playing program can examine more possible moves than a different chess-playing program run on the same computer under the same time constraints per move, the former program will have a better chance of winning than the latter.
answerChoices.B: How fast a given computer is has no effect on which chess-playing computer programs can run on that computer.
answerChoices.C: In general, the more moves a given chess-playing program is able to examine under given time constraints per move, the better the chances that program will win.
answerChoices.D: If two different chess-playing programs are running on two different computers under the same time constraints per move, the program running on the faster computer will be able to examine more possible moves in the time allotted.
answerChoices.E: If a chess-playing program is run on two different computers and is allotted more time to examine possible moves when running on the slow computer than when running on the fast computer, it will have an equal chance of winning on either computer.

questions.stimulus: In a recent study of dust-mite allergy sufferers, one group slept on mite-proof bedding, while a control group slept on bedding that was not mite-proof. The group using mite-proof bedding had a 69 percent reduction in the dust-mite allergen in their mattresses, whereas there was no significant reduction in the control group. However, even though bedding is the main source of exposure to dust mites, no symptom reduction was reported in either group.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent conflict in the statements above?

answerChoices.A: Dust-mite allergens in bedding tend to irritate many allergy sufferers’ nasal passages more than do the same allergens in other locations, such as carpets.
answerChoices.B: When people report their own allergy symptoms, they tend to exaggerate the severity of those symptoms.
answerChoices.C: The medical community does not fully understand how dust-mite allergens cause allergy.
answerChoices.D: For dust-mite allergy sufferers to get relief from their allergies, dust-mite allergens must be reduced by 90 to 95 percent.
answerChoices.E: All of the participants in the study were told that one group in the study would be sleeping on mite-proof bedding.

questions.stimulus: Five years ago, the hair dryer produced by the Wilson Appliance Company accounted for 50 percent of all sales of hair dryers nationwide. Currently, however, Wilson Appliance’s product makes up only 25 percent of such sales. Because of this decline, and because the average net income that Wilson receives per hair dryer sold has not changed over the last 5 years, the company’s net income from sales of the product must be only half of what it was 5 years ago.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: mistakes a decline in the market share of Wilson Appliance’s hair dryer for a decline in the total sales of that product
answerChoices.B: does not provide specific information about the profits hair dryers generate for the companies that produce them
answerChoices.C: fails to discuss sales figures for Wilson Appliance’s products other than its hair dryers
answerChoices.D: overlooks the possibility that the retail price of Wilson Appliance’s hair dryer may have increased over the past 5 years
answerChoices.E: provides no independent evidence that Wilson Appliance’s hair dryer is one of the company’s least profitable products

questions.stimulus: Whether or not one can rightfully call a person’s faithfulness a virtue depends in part on the object of that person’s faithfulness. Virtues are by definition praiseworthy, which is why no one considers resentment virtuous, even though it is in fact a kind of faithfulness—faithfulness to hatreds or animosities.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the overall conclusion drawn in the argument?

answerChoices.A: The object of a person’s faithfulness partially determines whether or not that faithfulness is virtuous.
answerChoices.B: Virtuous behavior is praiseworthy by definition.
answerChoices.C: Behavior that emerges from hatred or animosity cannot be called virtuous.
answerChoices.D: Faithfulness and resentment are obviously different, despite some similarities.
answerChoices.E: Resentment should not be considered a virtuous emotion.

questions.stimulus: Columnist: A government-owned water utility has received approval to collect an additional charge on water bills and to use that additional revenue to build a dam. A member of the legislature has proposed not building the dam but instead spending the extra money from water bills to build new roads. That proposal is unacceptable.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the columnist’s judgment that the legislator’s proposal is unacceptable?

answerChoices.A: Customers of a utility have a right to know how the money they pay to the utility will be used.
answerChoices.B: Money designated for projects that benefit an entire community should not be used for projects that benefit only some members of a community.
answerChoices.C: An additional charge on water bills should not be used to fund a project that most of the utility’s customers disapprove of.
answerChoices.D: An additional charge on water bills should not be imposed unless it is approved by the legislature.
answerChoices.E: A water utility should not collect an additional charge unless the money collected is used for water-related expenditures.

questions.stimulus: During its caterpillar stage, the leopard magpie moth feeds on a plant called the Natal grass cycad and by so doing laces its body with macrozamin, a toxin that makes the moth highly unpalatable to would-be predators. Since the Natal grass cycad is now endangered and facing extinction, the leopard magpie moth is also in danger of extinction.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: Feeding on the Natal grass cycad is the only means by which the leopard magpie moth can make itself highly unpalatable to predators.
answerChoices.B: The leopard magpie moth does not have the speed or the agility to escape from any of its potential predators.
answerChoices.C: Potential predators of the leopard magpie moth cannot determine from appearance alone whether a moth’s body is laced with macrozamin.
answerChoices.D: Leopard magpie moths are not able to locate Natal grass cycads unless those plants are abundant.
answerChoices.E: None of the potential predators of the leopard magpie moth have developed a tolerance to macrozamin.

questions.stimulus: Citizen: Our government has a large budget surplus, which our leaders wish to use to pay down the national debt. This makes no sense. Because of underfunding, our military is inadequate, the infrastructures of our cities are decaying, and our highways are in disrepair. If homeowners used all their money to pay off their mortgages early, while refusing to pay for upkeep of their homes, this would not make them better off financially. The same goes for the country as a whole.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the conclusion drawn in the citizen’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Homeowners should not pay off their mortgages early if they must neglect upkeep of their homes in order to do so.
answerChoices.B: It does not make sense for the government to use the budget surplus to pay down the national debt.
answerChoices.C: A homeowner’s personal financial situation is analogous in relevant ways to the financial situation of a country’s government.
answerChoices.D: Because of underfunding, the government does not maintain adequate standards in the services it provides.
answerChoices.E: Government leaders want to use the country’s large budget surplus to pay down the national debt.

questions.stimulus:
Peraski: Although driving gas-guzzling automobiles produces a greater level of pollution than driving smaller cars, those of us who drive smaller cars when we could use a bicycle cannot speak out against the use of gas guzzlers. We would be revealing our hypocrisy.
Jackson: I acknowledge I could do better in this area. But, it would be worse not to speak out against greater sources of pollution just because I am being hypocritical.
questions.questionStem: The dialogue provides the most support for the claim that Peraski and Jackson disagree over whether

answerChoices.A: driving a gas-guzzling automobile produces a greater level of pollution than driving a smaller car
answerChoices.B: speaking out against the use of gas guzzlers despite driving in situations in which one could use a bicycle reveals hypocrisy
answerChoices.C: driving even a small car when one could use a bicycle contributes to the level of pollution
answerChoices.D: one should speak out against polluting even if doing so reveals one’s own hypocrisy
answerChoices.E: there is no moral difference between driving a gas guzzler and driving a smaller car

questions.stimulus: For a species of large abalone shellfish to develop from a species of smaller ones, they must spend less energy on finding food and avoiding predators, and more on competition in mating. So it is surprising that the fossil record shows that a species of large abalones developed from a smaller one only after otters, which prey on abalones, began to dominate the waters in which the abalones lived.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

answerChoices.A: Otters and abalones also compete for the same types of food and so are drawn to the same waters.
answerChoices.B: The fossils that were studied showed the development of only one of the two species of large abalones known to exist.
answerChoices.C: Otters also prey on the abalones’ competitors for food and so indirectly make it easier for abalones to get food.
answerChoices.D: Small abalone species tend to reproduce more rapidly than larger abalone species.
answerChoices.E: Otters have a preference for large abalones over small ones and so prefer waters in which large abalones are found.

questions.stimulus: Some managers think that the best way to maximize employee performance is to institute stiff competition among employees. However, in situations where one competitor is perceived to be clearly superior, other competitors become anxious and doubt their own ability to perform. Thus, stiff competition can undermine the result it was intended to achieve.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion of the argument can be properly drawn if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Those who are perceived to be clearly superior almost always win.
answerChoices.B: The winner of a competition is often the competitor who exerts the most effort.
answerChoices.C: When competitors perceive the competition as winnable, their overall performance generally improves.
answerChoices.D: Doubting one’s own ability to perform can decrease one’s overall performance.
answerChoices.E: Competitors who work to undermine the confidence of other participants often do better in competitions.

questions.stimulus: Creating a database of all the plant species in the scientific record has proved to be no easy task. For centuries, botanists have been collecting and naming plants without realizing that many were in fact already named. And by using DNA analysis, botanists have shown that varieties of plants long thought to belong to the same species actually belong to different species.
questions.questionStem: Of the following claims, which one can most justifiably be rejected on the basis of the statements above?

answerChoices.A: Most of the duplicates and omissions among plant names in the scientific record have yet to be cleared up.
answerChoices.B: An accurate database of all the plant species in the scientific record can serve as an aid to botanists in their work.
answerChoices.C: Duplicates and omissions in the scientific record also occur in fields other than botany.
answerChoices.D: Botanists have no techniques for determining whether distinct plant species have been given distinct names.
answerChoices.E: A person who consults the scientific record looking under only one of a plant’s names may miss available information about that plant.

questions.stimulus: A year ago several regional hospitals attempted to reduce the number of patient injuries resulting from staff errors by implementing a plan to systematically record all such errors. The incidence of these injuries has substantially decreased at these hospitals since then. Clearly, the knowledge that their errors were being carefully monitored made the hospitals’ staffs much more meticulous in carrying out their patient-care duties.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Before the plan was implemented the hospitals already had a policy of thoroughly investigating any staff error that causes life-threatening injury to a patient.
answerChoices.B: The incidence of patient injuries at a regional hospital that did not participate in the plan also decreased over the year in question.
answerChoices.C: The plan did not call for the recording of staff errors that could have caused patient injuries but did not.
answerChoices.D: The decrease in the incidence of the injuries did not begin at any hospital until the staff there became aware that the records were being closely analyzed.
answerChoices.E: Under the plan, the hospitals’ staff members who were found to have made errors that caused injuries to patients received only reprimands for their first errors.

questions.stimulus: In a national park located on an island, a herd of moose was increasing in number and threatening to destroy species of native plants. Wolves were introduced to the island to reduce the herd and thereby prevent destruction of the vegetation. Although the wolves prospered, the moose herd continued to grow.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the failure of the strategy involving wolves?

answerChoices.A: The presence of wolves in an area tends to discourage other predators from moving into the area.
answerChoices.B: Attempts to control moose populations in other national parks by introducing predators have also been unsuccessful.
answerChoices.C: Wolves often kill moose weakened by diseases that probably would have spread to other moose.
answerChoices.D: Healthy moose generally consume more vegetation than do those that are diseased or injured.
answerChoices.E: Moose that are too old to breed are just as likely to die of natural causes as of attack by wolves.

questions.stimulus: If the purpose of laws is to contribute to people’s happiness, we have a basis for criticizing existing laws as well as proposing new laws. Hence, if that is not the purpose, then we have no basis for the evaluation of existing laws, from which we must conclude that existing laws acquire legitimacy simply because they are the laws.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed in that the argument

answerChoices.A: takes a sufficient condition for a state of affairs to be a necessary condition for it
answerChoices.B: infers a causal relationship from the mere presence of a correlation
answerChoices.C: trades on the use of a term in one sense in a premise and in a different sense in the conclusion
answerChoices.D: draws a conclusion about how the world actually is on the basis of claims about how it should be
answerChoices.E: infers that because a set of things has a certain property, each member of that set has the property

questions.stimulus: In order for life to exist on the recently discovered planet P23, there must be water on the planet’s surface. But there is no water on P23’s surface, so there is no life on planet P23.
questions.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in the argument above is most similar to that in which one of the following arguments?

answerChoices.A: A company must have efficient employees to be successful. And if a company’s employees are knowledgeable and hardworking, then they are probably efficient. Thus, in order for a company to be successful, it must have knowledgeable and hardworking employees.
answerChoices.B: The fact that the suspect was flustered when questioned by the police might be a result of the suspect’s surprise at being questioned. But if it is, the probability that the suspect is guilty is very low. Thus, the fact that the suspect was flustered is not necessarily a sign that the suspect is guilty.
answerChoices.C: Oil companies are not buying new drilling equipment. But if they were planning on increasing their drilling, they would be buying new drilling equipment. Thus, oil companies are not planning on increasing their drilling.
answerChoices.D: The price of real estate in a particular town is increasing. And if the town’s economy were improving, the price of real estate there would increase. Thus, the town’s economy is improving.
answerChoices.E: The exports of a particular nation have recently decreased. But whenever that nation’s exports decrease, its trade deficit increases. Thus, the nation’s trade deficit has recently increased.

questions.stimulus:
Sanchez: The sixteen new computers that the school purchased were not as expensive as many people assume. So it isn’t true that too much was spent on computers.
Merriweather: It isn’t that the school paid more for each computer than it was worth, but that the computers that were purchased were much more elaborate than they needed to be.
questions.questionStem: The dialogue provides the most support for the claim that Sanchez and Merriweather disagree over whether the school

answerChoices.A: needed sixteen new computers
answerChoices.B: purchased more computers than it should have
answerChoices.C: spent more in purchasing the sixteen computers than it should have
answerChoices.D: paid more for each computer than it was worth
answerChoices.E: has been harshly criticized for purchasing the sixteen computers

questions.stimulus: Airport administrator: According to the latest figures, less than 1 commercial flight in 2 million strays off course while landing, a number low enough to allow runways to be built closer together without a significant increase in risk. Opponents of closer runways claim that the number is closer to 1 in 20,000, but this figure is based on a partial review of air traffic control tapes and so is relatively unreliable compared to the other figure, which is based on a thorough study of the flight reports required of pilots for all commercial flights.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a flaw in the airport administrator’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The argument presumes, without providing justification, that building runways closer together will encourage pilots to be more cautious while landing.
answerChoices.B: The argument overlooks the fact that those who make mistakes are often unreliable sources of information about those mistakes.
answerChoices.C: The argument questions the integrity of those who are opposed to allowing runways to be built closer together.
answerChoices.D: The argument presumes, without providing justification, that the air traffic control tapes studied do not provide accurate information concerning specific flights.
answerChoices.E: The argument infers from a lack of conclusive evidence supporting the higher number’s accuracy that it must be inaccurate.

questions.stimulus: In deep temperate lakes, water temperatures vary according to depth. In winter, the coldest water is at the top; in summer, at the bottom. The changes in temperature distribution, or “turnover,” occur in fall and late winter. Lake trout will be found, as a rule, in the coldest water. So, if anglers seek lake trout in deep temperate lakes while these lakes are partially iced over in late winter, they will do best to eschew the lake trout’s summer haunts and fish instead in a shallow bay or close to the surface off a rocky point.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: The ease with which lake trout can be caught by anglers varies with the time of year and the water temperature.
answerChoices.B: Cold water is denser, and therefore heavier, than relatively warmer water.
answerChoices.C: Lake trout are found exclusively in deep temperate lakes.
answerChoices.D: Lake trout do not alter their feeding habits from one part of the year to another.
answerChoices.E: In deep temperate lakes that have ice residues on the surface, late-winter “turnover” has not yet occurred.

questions.stimulus:
Liang: Watching movies in which violence is portrayed as an appropriate way to resolve problems increases levels of aggression in viewers. Therefore, children’s access to these movies should be restricted.
Sarah: Watching a drama whose characters are violent allows the audience to vicariously experience the emotions associated with aggression and thus be purged of them. Hence, the access by mature audiences to such forms of entertainment should not be restricted.
questions.questionStem: The dialogue provides the most support for inferring that Liang and Sarah agree with each other that

answerChoices.A: people who experience an emotion vicariously are likely to purge themselves of that emotion
answerChoices.B: the members of a mature audience are unlikely to believe that violence is sometimes an appropriate way to resolve problems
answerChoices.C: if violence in certain movies causes violence in viewers, access to those movies should be restricted
answerChoices.D: the effects of dramatic depictions of violence on audiences are at least partially understood
answerChoices.E: children are more likely than adults to be attracted to dramas involving characters who behave violently

questions.stimulus: Politician: Of the candidates running, Thompson is the best person to lead this nation. For one thing, Thompson opposes higher taxes whereas the other candidates support them. Many would agree that anyone who opposes higher taxes will make a better leader than someone who supports them.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, casts the most doubt on the politician’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Opposing higher taxes is not a factor contributing to good leadership.
answerChoices.B: Being opposed to higher taxes is not a sufficient condition for good leadership.
answerChoices.C: Thompson has questionable opinions concerning important issues other than taxes.
answerChoices.D: All of the past leaders who supported higher taxes performed their jobs adequately.
answerChoices.E: All of the past leaders who supported higher taxes were hardworking.

questions.stimulus:
Patterson: Bone flutes dating to the Upper Paleolithic are the earliest evidence for music. Thus it is likely that music first arose during this period.
Garza: But the Upper Paleolithic is exceptional for the intensive use of bone, which typically survives well in archaeological contexts, unlike other materials commonly used for musical instruments, such as wood.
questions.questionStem: Garza responds to Patterson by doing which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: arguing that the body of evidence to which Patterson appeals is insufficient for Patterson’s purposes
answerChoices.B: offering evidence to challenge the truth of the premise of Patterson’s argument
answerChoices.C: presenting a counterexample to the general conclusion drawn in Patterson’s argument
answerChoices.D: presenting an argument analogous to Patterson’s argument to reveal a potential flaw in Patterson’s reasoning
answerChoices.E: using Patterson’s evidence to draw a conclusion inconsistent with the conclusion drawn in Patterson’s argument

questions.stimulus: No occupation should be subject to a licensing requirement unless incompetence in the performance of tasks normally carried out within that occupation poses a plausible threat to human health or safety.
questions.questionStem: The principle stated above, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning in which one of the following arguments?

answerChoices.A: Because some of the duties that police officers carry out have no connection to human health or safety, police officers should not be subject to a licensing requirement.
answerChoices.B: Because there are no realistic circumstances in which poor work by an interior designer poses a danger to human beings, interior designers should not be subject to a licensing requirement.
answerChoices.C: Because hospital administrators routinely make decisions that affect the health of hundreds of people, hospital administrators should be subject to a licensing requirement.
answerChoices.D: Because hair stylists regularly use substances that can pose a threat to human health if handled improperly, hair stylists should be subject to a licensing requirement.
answerChoices.E: Because tattoo artists who do not maintain strict sanitation pose a serious threat to human health, tattoo artists should be subject to a licensing requirement.

questions.stimulus: Most of the new cars that Regis Motors sold last year were purchased by residents of Blomenville. Regis Motors sold more new cars last year than it did in any previous year. Still, most new cars purchased by Blomenville residents last year were not purchased from Regis Motors.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

answerChoices.A: Regis Motors sold more new cars to residents of Blomenville last year than they had in any previous year.
answerChoices.B: The total number of new cars purchased by residents of Blomenville was greater last year than it was in any previous year.
answerChoices.C: A car retailer other than Regis Motors sold the most new cars to residents of Blomenville last year.
answerChoices.D: The number of new cars purchased last year by residents of Blomenville is greater than the number of new cars sold by Regis Motors.
answerChoices.E: Regis Motors’ share of the new car market in Blomenville last year increased over its share the year before.

questions.stimulus: Editorial: Teenagers tend to wake up around 8:00 A.M., the time when they stop releasing melatonin, and are sleepy if made to wake up earlier. Since sleepiness can impair driving ability, car accidents involving teenagers driving to school could be reduced if the school day began later than 8:00 A.M. Indeed, when the schedule for Granville’s high school was changed so that school began at 8:30 A.M. rather than earlier, the overall number of car accidents involving teenage drivers in Granville declined.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, provides the most support for the argument in the editorial?

answerChoices.A: Teenagers start releasing melatonin later at night and stop releasing it later in the morning than do young children.
answerChoices.B: Sleepy teenagers are tardy for school more frequently than teenagers who are well rested when the school day begins.
answerChoices.C: Teenagers who work at jobs during the day spend more time driving than do teenagers who attend high school during the day.
answerChoices.D: Many of the car accidents involving teenage drivers in Granville occurred in the evening rather than in the morning.
answerChoices.E: Car accidents involving teenage drivers rose in the region surrounding Granville during the time they declined in Granville.

questions.stimulus: Lucinda will soon be attending National University as an engineering major. At National University, most residents of Western Hall are engineering majors. Therefore, Lucinda will probably live in Western Hall.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments exhibits a flawed pattern of reasoning most similar to that exhibited by the argument above?

answerChoices.A: A major shopping mall is now being constructed in our city. Most cities with major shopping malls are regional economic hubs. Therefore, our city will probably become a regional economic hub.
answerChoices.B: Cities that are regional economic hubs generally experience tremendous economic growth at some point. Our city is a regional economic hub that has never experienced tremendous economic growth. Thus it will probably experience tremendous economic growth in the future.
answerChoices.C: Cities that are regional economic hubs always have excellent transportation systems. It is widely agreed that our city’s transportation system is inadequate. Therefore, our city will probably never become a regional economic hub.
answerChoices.D: A major shopping mall was built in our city ten years ago, and our city has experienced tremendous economic growth since then. Therefore, most cities in which major shopping malls are built will experience tremendous economic growth shortly afterward.
answerChoices.E: Most cities that are regional economic hubs contain major shopping malls. A major shopping mall is now being constructed in our city. Therefore, our city will probably become a regional economic hub.

questions.stimulus: Oceanographer: To substantially reduce the amount of carbon dioxide in Earth’s atmosphere, carbon dioxide should be captured and pumped deep into the oceans, where it would dissolve. The cool, dense water in ocean depths takes centuries to mix with the warmer water near the surface, so any carbon dioxide pumped deep into oceans would be trapped there for centuries.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption that the oceanographer’s argument requires?

answerChoices.A: Carbon dioxide will dissolve much more thoroughly if it is pumped into cold water than it will if it is pumped into warmer water.
answerChoices.B: Evaporation of warmer ocean water near an ocean’s surface does not generally release into the atmosphere large amounts of the carbon dioxide dissolved in the evaporating water.
answerChoices.C: Carbon dioxide dissolved in cool, dense water in ocean depths will not escape back into Earth’s atmosphere a long time before the water in which that carbon dioxide is dissolved mixes with warmer water near the surface.
answerChoices.D: It is the density of the water in the ocean depths that plays the main role in the trapping of the carbon dioxide.
answerChoices.E: Carbon dioxide should be pumped into ocean depths to reduce the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere only if the carbon dioxide pumped into ocean depths would be trapped there for hundreds of years.

questions.stimulus: Treat training consists of rewarding dogs with edible treats whenever they respond appropriately to commands. Most dogs will quickly learn what they need to do to receive a treat, so this appears to be an effective training method. However, most dogs who have been treat-trained will not obey commands unless they are shown a treat. Since you cannot always have treats on hand, you should instead use praise and verbal correction to train your dog.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: The more quickly a dog learns to respond to a stimulus, the more likely it is that the owner will continue to use that stimulus.
answerChoices.B: The more often a dog is given a stimulus, the more likely it is that the dog will obey its owner’s command even when the owner does not provide that stimulus.
answerChoices.C: A dog should be trained by the method that results in a high obedience rate in at least some circumstances.
answerChoices.D: A dog should be trained to respond to a stimulus that its owner can supply in all situations.
answerChoices.E: A dog should not be trained by a method that has not proven to be effective for any other dogs.

questions.stimulus: Archaeologist: For 2,000 years the ancient Sumerians depended on irrigation to sustain the agriculture that fed their civilization. But eventually irrigation built up in the soil toxic levels of the salts and other impurities left behind when water evaporates. When its soil became unable to support agriculture, Sumerian civilization collapsed. A similar fate is thus likely to befall modern civilizations that continue to rely heavily on irrigation for agriculture.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the archaeologist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Most modern civilizations could not feed themselves through agriculture without relying heavily on irrigation.
answerChoices.B: Factors unrelated to the use of irrigation would probably have caused Sumerian civilization to collapse sooner or later.
answerChoices.C: Many modern farmers use irrigation techniques that avoid the buildup of salts and other toxic impurities in the soil.
answerChoices.D: Many modern civilizations do not rely to any significant extent on irrigation for agriculture.
answerChoices.E: The soil of ancient Sumeria already contained some toxic salts and other impurities before the Sumerians started using irrigation for agriculture.

questions.stimulus: Researcher: Dinosaur fossils come in various forms, including mineralized bones and tracks in dried mud flats. However, mineralized dinosaur bones and dinosaur tracks in dried mud flats are rarely found together. This isn’t surprising, because creatures that scavenged dinosaur carcasses most likely frequented mud flats to find food.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most strengthen the researcher’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Dinosaur tracks are also found in locations other than mud flats.
answerChoices.B: Scavengers commonly drag a carcass away from the site where it was found.
answerChoices.C: Researchers have found more fossil dinosaur tracks than fossil dinosaur bones.
answerChoices.D: Dinosaur fossils other than mineralized bone or tracks in dried mud flats are quite common.
answerChoices.E: It takes longer for bone to mineralize than it takes for tracks to dry in mud flats.

questions.stimulus: Electric stovetop burners would cause fewer fires if their highest temperature were limited to 350°C (662°F), which provides more than enough heat for efficient and effective cooking. The lowest temperature at which cooking oil and most common fibers ignite is 387°C, and electric burners on high go well above 700°C.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the conclusion drawn in the argument?

answerChoices.A: Electric stovetop burners would cause fewer fires if their highest temperature were limited to 350°C.
answerChoices.B: A maximum temperature of 350°C provides more than enough heat for efficient and effective cooking.
answerChoices.C: The lowest ignition temperature for cooking oil and most common fibers is 387°C.
answerChoices.D: Electric burners on high go well above 700°C.
answerChoices.E: Electric stovetop burners cause fires because they go well above 700°C when set on high.

questions.stimulus: Jenkins maintains that the movie Firepower was not intended to provoke antisocial behavior, arguing that, on the contrary, it is in the interest of Firepower’s director to prevent such behavior. Yet Jenkins’s conclusion must be rejected, because the movie has clearly produced antisocial behavior among many of those who have seen it.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed in that it

answerChoices.A: rejects an argument on the grounds that it was offered by a person who was biased
answerChoices.B: concludes from a mere correlation between certain phenomena that those phenomena are causally related
