which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: In the wild, dolphins sometimes encounter strong electric fields.
answerChoices.B: Vibrissal crypts enable dolphins to sense electric fields.
answerChoices.C: Dolphins do not instinctually avoid electric fields, but they can be trained to do so.
answerChoices.D: Electric fields interfere with the normal functioning of dolphins’ vibrissal crypts.
answerChoices.E: Under normal circumstances, dolphins are unable to sense electric fields.

questions.stimulus:
In a study of honesty conducted in various retail stores,
customers who paid in cash and received change were
given an extra dollar with their change. Few people who
received an extra dollar returned it. So, among those who
received an extra dollar, most behaved dishonestly.
questions.questionStem:
The answer to which one of the following questions
would most help in evaluating the argument?

answerChoices.A: Did those who received an extra dollar count their change?
answerChoices.B: What percentage of the retail transactions studied were cash transactions?
answerChoices.C: Would the people who returned the extra dollar describe themselves as honest?
answerChoices.D: Did the people who returned the extra dollar suspect that it was given to them intentionally?
answerChoices.E: Does increasing the extra change to five dollars have an effect on people’s behavior?

questions.stimulus:
Dario: The government should continue to grant patents
for all new drug compounds. Patents promote
innovation by rewarding pharmaceutical
companies for undertaking the costly research
needed to develop new drugs. Cynthia: Promoting innovation is certainly important. For this reason, patents should be granted only
for truly innovative drugs, not for minor variants
of previously existing drugs. Since it is much
less expensive to tweak an existing drug than
to develop a wholly new one, pharmaceutical
companies tend to focus primarily on the cheaper
alternative.
questions.questionStem: Dario and Cynthia disagree over whether

answerChoices.A: pharmaceutical companies should be rewarded for pursuing innovation
answerChoices.B: patents should be granted for all drug compounds
answerChoices.C: developing truly innovative drugs is costly
answerChoices.D: pharmaceutical companies have an incentive to create minor variants of existing drugs
answerChoices.E: drug patents can promote innovation

questions.stimulus:
There are only two possible reasons that it would be
wrong to engage in an activity that causes pollution:
because pollution harms ecosystems, which are valuable
in themselves; or, ecosystems aside, because pollution
harms human populations. Either way, it would not be
wrong to perform mining operations on Mars. Although
doing so would pollute Mars, the small human presence
needed to run the mining operation would be completely
protected from the Martian environment and would suffer
no harm.
questions.questionStem:
The conclusion drawn above follows logically if which
one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Mining creates less pollution than many other human activities.
answerChoices.B: There are no ecosystems on Mars.
answerChoices.C: The economic benefits of mining on Mars would outweigh its costs.
answerChoices.D: It is technologically feasible to perform mining operations on Mars.
answerChoices.E: The more complex an ecosystem is, the more valuable it is.

questions.stimulus:
A person with low self-esteem will be treated
disrespectfully more often than will a person with high
self-esteem. Moreover, a recent experiment found that,
when people with low self-esteem and those with high
self-esteem are both confronted with the same treatment
by others, people with low self-esteem are much more
likely to feel that they have been treated disrespectfully.
Thus, _______.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most logically completes the
argument?

answerChoices.A: people with low self-esteem are usually right when they think they have been treated disrespectfully
answerChoices.B: being treated disrespectfully tends to cause a person to develop lower self-esteem
answerChoices.C: if an individual has been treated disrespectfully, it is probably because the individual was perceived to have low self-esteem
answerChoices.D: people with low self-esteem more frequently think that they are being treated disrespectfully than do people with high self-esteem
answerChoices.E: a person with low self-esteem will be more inclined to treat others disrespectfully than will a person with high self-esteem

questions.stimulus:
Watanabe: To protect the native kokanee salmon in the
lake, we must allow fishing of native trout. Each
mature trout eats about 250 mature kokanee
annually.
Lopez: The real problem is mysis shrimp, which were
originally introduced into the lake as food for
mature kokanee; but mysis eat plankton—young
kokanees’ food. The young kokanee are starving
to death. So eradicating the shrimp is preferable
to allowing trout fishing.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following principles, if valid, most
strongly supports Lopez’s conclusion?

answerChoices.A: Eliminating a non-native species from a habitat in which it threatens a native species is preferable to any other method of protecting the threatened native species.
answerChoices.B: When trying to protect the food supply of a particular species, it is best to encourage the method that will have the quickest results, all else being equal.
answerChoices.C: The number of species in a given habitat should not be reduced if at all possible.
answerChoices.D: No non-native species should be introduced into a habitat unless all the potential effects of that introduction have been considered.
answerChoices.E: When seeking to increase the population of a given species, it is most important that one preserve the members of the species who are in the prime reproductive stage of their lives.

questions.stimulus:
If rational-choice theory is correct, then people act only
in ways that they expect will benefit themselves. But
this means that rational-choice theory cannot be correct,
because plenty of examples exist of people acting in
ways that result in no personal benefit whatsoever.
questions.questionStem:
The argument above is most vulnerable to criticism on
the grounds that it

answerChoices.A: assumes as a premise the contention the argument purports to establish
answerChoices.B: concludes that a theory is false merely on the grounds that the evidence for it is hypothetical
answerChoices.C: takes for granted that people who are acting in ways that are personally beneficial expected that their actions would be personally beneficial
answerChoices.D: presumes, without justification, that examples of people acting in ways that are not personally beneficial greatly outnumber examples of people acting in ways that are personally beneficial
answerChoices.E: fails to consider that people acting in ways that result in no personal benefit may nonetheless have expected that acting in those ways would produce personal benefit

questions.stimulus:
Winds, the movement of gases in the atmosphere of a
planet, are ultimately due to differences in atmospheric
temperature. Winds on Earth are the result of heat from
the Sun, but the Sun is much too far away from Jupiter
to have any significant impact on the temperature of
Jupiter’s atmosphere. Nevertheless, on Jupiter winds
reach speeds many times those of winds found on Earth.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most helps to
explain the facts cited above about Jupiter and its winds?

answerChoices.A: Unlike Earth, Jupiter’s atmosphere is warmed by the planet’s internal heat source.
answerChoices.B: Jupiter’s atmosphere is composed of several gases that are found in Earth’s atmosphere only in trace amounts.
answerChoices.C: Gaseous planets such as Jupiter sometimes have stronger winds than do rocky planets such as Earth.
answerChoices.D: There are more planets that have winds stronger than Earth’s than there are planets that have winds weaker than Earth’s.
answerChoices.E: Planets even farther from the Sun than Jupiter are known to have atmospheric winds.

questions.stimulus:
Until recently it was widely believed that only a
limited number of species could reproduce through
parthenogenesis, reproduction by a female alone.
But lately, as interest in the topic has increased,
parthenogenesis has been found in a variety of
unexpected cases, including sharks and Komodo dragons.
So the number of species that can reproduce through
parthenogenesis must be increasing.
questions.questionStem:
The reasoning in the argument is most vulnerable to
criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: equates mere interest in a subject with real understanding of that subject
answerChoices.B: takes for granted that because one thing follows another, the one must have been caused by the other
answerChoices.C: takes ignorance of the occurrence of something as conclusive evidence that it did not occur
answerChoices.D: overlooks a crucial difference between two situations that the argument presents as being similar
answerChoices.E: presumes that because research is new it is, on that basis alone, better than older research

questions.stimulus:
Physician: Clinical psychologists who are not also
doctors with medical degrees should not be
allowed to prescribe psychiatric medications.
Training in clinical psychology includes at most a
few hundred hours of education in neuroscience,
physiology, and pharmacology. In contrast,
doctors with medical degrees must receive years
of training in these fields before they are allowed
to prescribe psychiatric medications.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following principles, if valid, would
most help to justify the reasoning in the physician’s
argument?

answerChoices.A: Clinical psychologists who are also doctors with medical degrees should be allowed to prescribe psychiatric medications.
answerChoices.B: Doctors without training in clinical psychology should not be allowed to prescribe psychiatric medications.
answerChoices.C: No one without years of training in neuroscience, physiology, and pharmacology should be allowed to prescribe psychiatric medications.
answerChoices.D: The training in neuroscience, physiology, and pharmacology required for a medical degree is sufficient for a doctor to be allowed to prescribe psychiatric medications.
answerChoices.E: Clinical psychologists should receive years of training in neuroscience, physiology, and pharmacology.

questions.stimulus:
Lobbyist: Those who claim that automobile exhaust
emissions are a risk to public health are mistaken. During the last century, as automobile exhaust
emissions increased, every relevant indicator of
public health improved dramatically rather than
deteriorated.
questions.questionStem:
The flaw in the lobbyist’s reasoning can most effectively
be demonstrated by noting that, by parallel reasoning,
we could conclude that

answerChoices.A: inspecting commercial airplanes for safety is unnecessary because the number of commercial airplane crashes has decreased over the last decade
answerChoices.B: smoking cigarettes is not bad for one’s health because not all cigarette smokers get smoking-related illnesses
answerChoices.C: using a cell phone while driving is not dangerous because the number of traffic accidents has decreased since the invention of the cell phone
answerChoices.D: skydiving is not dangerous because the number of injuries to skydivers has decreased in recent years
answerChoices.E: people with insurance do not need to lock their doors because if anything is stolen the insurance company will pay to replace it

questions.stimulus:
A recently discovered fossil, which is believed by some
to come from Archaeoraptor liaoningensis, a species of
dinosaur, can serve as evidence that birds evolved from
dinosaurs only if the entire fossil is from a single animal.
However, the fossil is a composite of bones collected
from various parts of the discovery site, so it does not
provide evidence that birds evolved from dinosaurs.
questions.questionStem:
The conclusion drawn in the argument follows logically
if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: The only paleontologists who believe that the entire fossil is from a single animal are those who were already convinced that birds evolved from dinosaurs.
answerChoices.B: If the fossil is a composite, then it has pieces of more than one animal.
answerChoices.C: There are other fossils that provide evidence that birds evolved from dinosaurs.
answerChoices.D: If the entire fossil is from a single animal, then it is a well-preserved specimen.
answerChoices.E: The fossil was stolen from the discovery site and sold by someone who cared much more about personal profit than about the accuracy of the fossil record.

questions.stimulus:
A new screening test has been developed for syndrome
Q. Research has shown that the test yields a positive
for syndrome Q whenever the person tested has that
syndrome. So, since Justine shows positive on the test,
she must have syndrome Q.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most accurately describes a
flaw in the reasoning in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It confuses the claim that a subject will test positive when the syndrome is present with the claim that any subject who tests positive has the syndrome.
answerChoices.B: It makes a general claim regarding the accuracy of the test for syndrome Q without providing adequate scientific justification for that claim.
answerChoices.C: It fails to adequately distinguish between a person’s not having syndrome Q and that person’s not testing positive for syndrome Q.
answerChoices.D: It confuses a claim about the accuracy of a test for syndrome Q in an arbitrary group of individuals with a similar claim about the accuracy of the test for a single individual.
answerChoices.E: It confuses the test’s having no reliable results for the presence of syndrome Q with its having no reliable results for the absence of syndrome Q.

questions.stimulus:
Music historian: In the past, radio stations would not play
rock songs that were more than three minutes
in length. Rock musicians claimed that such
commercial barriers limited their creativity, and
some critics argue that only since those barriers
have been lifted has rock music become artistic.
In fact, however, when these barriers were lifted,
the standards for song structures broke down and
the music became aimless, because the styles
from which rock derived were not well suited to
songs of extended length.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following is most strongly supported
by the music historian’s claims?

answerChoices.A: Rock music is not a good outlet for creative musicians who have a great many ideas.
answerChoices.B: Rock music must borrow from styles more conducive to songs of extended length if it is to become artistic.
answerChoices.C: Rock music requires more discipline than some other forms of music.
answerChoices.D: Rock music can sometimes benefit from the existence of commercial barriers rather than being harmed by them.
answerChoices.E: Rock music is best when it is made by musicians who do not think of themselves as being self-conscious artists.

questions.stimulus:
Some food historians conclude that recipes compiled by
an ancient Roman named Apicius are a reliable indicator
of how wealthy Romans prepared and spiced their
food. Since few other recipes from ancient Rome have
survived, this conclusion is far too hasty. After all, the
recipes of Apicius may have been highly atypical, just
like the recipes of many notable modern chefs.
questions.questionStem: The argument does which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: It rejects a view held by some food historians solely on the grounds that there is insufficient evidence to support it.
answerChoices.B: It offers support for a view held by some food historians by providing a modern analogue to that view.
answerChoices.C: It takes issue with the view of some food historians by providing a modern analogue that purportedly undercuts their view.
answerChoices.D: It uses a conclusion drawn by some food historians as the basis for a conclusion about a modern analogue.
answerChoices.E: It tries to bolster a conclusion about the similarity of historical times to modern times by comparing a conclusion drawn by some food historians to a modern analogue.

questions.stimulus:
Wood that is waterlogged or desiccated can be preserved
for a significant period, but, under normal conditions,
wood usually disintegrates within a century or two. For
this reason, archaeologists have been unable to find many
remains of early wheeled vehicles to examine. However,
archaeologists have found small ceramic models of
wheeled vehicles made at approximately the same time
as those early vehicles. Since these models have been
much less susceptible to disintegration than the vehicles
themselves, the main evidence regarding early wheeled
vehicles has come from these models.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following is most strongly supported
by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Most of the small ceramic models of early wheeled vehicles were made by the very individuals who made the vehicles upon which the ceramic vehicles were modeled.
answerChoices.B: Few, if any, small models of early wheeled vehicles were made of wood or other materials equally susceptible to disintegration under normal conditions.
answerChoices.C: The individuals who made the early wheeled vehicles were not always aware that wood can be preserved through waterlogging or desiccation.
answerChoices.D: An artifact will be more difficult for archaeologists to find if it has been preserved through waterlogging or desiccation than if it has been preserved under more normal conditions.
answerChoices.E: Of the early wheeled vehicles not preserved, more were made of wood than were made of materials no more susceptible to disintegration than are ceramic items.

questions.stimulus:
Traditional hatcheries raise fish in featureless
environments and subject them to dull routines, whereas
new, experimental hatcheries raise fish in visually
stimulating environments with varied routines. When
released into the wild, fish from the experimental
hatcheries are bolder than those from traditional
hatcheries in exploring new environments and trying new
types of food. Fish raised in the experimental hatcheries,
therefore, are more likely to survive after their release.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following is an assumption required by
the argument?

answerChoices.A: It is economically feasible for hatchery operators to expose fish to greater visual stimulation and to more varied routines.
answerChoices.B: The quality of the environments into which hatchery-raised fish are released has little effect on the fish’s survival rate.
answerChoices.C: Some fish raised in traditional hatcheries die because they are too timid in their foraging for food.
answerChoices.D: Hatchery-raised fish that are released into the wild need to eat many different types of food to survive.
answerChoices.E: Fish in the wild always live in visually stimulating environments.

questions.stimulus:
An analysis of the language in social media messages
posted via the Internet determined that, on average, the
use of words associated with positive moods is common
in the morning, decreases gradually to a low point
midafternoon, and then increases sharply throughout the
evening. This shows that a person’s mood typically starts
out happy in the morning, declines during the day, and
improves in the evening.
questions.questionStem:
The reasoning in the argument is most vulnerable to
criticism on the grounds that the argument overlooks the
possibility that

answerChoices.A: people’s overall moods are lowest at the beginning of the workweek and rise later, peaking on the weekend
answerChoices.B: many people who post social media messages use neither words associated with positive moods nor words associated with negative moods
answerChoices.C: the frequency in the use of words in social media is not necessarily indicative of the frequency of the use of those words in other forms of communication
answerChoices.D: the number of social media messages posted in the morning is not significantly different from the number posted in the evening
answerChoices.E: most of the social media messages posted in the evening are posted by people who rarely post such messages in the morning

questions.stimulus:
Economist: The wages of many of the lowest-paid
corporate employees in this country would be
protected from cuts by enacting a maximum
wage law that prohibits executives at any
corporation from earning more than, say, 50 times
what the corporation’s lowest-paid employees
in this country earn. Currently, some executives
try to increase corporate profits—and their own
salaries—by cutting the pay and benefits of their
corporations’ employees. A maximum wage law
would remove this incentive for these executives
to cut the wages of their lowest-paid employees.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following is an assumption the
economist’s argument requires?

answerChoices.A: All of the lowest-paid corporate employees in the economist’s country are employed at corporations at which the executives earn more than 50 times what the corporations’ lowest-paid employees in the economist’s country earn.
answerChoices.B: Some corporate executives who cut the pay of their corporations’ lowest-paid employees in the economist’s country in order to increase their own salaries already earn less than 50 times what their corporations’ lowest-paid employees in the economist’s country earn.
answerChoices.C: No corporate executives in the economist’s country would raise the wages of their corporations’ lowest-paid employees in the economist’s country unless such a maximum wage law linked executive wages to those of their corporations’ lowest-paid employees in the economist’s country.
answerChoices.D: If corporate executives could not increase their own salaries by cutting the pay and benefits of their corporations’ lowest-paid employees in the economist’s country, they would never change the wages of those employees.
answerChoices.E: If such a maximum wage law were enacted in the economist’s country, one or more corporate executives would not cut the pay and benefits of their corporations’ lowest-paid employees in the economist’s country.

questions.stimulus:
The level of triglycerides in the blood rises when
triglycerides are inadequately metabolized. Research
shows that patients with blood triglyceride levels above
1 milligram per milliliter are twice as prone to heart
attacks as others. Thus, it is likely that consuming large
amounts of fat, processed sugar, or alcohol, each known
to increase triglyceride levels in the blood, is a factor
causing heart disease.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the
argument?

answerChoices.A: People with a high-fat diet who engage in regular, vigorous physical activity are much less likely to develop heart disease than are sedentary people with a low-fat diet.
answerChoices.B: Triglyceride levels above 2 milligrams per milliliter increase the risk of some serious illnesses not related to heart disease.
answerChoices.C: Shortly after a person ceases to regularly consume alcohol and processed sugar, that person’s triglyceride levels drop dramatically.
answerChoices.D: Heart disease interferes with the body’s ability to metabolize triglycerides.
answerChoices.E: People who maintain strict regimens for their health tend to adopt low-fat diets and to avoid alcohol and processed sugar.

questions.stimulus:
In an experiment, some volunteers were assigned to
take aerobics classes and others to take weight-training
classes. After three months, each performed an arduous
mathematical calculation. Just after that challenge, the
measurable stress symptoms of the volunteers in the
aerobics classes were less than those of the volunteers in
the weight-training classes. This provides good evidence
that aerobic exercise helps the body handle psychological
stress.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following is an assumption the
argument requires?

answerChoices.A: Three months is enough time for the body to fully benefit from aerobic exercise.
answerChoices.B: The volunteers who were assigned to the aerobics classes did not also lift weights outside the classes.
answerChoices.C: On average, the volunteers who were assigned to the aerobics classes got more exercise in the months in which they took those classes than they had been getting before beginning the experiment.
answerChoices.D: On average, the volunteers assigned to the aerobics classes found it less difficult to perform the mathematical calculation than did the volunteers assigned to the weight-training classes.
answerChoices.E: On average, the volunteers assigned to the aerobics classes got a greater amount of aerobic exercise overall during the experiment, including any exercise outside the classes, than did the volunteers assigned to the weight-training classes.

questions.stimulus:
Insurers and doctors are well aware that the incidence
of lower-back injuries among office workers who spend
long hours sitting is higher than that among people who
regularly do physical work of a type known to place
heavy stresses on the lower back. This shows that office
equipment and furniture are not properly designed to
promote workers’ health.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most undermines the
reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: When they are at home, laborers and office workers tend to spend similar amounts of time sitting.
answerChoices.B: Insurance companies tend to dislike selling policies to companies whose workers often claim to have back pain.
answerChoices.C: People who regularly do physical work of a type known to place heavy stress on the lower back are encouraged to use techniques that reduce the degree of stress involved.
answerChoices.D: Most of the lower-back injuries that office workers suffer occur while they are on the job.
answerChoices.E: Consistent physical exercise is one of the most effective ways to prevent or recover from lower-back injuries.

questions.stimulus:
Researchers have found that some unprotected areas
outside of a national park that was designed to protect
birds have substantially higher numbers of certain bird
species than comparable areas inside the park.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most helps to
explain the researchers’ finding?

answerChoices.A: Moose are much more prevalent inside the park, where hunting is prohibited, than outside the park, and moose eat much of the food that the birds need to survive.
answerChoices.B: The researchers also found that some unprotected areas outside of the park have substantially higher numbers of certain reptile species than comparable areas inside the park.
answerChoices.C: Researchers tagged a large number of birds inside the park; three months later some of these birds were recaptured outside the park.
answerChoices.D: Both inside the park and just outside of it, there are riverside areas containing willows and other waterside growth that the bird species thrive on.
answerChoices.E: The park was designed to protect endangered bird species, but some of the bird species that are present in higher numbers in the unprotected areas are also endangered.

questions.stimulus:
A recent poll of a large number of households found that
47 percent of those with a cat had at least one person
with a university degree, while 38 percent of households
with a dog had at least one person with a university
degree. Clearly, people who hold university degrees are
more likely to live in a household with a cat than one
with a dog.
questions.questionStem:
The reasoning in the argument is flawed in that the
argument

answerChoices.A: ignores the possibility that a significant number of households might have both a cat and a dog
answerChoices.B: takes for granted that there are not significantly more households with a dog than ones with a cat
answerChoices.C: fails to consider how many of the households have at least one person without a university degree
answerChoices.D: fails to consider to what extent people with university degrees participate in decisions about whether their households have a cat or dog
answerChoices.E: ignores the possibility that two things can be correlated without being causally connected

questions.stimulus:
Keeler wanted the institute to receive bad publicity.
He and Greene were the only ones in a position to tell
the press about the institute’s potentially embarrassing
affiliations, but Greene had no reason to do so. Therefore,
it must have been Keeler who notified the press.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following arguments is most closely
parallel in its reasoning to the argument above?

answerChoices.A: The only people who had any reason to write the anonymous letter were Johnson and Ringwold. Johnson and Ringwold both deny doing so. Ringwold, however, admits that she has written anonymous letters in the past. Thus, it must have been Ringwold who wrote the letter.
answerChoices.B: Carter and Whitequill were the only ones who had any motive to bribe the public official. But Whitequill would have been too fearful that the bribery might somehow be made public. Carter, therefore, must be the person who bribed the public official.
answerChoices.C: Other than Helms and Lapinski, no one had access to the equipment on Thursday, the day it was tampered with. Thus, since Helms had reason to tamper with the equipment and Lapinski did not, it must have been Helms who did it.
answerChoices.D: When the bridge was designed, Fleming and Solano were the only ones capable of creating such a design. Fleming, however, had a strong reason to take credit for the design if it were his. Thus, since no one took credit for the design, it must have been the work of Solano.
answerChoices.E: Cutter and Rengo are the only serious candidates for designing the new monument. Rengo has designed several beautiful monuments and has connections to the selection committee. Therefore, it will probably be Rengo who is awarded the job of designing the monument.

questions.stimulus:
Joe: All vampire stories are based on an absurd set of
premises. Since, according to such stories, every
victim of a vampire becomes a vampire, and
vampires have existed since ancient times and are
immortal, vampires would by now have almost
completely eliminated their prey. Maria: In most of the vampire stories I am familiar with,
vampires turn only a few of their victims into
vampires. The rest are permanently dead.
questions.questionStem:
Joe and Maria disagree over the truth of which one of
the following?

answerChoices.A: Vampires are always depicted in vampire stories as immortal.
answerChoices.B: Vampires are always depicted in vampire stories as having existed since ancient times.
answerChoices.C: No vampire stories are incoherent.
answerChoices.D: No vampire stories depict the vampire population as being very large.
answerChoices.E: In all vampire stories, every victim of a vampire becomes a vampire.

questions.stimulus:
A company decided to scan all of its salespersons’
important work that existed only in paper form into a
central computer database that could be easily accessed
using portable computers, thereby saving salespersons
the effort of lugging their paper files all over the country.
The project was a dismal failure, however; salespersons
rarely accessed the database and continued to rely on
many paper files, which they had refused to turn over to
the staff responsible for creating the database.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most helps to
account for the failure described above?

answerChoices.A: Some of the salespersons gave huge paper files to the staff responsible for creating the database while other salespersons gave them much smaller files.
answerChoices.B: Most of the salespersons already had portable computers before the new database was created.
answerChoices.C: The papers that the salespersons found most important all contained personal information about employees of client companies, which the salespersons did not want in a central database.
answerChoices.D: All of the salespersons were required to attend a series of training sessions for the new database software even though many of them found the software easy to use even without training.
answerChoices.E: The number of staff required to create the database turned out to be larger than anticipated, and the company had to pay overtime wages to some of them.

questions.stimulus:
Politician: The legal right to free speech does not
protect all speech. For example, it is illegal
to shout “Fire!” in a crowded mall if the
only intent is to play a practical joke; the
government may ban publication of information
about military operations and the identity of
undercover agents; and extortion threats and
conspiratorial agreements are also criminal acts. The criminalization of these forms of speech is
justified, since, although they are very different
from each other, they are all likely to lead directly
to serious harm.
questions.questionStem: In the statements above, the politician argues that

answerChoices.A: it is legitimate to prohibit some forms of speech on the grounds that they are likely to lead directly to serious harm
answerChoices.B: a form of speech can be restricted only if it is certain that it would lead directly to serious harm
answerChoices.C: in all but a few cases, restricting speech eventually leads directly to serious harm
answerChoices.D: any form of speech may, one way or another, lead directly to serious harm
answerChoices.E: all but one of several possible reasons for restricting freedom of speech are unjustified

questions.stimulus:
Art critic: Nowadays, museum visitors seldom pause to
look at a work of art for even a full minute. They
look, perhaps take a snapshot, and move on. This
tells us something about how our relationship to
art has changed over time. People have become
less willing to engage with works of art than they
once were.
questions.questionStem: The art critic’s argument depends on the assumption that

answerChoices.A: museum visitors today generally look at more pieces of art during each museum visit than museum visitors looked at in the past
answerChoices.B: the ease with which museum visitors can take snapshots of art contributes to the speed with which they move through art museums
answerChoices.C: visitors would enjoy their museum experiences more if they took more time with individual works of art
answerChoices.D: museum visitors who take snapshots of works of art rarely look at the pictures afterward
answerChoices.E: the amount of time spent looking at a work of art is a reliable measure of engagement with that work

questions.stimulus:
Heavy tapestry fabrics are appropriate only for use in
applications that will not need to be laundered frequently.
These applications do not include any types of clothing—
such as skirts or even jackets—but instead include
swags and balloon valances, which are types of window
treatments.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following statements is most supported
by the information above?

answerChoices.A: If a fabric is not a heavy tapestry fabric, then it is not appropriate for use in swags.
answerChoices.B: Heavy tapestry fabrics should not be used unless swags or balloon valances are being made.
answerChoices.C: If heavy tapestry fabrics are appropriate for a particular application, then that application must be a window treatment.
answerChoices.D: If a fabric is appropriate for use in a skirt or jacket, then that fabric is not a heavy tapestry fabric.
answerChoices.E: Heavy tapestry fabrics are sometimes appropriate for use in types of clothing other than skirts and jackets.

questions.stimulus:
The construction of new apartments in Brewsterville
increased the supply of available housing there.
Ordinarily, increasing the supply of available housing
leads to lower rents for existing apartments. But in
Brewsterville, rents for existing apartments rose.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most helps to
explain the discrepancy described above?

answerChoices.A: Fewer new apartments were constructed than originally planned.
answerChoices.B: The new apartments were much more desirable than the existing apartments.
answerChoices.C: Rents in some areas close to Brewsterville dropped as a result of the construction of the new apartments.
answerChoices.D: A sizeable number of people moved out of the existing apartments while the new apartments were being constructed.
answerChoices.E: The new apartments were constructed at the outset of a trend of increasing numbers of people seeking residence in Brewsterville.

questions.stimulus:
Politicians often advocate increased overall economic
productivity while ignoring its drawbacks. For example,
attempting to increase the productivity of a corporation
means attempting to increase its profitability, which
typically leads to a reduction in the number of workers
employed by that corporation. Thus, attempting to
increase productivity in the economy as a whole may
benefit business owners, but will increase the number of
unemployed workers.
questions.questionStem:
The reasoning in the argument is most vulnerable to
criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: presumes, without providing justification, that increased unemployment is sufficient reason to abandon increased productivity as an economic goal
answerChoices.B: fails to justify its presumption that attempting to increase productivity in the economy as a whole would produce results similar to those produced by attempting to increase productivity in a single corporation
answerChoices.C: unfairly criticizes politicians in general on the basis of the actions of a few who are unwilling to consider the drawbacks of attempting to increase productivity
answerChoices.D: fails to justify its presumption that attempting to increase productivity in the economy as a whole is always more important than the interests of workers or business owners
answerChoices.E: fails to address all potential drawbacks and benefits of attempting to increase productivity at a single corporation

questions.stimulus:
A good movie reviewer should be able to give favorable
reviews of movies that are not to his or her taste. Because
movie reviewers have seen so many movies, their tastes
are very different from and usually better informed than
those of most moviegoers. Yet the function of movie
reviewers, as opposed to film critics, is to help people
determine which movies they might enjoy seeing, not to
help them better appreciate movies.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most accurately expresses
the overall conclusion drawn in the argument?

answerChoices.A: Movie reviewers’ tastes in movies are very different from and usually better informed than those of most moviegoers.
answerChoices.B: If a movie reviewer is good, he or she should be able to give favorable reviews of movies that are not to his or her taste.
answerChoices.C: The function of a movie reviewer is different from that of a film critic.
answerChoices.D: Movie reviewers see many more movies than most moviegoers see.
answerChoices.E: The role of movie reviewers is to help people determine which movies they might enjoy seeing, not to help people better appreciate movies.

questions.stimulus:
The brain area that enables one to distinguish the
different sounds made by a piano tends to be larger in a
highly skilled musician than in someone who has rarely,
if ever, played a musical instrument. This shows that
practicing on, and playing, a musical instrument actually
alters brain structure.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most accurately describes a
flaw in the argument?

answerChoices.A: The argument presumes, without providing justification, that what is true about the brain structures of highly skilled pianists is also true of the brain structures of other highly skilled musicians.
answerChoices.B: The argument fails to address the possibility that people who become highly skilled musicians do so, in part, because of the size of a certain area of their brains.
answerChoices.C: The argument draws a conclusion about a broad range of phenomena from evidence concerning a much narrower range of phenomena.
answerChoices.D: The argument fails to address the possibility that a certain area of the brain is smaller in people who have listened to a lot of music but who have never learned to play a musical instrument than it is in people who have learned to play a musical instrument.
answerChoices.E: The argument presumes, without providing justification, that highly skilled musicians practice more than other musicians.

questions.stimulus:
Researcher: Overhearing only one side of a cell-phone
conversation diverts listeners’ attention from
whatever they are doing. Hearing only part of a
conversation leaves listeners constantly trying
to guess what the unheard talker has just said. Listeners’ attention is also diverted because cell-
phone talkers speak abnormally loudly.
questions.questionStem:
The researcher’s statements, if true, most strongly
support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: The risk that a driver will cause an accident is increased when the driver is talking on a cell phone.
answerChoices.B: When a driver hears a passenger in the driver’s vehicle talking on a cell phone, that detracts from the driver’s performance.
answerChoices.C: Overhearing one side of a conversation on a traditional telephone does not divert listeners’ attention from tasks at hand.
answerChoices.D: People who overhear one side of a cell-phone conversation inevitably lose track of their thoughts.
answerChoices.E: Conversing on a cell phone requires making more guesses about what one’s conversational partner means than other forms of conversation do.

questions.stimulus:
A new treatment for muscle pain that looked very
promising was tested in three separate studies. Although
the results were positive, it turned out that all three
studies had critical methodological flaws. So the
treatment is probably not actually effective.
questions.questionStem:
The flawed nature of the argument above can most
effectively be demonstrated by noting that, by parallel
reasoning, we could conclude that

answerChoices.A: since the judges in a baking contest did not have uniform criteria for selecting a winner, the cake that won is probably a bad one
answerChoices.B: since some people who fish seldom catch any fish, they probably have some reason for fishing other than catching fish
answerChoices.C: since some foods have very little nutritional value, people who include those foods in their diets are probably malnourished
answerChoices.D: since all scarves are at least somewhat decorative, it is likely that when scarves were first adopted, they were purely decorative
answerChoices.E: since all members of the city council have a financial stake in the city’s development, any development proposal they make is likely to be motivated purely by self-interest

questions.stimulus:
If future improvements to computer simulations of
automobile crashes enable computers to provide as much
reliable information about the effectiveness of automobile
safety features as is provided by actual test crashes, then
manufacturers will use far fewer actual test crashes. For
the costs of designing and running computer simulations
are much lower than those of actual test crashes.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most strongly
supports the argument?

answerChoices.A: Apart from information about safety features, actual test crashes provide very little information of importance to automobile manufacturers.
answerChoices.B: It is highly likely that within the next 20 years computer simulations of automobile crashes will be able to provide a greater amount of reliable information about the effectiveness of automobile safety features than can be provided by actual test crashes.
answerChoices.C: If computer simulations will soon be able to provide more information about the effectiveness of automobile safety features, automobile manufacturers will soon be able to produce safer cars.
answerChoices.D: The cost per automobile of testing and designing safety features is decreasing and will continue to decrease for the foreseeable future.
answerChoices.E: For years, the aviation industry has been successfully using computer simulations of airplane crashes to test the effectiveness of safety features of airplane designs.

questions.stimulus:
Legislator: My colleague says we should reject this act
because it would deter investment. But because
in the past she voted for legislation that inhibited
investment, this surely is not the real reason she
opposes the act. Since she has not revealed her
real reason, it must not be very persuasive. So we
should vote to approve the act.
questions.questionStem:
The reasoning in the legislator’s argument is most
vulnerable to the criticism that the argument

answerChoices.A: treats a personal character trait as if it were evidence of the professional viewpoint of the person having that trait
answerChoices.B: fails to address the grounds on which the colleague claims the act should be rejected
answerChoices.C: presumes, without providing justification, that the colleague’s opposition to the act is the minority position in the legislature
answerChoices.D: presumes, without providing justification, that voters will oppose legislation that deters investment
answerChoices.E: fails to consider that the colleague’s opposition to the act may be a response to constituents’ wishes

questions.stimulus:
A new computer system will not significantly increase
an organization’s efficiency unless the computer system
requires the organization’s employees to adopt new,
more productive ways of working. The Ministry of
Transportation is having a new computer system custom
built to fit the ministry’s existing ways of working, so
_______.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most logically completes the
argument?

answerChoices.A: the new computer system will not increase the efficiency of the Ministry of Transportation to any appreciable degree
answerChoices.B: it is likely that the new computer system will not function correctly when it is first installed
answerChoices.C: the leaders of the Ministry of Transportation must not be concerned with the productivity of the ministry’s employees
answerChoices.D: the new computer system will be worthwhile if it automates many processes that are currently performed manually
answerChoices.E: it will be easy for employees of the Ministry of Transportation to learn to use the new computer system

questions.stimulus:
Columnist: Many car manufacturers trumpet their cars’
fuel economy under normal driving conditions. For all three of the cars I have owned, I have
been unable to get even close to the fuel economy
that manufacturers advertise for cars of those
makes. So manufacturers probably inflate those
numbers.
questions.questionStem:
The reasoning in the columnist’s argument is most
vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: draws a conclusion on the basis of a sample that is too small
answerChoices.B: presumes, without providing justification, that driving conditions are the same in every geographical region
answerChoices.C: overlooks the possibility that the source of a cited claim may be biased and hence unreliable
answerChoices.D: presumes, without providing justification, that car manufacturers knowingly market cars that fail to meet minimum fuel efficiency standards
answerChoices.E: uses the term “fuel economy” in two different senses

questions.stimulus:
Tenants who do not have to pay their own electricity bills
do not have a financial incentive to conserve electricity.
Thus, if more landlords install individual electricity
meters on tenant dwellings so that tenants can be billed
for their own use, energy will be conserved as a result.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the
argument?

answerChoices.A: Tenants who do not have to pay their own electricity bills generally must compensate by paying more rent.
answerChoices.B: Many initiatives have been implemented to educate people about how much money they can save through energy conservation.
answerChoices.C: Landlords who pay for their tenants’ electricity have a strong incentive to make sure that the appliances they provide for their tenants are energy efficient.
answerChoices.D: Some tenant dwellings can only support individual electricity meters if the dwellings are rewired, which would be prohibitively expensive.
answerChoices.E: Some people conserve energy for reasons that are not related to cost savings.

questions.stimulus:
The position that punishment should be proportional to
how serious the offense is but that repeat offenders should
receive harsher punishments than first-time offenders is
unsustainable. It implies that considerations as remote
as what an offender did years ago are relevant to the
seriousness of an offense. If such remote considerations
were relevant, almost every other consideration would be
too. But this would make determining the seriousness of
an offense so difficult that it would be impossible to apply
the proportionality principle.
questions.questionStem:
The statement that considerations as remote as what an
offender did years ago are relevant to the seriousness of
an offense plays which one of the following roles in the
argument?

answerChoices.A: It is a statement the argument provides grounds to accept and from which the overall conclusion is inferred.
answerChoices.B: It is a statement inferred from a position the argument seeks to defend.
answerChoices.C: It is the overall conclusion in favor of which the argument offers evidence.
answerChoices.D: It is an allegedly untenable consequence of a view rejected in the argument’s overall conclusion.
answerChoices.E: It is a premise offered in support of an intermediate conclusion of the argument.

questions.stimulus:
Blogger: Traditionally, newspapers have taken objectivity
to be an essential of good journalism. However,
today’s newer media are more inclined to try
to create a stir with openly partisan reporting.
This contrast in journalistic standards is best
understood in terms of differing business
strategies. The newer media outlets need
to differentiate themselves in a crowded
marketplace. The standard of objectivity
developed primarily among newspapers with no
serious rivals, so the most important objective
was to avoid offending potential readers.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following is an assumption required by
the blogger’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Journalists at traditional newspapers are just as partisan as journalists who work for newer media outlets.
answerChoices.B: People prefer objective reporting to partisan reporting that merely reinforces their own partisan leanings.
answerChoices.C: The newer media outlets are increasing in popularity at the expense of traditional newspapers.
answerChoices.D: Newspapers have regarded objective reporting as less likely to offend people than openly partisan reporting.
answerChoices.E: There can be no basis for taking objectivity to be an essential journalistic standard.

questions.stimulus:
Any government practice that might facilitate the abuse
of power should not be undertaken except in cases in
which there is a compelling reason to do so. The keeping
of government secrets is one such practice. Though
government officials are sometimes justified in keeping
secrets, too often they keep secrets for insubstantial
reasons, and in so doing they wind up enabling abuses
of power. When government officials conceal from the
public the very fact that they are keeping a secret, this
practice opens up even greater opportunity for abuse.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following can be properly inferred
from the statements above?

answerChoices.A: In most cases in which government officials conceal information from the public, they are not justified in doing so.
answerChoices.B: In those cases in which government officials have a compelling reason to keep a secret, doing so does not facilitate an abuse of power.
answerChoices.C: A government official who justifiably keeps a secret should not conceal its existence without having a compelling reason to do so.
answerChoices.D: Government officials who conceal information without a compelling reason are thereby guilty of an abuse of power.
answerChoices.E: Government officials should keep information secret only if doing so does not make it easier for those officials to abuse their power.

questions.stimulus:
According to a theory embraced by some contemporary
musicians, music is simply a series of sounds, bereft of
meaning. But these musicians, because they understand
that their theory is radically nonconformist, encourage
audience acceptance by prefacing their performances
with explanations of their intentions. Thus, even their
own music fails to conform to their theory.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if assumed, enables the
argument’s conclusion to be properly drawn?

answerChoices.A: The human ability to think symbolically and to invest anything with meaning makes it very difficult to create music that has no meaning.
answerChoices.B: It will be possible for musicians to create music that means nothing only when listeners are able to accept such a theory of music.
answerChoices.C: The fact that music is distinguishable from a random series of sounds only when it has meaning makes music with meaning more appealing to audiences than music without meaning.
answerChoices.D: Music that opposes current popular conceptions of music is less likely to be enjoyed by audiences than is music that accords with such conceptions.
answerChoices.E: Musicians whose music has no meaning do not preface their performances with explanations of their intentions.

questions.stimulus:
Evolution does not always optimize survival of an
organism. Male moose evolved giant antlers as a way
of fighting other males for mates, giving those with the
largest antlers an evolutionary advantage. But those
antlers also make it harder to escape predators, since they
can easily get tangled in trees. All male moose would be
better off with antlers half the current size: they would all
be less vulnerable to predators, and those with the largest
antlers would maintain their relative advantage.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following is a technique of reasoning
used in the argument?

answerChoices.A: citing an example to cast doubt on a competing argument
answerChoices.B: employing an analogy in order to dispute a generalization
answerChoices.C: challenging a general claim by presenting a counterexample
answerChoices.D: disputing the relevance of an example thought to support an opposing view
answerChoices.E: undermining a claim by showing that it is self-contradictory

questions.stimulus:
Biologist: When bacteria of a particular species are
placed in a test tube that has different areas lit
with different colors of light, the bacteria move
only into the areas lit with a particular shade of
red. The bacteria contain chlorophyll, a chemical
that allows them to produce energy more
effectively from this color of light than from any
other. This suggests that the bacteria detect this
color of light by monitoring how much energy
their chlorophyll is producing.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the
biologist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: If the chlorophyll is removed from the bacteria, but the bacteria are otherwise unharmed, they no longer show any tendency to move into the areas lit with the particular shade of red.
answerChoices.B: The bacteria show little tendency to move into areas containing light in colors other than the particular shade of red, even if their chlorophyll can produce some energy from light in those colors.
answerChoices.C: The areas of the test tube lit with the particular shade of red favored by the bacteria are no warmer, on average, than areas lit with other colors.
answerChoices.D: The bacteria show no tendency to move into areas lit with blue even when those areas are lit so brightly that the bacteria’s chlorophyll produces as much energy in those areas as it does in the red areas.
answerChoices.E: There are species of bacteria that do not contain chlorophyll but do move into areas lit with particular colors when placed in a test tube lit with different colors in different places.

questions.stimulus:
If a piece of legislation is the result of negotiation and
compromise between competing interest groups, it will
not satisfy any of those groups. So, we can see that the
recently enacted trade agreement represents a series of
compromises among the various interest groups that are
concerned with it, because all of those groups are clearly
unhappy with it.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most accurately describes a
logical flaw in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It draws a conclusion that is merely a disguised restatement of one of its premises.
answerChoices.B: It concludes that a condition is necessary for a certain result merely from the claim that the condition leads to that result.
answerChoices.C: It relies on understanding a key term in a quite different way in the conclusion from the way that term is understood in the premises.
answerChoices.D: It takes for granted that no piece of legislation can ever satisfy all competing interest groups.
answerChoices.E: It bases a conclusion about a particular case on a general principle that concerns a different kind of case.

questions.stimulus:
After a nuclear power plant accident, researchers found
radioactive isotopes of iodine, tellurium, and cesium—
but no heavy isotopes—in the atmosphere downwind. This material came either from spent fuel rods or from
the plant’s core. Spent fuel rods never contain significant
quantities of tellurium isotopes. Radioactive material
ejected into the atmosphere directly from the core would
include heavy isotopes. After the accident, steam, which
may have been in contact with the core, was released
from the plant. The core contains iodine, tellurium, and
cesium isotopes, which are easily dissolved by steam.
questions.questionStem:
Of the following statements, which one is most strongly
supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Radioactive material ejected into the environment directly from a nuclear power plant’s core would not include tellurium isotopes.
answerChoices.B: The radioactive material detected by the researchers was carried into the atmosphere by the steam that was released from the plant.
answerChoices.C: The nuclear power plant’s spent fuel rods were not damaged.
answerChoices.D: The researchers found some radioactive material from spent fuel rods as well as some material that was ejected into the atmosphere directly from the plant’s core.
answerChoices.E: Spent fuel rods do not contain heavy isotopes in significant quantities.

questions.stimulus:
If ecology and the physical sciences were evaluated by
the same criteria, ecology would fail to be a successful
science because it cannot be captured by a set of simple
laws. But ecology is a successful science, although of a
different sort from the physical sciences. Therefore, it
clearly is not being evaluated by means of the criteria
used to evaluate the physical sciences.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following arguments is most similar in
its reasoning to the argument above?

answerChoices.A: If sales taxes are increased, then either the price of woodchips will go up and the consumer will have to pay more for them, or the woodchip industry will disappear. But the market cannot bear an increase in the price of woodchips, so the woodchip industry will disappear.
answerChoices.B: If this gallery could borrow some of Matisse’s early works, then, together with its own permanent collection of Matisse, the gallery could have the largest exhibition of Matisse ever. But there is no demand for larger exhibitions of Matisse’s work. Therefore, no gallery will be inclined to lend their early Matisses to this gallery.
answerChoices.C: If cars of the future are made of lighter and stronger materials, then the number of fatalities due to driving accidents will be drastically reduced. It is obvious that cars will be made of lighter and stronger materials in the future. Therefore, the number of fatalities due to driving accidents will be drastically reduced.
answerChoices.D: If physicists attempted research in the social sciences, they would probably be as successful in those areas as researchers who restrict their concentration to the social sciences. However, physicists rarely attempt social science research. Therefore, physicists are not among the most successful researchers in the social sciences.
answerChoices.E: If any economic theory were an adequate description of the principles according to which economies operate, then it would be possible to make accurate economic forecasts. But accurate economic forecasts cannot be made. Therefore, no economic theory is an adequate description of the principles according to which economies operate.

questions.stimulus: Researcher: During the rainy season, bonobos (an ape species closely related to chimpanzees) frequently swallow whole the rough-surfaced leaves of the shrub Manniophyton fulvum. These leaves are likely ingested because of their medicinal properties, since ingestion of these leaves facilitates the elimination of gastrointestinal worms.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the researcher’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Bonobos rarely swallow whole leaves of any plants other than M. fulvum.
answerChoices.B: Chimpanzees have also been observed to swallow rough-surfaced leaves whole during the rainy season.
answerChoices.C: Of the rough-leaved plants available to bonobos, M. fulvum shrubs are the most common.
answerChoices.D: The leaves of M. fulvum are easier to swallow whole when they are wet.
answerChoices.E: The rainy season is the time when bonobos are most likely to be infected with gastrointestinal worms.

questions.stimulus: Policy analyst: Those concerned with safeguarding public health by reducing the risk of traffic fatalities typically focus their efforts on automotive safety measures such as increasing seat belt use, reducing distracted driving, and improving automotive technology. But what would contribute the most to safeguarding public health is a reduction in total miles traveled on our roads. The fact is that traveling by car is itself a major risk factor.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the overall conclusion drawn in the policy analyst’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Public health can be safeguarded through reducing traffic fatalities.
answerChoices.B: Those concerned with safeguarding public health should focus their efforts on reducing traffic fatalities.
answerChoices.C: Increasing seat belt use, reducing distracted driving, and improving automotive technology all safeguard public health.
answerChoices.D: A reduction in total miles traveled would contribute more to safeguarding public health than would any automotive safety measure.
answerChoices.E: Traveling by car is itself a major risk factor for traffic fatalities.

questions.stimulus: Letter to the Editor: The arts section of this paper shows a lamentable bias toward movies and against local theatrical productions. Over the last year alone, the paper has published over five times as many movie reviews as reviews of live plays.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Some newspapers do not publish any reviews of live plays.
answerChoices.B: The number of movies released last year was significantly greater than the number of live plays performed locally.
answerChoices.C: The newspaper has five movie critics, but only one theater critic.
answerChoices.D: The newspaper does not have the space in the arts section to publish a review of every movie that is released or every live play that is locally performed.
answerChoices.E: The newspaper published more reviews of live plays in the last year than it did two years ago.

questions.stimulus: Archaeologist: Our university museum possesses several ancient artifacts whose ownership is in dispute. Although the museum has documentation showing that the items were obtained legally, there is an overriding principle that any important ancient artifact belongs by rights to the nation on whose territory it was discovered. Given that an institution is obliged to honor those rights, our museum should return the artifacts.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the overall conclusion of the archaeologist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The university museum should return the ancient artifacts in dispute.
answerChoices.B: Any important ancient artifact belongs by rights to the nation on whose territory it was discovered.
answerChoices.C: The ancient artifacts whose ownership is in dispute were obtained legally by the university museum.
answerChoices.D: The university museum is in possession of several artifacts whose ownership is in dispute.
answerChoices.E: There is an overriding principle that any important ancient artifact belongs by rights to the nation on whose territory it was discovered.

questions.stimulus: Many fictional works have characters who are supposedly precognitive—that is, able to accurately perceive future events. But a perception of a future event is accurate only if that event comes to pass. Thus, the plots of these works often show that the characters are not truly precognitive, since some of the future events the characters perceive do not in fact come to pass.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: A character is truly precognitive only if all of that character’s perceptions of future events are accurate.
answerChoices.B: It is impossible for someone to perceive future events accurately with absolute consistency.
answerChoices.C: The plots of fictional works that portray characters as precognitive often do not specify whether the future events those characters perceive come to pass.
answerChoices.D: When fictional works portray characters as precognitive, those characters’ perceptions of future events are generally central to the plots of those works.
answerChoices.E: No work of fiction has portrayed a truly precognitive character.

questions.stimulus: Economist: There have been large declines in employment around the globe, so it’s not surprising that the number of workers injured on the job has decreased. What is surprising, however, is that the percentage of workers injured on the job has also decreased.
questions.questionStem: Each of the following, if true, helps to explain the surprising result mentioned by the economist except:

answerChoices.A: Overall, people who are employed are working fewer hours each day.
answerChoices.B: A decrease in the demand for products has reduced the pressure on workers to meet production quotas and deadlines.
answerChoices.C: Some of the most dangerous industries have had especially big declines in employment.
answerChoices.D: There has been a general decline in the resources devoted to workplace safety.
answerChoices.E: Inexperienced workers have lost their jobs at higher rates than experienced ones.

questions.stimulus: Editorial: Animated films appropriate for children are those that are innocently whimsical, mischievous perhaps, but not threatening. Since new animated films aimed at adults have dark themes such as poverty and despair, such films cannot be considered appropriate for children.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption that would allow the conclusion to be properly drawn?

answerChoices.A: Films that are whimsical and mischievous are not threatening.
answerChoices.B: Films that are appropriate for adults are seldom appropriate for children.
answerChoices.C: Films that have dark themes are threatening.
answerChoices.D: Children enjoy films only if the films include animation.
answerChoices.E: Children do not attend to some details in films aimed at adults.

questions.stimulus: Monarch butterflies must contend with single-celled parasites that can cause deformities that interfere with their flight. In populations of monarch butterflies that have not migrated, as many as 95 percent are heavily infected by the parasites, while less than 15 percent of those in migrating populations are infected. This shows that migrating allows monarch butterflies to avoid these parasites.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed in that the argument overlooks the possibility that

answerChoices.A: monarch butterflies are unable to detect which areas are free from parasites
answerChoices.B: long migrations are no better protection from parasites than are short migrations
answerChoices.C: populations of monarch butterflies that have not migrated are much larger than migrating populations
answerChoices.D: monarch butterflies infected with parasites are typically unable to migrate
answerChoices.E: populations of monarch butterflies tend not to migrate if they have stable food sources

questions.stimulus: Legal doctrine: The government cannot appropriate private property without offering fair compensation to the property owner. Application: If the government institutes a regulation that blocks construction on undeveloped private lots on the shore of Lake Crowell—thereby diminishing their market value—it must offer fair compensation to the owners of that property.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most justifies the above application of the legal doctrine?

answerChoices.A: A government should not implement a regulation on lakeside property that it would not implement on other types of property.
answerChoices.B: Governments must balance the rights of private property holders with the rights of those who value undeveloped wilderness environments.
answerChoices.C: Regulations that significantly diminish the economic value of a piece of property constitute an appropriation of that property.
answerChoices.D: Owners of private property are alone responsible for the economic risks associated with government regulations that affect the use of that property.
answerChoices.E: A government can appropriate private property only if it is in response to a compelling public interest.

questions.stimulus: When a bird flies, powerful forces converge on its shoulder joints. The bird’s wings must be kept stable during flight, which cannot happen unless something balances these forces. The only structure in birds capable of balancing them is a ligament that connects the wing to the shoulder joint. So that ligament must be _______.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most logically completes the argument?

answerChoices.A: the only structure that is indispensable to bird flight
answerChoices.B: the reason that a bird’s wings must be kept stable during flight
answerChoices.C: the sole connection between the wing and the shoulder joint
answerChoices.D: the source of the powerful forces that converge on the shoulder joint
answerChoices.E: the means by which a bird stabilizes its wings during flight

questions.stimulus: As part of a project to enhance the downtown area, the transit authority plans to build a majestic new subway station on the Longview line. However, the current design of the station does not include a connection to the nearby Waterfront line. Adding a tunnel from the station to the Waterfront line using the current design would make the station much more convenient to commuters but would also put the project over budget. Since the budget cannot be increased, a more modest station should be built so that a tunnel can be included.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: The transit authority should design a subway station that costs less than the amount budgeted.
answerChoices.B: The transit authority should consider all potential additions to the subway station that would make it more convenient to commuters.
answerChoices.C: In the enhancement of the downtown area, convenience to commuters should be given priority over majestic design.
answerChoices.D: Unless a subway station can be built within budget that is both convenient to commuters and in keeping with the new design, the transit authority should abandon plans to build a station.
answerChoices.E: The new subway station should enhance the downtown area more than any other potential project that is similar in cost.

questions.stimulus: A study found that most of the strokes diagnosed by doctors occurred in the left side of patients’ brains. This suggests that right-side strokes are more likely than left-side strokes to go undiagnosed since _______.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion of the argument is strongly supported if which one of the following completes the passage?

answerChoices.A: patients who have strokes typically also have other health problems
answerChoices.B: it is very likely that just as many strokes occur in the right side of the brain as in the left side
answerChoices.C: doctors vary greatly in the accuracy of their diagnoses of strokes
answerChoices.D: the symptoms of right-side strokes tend to be different than the symptoms of left-side strokes
answerChoices.E: other studies have suggested that a large number of minor strokes go undiagnosed

questions.stimulus: When so many oysters died off the coast of Britain that some native species were threatened with extinction, the fact that the water temperature had recently risen was at first thought to be the cause. Later, however, the cause was determined to be the chemical tributyl tin (TBT), used to keep barnacles off the hulls of boats. Legislation that banned TBT has nearly eliminated that chemical from British waters, yet the populations of the endangered oyster species have not grown.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the failure of the native oyster populations to recover?

answerChoices.A: The increase in water temperature has slowed in the years since the legislation was passed.
answerChoices.B: Native oysters rely on different sources of food than do the barnacles that live on the hulls of boats.
answerChoices.C: TBT also killed imported varieties of oysters that flourish at the expense of native oysters now that the waters are warmer.
answerChoices.D: Other chemicals that are used to remove barnacles from the hulls of boats seem to have little effect on the oyster populations.
answerChoices.E: TBT is more deadly to oysters in colder waters than in warmer waters.

questions.stimulus: Pratt: Almost all cases of rabies in humans come from being bitten by a rabid animal, and bats do carry rabies. But there is little justification for health warnings that urge the removal of any bats residing in buildings where people work or live. Bats are shy animals that rarely bite, and the overwhelming majority of bats do not have rabies.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens Pratt’s argument?

answerChoices.A: A rabid bat is much more likely to infect another bat than to infect any other type of animal.
answerChoices.B: Rabid bats are less mobile than other bats but are much more aggressive.
answerChoices.C: Most animals that carry rabies are animals of species that, under normal conditions, very rarely bite people.
answerChoices.D: The bat species with the highest incidence of rabies do not live in buildings.
answerChoices.E: People are more likely to be aware of having been bitten by a bat if they were bitten by the bat inside a building.

questions.stimulus: It has been said that understanding a person completely leads one to forgive that person entirely. If so, then it follows that complete self-forgiveness is beyond our reach, for complete self-understanding, however desirable, is unattainable.
questions.questionStem: A flaw in the reasoning in the argument above is that this argument

answerChoices.A: treats the failure to satisfy a condition that brings about a particular outcome as if satisfying that condition is the only way to realize the outcome
answerChoices.B: confuses something that is necessary for an action to occur with something that necessarily results from that action
answerChoices.C: takes for granted that something that has merely been said to be true is, in fact, true
answerChoices.D: ignores the possibility that a state of affairs is desirable even if it cannot be attained
answerChoices.E: uses the difficulty of attaining a state of affairs as a reason for not attempting to attain it

questions.stimulus: A popular complaint about abstract expressionist paintings—that “a child could paint that”—holds that their stylistic similarities to young children’s paintings show that they are no more aesthetically pleasing than those inexpert works. But most participants in a psychological study, when shown pairs of paintings consisting of an abstract expressionist painting and a preschooler’s painting, consistently rated the abstract expressionist painting as aesthetically better, refuting this complaint and thereby establishing that abstract expressionist paintings are aesthetically pleasing.
questions.questionStem: The argument depends on assuming which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: People are better at judging the aesthetic value of a painting when they compare it with another painting.
answerChoices.B: Most of the preschoolers’ paintings used in the study were not aesthetically displeasing.
answerChoices.C: Each painting shown to the participants had a label that accurately indicated whether it was an abstract expressionist painting or a preschooler’s painting.
answerChoices.D: Participants who did not consistently rate the abstract expressionist paintings as aesthetically better nonetheless rated them better more often than not.
answerChoices.E: There were few stylistic similarities between the abstract expressionist paintings that participants were shown and the preschoolers’ paintings with which they were paired.

questions.stimulus: Xavier: The new fast-food place on 10th Street is out of business already. I’m not surprised. It had no indoor seating, and few people want to sit outside and breathe exhaust fumes while they eat. Miranda: The bank should have realized that with all the fast-food places on 10th Street, one lacking indoor seating was likely to fail. So it was irresponsible of them to lend the money for it.
questions.questionStem: It can be inferred from the dialogue that Xavier and Miranda agree that

answerChoices.A: few people want to sit outside while they eat
answerChoices.B: banks should not finance restaurants lacking indoor seating
answerChoices.C: if the new fast-food place had indoor seating, it probably would have been successful
