answerChoices.A: Solving a problem never requires finding the root cause of the problem.
answerChoices.B: Knowing the cause of the current recession would not necessarily enable people to find a solution to it.
answerChoices.C: The question of what caused the current recession is subject to considerable debate.
answerChoices.D: One need not ascertain the cause of the current recession in order to improve the economy.
answerChoices.E: Long before the cause of myopia was known to be genetic, corrective lenses were being used as an effective treatment for the disease.

questions.stimulus:
Generally, it is important that people practice what
 they preach, yet there are exceptions. For instance, it
 is no more necessary for logicians to be logical in their
 discussions of logic than it is for physicians to have
 healthy lifestyles in order to treat people.
questions.questionStem:
A questionable aspect of the reasoning above is that it
 fails to take into account that

answerChoices.A: logicians’ being illogical in their discussions of logic constitutes incompetence, whereas physicians’ having an unhealthy lifestyle does not
answerChoices.B: if a physician’s health deteriorates badly, the physician may not be able to treat patients effectively
answerChoices.C: physicians who are incompetent to practice medicine can cause more harm than can logicians who discuss logic illogically
answerChoices.D: it is more difficult to become logical in one’s discussions of logic than it is to modify an unhealthy lifestyle
answerChoices.E: although it is not necessary for logicians to be logical in order to be competent to discuss logic, it is highly desirable

questions.stimulus:
Domesticated animals, such as dogs, have come into
 existence by the breeding of only the individuals of a
 wild species that are sufficiently tame. For example, if
 when breeding wolves one breeds only those that display
 tameness when young, then after a number of generations
 the offspring will be a species of dog. Therefore, all
 animals can, in principle, be bred for domesticity.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the
 argument?

answerChoices.A: Domesticated animals cannot be turned into wild species by breeding only those animals that display some wild characteristics.
answerChoices.B: In some animal species, wild members mate more frequently than tame members.
answerChoices.C: In some animal species, no members ever display tameness.
answerChoices.D: In some animal species, tame members are less fertile than wild members.
answerChoices.E: In some domesticated animal species, some members are much more tame than other members.

questions.stimulus:
Surprisingly, a new study has revealed that shortly after a
 heavy rainfall, pollution levels in Crystal Bay reach their
 highest levels. This occurs despite the fact that rainwater
 is almost totally pure and one would therefore expect that
 it would dilute the polluted seawater.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most helps to
 explain why pollution levels in Crystal Bay increase
 after a heavy rainfall?

answerChoices.A: Compared to the total amount of polluted seawater, the amount of rainwater that falls into Crystal Bay is negligible.
answerChoices.B: Most of the rainwater that eventually reaches Crystal Bay falls on pesticide-treated fields before being carried into the bay.
answerChoices.C: Most rainwater carried by clouds consists of water that has evaporated from oceans around the world.
answerChoices.D: The single leading cause of pollution in Crystal Bay is beachgoers’ leaving behind their trash and debris, which then blows into the bay.
answerChoices.E: Other nearby ocean areas experience a pattern of pollutant increase and decrease that is extremely similar to that of Crystal Bay.

questions.stimulus:
Ethicist: This hospital’s ethics code states that hospital
 staff must not deceive patients about their
 medical treatment. But we know that Dr. Faris
 administered medication A to a patient and
 informed him that it would help him sleep.
 Medication A has no known sleep-inducing
 properties. So, Dr. Faris is clearly in violation of
 the ethics code, despite the fact that the patient’s
 sleep did improve after taking medication A.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most seriously
 weakens the ethicist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Dr. Faris was aware that medication A had no known sleep-inducing properties.
answerChoices.B: A committee at the hospital is currently considering revisions to the hospital’s ethics code.
answerChoices.C: Medication A is a pain reliever that can indirectly lead to sleep due to a reduction in the patient’s discomfort.
answerChoices.D: Several other members of the hospital staff prescribed medication A to patients who had trouble sleeping.
answerChoices.E: Dr. Faris knew that the patient was not taking any other medications that have sleep-inducing properties.

questions.stimulus:
Student: My paper was not graded in accordance with
 the professor’s stated criteria. The professor said
 that she would give A’s only to papers whose
 conclusions were supported by reliable statistical
 evidence. The professor acknowledges that my
 conclusions were supported by reliable statistical
 evidence, but she gave my paper a B.
questions.questionStem:
The reasoning in the student’s argument is flawed in that
 the argument

answerChoices.A: discusses the professor’s stated criteria in order to draw attention away from the shortcomings of the student’s paper
answerChoices.B: attempts to draw an evaluative conclusion solely on the basis of factual claims
answerChoices.C: takes a condition that is among the requirements for a particular grade to be a condition that is enough to guarantee that grade
answerChoices.D: is based on the report of a biased participant in the controversy
answerChoices.E: fails to make a necessary distinction between the professor’s grading criteria and the objective criteria of a paper’s quality

questions.stimulus:
Consumer advocate: Even relatively minor drug-related
 interactions can still be harmful to patients.
 For example, aspirin taken with fruit juice
 is ineffective. People unaware of this suffer
 unnecessary discomfort or take more aspirin than
 necessary. The government should, therefore,
 require drug companies to notify consumers of all
 known drug-related interactions.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the
 consumer advocate’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Providing information on minor drug-related interactions would detract from a patient’s attention to serious interactions.
answerChoices.B: Many drugs have fewer documented drug-related interactions than does aspirin.
answerChoices.C: Providing information about all drug-related interactions would result in only negligible price increases for consumers.
answerChoices.D: Current research is such that many drug-related interactions have not yet been identified.
answerChoices.E: Pharmacists usually draw patients’ attention to printed warnings that are provided with drugs.

questions.stimulus:
Radioactive elements may have been created when
 the universe began. However, even if this occurred,
 these elements are clearly still being created in the
 universe today. Radioactive elements are unstable, so
 most of them decay within at most a few million years
 into other, nonradioactive elements. So, if no new
 radioactive elements had been created after the universe
 began, almost no radioactive elements would be left in
 the universe today, but there is an abundance of such
 elements.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most accurately expresses
 the main conclusion of the argument?

answerChoices.A: Any radioactive elements created when the universe began have probably decayed into other, nonradioactive elements.
answerChoices.B: Radioactive elements are being created in the universe today.
answerChoices.C: If no new radioactive elements had been created after the universe began, almost no radioactive elements would be left in the universe today.
answerChoices.D: It is possible that radioactive elements were created when the universe began.
answerChoices.E: Due to their instability, most of the universe’s radioactive elements decay within at most a few million years into other, nonradioactive elements.

questions.stimulus:
There is evidence that a certain ancient society burned
 large areas of land. Some suggest that this indicates the
 beginning of large-scale agriculture in that society—
 that the land was burned to clear ground for planting.
 But there is little evidence of cultivation after the fires.
 Therefore, it is likely that this society was still a hunter-
 gatherer society.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the
 argument?

answerChoices.A: Many ancient cultures had agriculture before they began using fire to clear large tracts of land.
answerChoices.B: Hunter-gatherer societies used fire for cooking and for heat during cold weather.
answerChoices.C: Many plants and trees have inedible seeds that are contained in hard shells and are released only when subjected to the heat of a great fire.
answerChoices.D: Hunter-gatherer societies are known to have used fire to move animal populations from one area to another.
answerChoices.E: Few early societies were aware that burning organic material can help create nutrients for soil.

questions.stimulus:
Professor Shanaz: People generally notice and are
 concerned about only the most obvious public
 health problems. Although there is indisputable
 evidence that ozone, an air pollutant, can be
 dangerous for severe asthmatics even if found
 in levels much lower than maximum levels
 permitted by law, most people are currently
 well aware that contaminated water presents a
 much more widespread threat to our community.
 Hence, there is unlikely to be a widespread,
 grassroots effort for new, more restrictive air
 pollution controls at this time.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most accurately describes
 the role played in Professor Shanaz’s argument by the
 claim that people generally notice and are concerned
 about only the most obvious public health problems?

answerChoices.A: It is a premise offered in support of the claim that contaminated water currently presents a much more widespread threat to the community than does ozone.
answerChoices.B: It is a premise offered in support of the claim that there is unlikely to be a widespread, grassroots effort for new, more restrictive air pollution controls at this time.
answerChoices.C: It is used to explain the current public awareness of the severity of the problem of contaminated water.
answerChoices.D: It is presented as indisputable evidence that ozone can be dangerous for severe asthmatics even if found in levels much lower than maximum levels permitted by law.
answerChoices.E: It is the main conclusion drawn in the argument.

questions.stimulus:
Psychotherapist: The troubles from which a patient
 seeks relief through psychotherapy do not have
 purely internal causes; rather, those troubles
 result in part from the patient’s relationships with
 other people. Hence, to help the patient heal,
 the psychotherapist must focus on the need for
 positive change in those relationships.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following is an assumption the
 psychotherapist’s argument requires?

answerChoices.A: Psychotherapists cannot help change their patients’ relationships unless those patients focus on other people’s troubles.
answerChoices.B: At least some psychotherapy patients cannot be healed if a psychotherapist helps them change their relationships with other people.
answerChoices.C: Those psychotherapy patients who change their relationships with other people will thereby find relief from at least some of their troubles.
answerChoices.D: No psychotherapist can help a patient heal solely by addressing the internal causes of the patient’s troubles.
answerChoices.E: If a psychotherapist helps patients focus on troubles that are purely internal, then that psychotherapist thereby provides them the relief they seek.

questions.stimulus:
Some freelance journalists sell their work to magazines
 that have lax editorial standards. No self-respecting
 writer sells his or her work to magazines that have lax
 editorial standards. Therefore, some self-respecting
 writers are not freelance journalists.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following displays a flawed pattern of
 reasoning most similar to the one in the argument
 above?

answerChoices.A: Some high school teachers teach biology. No kindergarten teachers teach biology. Therefore, biology is not taught by all teachers.
answerChoices.B: Most school board members were once teachers. No one who was once a teacher prefers administrative work to teaching. Hence, few school board members prefer administrative work to teaching.
answerChoices.C: Some students prefer history to mathematics. No member of the Calculus Club prefers history to mathematics. Thus, some members of the Calculus Club are not students.
answerChoices.D: Some principals are harsh disciplinarians. No adviser to a debate team is a harsh disciplinarian. Hence, some principals are not advisers to a debate team.
answerChoices.E: Some teachers who let their students leave early are popular. No coaches allow their students to leave before three o’clock. Therefore, some popular teachers are not coaches.

questions.stimulus:
Selling syndicated reruns of a popular network television
 program while the program is still running on the
 network can lead to decreased revenues for that network. The show’s producers do earn a great deal of money from
 the sale of the syndication rights because the stations
 rerunning the program are assured of a successful show. However, a recent study shows that over 80 percent
 of the programs that are made available as reruns and
 as first-run episodes during the same season suffer an
 immediate ratings drop for their first-run episodes.
questions.questionStem:
The argument depends on assuming which one of the
 following?

answerChoices.A: Programs that are sold into syndication early tend to be long-running hits that are likely to decline soon.
answerChoices.B: A drop in ratings has a negative effect on the network’s revenues.
answerChoices.C: The price of syndication rights includes some compensation for the network’s probable losses.
answerChoices.D: The audience of a popular program will usually prefer first-run episodes to reruns.
answerChoices.E: Most programs are never sold into syndication.

questions.stimulus:
If a belief is based on information from a reliable source,
 then it is reasonable to maintain that belief. Furthermore,
 some beliefs are based on information from a reliable
 source and yet are neither self-evident nor grounded in
 observable evidence.
questions.questionStem:
If all the statements above are true, which one of the
 following statements must be true?

answerChoices.A: Beliefs for which a person does not have observable evidence are unreasonable.
answerChoices.B: Beliefs based on information from a reliable source are self-evident.
answerChoices.C: All reasonable beliefs for which a person has no observable evidence are based on information from a reliable source.
answerChoices.D: If a belief is not grounded in observable evidence, then it is not self-evident either.
answerChoices.E: Among reasonable beliefs that are not self-evident, there are some beliefs that are not grounded in observable evidence.

questions.stimulus:
Situation: A physical therapist wants her patients to
 derive more enjoyment from the challenge of
 developing physical skills. She also wants them
 to spend more time practicing those skills. Analysis: Success in meeting the first objective will bring
 about success in meeting the second.
questions.questionStem:
The analysis provided for the situation above could be
 appropriate for each of the following situations except:

answerChoices.A: A math teacher wants her students to understand the mathematical principles taught in her course and wants them to apply these principles routinely in everyday life.
answerChoices.B: A software manufacturer wants its customers to be more satisfied with its product, and it wants them to place fewer calls to the service representative about how to use the product.
answerChoices.C: A librarian wants fewer of the books borrowed from the library to be lost or stolen, and he wants more of the library’s books to be returned on time.
answerChoices.D: A hardware retail company wants to construct a new, larger warehouse and wants its employees to help plan how the old warehouse will be expanded to meet any need for more space.
answerChoices.E: A concert series director wants to present a more varied repertoire and wants to attract new patrons.

questions.stimulus:
Classicist: Our mastery of Latin and Ancient Greek is
 at best imperfect. The best students of a modern
 language may so immerse themselves in a
 country where it is spoken as to attain nearly
 perfect knowledge; but you cannot travel back in
 time to spend a year abroad at Plato’s Academy.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most accurately describes
 the role played in the classicist’s argument by the claim
 that you cannot travel back in time to spend a year
 abroad at Plato’s Academy?

answerChoices.A: It is the main conclusion drawn in the argument.
answerChoices.B: It points up by example a contrast from which the conclusion is drawn.
answerChoices.C: It is a mere rhetorical flourish having no logical relation to the argument’s conclusion.
answerChoices.D: It is a premise that guarantees the truth of the argument’s conclusion.
answerChoices.E: It is an ancillary conclusion drawn in the argument.

questions.stimulus:
For there to be a thriving population of turtles in a pond,
 conditions at that pond must be beneficial to turtles. The
 water in Wallakim Pond, unlike that in Sosachi Pond, is
 acidic. Thus, there must not be a thriving population of
 turtles at Wallakim Pond.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if assumed, enables the
 argument’s conclusion to be properly drawn?

answerChoices.A: If the water in a pond is not acidic, the conditions at that pond are beneficial to turtles.
answerChoices.B: The most important factor that determines whether a pond will have a thriving turtle population is the acidity of the water.
answerChoices.C: The water conditions at Sosachi Pond are more beneficial to turtles than are the water conditions at Wallakim Pond.
answerChoices.D: Wallakim Pond would have a thriving population of turtles if it were not acidic.
answerChoices.E: The conditions at a pond are beneficial to turtles only if the water in the pond is not acidic.

questions.stimulus:
The study of primates is interesting for many reasons,
 including the fact that only primates have opposable
 thumbs. The lemurs are lower primates and the only
 primates indigenous to Madagascar, a large island off the
 coast of southeastern Africa. Some species of lemurs are
 the only living lower primates that are diurnal—that is,
 active primarily during the day. All higher primates are
 thought to have evolved from a single diurnal species of
 lower primates.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following can be properly inferred
 from the information above?

answerChoices.A: The chimpanzee, a higher primate, evolved from the lemur.
answerChoices.B: No primates indigenous to Madagascar are diurnal higher primates.
answerChoices.C: No higher primate is nocturnal.
answerChoices.D: There are some lemurs without opposable thumbs.
answerChoices.E: There are no nocturnal lemurs.

questions.stimulus:
Professor: Many scientists hypothesize that there is an
 invisible “light-absorbing medium” in outer
 space. In support, they argue that the medium’s
 existence would explain the low visibility of
 other star systems from Earth. But there is
 actually no reason to believe that the hypothesis
 is correct, since the low visibility in question
 is already completely explained by the general
 theory of relativity.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following is an assumption required by
 the professor’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The low visibility of other star systems from Earth would not be adequately explained by the existence of an invisible light-absorbing medium in outer space, even if there were such a medium.
answerChoices.B: The hypothesis of an invisible light-absorbing medium in outer space is correct only if it adequately explains the low visibility of other star systems from Earth.
answerChoices.C: A hypothesis is likely to be correct if there is some phenomenon that it adequately accounts for and that is not adequately accounted for by an existing theory.
answerChoices.D: Most scientists who posit the invisible light-absorbing medium accept the general theory of relativity.
answerChoices.E: The general theory of relativity does not depend upon the hypothesis that there exists an invisible light-absorbing medium in outer space.

questions.stimulus:
Some researchers claim that people tend to gesture less
 when they articulate what would typically be regarded
 as abstract rather than physical concepts. To point out
 that such a correlation is far from universal is insufficient
 reason to reject the researchers’ claim, because some
 people perceive words like “comprehension” as
 expressing a physical action, like grasping something,
 rather than a state of understanding, which is abstract.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most accurately describes
 the method of reasoning used in the argument?

answerChoices.A: appealing to the ambiguity of a word in an attempt to show that a correlation is universal
answerChoices.B: appealing to a universal psychological generalization in an attempt to support a claim about the use of gestures
answerChoices.C: citing a psychological fact to try to reconcile a generalization with apparently disconfirming evidence
answerChoices.D: advocating an explanation for a phenomenon by attempting to demonstrate that other possible explanations are implausible
answerChoices.E: offering a reason for believing that a widely accepted generalization requires still more supporting evidence

questions.stimulus:
According to rational-choice theory, popular support for
 various political parties can be explained sufficiently
 in terms of deliberate decisions by individual voters to
 support the party whose policies they believe will yield
 them the greatest economic advantage. This theory is
 opposed by many sociologists on the grounds that a
 complex phenomenon such as the rise of a political
 organization cannot be caused by a simple phenomenon.
questions.questionStem:
It can be properly inferred from the statements above
 that many sociologists believe that

answerChoices.A: economically motivated decisions by voters need not constitute a complex phenomenon
answerChoices.B: a complex phenomenon generally will have many complex causes
answerChoices.C: political phenomena often have religious and cultural causes as well as economic ones
answerChoices.D: popular support for political parties is never a complex phenomenon
answerChoices.E: the decisions of individual voters are not usually influenced by their beliefs about which policies will yield them the greatest economic advantage

questions.stimulus:
Scientist: Some consumer groups claim that the
 economic benefits of genetically engineered
 foodstuffs may be offset by hidden health risks to
 humans. However, the risk is minimal. In most
 cases of deliberate alteration of a plant’s genetic
 structure only a single gene in about 750,000 has
 been changed. Since the change in the organism’s
 genetic structure is so slight, it cannot have
 effects significant enough to be worrisome.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the
 scientist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The genetically engineered plants that have been developed so far have few advantages over plants that are not genetically engineered.
answerChoices.B: Whatever health risks there are in food from genetically altered plants may be somewhat reduced by other factors such as enrichment of the plants’ vitamin and mineral content.
answerChoices.C: Scientists have yet to determine, for each characteristic of some plants and animals used for food, the precise location of the genes that determine that characteristic.
answerChoices.D: There are plants that are known to be toxic to some animals and whose toxicity is known to be affected by the alteration of a single gene.
answerChoices.E: Research has shown that those consumers who are most strongly opposed to genetically altered foods tend to be ill-informed on the issue.

questions.stimulus:
A government is justified in interfering with a person’s
 action if the action would increase the likelihood of
 physical harm to others and the action is not motivated by
 a desire to help others.
questions.questionStem:
Of the following judgments, which one most closely
 conforms to the principle above?

answerChoices.A: Jerry’s hobby, making home movies, does not harm anyone, nor does it increase the likelihood of harm to anyone. He does it because he thinks that it will benefit his children by preserving a record of their childhoods. So the government is unjustified in interfering with Jerry’s moviemaking.
answerChoices.B: It is well known that a property is aesthetically less pleasing when neighboring properties have unkempt lawns. My neighbor often forgets to mow his lawn for several weeks. The city council, therefore, is justified in fining my neighbor for not mowing his lawn more frequently.
answerChoices.C: Because a motorcyclist who is not wearing a helmet is much more likely to suffer a serious head injury in the event of an accident, the government is justified in requiring motorcyclists to wear helmets.
answerChoices.D: Because Zabziew Pharmaceutical Corporation’s research is motivated by the desire to make profits and not by the desire to benefit customers, it has been of little help to people suffering from serious illness. So the government is justified in suspending Zabziew’s license to test new drugs.
answerChoices.E: To further her own political ambitions, Jill wanted to give a speech advocating the use of violence to achieve political ends. But her speech would most likely have caused a riot and people would have gotten hurt. Hence, the government was justified in preventing her from giving her speech.

questions.stimulus:
The government’s tax collection agency has not followed
 through on its plan, announced a year ago, to crack down
 on violations of corporate income tax law. Audits are
 the primary tool for detecting such violations, and over
 the past year, not a single audit of corporate income tax
 returns has been completed.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the
 argument?

answerChoices.A: The plan to crack down on violations of corporate income tax law is part of a broad campaign against corporate misconduct.
answerChoices.B: The number of personal income tax returns audited over the past year is greater than in previous years.
answerChoices.C: Most audits of corporate income tax returns do not reveal any significant violations.
answerChoices.D: It generally takes longer than one year to complete an audit of a corporate income tax return.
answerChoices.E: Over the last five years, fewer audits of corporate income tax returns have been completed than in the preceding five years.

questions.stimulus:
Columnist: Making some types of products from
 recycled materials is probably as damaging to
 the environment as it would be to make those
 products from entirely nonrecycled materials. The recycling process for those products requires
 as much energy as producing them from raw
 materials, and almost all energy production
 damages the environment.
questions.questionStem:
The reasoning in the columnist’s argument is most
 vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: uses the word “environment” in one sense in a premise and in a different sense in the conclusion drawn from that premise
answerChoices.B: treats an effect of energy-related damage to the environment as if it were instead a cause of such damage
answerChoices.C: fails to consider that the particular types of recycled products that it cites may not be representative of recycled products in general
answerChoices.D: fails to consider that making products from recycled materials may have environmental benefits unrelated to energy consumption
answerChoices.E: presumes that simply because one phenomenon follows another phenomenon the earlier phenomenon must be a cause of the later one

questions.stimulus:
Physician: We are constantly bombarded by warnings,
 based on initial studies’ tentative conclusions,
 about this or that food having adverse health
 effects. If the medical establishment wants people
 to pay attention to health warnings, it should
 announce only conclusive results, the kind that
 can come only from definitive studies. After all,
 people who are constantly subjected to fire drills
 eventually come to ignore the fire alarm.
questions.questionStem:
The statement that people who are constantly subjected
 to fire drills eventually come to ignore the fire alarm
 plays which one of the following roles in the physician’s
 argument?

answerChoices.A: It is presented as an example of the sort of warning referred to in the argument’s overall conclusion.
answerChoices.B: It is a statement that plays no logical role in the argument but that instead serves to impugn the motives of the medical establishment.
answerChoices.C: It is an analogy offered in support of the argument’s overall conclusion.
answerChoices.D: It is an analogy that forms part of a specific objection to the argument’s overall conclusion.
answerChoices.E: It is an analogy offered to clarify the distinction the physician makes between an initial study and a definitive study.

questions.stimulus:
A club wanted to determine whether it could increase
 attendance by changing its weekly meetings from
 Tuesday to another day. At one Tuesday meeting, the
 club’s president took a survey of all members present. Of
 those surveyed, 95 percent said that they had no difficulty
 attending on Tuesdays. On the basis of this survey
 result, the club’s president concluded that the attendance
 problem was not due primarily to schedule conflicts.
questions.questionStem:
A questionable technique used in the club president’s
 reasoning is

answerChoices.A: drawing a conclusion on the basis of circular reasoning
answerChoices.B: making a generalization on the basis of a sample that is likely to be unrepresentative
answerChoices.C: treating a generalization that applies to most cases as if it applied without exception
answerChoices.D: drawing a conclusion on the basis of premises that contradict one another
answerChoices.E: inferring, solely from the claim that a change is not sufficient to solve a problem, that it is not necessary either.

questions.stimulus:
The railway authority inspector who recently thoroughly
 checked the tracks testified that they were in good
 condition. Thus, since the inspector has no bias in
 the matter, we should be suspicious of the newspaper
 reporter’s claim that the tracks are in poor condition.
questions.questionStem:
The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to
 the reasoning in which one of the following arguments?

answerChoices.A: My pottery instructor says that making pottery will not cause repetitive-motion injuries if it is done properly. So I will probably not get such injuries, for whenever I do pottery I use the proper techniques that my instructor taught me.
answerChoices.B: Gardner, a noted paleontologist who has no vested interest in the case, assures us that the alleged dinosaur bones are not old enough to be from dinosaurs. So we should be skeptical of Penwick’s claim to have found dinosaur bones, for Gardner inspected the bones carefully.
answerChoices.C: The engineer hired by the company that maintains the bridge has examined the bridge and declared it safe. This engineer is the only one who has given the bridge a close examination recently. Thus, we should consider the bridge safe.
answerChoices.D: The reporter who recently interviewed the prime minister said the prime minister appeared to be in poor health. But despite the fact that the reporter works for a paper with opposition leanings, we should accept that the prime minister is in poor health. After all, reporters won’t let their bias affect them when the truth of their claims will eventually be discovered.
answerChoices.E: The snowblower salesperson claims that there will be above-average snowfall this winter, but because the salesperson is biased, we can discount that claim.

questions.stimulus:
If the proposed air pollution measures were to be
 implemented, ozone levels in the city’s air would be one
 fifth lower than current levels. Since the ozone in our air
 is currently responsible for over $5 billion in health costs,
 we would spend about a billion dollars less on these
 ozone-related health costs should the proposed measures
 be adopted.
questions.questionStem:
The argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the
 grounds that it

answerChoices.A: fails to consider the possibility that other types of pollution not involving ozone might rise, perhaps even producing an overall increase in health costs
answerChoices.B: presumes, without providing evidence, that ozone-related health costs in the city vary roughly in proportion to ozone levels
answerChoices.C: provides no explicit reason for believing that the proposed air pollution measures will in fact be adopted
answerChoices.D: attempts to support its conclusion by making an appeal to emotions
answerChoices.E: discusses air pollution in order to draw attention away from more significant sources of health-related costs

questions.stimulus:
Newspaper article: Recently discovered clay tablets
 from southern Egypt date to between 3300 and
 3200 B.C. Though most of the tablets translated
 thus far are tax records, one of them appears
 to contain literary writing. Hence, these tablets
 challenge the widely held belief among historians
 that the Sumerian civilization in Mesopotamia
 was the first to create literature.
questions.questionStem:
The argument in the newspaper article requires the
 assumption that

answerChoices.A: most of the recently discovered tablets that have not yet been translated contain literary writing
answerChoices.B: every civilization that has kept tax records has also kept other written records
answerChoices.C: historians generally believe that the Sumerians did not create literature earlier than 3300 B.C.
answerChoices.D: some historians are skeptical about the authenticity of the recently discovered tablets
answerChoices.E: the Sumerian civilization arose sometime between 3300 and 3200 B.C.

questions.stimulus:
Climatologist: The waters off the Pacific coast of North
 America have warmed about 4 degrees over
 the past 15 years. Some scientists claim that
 this trend is a symptom of a more general,
 global warming caused by human-generated air
 pollution. However, this conclusion is far from
 justified—it is known that there are many natural
 cycles of ocean temperature changes that last 60
 years or more.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most accurately expresses
 the main conclusion drawn in the climatologist’s
 argument?

answerChoices.A: Some scientists have found evidence that the waters off the Pacific coast of North America have grown significantly warmer over the past 15 years.
answerChoices.B: The warming of the waters off the Pacific coast of North America is not a symptom of a more general, global warming caused by human-generated air pollution.
answerChoices.C: The conclusion that the warming of the waters off the Pacific coast of North America is a symptom of a more general, global warming caused by human-generated air pollution is far from justified.
answerChoices.D: The warming of the waters off the Pacific coast of North America may be the result of a natural cycle of ocean temperature changes.
answerChoices.E: If the warming of the waters off the Pacific coast of North America is due to a natural cycle of ocean temperature changes, then it is not a symptom of a more general, global warming caused by human-generated air pollution.

questions.stimulus:
Robin: Archaeologists can study the artifacts left by
 ancient cultures to determine whether they were
 nomadic or sedentary. If the artifacts were made
 to last rather than to be quickly discarded, the
 culture was likely sedentary. Kendall: But what artifacts a people make is determined
 largely by the materials available to them.
questions.questionStem:
Their statements commit Robin and Kendall to
 disagreeing over whether

answerChoices.A: the distinction that Robin makes between two kinds of cultures is illicit
answerChoices.B: it is reasonable to assume that a culture whose artifacts were not durable was nomadic
answerChoices.C: any evidence other than the intended durability of a culture’s artifacts can establish conclusively which of the two kinds of cultures a particular culture was
answerChoices.D: the distinction that Robin makes between the different kinds of cultures is as important as many archaeologists have thought
answerChoices.E: studying a culture’s artifacts can reveal a great deal about the culture

questions.stimulus:
Railroads rely increasingly on automation. Since fewer
 railroad workers are needed, operating costs have been
 reduced. This means that we can expect the volume of
 freight shipped by rail to grow. The chief competitor of
 railway shipping is shipping by truck, and no reduction in
 operating costs is predicted for the trucking industry.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following most accurately states the
 argument’s overall conclusion?

answerChoices.A: The volume of freight shipped by rail can be expected to increase.
answerChoices.B: Increasing reliance on automation means that fewer railroad workers are needed.
answerChoices.C: No reduction in operating costs is predicted for the trucking industry.
answerChoices.D: Operating costs for railroads have been reduced as a result of increased reliance on automation.
answerChoices.E: The chief competitor of railway shipping is shipping by truck.

questions.stimulus:
In the past, infants who were not breast-fed were fed
 cow’s milk. Then doctors began advising that cow’s milk
 fed to infants should be boiled, as the boiling would
 sterilize the milk and prevent gastrointestinal infections
 potentially fatal to infants. Once this advice was widely
 implemented, there was an alarming increase among
 infants in the incidence of scurvy, caused by vitamin C
 deficiency. Breast-fed infants, however, did not contract
 scurvy.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following is most strongly supported
 by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Boiled cow’s milk makes less vitamin C available to infants than does the same amount of mother’s milk.
answerChoices.B: Infants who consume cow’s milk that has not been boiled frequently contract potentially fatal gastrointestinal infections.
answerChoices.C: Mother’s milk can cause gastrointestinal infections in infants.
answerChoices.D: When doctors advised that cow’s milk fed to infants should be boiled, they did not know that scurvy was caused by vitamin C deficiency.
answerChoices.E: When doctors advised that cow’s milk fed to infants should be boiled, most mothers did not breast-feed their infants.

questions.stimulus:
The only effective check on grass and brush fires is rain.
 If the level of rainfall is below normal for an extended
 period of time, then there are many more such fires. Yet
 grass and brush fires cause less financial damage overall
 during long periods of severe drought than during periods
 of relatively normal rainfall.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, would most help to
 resolve the apparent paradox described above?

answerChoices.A: Fire departments tend to receive less funding during periods of severe drought than during periods of normal rainfall.
answerChoices.B: Areas subject to grass and brush fires tend to be less densely populated than areas where there are few such fires.
answerChoices.C: Unusually large, hard-to-control grass and brush fires typically occur only when there is a large amount of vegetation for them to consume.
answerChoices.D: Grass and brush fires that are not caused by human negligence or arson tend to be started by lightning.
answerChoices.E: When vegetation is destroyed in a grass or brush fire, it tends to be replaced naturally by vegetation that is equally if not more flammable.

questions.stimulus:
Medical researcher: A new screening test detects certain
 polyps at such an early stage that it is generally
 unclear whether the polyps are malignant. But
 the risk that a polyp might be malignant leads
 doctors, in most cases, to have such polyps
 surgically removed, which is a dangerous
 process. Yet some of those polyps turn out not to
 be malignant. Thus, the new screening test can
 prompt dangerous operations that actually are not
 medically necessary.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following is an assumption that the
 medical researcher’s argument requires?

answerChoices.A: A surgical operation that is dangerous is ethically justified only for treating a medical condition that is more dangerous.
answerChoices.B: Surgical removal of nonmalignant polyps detected by the new screening test is not always medically necessary.
answerChoices.C: If the new screening test encourages medically unnecessary operations, then probably it either should not be used or its use should be modified.
answerChoices.D: A polyp detected by the new screening test should be surgically removed if it is malignant.
answerChoices.E: The screening test is medically useful only when it detects a polyp that requires treatment.

questions.stimulus:
Psychologist: Most people’s blood pressure rises when
 they talk. But extroverted people experience
 milder surges when they speak than do
 introverted people, for whom speaking is more
 stressful. This suggests that the increases result
 from the psychological stress of communicating
 rather than from the physical exertion of speech
 production.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the
 psychologist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Medications designed to lower blood pressure do not keep the people who take them from experiencing blood-pressure fluctuations when speaking.
answerChoices.B: In general, the lower one’s typical blood pressure, the more one’s blood pressure will increase under stress.
answerChoices.C: Introverted people who do not have chronically high blood pressure often sense the rises in blood pressure that occur when they speak in conversation.
answerChoices.D: Deaf people experience increased blood pressure when they sign, but no change when they move their hands for other reasons.
answerChoices.E: Extroverted people are more likely to have chronically high blood pressure than are introverted people and are more likely to take medication to lower their blood pressure.

questions.stimulus:
One should only buy a frying pan that has a
 manufacturer’s warranty, even if it requires paying
 more, and even if one would never bother seeking
 reimbursement should the pan not work well or last
 long. Manufacturers will not offer a warranty on
 a product if doing so means that they will need to
 reimburse many customers because the product did not
 work well or last long.
questions.questionStem:
The conclusion of the argument is strongly supported if
 which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Most people who buy a frying pan with a manufacturer’s warranty would seek reimbursement should the pan fail to work well or last long.
answerChoices.B: All of the frying pans currently on the market that are covered by a manufacturer’s warranty work at least as well at the time of purchase as any of the frying pans not covered by a warranty.
answerChoices.C: The more a frying pan costs, the more likely it is to be covered by a manufacturer’s warranty.
answerChoices.D: The most expensive frying pans are the ones most likely to work well for many years.
answerChoices.E: Most frying pan manufacturers’ warranties provide for full customer satisfaction.

questions.stimulus:
Journalist: When judges do not maintain strict control
 over their courtrooms, lawyers often try to
 influence jury verdicts by using inflammatory
 language and by badgering witnesses. These
 obstructive behaviors hinder the jury’s effort to
 reach a correct verdict. Whenever lawyers engage
 in such behavior, therefore, it is reasonable to
 doubt whether the verdict is correct.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the
 journalist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Court proceedings overseen by judges who are very strict in controlling lawyers’ behavior are known to result sometimes in incorrect verdicts.
answerChoices.B: Lawyers tend to be less concerned than are judges about whether the outcomes of jury trials are just or not.
answerChoices.C: People who are influenced by inflammatory language are very unlikely to admit at some later time that they were influenced by such language.
answerChoices.D: Obstructive courtroom behavior by a lawyer is seldom effective in cases where jurors are also presented with legitimate evidence.
answerChoices.E: The selection of jurors is based in part on an assessment of the likelihood that they are free of bias.

questions.stimulus:
Mateo: Global warming has caused permafrost to melt
 under several arctic villages, forcing all their
 inhabitants to relocate at great expense. Since
 pollution from automobiles is a major contributor
 to global warming, the automotive industry
 should be required to help pay for the villagers’
 relocation.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following principles, if valid, would
 most help to justify Mateo’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Any industry has an obligation to pay for any damage that it should have known would result from its activities.
answerChoices.B: Manufacturers should be required to produce goods in a way that minimizes harm to people and the environment.
answerChoices.C: When the use of a product causes damage, governments should not be required to help pay for the damage unless those responsible for manufacturing the product are also required to help pay for them.
answerChoices.D: Any industry manufacturing a product whose use contributes to costly damage for others should be liable for any damage generated by that product’s use.
answerChoices.E: An industry that contributes to global warming should be required to help pay for resulting damage to specific communities only if it has a general obligation to help pay for all damage produced by global warming.

questions.stimulus:
Lindsey: Several people claim that our company was
 unfair when it failed to give bonuses to the staff. Perhaps they recalled that the company had
 promised that if it increased its profits over last
 year’s, the staff would all get bonuses. However,
 the company’s profit was much smaller this year
 than it was last year. Clearly, then, the company
 acted fairly.
questions.questionStem: The argument is flawed in that it

answerChoices.A: relies on the opinions of certain unnamed people without establishing that those people were well informed on the matter
answerChoices.B: infers that an opinion is false merely because one potential reason for that opinion has been undermined
answerChoices.C: dismisses a claim on the basis of certain irrelevant attributes of the people who made the claim
answerChoices.D: confuses the size of a quantity with the amount by which that quantity has increased
answerChoices.E: overlooks the possibility that a policy can be fair even when it is not generous

questions.stimulus:
It is widely known that the rescue squads serving high
 mountain areas with treacherous weather save the lives
 of many mountain climbers every year. However, many
 experienced climbers believe that the rising annual toll of
 deaths and injuries among climbers in these regions can
 be significantly reduced only by completely abolishing
 the rescue squads.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, would most help to
 justify the apparently paradoxical belief of the
 experienced climbers?

answerChoices.A: It is difficult to recruit and train members for the rescue squads.
answerChoices.B: The recording of deaths and injuries tends to be more accurate in mountain regions served by rescue squads.
answerChoices.C: People who commonly take risks with their lives and health do not expect other people to take those risks to rescue them.
answerChoices.D: Most of the people injured or killed while mountain climbing were not adequately prepared for the dangers they would face.
answerChoices.E: The lower the risk of climbing a particular mountain is perceived to be, the greater the number of less competent climbers who attempt to climb it.

questions.stimulus:
Paula: Earthlike planets seem to be the rule rather than
 the exception, so there probably are intelligent
 beings on other planets. Furthermore, we can
 expect our radio telescopes to detect signs of
 such beings. Alien scientists would have basically
 the same understanding of mathematics and
 physics that humans have. Thus they would
 inevitably discover gravity, electromagnetism,
 and other fundamental physical phenomena
 and then develop technologies such as radio
 communication. Ashley: That is like saying they would inevitably have
 the same legal or political systems that humans
 do. Our science, mathematics, and technology are
 unique outgrowths of our physiology, cognitive
 makeup, and environment. Using radio telescopes
 to search for intelligent life is a waste of time and
 money.
questions.questionStem:
The dialogue provides the most evidence that Paula and
 Ashley disagree with each other about whether

answerChoices.A: it is probable that there are intelligent alien beings who have developed radio communication
answerChoices.B: it is probable that there are intelligent alien beings who have the same legal or political systems that humans do
answerChoices.C: our technology is influenced by our cognitive makeup
answerChoices.D: there is likely to be intelligent life on other planets
answerChoices.E: scientists should spend more time and money on the search for intelligent extraterrestrial life

questions.stimulus:
Developer: The builders of the Glen Veil apartment
 complex will not complete the complex unless
 a road connecting it to the town of Sierra is
 built. The completed apartment complex would
 strengthen Sierra’s economy, and a stronger
 economy would benefit every Sierra resident.
 Therefore, the residents of Sierra should vote in
 favor of a local tax to fund construction of the
 proposed road.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following principles, if valid, would
 most help to justify the developer’s reasoning?

answerChoices.A: If a construction project is necessary in order to strengthen a town’s economy, then the residents of that town should vote in favor of a local tax to fund that construction project.
answerChoices.B: The residents of a town should not vote in favor of a local tax to fund a construction project unless that construction project will produce results that benefit all of those residents.
answerChoices.C: Whenever a town funds a construction project, it should do so by means of a tax rather than debt.
answerChoices.D: Only those residents who will benefit from the results of a construction project should be required to pay a tax to fund that project.
answerChoices.E: Anyone who would benefit from the results of a construction project should vote in favor of a local tax to fund that project.

questions.stimulus:
Historian: Because medieval epistemology (theory of
 knowledge) is a complex subject, intellectual
 historians have, until recently, failed to produce
 a definition that would help to determine what
 should and what should not be included in
 it. Clearly, the solution is to define medieval
 epistemology simply as “the epistemological
 beliefs of the medieval epistemologists.” That
 way, if we want to know whether medieval
 epistemology includes some epistemological
 claim, we just ask whether any medieval
 epistemologists believed it. If any did, it is part
 of medieval epistemology; if any medieval
 epistemologists believed the opposite, then that
 opposite claim is part of medieval epistemology.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, would most weaken
 the historian’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Medieval epistemologists held some of the same epistemological beliefs as did ancient epistemologists.
answerChoices.B: The epistemological beliefs of medieval epistemologists depended upon their beliefs about nonepistemological matters.
answerChoices.C: The writings of most medieval epistemologists include passages that are clearly not about epistemology.
answerChoices.D: Some medieval epistemologists had epistemological beliefs that contradicted the epistemological beliefs of other medieval epistemologists.
answerChoices.E: There is much debate as to which medieval thinkers, if any, were epistemologists.

questions.stimulus:
Official: Six months ago, the fines for parking violations
 on the city’s streets were raised to help pay for
 the parking garage that had just opened. Since
 then, parking violations on our streets have
 dropped by 50 percent. Hence, if we want there
 to be even fewer parking violations, the fines
 should be raised again.
questions.questionStem:
The reasoning in the official’s argument is flawed in that
 the argument

answerChoices.A: takes a possible effect of a reduction to be a possible cause of that reduction
answerChoices.B: takes for granted that raising fines a second time will reduce parking violations at least as much as it did the first time
answerChoices.C: fails to take into account the financial benefits the city is now deriving from fines for parking violations
answerChoices.D: takes for granted that people who park their cars illegally would prefer to park legally
answerChoices.E: fails to establish that the initial decrease in parking violations was not due to the availability of additional parking spaces

questions.stimulus:
Consumer advocate: Some agricultural crops are
 now being genetically engineered to produce
 important pharmaceuticals. However, this
 development raises the possibility that the drugs
 will end up in the general food supply, since if
 pollen from a drug-producing crop drifts into
 a nearby field in which an ordinary, non-drug-
 producing crop of the same species is being
 grown, the pollen could fertilize that crop and
 turn it into a drug-producing crop as well.
questions.questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, would most weaken
 the consumer advocate’s argument?

answerChoices.A: As far as scientists know, none of the pharmaceuticals produced by genetically engineered crops would present any danger to public health if they were present in the general food supply.
answerChoices.B: If pollen from a genetically engineered crop is prevented from drifting into fields in which ordinary crops of the same species are being grown, then there is no risk of the pollen fertilizing the latter crops.
answerChoices.C: The genetically engineered crops that produce pharmaceuticals are not among the crop species that comprise the largest portions of the general food supply.
answerChoices.D: In crops genetically engineered to produce pharmaceuticals, the drugs are not present in any part of the plant used for food in ordinary crops of the same species.
answerChoices.E: If pollen from a drug-producing crop turned an ordinary crop of the same species into a drug-producing crop, it would be possible for scientists to identify the latter crop.

questions.stimulus:
Most of the members of Bargaining Unit Number 17 of the
 government employees’ union are computer programmers.
 Thus it is certain that some of the government employees
 who work in the Hanson Building are computer
 programmers, since _______.
questions.questionStem:
The conclusion of the argument follows logically if which
 one of the following completes the passage?

answerChoices.A: most of the government employees who belong to Bargaining Unit Number 17 but are not computer programmers work in the Hanson Building
answerChoices.B: most members of the executive committee of Bargaining Unit Number 17 work in the Hanson Building
answerChoices.C: most of the government employees who work in the Hanson Building are members of Bargaining Unit Number 17
answerChoices.D: most of the members of Bargaining Unit Number 17 work in the Hanson Building
answerChoices.E: most of the people who work in the Hanson building are government employees

questions.stimulus:
Every Labrador retriever in my neighborhood is a well-
 behaved dog. However, no pet would be well behaved
 if it were not trained. Thus it is training, not the genetic
 makeup of the breed, that accounts for these Labrador
 retrievers’ good behavior.
questions.questionStem:
The flawed reasoning in which one of the following is
 most closely parallel to the flawed reasoning in the
 argument above?

answerChoices.A: All the students at Bryker School excel in their studies. However, students at Bryker School would not excel if they did not have good teachers. Thus, all schools should hire good teachers if they want their students to excel.
answerChoices.B: Whenever it snows there are relatively more car crashes on the highways. Yet in general, there would not be car crashes unless people were careless. So it is not icy roads, but carelessness, that causes car crashes when it snows.
answerChoices.C: Every musician I know is a good dancer. Every mathematician I know is a bad dancer. Thus, it is a sense of rhythm, not the ability to count, that is most responsible for good dancing.
answerChoices.D: All of the good cooks in my country use butter, not margarine, in their cooking. Thus, if you want to be a good cook, you must use butter, not margarine, in your cooking.
answerChoices.E: All of the students in my algebra class received an A, even though none of them can solve word problems. No student who is unable to solve word problems has an adequate understanding of algebra. It follows that the students in my class received A’s not because they did any good work.

questions.stimulus: Columnist: The dangers of drinking are greatly exaggerated in the medical press. We are always hearing about the extent to which alcohol can shorten one’s life, but my grandfather drank heavily his entire life and lived to be 95.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the columnist’s argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: does not address moral objections to alcohol consumption
answerChoices.B: fails to consider factors other than alcohol consumption that can shorten one’s life
answerChoices.C: only addresses the length of a life, and not the quality of that life
answerChoices.D: confuses the cause of a phenomenon with an effect of that phenomenon
answerChoices.E: relies merely on anecdotal evidence to challenge a general claim

questions.stimulus: Some have argued that using food crops to produce fuel represents an unprecedented attack on the food supply. It seems immoral to divert crops from the food supply while there is a need for food. But we currently divert crops from the human food supply to feed livestock. So the diversion of food to fuel is not actually a radical break with traditional practices.
questions.questionStem: The argument proceeds by

answerChoices.A: arguing that the bad consequences of a practice are outweighed by the good consequences of that practice
answerChoices.B: countering the charge that a practice has a bad consequence by trying to show that the practice does not actually have that consequence
answerChoices.C: rebutting a charge that a practice is radical by contending that the practice is analogous with an existing one
answerChoices.D: rejecting the charge that a practice is immoral by trying to undercut the moral foundation of the charge
answerChoices.E: supporting a moral objection to a practice by trying to show that the practice is actually different from practices that might seem similar

questions.stimulus: Hernandez: Celebrities’ public pronouncements can warp a debate because people grant more weight to celebrities’ opinions than to ordinary people’s. For that reason, celebrities should avoid talking publicly about controversial issues on which they have no expertise. Liu: But celebrities are full members of their communities. It is not their fault if people give their opinions more credence than they should. So it is absurd that they should not feel free to join controversial debates.
questions.questionStem: Hernandez and Liu disagree with each other about which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: People grant more weight to celebrities’ opinions than to ordinary people’s.
answerChoices.B: Celebrities should avoid talking publicly about controversial issues on which they have no expertise.
answerChoices.C: Celebrities’ pronouncements on controversial issues can warp debates on those issues.
answerChoices.D: The public should disregard what celebrities say about controversial issues.
answerChoices.E: Celebrities are responsible for the fact that people give their opinions more credence than they should.

questions.stimulus: A process of extracting caffeine from coffee without seriously compromising the coffee’s taste was introduced a number of years ago. When this decaffeinated coffee first came on the market, however, many coffee drinkers reported that it tasted rather bad.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the statements above?

answerChoices.A: The percentage of coffee drinkers who drink only decaffeinated coffee is much larger today than it was at the time the process was introduced.
answerChoices.B: Many coffee drinkers would not drink decaffeinated coffee even if they believed that it tasted as good as regular coffee.
answerChoices.C: The taste of any kind of coffee can be affected by the foods that are consumed along with it.
answerChoices.D: Coffee that is decaffeinated through this process generally costs more than regular coffee.
answerChoices.E: During the years in which the process was introduced, coffee processors used only low-quality coffee beans for their decaffeinated products.

questions.stimulus: Researchers gave each of eighteen subjects a playing card, then offered them money to lie to a computer about the identity of the card while undergoing a scan by functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). When subjects lied, the scans revealed increased activity in several regions of the brain known to be stimulated by stress. This supports the idea that fMRI can eventually form the basis of an effective lie detector.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following would, if true, most weaken the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Existing methods of lie detection, including the polygraph, have not been shown to be reliable.
answerChoices.B: The majority of people regard lying in an experimental situation as unethical.
answerChoices.C: The amount of stress that accompanies lying varies widely from person to person and is also affected by the circumstances in which the lie is told.
answerChoices.D: Telling a carefully planned lie causes less stress than telling a lie spontaneously.
answerChoices.E: Stress reactions in the brains of subjects who are being truthful are similar to those that occur in the brains of subjects who are lying.

questions.stimulus: Prominent government officials have denied that their policies have produced serious environmental degradation. But the facts show otherwise. Last year, at the urging of certain mining companies, the government repealed a long-standing provision prohibiting the dumping of mining wastes into streams. Since that time, hundreds of miles of vital streams have been buried under bulldozed mining wastes.
questions.questionStem: The argument relies on which one of the following assumptions?

answerChoices.A: Without the urging of certain mining companies, the government would not have lifted the ban on dumping mining wastes into streams.
answerChoices.B: The prominent government officials who deny that government policies have produced serious environmental degradation do not really believe what they are claiming.
answerChoices.C: The mining companies that urged repeal of the ban on dumping mining wastes in streams were among those that buried hundreds of miles of streams under mining wastes.
answerChoices.D: The government is generally more responsive to pressures from the mining industry than from environmentalists.
answerChoices.E: If the ban on dumping mining wastes in streams had not been repealed, considerably less mining waste would have found its way into streams.

questions.stimulus: Critic: It generally holds true of concert pianists that the more famous the musician, the greater the pleasure of his or her audience. In my view, this is only fair and should give no cause for cynicism about the ability of audiences to distinguish good playing from bad.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strongly supports the critic’s view?

answerChoices.A: The fame of concert pianists usually reflects their talent as musicians.
answerChoices.B: Some of the finest concert pianists are unknown to the general public.
answerChoices.C: In general, the more famous the pianist, the larger the audiences that he or she can draw.
answerChoices.D: Even the finest concert pianists cannot play consistently well at every performance.
answerChoices.E: The very best concert pianists often perform works that are difficult for audiences to appreciate.

questions.stimulus: Scientists found the remains of several species of mites trapped in rocks in a high-altitude cave. Radioactive dating shows that the mites were trapped about 2,000 years ago. The mite species in the rocks no longer live in the vicinity of the cave, but they are found a few miles away in a cooler area. Therefore, the area around the cave was probably cooler 2,000 years ago, since _______.
questions.questionStem: The conclusion of the argument is most strongly supported if which one of the following completes the passage?

answerChoices.A: the mite species found in the rocks can only survive in very specific climates
answerChoices.B: the cooler area a few miles away from the cave also has a somewhat wetter climate
answerChoices.C: the mite species that were trapped in the rocks did not live in the vicinity of the cave much earlier than 2,000 years ago
answerChoices.D: the mite species found in the rocks only live at high altitudes
answerChoices.E: there are fewer mite species living in the vicinity of the cave today than there were 2,000 years ago

questions.stimulus: Market studies confirm that consumers shopping for automobiles primarily seek those that are most reliable. An automobile is reliable if it very rarely breaks down and it does not require significantly more maintenance than average. Strangely enough, however, some of the most reliable models do not sell well with those who say they care most about reliability.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

answerChoices.A: Consumers who are shopping for an automobile claim to care more about reliability than about fuel efficiency.
answerChoices.B: Consumers often choose automobile models based on a reputation for reliability, and reputations can be out of date.
answerChoices.C: Some owners of reliable automobiles are reluctant to trade them in for newer vehicles and tend to hold on to them for the life of the automobile.
answerChoices.D: Some automobile models that have been shown to require a lot of maintenance very rarely break down.
answerChoices.E: Some of the most stylish automobiles are some of the most unreliable.

questions.stimulus: A recent study found that most individuals believe that they sleep less than most other people. However, it is obviously not possible that most people sleep less than most other people. Therefore, _______.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following most logically completes the argument?

answerChoices.A: some people believe things that could not possibly be true even in principle
answerChoices.B: most people are not aware of how much they sleep
answerChoices.C: most people underestimate how much they sleep in comparison to others
answerChoices.D: most people think that they do not sleep as much as they should
answerChoices.E: some people incorrectly believe that they sleep less than most other people

questions.stimulus: Ross: Many governments have attempted to regulate strictly or even outlaw theater because of its subversive power. Such strategies have rarely succeeded, probably because people strongly desire theater for entertainment and dramatists always find subtle ways to criticize authorities who treat them harshly. Thus, since dramatists will not criticize governments of which they are honored employees, an effective strategy for controlling theater and satisfying the public is to make dramatists and performers honored employees of the government.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most weaken Ross’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Few governments are willing to shoulder the expense of employing dramatists and performers.
answerChoices.B: Even when completely unregulated, theater rarely leads to the overthrow of a government.
answerChoices.C: Some dramatists criticize their governments even though those governments do not treat them harshly.
answerChoices.D: Most theatrical productions neither criticize government nor support it.
answerChoices.E: The public generally dislikes plays written or performed by government employees.

questions.stimulus: Many hikers now carry cell phones so they can call for emergency assistance from remote areas. Many also use their cell phones to call wildlife offices when they see poachers breaking game laws, enabling wildlife agents to reach the scene before the lawbreakers leave. Poachers, however, avoid areas they know to be frequented by hikers.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Most hikers can afford cell phones.
answerChoices.B: Poaching has decreased as cell phone use has increased.
answerChoices.C: Wildlife agents do not usually carry cell phones.
answerChoices.D: Some hikers hike in areas that are not known by poachers to be frequented by hikers.
answerChoices.E: Cell phones are becoming one of the most effective tools in the effort to protect wildlife from poachers.

questions.stimulus: A cognitive psychologist has claimed that intelligence is the ability to figure out how things work in order to overcome obstacles. If, however, we were to become convinced that a particular being had acquired an understanding of how things work, we would certainly not deny that that being possessed intelligence, even if we were sure that its acquisition of this understanding was not prompted by the desire to overcome some specific obstacle. Clearly, then, the cognitive psychologist’s definition is inadequate.
questions.questionStem: In the passage the author does which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: rejects a definition on the grounds that the terms employed in the definition would make it impractical to determine which cases it covers
answerChoices.B: uses a hypothetical application of a definition to argue that the definition would have unacceptably counterintuitive consequences
answerChoices.C: argues that a proposed definition does not specify the meaning of the concept being defined narrowly enough for the definition to be applied
answerChoices.D: rejects a definition on the grounds that if it were accepted as correct, the term being defined would apply to things to which it normally does not apply
answerChoices.E: argues against a proposed definition on the grounds that those who support it do so at least partly on an inappropriate appeal to authority

questions.stimulus: Environmentalist: The adoption of genetically engineered crops in agriculture is moving so rapidly and is monitored so loosely that it poses a significant risk of damaging sensitive ecosystems. One such crop had already been widely planted when a study found that it could threaten monarch butterflies. Therefore, before any new genetically engineered crop is put into agricultural production, rigorous testing of its safety should be required.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the environmentalist’s reasoning?

answerChoices.A: A genetically engineered crop should not be put into agricultural production if rigorous testing has shown it to be risky.
answerChoices.B: If a crop has no potential for posing environmental risks, it may be put into agricultural production without testing of its safety.
answerChoices.C: No crop that might present risks to the environment should be allowed into agricultural production unless its safety has been thoroughly tested.
answerChoices.D: If rigorous testing of any genetically engineered crop that is in agricultural production shows that that crop poses environmental risks, production of that crop should be discontinued.
answerChoices.E: If rigorous studies do not find evidence that a crop would present risks if it is brought into agricultural production, no further testing of that crop’s safety is required.

questions.stimulus: Faculty member: The university’s financially minded president holds that some academic programs should be eliminated because they do not serve student demands. According to him, the university is a business and the students are consumers, and it is the responsibility of any business to satisfy consumer demand. But the education of students is not analogous to the providing of consumer goods. Therefore, the president is mistaken in claiming that academic programs should be tailored to suit student demand.
questions.questionStem: The faculty member’s argument is most vulnerable to the criticism that it

answerChoices.A: argues for a view without showing that an argument against that view fails
answerChoices.B: appeals to popular opinion to justify a conclusion
answerChoices.C: treats merely analogous things as identical
answerChoices.D: improperly attacks the university president’s moral character
answerChoices.E: rejects a view on the grounds that someone has given inadequate reasons for accepting that view

questions.stimulus: A recent study carefully tracked the specific behaviors of five East African chimpanzee groups of one subspecies, and of two West African groups of another subspecies, in activities such as grooming and foraging. The study found that one of the East African groups was behaviorally more similar to the West African groups than to the other East African groups. It is therefore likely that these behaviors are determined by cultural factors rather than by genetics.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, provides the most support for the argument?

answerChoices.A: Chimpanzees sometimes copy the behavior of other chimpanzees, whether or not they are closely related genetically.
answerChoices.B: Chimpanzees that are new to a group sometimes bring with them new behaviors as well as new genetic characteristics.
answerChoices.C: The chimpanzee groups studied face different environmental challenges due to their different locations in Africa.
answerChoices.D: The behavioral differences in the chimpanzee groups studied are sufficient to make each group recognizably distinct from all the others.
answerChoices.E: Of the chimpanzee groups studied, the five East African groups live in closer proximity to each other than do the two West African groups.

questions.stimulus: Essayist: It would be wrong to defend current testing procedures for new medications simply by appealing to the fact that test subjects are volunteers who are both apprised of and compensated for the risks involved. For while it is not wrong to pay people to do something if they are freely choosing to do it, the same cannot be said if the choice is made under duress.
questions.questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the essayist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Possessing information about the possible consequences of the choices one makes does not ensure that one’s choices are free.
answerChoices.B: No transaction can be justified merely on the grounds that those participating in the transaction do so voluntarily.
answerChoices.C: Anyone who acts without complete freedom is acting under some form of externally imposed duress.
answerChoices.D: There is nothing wrong with accepting money for putting oneself at risk.
answerChoices.E: People should be permitted to perform any action so long as that action is freely chosen.

questions.stimulus: Putting a tap in a healthy maple that has a trunk 12 or more inches in diameter will not harm the tree. Silver maples, red maples, and Manitoba maples can all be tapped for making maple syrup. The sugar maple, however, is best for syrup making, because of all the maples its sap has the highest concentration of sugar.
questions.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

answerChoices.A: A maple whose trunk is more than 12 inches in diameter is unhealthy if it is harmed by tapping.
answerChoices.B: The healthiest maple trees are usually those with the largest trunks.
answerChoices.C: A maple tree that has been harmed will produce very little sap.
answerChoices.D: Putting a tap into an unhealthy maple tree that is less than 12 inches in diameter will harm it.
answerChoices.E: The maple trees most commonly used for making syrup are sugar maples.

questions.stimulus: Company spokesperson: Although our products are the most expensive in our industry, they are also the best available. After all, consider any less expensive product made by one of our competitors. If it were as good as, or better than, our product, it would cost as much, or more.
questions.questionStem: The reasoning in the company spokesperson’s argument is flawed in that the argument

answerChoices.A: contains a premise that presupposes the truth of the conclusion
answerChoices.B: fails to make a needed distinction between the best product currently available and the best product that could be produced
answerChoices.C: treats a cause of a product being the most expensive as an effect of its being the most expensive
answerChoices.D: presumes that because something is true of each of a company’s products it is also true of the company as a whole
answerChoices.E: bases a conclusion on claims that are inconsistent with each other
